0.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, CMS-855S ownership fields list foreign-national nominee owners whose identity documents repeat across dozens of unrelated supplier NPIs. Newly acquired supplier NPIs jump from dormant to top-decile DMEPOS claim volume within weeks of a PECOS change-of-ownership filing. Beneficiary HICN/MBI identifiers on the claims span states far outside the supplier's PECOS service area with no prior utilisation history. Multiple supplier NPIs share one bank routing and account number on the CMS-588 EFT authorisation record. Suboxone and lab claims carry rendering NPIs whose state licence board file shows lapsed licensure or an OIG LEIE exclusion match.
0.features_to_create: 1) Post-acquisition volume spike: on supplier NPI x week, compute billed DMEPOS charges divided by the provider's trailing 26-week median in the 12 weeks after a PECOS ownership-change date; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 2) Shared payment-instrument degree: on bank account number from CMS-588, compute the count of distinct billing NPIs and distinct TINs mapped to it; fires when that count exceeds one without a disclosed common-ownership record; action prepay edit plus site visit. 3) Rendering-provider registry mismatch: on claim line, compare rendering NPI against the state licence board active-licence file and OIG LEIE on the date of service; fires on an exact exclusion or expired-licence match; action claim suspension.

1.ways_to_identify: This item is an annual enforcement summary rather than a single case, so no specific claim, provider NPI or adjudication point is identified. Without dates of service, billed codes or a payer file, no prepay signal can be derived from it. The nearest non-claims route is tracking the named defendants from the published charging documents into PECOS and OIG LEIE for enrolment revocation.
1.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is an automated feed of DOJ charging announcements matched to NPPES and PECOS records to trigger enrolment review and exclusion listing.

2.ways_to_identify: This is municipal bribery and grant embezzlement, so there is no health care claim and no adjudication point. No provider NPI, HCPCS code or date of service exists to edit against. The nearest detection route is grant subrecipient audit comparing nonprofit disbursement ledgers to bank transfers reaching officials or intermediaries.
2.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is a grants-management rule matching subrecipient payee bank accounts against the city's official financial-disclosure and vendor files.

3.ways_to_identify: This is street diversion of pills obtained from physician offices, so there is no submitted claim and no adjudication point. The pills were taken from office stock rather than dispensed under a billed NDC. The nearest detection route is state PDMP and DEA 222/ARCOS reconciliation of office-stock oxycodone acquisitions against documented administrations. Office inventory shrinkage reported on DEA Form 106 loss reports gives a second non-claims signal.
3.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is an ARCOS-to-PDMP reconciliation on DEA registrant number computing acquired controlled-substance dosage units minus dispensed and administered units.

4.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Day Habilitation units billed exceed the attendance hours recorded in the OPWDD service documentation and daily attendance log. Self-identified overpayments appear in the provider's internal review files but no matching claim void or adjustment reaches the payer's remittance history. Billed units per beneficiary per day exceed the maximum authorised in the person-centred service plan on file. Staff-to-participant ratios implied by billed units exceed the employees on the payroll register for that date of service. The 60-day report-and-return clock elapses with no credit-balance submission for known overpaid claim control numbers.
4.features_to_create: 1) Unreturned self-identified overpayment: on provider NPI x claim control number identified in an internal review, compute days between the review completion date and any voided or adjusted claim in remittance history; fires when the gap exceeds 60 days; action postpay audit. 2) Units versus attendance: on beneficiary x date of service, compute billed Day Habilitation units minus documented attendance units in the OPWDD log; fires when the difference is positive; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Staffing capacity: on provider NPI x date of service, compute total billed service hours divided by direct-care hours on the payroll register; fires when the ratio exceeds the programme's authorised staffing ratio; action prepay edit.

5.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, procedure claim volume for the gynecologic CPT codes far exceeds the single-use device units the practice purchased per wholesaler and distributor pedigree invoices. The same disposable device HCPCS is billed fewer times than the procedures that require it on matching dates of service. Procedure counts per rendering NPI per day exceed the room-time hours physically available in a 24-hour period. Beneficiaries show repeat post-procedure infection diagnosis claims clustered on one rendering NPI within 30 days. State licence board and accreditation survey files record insanitary-condition or infection-control deficiencies at the practice address.
5.features_to_create: 1) Device-purchase reconciliation: on provider NPI x quarter, compute count of procedure claim lines requiring a single-use device minus device units on wholesaler pedigree and 340B/purchase invoices; fires when the difference is positive; action postpay audit plus documentation request (ADR). 2) Same-day procedure capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of CMS work-time minutes for all billed procedures; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 3) Post-procedure infection rate: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of procedure beneficiaries with an infection diagnosis claim within 30 days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

6.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, summed timed-psychotherapy minutes for CPT 90837 and 90834 per rendering NPI per date of service exceed 24 hours. Session start times recorded in the encounter record repeat at identical clock intervals with no AM/PM designation across many beneficiaries. The provider bills 90837 at a share of all psychotherapy lines far above same-specialty peers in the remittance history. Progress notes attached to ADR responses are byte-identical to prior visit notes for the same beneficiary. Facility staff roster hours on payroll records are fewer than the counselling hours billed under supervised NPIs that day.
6.features_to_create: 1) Impossible clinician day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of CPT-defined minimum minutes for all timed psychotherapy lines; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) High-intensity code share: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute 90837 lines divided by all psychotherapy lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Note duplication: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of consecutive encounter notes with identical text hashes in submitted documentation; fires when that count exceeds one; action postpay audit.

7.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed nursing time units per date of service exceed the aggregate nurse hours on the facility's payroll timesheets. A single licensed nurse NPI appears on claims totalling more than 24 hours in one calendar day. Billed nursing units exceed the staffing hours reported to the state licensing agency for that group home census. Nurse licence numbers on the claims do not appear on the state board of nursing active file for the service dates. Units per resident per day exceed the level authorised in the DMAS service authorisation record.
7.features_to_create: 1) Payroll-hours ceiling: on provider NPI x date of service, compute billed nursing time units converted to hours minus nurse hours on the payroll timesheet file; fires when the difference is positive; action prepay edit. 2) Single-nurse day limit: on nurse licence number x date of service, compute total billed service hours across all facilities; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Authorisation overage: on beneficiary x date of service, compute billed units minus service-authorisation units on file; fires when positive; action documentation request (ADR).

8.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, revision-arthroplasty CPT claims within a short interval of the index implant cluster on one device catalogue number and UDI. The implant UDI on the hospital claim maps to a device with no FDA clearance record in the GUDID and 510(k) databases. Surgeons with the highest use of the implant appear in Open Payments with consulting fees and travel from the manufacturer. Adverse-event volume in MAUDE for the device is far below the payer's observed revision counts. Prior-authorisation records show the same surgeon NPI concentrating one manufacturer's device far above peers.
8.features_to_create: 1) Early revision rate by device: on device catalogue number or UDI, compute the share of implant claims followed by a revision CPT within 24 months; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus other implants in the same product category; action postpay audit. 2) Clearance-registry mismatch: on claim line, match the billed device UDI against the FDA GUDID and 510(k) clearance file on the date of service; fires on an exact absence of clearance; action prepay edit. 3) Payment-linked device concentration: on surgeon NPI x manufacturer, compute the share of implants from that manufacturer alongside Open Payments transfer-of-value totals; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement.

9.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, index implant claims for one device catalogue number show revision surgery within 24 months at rates above comparable knee systems. The implant UDI on hospital claims has no matching clearance entry in the FDA GUDID or 510(k) file. Open Payments records show consulting fees, travel and entertainment from the manufacturer to the highest-volume implanting surgeon NPIs. MAUDE adverse-event counts for the device are far below the revision volume observed in paid claims. Prior-authorisation files show one surgeon NPI selecting a single manufacturer's implant far above same-specialty peers.
9.features_to_create: 1) Device-level early failure: on device catalogue number or UDI, compute revisions within 24 months divided by index implants; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer implants in the same category; action postpay audit plus coverage review. 2) Unlisted-device edit: on claim line, match billed UDI to the FDA clearance registry active on the date of service; fires on exact registry absence; action prepay edit. 3) Transfer-of-value concentration: on implanting NPI x manufacturer x year, compute manufacturer share of implants and Open Payments dollars received; fires when both exceed the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement.

10.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the genomic assay CPT is ordered by one referring NPI in identical volume every month, consistent with a standing order rather than per-patient decisions. Orders arrive without an intervening E/M or oncology encounter claim between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary. A small set of ordering NPIs accounts for a disproportionate share of one laboratory's test volume. Those same ordering NPIs appear in Open Payments with honoraria, meals and gift-card-equivalent transfers from the laboratory. Test claims lack a supporting breast-cancer diagnosis code meeting the payer's coverage policy on the date of service.
10.features_to_create: 1) Standing-order signature: on ordering NPI x HCPCS x month, compute the coefficient of variation of monthly order counts and the share of ordered tests lacking a prior E/M encounter with the same beneficiary; fires when order counts are near-constant and the no-encounter share exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Referral concentration: on laboratory NPI, compute the share of test volume from the top ordering NPIs plus Open Payments dollars those orderers received from the lab; fires when both exceed the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Coverage-diagnosis match: on claim line, compare the submitted diagnosis to the payer's coverage policy list for the genomic CPT; fires on exact absence of a covered diagnosis; action claim suspension.

11.ways_to_identify: This is estate and bank fraud against an incapacitated individual, so there is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point. No NPI, HCPCS code or date of service exists to edit. The nearest detection route is bank elder-financial-exploitation monitoring of large beneficiary changes and fiduciary fee arrangements.
11.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is a financial-institution rule comparing testamentary or account beneficiary changes for customers over 80 against recent capacity-related medical or guardianship records.

12.ways_to_identify: This is estate and bank fraud, with no claim submitted to any health plan and no adjudication point. No provider, code or service date exists that a payer could edit against. The nearest detection route is SAR filing by the bank on abrupt beneficiary designation changes benefiting a non-relative.
12.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is a bank monitoring rule computing the dollar share of an elderly customer's estate redirected to a single non-relative payee within a short window.

13.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on the L-code brace and genomic test claims has no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. One ordering NPI signs orders for beneficiaries across many states within a single week. The beneficiary's other claims show no telehealth encounter claim from that ordering NPI near the order date. Order signature timestamps cluster in bursts far exceeding a plausible per-order review time in a workday. Ordered volume routes to a small closed set of supplier and laboratory NPIs sharing an address in PECOS.
13.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M or telehealth claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer geographic dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct billing supplier NPIs on ordered claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Orderer-supplier closure: on ordering NPI, compute the share of ordered DMEPOS and lab claims billed by supplier NPIs sharing a PECOS practice address; fires when that share exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR).

14.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, brace and genetic test claims carry an ordering NPI with no prior evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiary. That ordering NPI's daily signed-order count exceeds the number of patient contacts possible in a 24-hour day. Beneficiaries on the orders reside in states far from the ordering physician's NPPES practice location. No telehealth encounter claim exists from the ordering NPI within the coverage-required window before the order date. Ordered claims concentrate in a handful of supplier and laboratory NPIs paying per-order arrangements not disclosed in PECOS.
14.features_to_create: 1) No-encounter order edit: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the gap in days to the nearest qualifying E/M or telehealth claim with the same beneficiary; fires when none exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Signing-capacity ceiling: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries on newly ordered DMEPOS and lab claims; fires when the implied per-patient time falls below a physically possible visit length in 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Orderer-to-supplier concentration: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute the share of ordered volume billed by the top three supplier or lab NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

15.ways_to_identify: This is pandemic small-business loan fraud with no health care claim and no payer adjudication point. The falsified artefacts are IRS payroll forms and bank applications, not claim lines. The nearest detection route is matching applicant-reported employee counts and payroll to IRS Form 941 filings and state unemployment wage records before disbursement.
15.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is a loan-underwriting check on applicant EIN comparing claimed payroll to IRS 941 transcripts and state wage-base filings, and shared bank accounts across affiliated applications.

16.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, dispensed NDC units billed exceed the pharmacy's purchased units in wholesaler pedigree and 867 acquisition data for the same period. Beneficiaries show no corresponding office visit or prescriber encounter claims supporting the high-cost NDCs billed. Refill intervals for Invega Sustenna and Humira are shorter than the days-supply previously paid in remittance history. Prescriber NPIs on the claims report no prescribing relationship in the state PDMP or the plan's prior-authorisation records. Beneficiaries reside far outside the pharmacy's service radius shown in NPPES with no delivery documentation.
16.features_to_create: 1) Purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed dispensed units minus units acquired per wholesaler pedigree invoices; fires when the difference is positive; action payment suspension. 2) Early-refill impossibility: on beneficiary x NDC, compute days between fill dates minus days supply on the prior paid claim; fires when the gap is negative beyond the plan's refill tolerance; action prepay edit. 3) Prescriber-relationship gap: on claim line, compute the count of prior encounter claims between the prescribing NPI and the beneficiary in the lookback window; fires when zero for a high-cost specialty NDC; action documentation request (ADR).

17.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, BLS non-emergency transport claims lack a Physician Certification Statement supporting bed-confined or medically necessary status. Origin and destination modifiers pair residence to a destination with no same-day facility or treatment claim for the beneficiary. Loaded mileage HCPCS A0425 units do not match the road distance between the billed origin and destination ZIP codes. The beneficiary's other claims show ambulatory status, such as outpatient therapy or self-transport-consistent visits, near the transport dates. Repeat round-trip transports for one beneficiary exceed the frequency same-specialty ambulance peers bill for that condition.
17.features_to_create: 1) Destination corroboration: on claim line, compute the count of facility or professional claims for the same beneficiary at the destination on the transport date; fires when zero; action prepay edit. 2) Mileage geometry: on claim line, compute billed A0425 units minus computed road miles between origin and destination ZIP centroids; fires when the difference exceeds the mapping tolerance; action claim suspension. 3) Repeat non-emergency intensity: on beneficiary x supplier NPI x month, compute the count of paid BLS non-emergency transports; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement.

18.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on brace and genomic test claims has no prior encounter claim with the beneficiary. Dates of service fall after the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File and the payer's eligibility file. Limb-specific brace HCPCS are billed for beneficiaries with prior amputation diagnosis or amputation procedure codes in claim history. Component respiratory and UTI PCR CPT codes are billed separately on the same date instead of the correct panel code. Panel testing volume per rendering NPI far exceeds same-specialty urgent-care peers for the same diagnosis mix.
18.features_to_create: 1) Death and anatomy edits: on claim line, compare date of service to the Death Master File date and compare limb-specific HCPCS to prior amputation diagnosis history; fires on an exact registry or anatomical contradiction; action prepay edit. 2) Per-order signing volume: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute distinct beneficiaries with new DMEPOS or genetic test orders and the count lacking any prior E/M; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Panel unbundling: on rendering NPI x beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of individual PCR component CPT codes billed where a single panel code exists; fires when the count exceeds the panel's component threshold; action prepay edit and postpay audit.

19.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a small cluster of plan member IDs from one employer worksite accounts for a disproportionate share of one provider's billings. Treatment dates for those members overlap with shifts recorded in the employer's timekeeping and duty-roster files. Members show identical service code sequences and visit counts across unrelated providers, suggesting scripted billing. Members and their dependents receive services at a frequency far above the plan's same-employer peer distribution. Providers bill members residing far outside the practice's NPPES service area with no referral record.
19.features_to_create: 1) Member-provider concentration: on member ID x rendering NPI, compute the count of paid visits and that member's share of the provider's annual claim volume; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Shift conflict: on member ID x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between billed service times and the employer timekeeping record; fires when overlap is positive; action claim suspension. 3) Recruiter cluster: on rendering NPI, compute the count of distinct members sharing a worksite code who each exceed the calibrated visit percentile; fires when that count exceeds the peer baseline; action payment suspension.

20.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a single member ID appears on acupuncture and podiatry claim lines from unrelated rendering NPIs on the same dates. Claim service dates fall on days the member's employer timekeeping file shows the member on shift far from the provider ZIP. The provider bills an implausible count of services per member per year versus plan norms in the remittance history. No referral or E/M encounter from any other treating NPI precedes the sustained treatment series in the member's claim history. A small cluster of members from one employer group accounts for most of the provider's paid volume in the plan enrolment file.
20.features_to_create: 1) Member super-utiliser: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of paid visit lines per rolling 90 days from claim history; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Employer-cluster concentration: on rendering NPI, compute the share of paid dollars attributable to a single employer group ID over distinct members; fires when concentration exceeds the provider's own trailing baseline; action postpay audit. 3) Shift conflict: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between billed service times and employer timekeeping shift hours; fires when overlap is greater than zero; action prepay edit.

21.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, members show recurring acupuncture and podiatry lines with identical CPT sequences repeated on fixed weekly cadence across many dates. The rendering NPI's paid population is drawn almost entirely from one self-insured employer group in the plan eligibility file. Members' claim histories show no supporting diagnosis, imaging, or E/M encounter from any other NPI. Service dates conflict with employer timesheet and travel records for the member. Provider paid volume rose from near zero to top-decile within weeks of the first member enrolling, per remittance history.
21.features_to_create: 1) Cadence repetition: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of identical CPT-modifier line sets billed at regular intervals over 12 months; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Single-employer dependence: on rendering NPI, compute the ratio of paid dollars from one employer group to total plan dollars; fires when above the provider's trailing baseline; action postpay audit. 3) Attendance conflict: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between billed encounter time and employer timeclock hours; fires when overlap exceeds zero; action claim suspension.

22.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, J-code units billed across all payers exceed units the practice purchased per wholesaler pedigree and 340B/distributor invoice data. Claim lines show the same infusion HCPCS at full-vial units for every patient with no JW drug-wastage or partial-dose variation. E/M levels billed by the rendering NPI skew to 99214/99215 far above same-specialty peers in remittance history. Some infusion dates of service conflict with the beneficiary's other claims placing them elsewhere. Manufacturer free-sample distribution records list the practice as a sample recipient for the same NDCs billed.
22.features_to_create: 1) Purchase-to-billed reconciliation: on provider TIN x NDC/HCPCS per quarter, compute billed units minus units acquired from wholesaler pedigree data; fires when billed units exceed acquired units; action payment suspension and postpay audit. 2) E/M level skew: on rendering NPI, compute the share of 99214 and 99215 among all office E/M lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit on high-level codes. 3) Dose uniformity: on ordering NPI x J-code, compute the distinct-value count of billed unit quantities across beneficiaries; fires when that count is one despite varying patient weights; action documentation request (ADR).

23.ways_to_identify: At enrolment and credentialing, CMS-855A/855B ownership and contracting fields show pain practices under contract with the referral-receiving laboratory entity. Physician compensation schedules tie bonus amounts to laboratory referral volume, visible in Stark financial-relationship disclosures. At adjudication, contracted practices' referral rates for toxicology and clinical lab panels exceed same-specialty peers sharply. Lab claims cluster to a narrow set of ordering NPIs all sharing one corporate TIN in NPPES and PECOS. Ordering volume per practice moves in step with quarterly bonus payment dates in the entity's ledgers.
23.features_to_create: 1) Referral concentration graph: on laboratory NPI, compute the share of paid lab dollars originating from ordering NPIs sharing common ownership per CMS-855 fields; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action postpay audit. 2) Ordering intensity by affiliation: on ordering NPI x HCPCS, compute lab tests ordered per 100 patient encounters; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Stark disclosure mismatch: on provider TIN, compute the count of financial relationships present in contracts but absent from enrolment disclosure fields; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension pending enrolment correction.

24.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, summed timed-service minutes for the rendering NPI on one date of service exceed 24 hours. Dates of service fall inside inpatient stays shown on the beneficiary's institutional claims for the same days. Some dates of service postdate the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File. Service dates coincide with border-crossing or travel records showing the rendering physician outside the country. Claim lines pair an E/M code with an add-on psychotherapy code on nearly every encounter, above same-specialty peers.
24.features_to_create: 1) Impossible day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total billed service minutes from CPT time definitions; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Inpatient and decedent conflict: on claim line, compute whether the date of service falls inside an inpatient admit-discharge span or after the Death Master File date; fires on any overlap; action claim suspension. 3) Psychotherapy add-on saturation: on rendering NPI, compute the ratio of E/M lines carrying 90833/90836 add-ons to total E/M lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

25.ways_to_identify: There is no claim submitted to a payer and no adjudication point, because the loss occurred inside a benefits trust account before premiums reached carriers. The nearest detection route is reconciliation of client remittance deposits against carrier premium receipts and 401(k) custodian postings for the same period. Carrier lapse and non-payment notices for covered employees are the earliest external symptom of diverted funds. Bank-level review of withdrawals from the master trust against the contractual per-employee-per-month fee schedule shows unauthorised transfers. Form 5500 filings and ERISA plan audits disclose trust balances inconsistent with participant contributions.
25.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Trust reconciliation: on bank account x month, compute deposits received minus premiums remitted to carriers minus the contracted per-employee-per-month fee times enrolled headcount; fires when the residual is positive or withdrawals lack a matching carrier payment; action postpay audit by the plan fiduciary and referral to EBSA.

26.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim and no adjudication point, because the loss occurred through vendor contracts paid from tribal healthcare grant funds. The nearest detection route is vendor-master screening comparing payee TINs and addresses against officer and executive home addresses in corporate registry filings. Accounts-payable analysis showing a single new vendor receiving an outsized share of disbursements without deliverables is the earliest symptom. Grant-recipient single audits under Uniform Guidance should test contracts for competitive procurement and documented services rendered.
26.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Related-party vendor match: on bank account x payee TIN, compute the count of exact matches between vendor addresses or beneficial owners and organisation officers in state corporate registry and payroll files; fires when the count exceeds zero; action payment suspension and postpay audit by the grantor.

27.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Q-code skin-substitute graft units per beneficiary and per wound far exceed same-specialty peer norms for the same wound size. Billed graft square centimetres exceed documented wound surface area on the ordering NPI's assessment records. Beneficiaries are concurrently on the hospice benefit per the hospice election record, making the graft duplicative. A small set of rendering NPIs order exclusively the largest-size grafts from one distributor NDC/HCPCS, with no size variation. Sales-representative payments and distributor rebate flows appear in Open Payments and CMS-855 ownership disclosures.
27.features_to_create: 1) Graft area versus wound: on beneficiary x wound episode, compute total billed graft square centimetres from Q-code units divided by documented wound area; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Size uniformity: on ordering NPI x HCPCS, compute the distinct-value count of graft sizes billed and the share of the largest size; fires when the largest size share is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Hospice overlap: on claim line, compute whether the date of service falls inside an active hospice election period; fires on any overlap; action prepay edit.

28.ways_to_identify: There is no insurance claim and no adjudication point, because patients paid roughly $300 in cash for the purported scans. The nearest detection route is state licence board and NPPES verification of the claimed doctoral credential against the issuing institution's registrar. FDA and state health department complaint intake on unapproved diagnostic devices and drug claims is the practical trigger. Sale of a veterinary anthelmintic for human cancer treatment is detectable through distributor purchase records and marketing content.
28.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Credential verification: on rendering NPI or practitioner record, compute exact-match count between claimed degrees and issuing-institution registrar and state licence board files; fires when the match count is zero; action site visit and referral to state licensing authority.

29.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the claimed Purple Heart award has no matching entry in DD-214 and service department award records. Medicare entitlement derives from an SSA disability determination that itself rests on the unverified VA rating, visible in the cross-agency eligibility file. Submitted supporting documents show altered fonts, duplicated letterhead, or issuing-office numbers absent from VA document registries. Claimed total inability to self-care conflicts with the beneficiary's own Medicare claims history showing no corresponding care utilisation. Earnings reported to SSA payroll records conflict with the sworn inability to work.
29.features_to_create: 1) Award registry mismatch: on beneficiary claim file, compute exact-match count between claimed decorations and the service department award registry; fires when the count is zero; action claim suspension pending verification. 2) Utilisation-versus-severity gap: on beneficiary x year, compute the count of paid claims consistent with the certified disabling condition; fires when zero while a total-disability rating is in force; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Earnings conflict: on beneficiary x quarter, compute reported wage earnings from SSA payroll data during certified unemployability; fires when earnings exceed the program threshold; action payment suspension.

30.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI has no prior or contemporaneous E/M claim with the beneficiary before the DME, cream, or CGx order. One ordering NPI signs orders for beneficiaries across dozens of states within a single week per claim ZIPs. Ordered items span unrelated categories - braces, topical compounds, and hereditary cancer panels - from unrelated supplier NPIs. Telehealth encounter durations, where billed, sum to more than 24 hours in a day for that rendering NPI. Beneficiaries have no cancer diagnosis in claim history supporting hereditary cancer panel orders.
30.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states, distinct supplier NPIs, and distinct HCPCS categories ordered; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) CGx indication check: on beneficiary x CPT 81162-series line, compute the count of cancer or family-history diagnoses in 12-month claim history; fires when the count is zero; action prior-authorisation requirement.

31.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, because the funds were NIH research grant awards rather than reimbursed services. The nearest detection route is comparing images in grant applications and progress reports against prior published figures using duplication-detection software at peer review. 92.features_to_create: 1) Nominee-owner linkage: on new supplier NPI at enrolment, compute the count of shared addresses, phone numbers, bank accounts, and authorised officials with any suspended or revoked supplier in PECOS; fires when any exact match exists; action claim suspension plus site visit. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the nearest E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 3) Shared-bank-account graph: on bank account, compute the distinct count of supplier NPIs and TINs receiving EFT payments; fires when the count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership; action payment suspension.

93.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the pharmacy NDC mix shows opioid, benzodiazepine, and muscle relaxant trinity combinations far above peer pharmacies. Cash-equivalent inducements appear as zero copay collected on Part D claims despite required cost sharing in the remittance record. Beneficiaries travel unusual distances to this pharmacy, measured from residence ZIP to pharmacy ZIP on the claim. ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree data show controlled-substance purchase volumes above the calibrated percentile for the pharmacy's dispensing population. Multiple prescribers write nearly identical controlled-substance regimens filled almost exclusively at this pharmacy.
93.features_to_create: 1) Trinity combination rate: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of beneficiaries with overlapping opioid, benzodiazepine, and carisoprodol days supply across NDCs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action prepay edit. 2) Copay waiver detection: on beneficiary x pharmacy NPI, compute the share of Part D claims with patient-paid amount of zero where cost sharing was owed; fires when the share exceeds the pharmacy's own trailing baseline and peer norm; action postpay audit. 3) Patient draw distance: on pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute the median miles from beneficiary residence ZIP to the pharmacy for controlled-substance fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action documentation request (ADR).

94.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the date of service is later than the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File and Medicare enrolment record. The rendering NPI's state licence board file shows no active affiliation, and NPPES shows a changed practice address after resignation. Psychotherapy CPT units per rendering NPI per day exceed feasible therapy minutes in a 24-hour period. The clinic bills the same rendering NPIs continuously with no gaps, unlike normal clinician schedules with absences. Rendering clinicians simultaneously appear on claims from unrelated employers in other cities on identical dates.
94.features_to_create: 1) Deceased beneficiary edit: on claim line, compute the day gap between date of service and the date of death in the Death Master File and enrolment database; fires when the service date is after death; action prepay edit. 2) Rendering-clinician capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total psychotherapy CPT minutes summed across all payers; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the licensed workday; action claim suspension. 3) Departed-clinician billing: on rendering NPI x billing TIN, compute the count of claim lines dated after the clinician's last verified employment or licence affiliation date; fires when that count is above zero; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension.

95.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI has no E/M or telehealth claim with the beneficiary before the genetic test or brace order. Portal audit logs show order-signing intervals of seconds per record for a single ordering NPI. Dates of service postdate beneficiary death recorded in the Death Master File. Lower-limb brace L-codes are ordered for beneficiaries with prior amputation diagnosis codes in their claim history. One ordering NPI writes orders spanning many states and dozens of unrelated supplier and lab NPIs weekly.
95.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the nearest E/M or telehealth claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) Anatomic contradiction: on claim line, compute whether the ordered orthotic HCPCS body site matches a limb with a prior amputation diagnosis or amputation procedure in the beneficiary's claim history; fires on exact contradiction; action prepay edit. 3) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the distinct count of beneficiary states, supplier NPIs, and laboratory NPIs on signed orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

96.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a single rendering NPI is attached to a volume of E/M claims that exceeds feasible encounter minutes per day. Level 3-5 E/M codes are billed on the same dates as specimen collection codes at temporary drive-through place-of-service settings. The distribution of E/M levels for the practice is nearly all high-level, an outlier versus same-specialty peers. Two E/M encounters are billed per beneficiary per test event, one on the collection date and one on the result date. Payroll and credentialing records show only medical assistants staffing the sites, with no supervising physician onsite documentation.
96.features_to_create: 1) Rendering-NPI capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total E/M typical-time minutes summed across all claim lines; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) E/M level distribution: on billing TIN x month, compute the share of E/M claim lines at levels 3 through 5 for COVID testing encounters; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Duplicate result-call encounter: on beneficiary x testing episode, compute the count of E/M claim lines within the days following the specimen collection date; fires when a second E/M line exists without a documented separately identifiable service; action prepay edit.

97.ways_to_identify: This is an assault prosecution with no billed service, no payer, and no adjudication point. No claim, enrolment, or prior-authorisation signal exists to observe. The nearest route is law enforcement incident reporting, outside any payment system.
97.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Handle through law enforcement incident reporting rather than claims analytics.

98.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI has no prior E/M or telehealth claim with the beneficiary for the genetic test or brace order. Portal signing logs show hundreds of orders signed per session by one ordering NPI with negligible review time. The same ordering NPI supplies orders to many unrelated laboratory and supplier NPIs across widely dispersed states. Cancer and pharmacogenetic panel CPT codes are ordered without any oncology or medication-management diagnosis in the beneficiary's history. Payments from the telehealth aggregator to the signing physician appear as per-order fees in the entity's disclosed financial relationships.
98.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the order date and the nearest E/M or telehealth encounter claim with that beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Signing velocity: on ordering NPI x day, compute the count of signed orders divided by logged portal minutes; fires when orders per minute exceed a physically feasible review rate; action claim suspension. 3) Clinical indication mismatch: on claim line for hereditary cancer or pharmacogenetic panels, compute the presence of a supporting diagnosis or prescribed drug in the beneficiary's 12-month claim history; fires when none exists; action prior-authorisation requirement.

99.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, crisis intervention codes make up nearly all of the provider's billed behavioral health lines, an outlier versus peers. Crisis units per rendering counselor per day exceed feasible service minutes in a 24-hour period. Progress notes requested under ADR are byte-identical across unrelated beneficiaries in the same provider's records. Beneficiaries billed for crisis services have no emergency department, ambulance, or inpatient psychiatric claims around those dates. Beneficiary recruitment is suggested by many enrollees sharing a single address or referral source in the Medicaid eligibility file.
99.features_to_create: 1) Crisis code concentration: on provider NPI x month, compute the share of behavioral health claim lines billed at the crisis intervention code and the paid dollars per beneficiary; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Counselor daily minutes: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed service units converted to minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the scheduled shift length; action claim suspension. 3) Note duplication: on provider NPI, compute the pairwise text-similarity share among submitted progress notes across distinct beneficiaries; fires when the identical-note share is above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension.

100.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim here and no adjudication point, since the money moved as a forgivable SBA loan.
100.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control is a pre-forgiveness affiliation check joining the applicant EIN to common-ownership and parent-subsidiary records in Dun & Bradstreet, SAM.gov and IRS EIN filings before forgiveness is granted.

101.ways_to_identify: At adjudication the prescriber DEA number on the NDC claim fails validation against the DEA CSA registration file for that date. The prescriber NPI specialty in NPPES is obstetrics-gynecology while the beneficiary is male on the eligibility file. Distance between the prescriber practice address in PECOS and the dispensing pharmacy address exceeds any plausible care radius. The pharmacy's dispensed quantity of hydrocodone and carisoprodol per month far exceeds ARCOS purchase volume of same-size peers. The same beneficiary receives overlapping opioid and muscle-relaxant fills from a single pharmacy on repeated dates in PDMP data.
101.features_to_create: 1) DEA registration validity: on claim line, compare the prescriber DEA number and schedule authority against the DEA registration file on the fill date; fires on exact registry mismatch or expiry; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber-patient geography: on beneficiary x pharmacy NPI, compute road miles between the prescriber PECOS practice address and pharmacy service address on controlled-substance fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Specialty-drug incongruity: on prescriber NPI x NDC, compute the share of Schedule II-IV fills whose beneficiary sex or diagnosis is incompatible with the NPPES taxonomy; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

102.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, attendance-based service-day counts per beneficiary cluster tightly at the maximum billable days per week in the claim history. Cost-report and bank data show large gift-card and cash-equivalent purchases funded from Medicaid remittance deposits. Nearly every attending beneficiary also has definitive urine drug testing claims from one single referral laboratory TIN. Documentation produced to auditors shows identical group-note text across beneficiaries and dates of service. Provider enrollment on CMS-855 lists staff counts too small to support the billed daily census hours.
102.features_to_create: 1) Attendance saturation: on beneficiary x provider NPI x month, compute billed service days as a fraction of maximum allowable days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Lab referral concentration: on treatment provider NPI x quarter, compute the share of attending beneficiaries with definitive UDT claims billed by a single laboratory TIN; fires when concentration is above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action postpay audit. 3) Capacity-versus-census: on provider NPI x date of service, compute billed patient-hours divided by credentialed staff hours from the CMS-855 and payroll file; fires when the ratio implies more than 24 staff-hours per staff member per day; action payment suspension.

103.ways_to_identify: This case is post-conviction concealment of assets from restitution collection, so there is no claim and no adjudication point.
103.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control is a monthly join of convicted-provider identifiers to OIG LEIE, PECOS ownership and payer bank-account records so any new TIN or bank account sharing the individual triggers payment offset.

104.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the share of the practice's Medicaid patients escalating from preventive codes to restorative or surgical codes exceeds peers. Practice bank and general-ledger records show recurring per-head payments to a marketing entity tracking new Medicaid patient counts. New beneficiaries arrive in geographic clusters far from the practice address on the CMS-855 enrollment file. Many new patients share the same referral source field and have no prior dental claim history with any local provider. The practice's new-patient volume steps up abruptly relative to its own trailing remittance baseline after a marketing contract begins.
104.features_to_create: 1) Preventive-to-treatment conversion: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of beneficiaries with D2000-D7999 claims to beneficiaries with only D0100-D1999 claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 2) Recruiter cluster: on practice NPI x month, compute the count of new Medicaid beneficiaries whose residence ZIP lies outside the enrolled service area, divided by all new beneficiaries; fires when above the provider's trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Per-patient marketing spend: on TIN x quarter, compute vendor payments to marketing entities divided by count of new Medicaid beneficiaries billed; fires when the quotient approximates a fixed per-patient amount; action payment suspension.

105.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, new Medicaid patient arrivals per month step far above the practice's own trailing remittance baseline. Practice ledgers show payments to a recruiting vendor scaling linearly with counts of new Medicaid beneficiaries billed. Referred beneficiaries reside in ZIPs outside the service area declared on the CMS-855 enrollment record. Multiple unrelated dental TINs pay the same vendor and share overlapping referred-beneficiary rosters in claim history. Provider agreement attestations in the CTDHP provider manual bar per-patient compensation, which conflicts with the vendor invoices.
105.features_to_create: 1) Shared-recruiter graph: on marketing vendor TIN, compute the count of distinct dental provider NPIs paying it and the count of beneficiaries appearing across their claims; fires when graph degree is above the calibrated percentile versus peer vendors; action postpay audit. 2) New-patient surge: on provider NPI x month, compute new Medicaid beneficiaries billed versus the provider's trailing twelve-month mean; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline by the calibrated multiple; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Out-of-area referral rate: on provider NPI x quarter, compute the share of billed beneficiaries whose ZIP falls outside the enrolled service area; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement.

106.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, presumptive codes 80305-80307 and definitive codes G0480-G0483 appear for the same beneficiary on the same date of service. The ordering NPI has no clinical encounter claim between the presumptive result date and the confirmatory order date. Definitive testing is billed at the highest analyte tier for nearly every beneficiary regardless of diagnosis. Beneficiary addresses concentrate at a small number of sober-home addresses in the eligibility file. Testing frequency per beneficiary per month exceeds treatment-plan intervals documented in prior-authorisation records.
106.features_to_create: 1) Same-day reflex without review: on beneficiary x date of service, compute whether both a presumptive UDT code and a definitive UDT code are billed with no intervening practitioner E/M claim; fires when both present and gap is zero days; action prepay edit. 2) Tier uniformity: on laboratory NPI x quarter, compute the share of definitive UDT claims at the highest analyte tier; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Congregate-address density: on residence address x laboratory NPI, compute the distinct beneficiary count and monthly tests per beneficiary; fires when tests per beneficiary per month exceed the plan-documented interval; action postpay audit.

107.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on L-code brace claims has no prior E/M encounter with that beneficiary. One telemedicine ordering NPI signs orders for beneficiaries across dozens of states within a single week. Beneficiary residence ZIPs fall far outside the service area on the supplier's CMS-855S enrollment record. The same beneficiary receives the same L-code brace from several unrelated supplier NPIs inside one month. Multiple supplier NPIs with different TINs share one billing agent identifier and one remittance bank account.
107.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim linking that ordering NPI to the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs on ordered DMEPOS claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Shared payee graph: on bank account, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs and TINs receiving remittance; fires when that count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership in PECOS; action site visit.

108.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Modifier 25 appears on nearly every E/M line paired with a same-day injection procedure code. The provider's Modifier 25 rate exceeds the same-specialty peer distribution in the payer's claim history. The provider continued the same modifier pattern after a documented overpayment notice in the remittance and correspondence file. Submitted records show identical E/M note text and no separately identifiable problem beyond the injection indication. The beneficiary's other claims show no distinct diagnosis code supporting a separate evaluation on that date.
108.features_to_create: 1) Modifier 25 intensity: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute Modifier 25 E/M lines divided by all E/M lines billed with a same-day procedure; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Post-notice persistence: on provider NPI, compute the Modifier 25 rate in the 90 days after an overpayment notice versus the 90 days before; fires when the rate does not decline below the provider's own prior baseline; action payment suspension. 3) Diagnosis distinctness: on claim line, compute whether the E/M diagnosis code differs from the procedure diagnosis code on the same date; fires when the codes are identical on a Modifier 25 line; action documentation request (ADR).

109.ways_to_identify: At invoice adjudication, the named employee's degree and years of experience in the contract qualification file fail the labor-category minimums in the Blanket Purchase Agreement. Billed hourly rates for individual staff exceed the rate ceiling for the category their resume supports. Subcontractor staff appear on invoices without a qualification package on file for the billed category. Monthly invoices show the same employee billed under a higher category than in prior periods without any credential change.
109.features_to_create: 1) Category qualification match: on invoice line x employee identifier, compare degree and experience years in the personnel qualification file against the BPA labor-category minimums; fires on exact mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Rate ceiling test: on invoice line, compute billed hourly rate minus the contract ceiling rate for the substantiated category; fires when the difference is positive; action claim suspension. 3) Category drift: on employee identifier x month, compute changes in billed labor category versus the prior invoice with no new credential record; fires when the category rises without a credential update; action postpay audit.

110.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the rendering physician NPI's billed service hours across all sites exceed 24 hours per day. Listed physician NPIs have no payroll, credentialing or CMS-855 reassignment record tied to the billing TIN. Claims are billed from clinic addresses hundreds of miles from the physician's NPPES practice location on the same day. One billing TIN routes remittance to a large number of distinct bank accounts. Medical records supplied after an ADR were created after the request date per document metadata.
110.features_to_create: 1) Reassignment registry match: on claim line, compare the rendering NPI to the CMS-855R reassignment and credentialing roster for the billing TIN on the date of service; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Physician time impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of CPT time-based service minutes across all TINs; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action payment suspension. 3) Payee fan-out: on billing TIN, compute the distinct count of remittance bank accounts and payee names over a rolling quarter; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action site visit.

111.ways_to_identify: At cost-report review, reported direct resident-care spending per patient day falls far below the facility's Medicare and Medicaid revenue per patient day. Owner distributions and related-party payments in the Medicare cost report Worksheet S-2 and A-8-1 rise while vendor payables age. State survey and complaint files show unpaid vendors, staffing shortfalls and supply gaps across commonly owned facilities. Payroll-Based Journal staffing hours per resident day fall below the levels implied by billed acuity in MDS assessments. IRS payroll deposit records show withheld employment taxes never remitted for the same TIN.
111.features_to_create: 1) Care-spend ratio: on facility CCN x cost-report year, compute direct resident-care expense divided by Medicare and Medicaid revenue; fires when below the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action postpay audit. 2) Related-party leakage: on owner TIN, compute the sum of distributions and related-party payments across all commonly owned CCNs in PECOS divided by total program revenue; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer chains; action payment suspension. 3) Staffing-versus-acuity gap: on facility CCN x quarter, compute Payroll-Based Journal nurse hours per resident day minus the hours implied by billed MDS case mix; fires when the gap is negative beyond the calibrated threshold; action site visit.

112.ways_to_identify: At cost-report review, direct care expense per resident day diverges sharply from program revenue per resident day across every facility in the chain. Worksheet A-8-1 related-party and owner-distribution amounts climb while Payroll-Based Journal hours fall. Vendor and third-party administrator complaints of nonpayment appear in state survey files for multiple commonly owned CCNs. Resident personal-needs account balances reported to the state do not reconcile with facility bank records. IRS records show withheld employment taxes and 401(k) remittances not deposited for the chain TIN.
112.features_to_create: 1) Chain cash diversion: on owner TIN x quarter, compute owner distributions plus related-party transfers divided by Medicare and Medicaid remittance received across all CCNs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer chains; action payment suspension. 2) Payroll trust mismatch: on facility TIN x quarter, compute withheld employment tax and benefit amounts from payroll files minus amounts deposited per IRS and plan-administrator records; fires when the difference is positive; action claim suspension. 3) Resident fund reconciliation: on facility CCN x month, compute reported resident trust balances minus segregated bank account balances; fires when the difference is nonzero; action site visit.

113.ways_to_identify: At claim adjudication, the incident report and use-of-force log for the claimed date contain no injury entry for that employee. Independent medical examiner findings contradict the treating physician's restriction letters in the workers' compensation file. Surveillance-equivalent evidence such as payroll, secondary-employment or activity records conflicts with total-disability certifications. Benefit duration for the claimed injury type exceeds the disability duration guideline for that body part. Multiple claimants from the same facility file similar injury claims naming the same treating physician.
113.features_to_create: 1) Incident corroboration: on claim, compare the claimed injury date and mechanism against the employer incident and use-of-force log entries; fires on exact registry mismatch or absence; action claim suspension. 2) Duration outlier: on claimant x injury ICD code, compute paid indemnity weeks divided by the published disability duration guideline; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-injury peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Treating-provider cluster: on treating physician NPI x employer, compute the count of distinct claimants certified totally disabled per quarter; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

114.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the applicant's submitted SSN and name fail SSA Numident verification against date of birth. Two active enrollment records share one SSN with different photographs and biometric identifiers in the state ID file. Claims are paid under the identity on dates when border-crossing or other government records place the true holder elsewhere. The enrollee's claim history shows a demographic profile inconsistent with prior claims under the same SSN.
114.features_to_create: 1) Identity verification: on applicant record, compare submitted SSN, name and date of birth against SSA Numident and state DMV issuance records; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Duplicate identity: on SSN, compute the count of distinct enrollee records with differing photograph hashes or dates of birth; fires when that count exceeds one; action claim suspension. 3) Profile discontinuity: on beneficiary ID, compute the count of claim attributes such as sex, age and chronic diagnoses that change abruptly versus prior claim history; fires when changes exceed the calibrated threshold; action documentation request (ADR).

115.ways_to_identify: This is investor fraud over PPE supply contracts, so there is no health care claim and no adjudication point.
115.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control is verification of purported manufacturing and distribution contracts and bank statements with the named counterparties and issuing banks before investor funds are transferred.

116.ways_to_identify: This document is an appointment announcement with no defendant, no claim and no adjudication point.

117.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on the DMEPOS claim has no prior encounter claim with the beneficiary. Beneficiaries billed by the supplier are geographically scattered far outside the CMS-855S service area. Ordering physician NPIs appear on claims after their NPPES records show retirement, relocation or death. Beneficiaries report no receipt and have no companion diagnosis claims supporting the billed HCPCS. All supplier remittances route to a single bank account tied to a third-party billing agent.
117.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the nearest prior E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Identity reuse velocity: on supplier NPI x week, compute the distinct count of ordering NPIs and beneficiary states on submitted DMEPOS claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) New-supplier ramp: on supplier NPI, compute weekly billed dollars versus its trailing baseline since PECOS enrollment approval; fires when the increase exceeds the calibrated percentile for newly enrolled suppliers; action site visit.

118.ways_to_identify: At credentialing, the facility holds no state licence for the residential or partial hospitalization level of care it bills. The revenue codes and HCPCS billed exceed the service categories authorised in the VA Community Care contract file. Rendering staff NPIs on claims lack the licensure required for the billed level of care in the state board file. Staffing ratios in payroll records fall below the licensure minimum for the billed daily census. Treatment records supplied on ADR lack individualised plans and signatures required for the billed level of care.
118.features_to_create: 1) Licence-to-service match: on claim line, compare the billed level-of-care code against the facility's state licence categories and contract scope on the date of service; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Credentialed staff coverage: on facility NPI x date of service, compute billed patient-days divided by licensed clinician hours from payroll and state board files; fires when the ratio breaches the licensure minimum staffing ratio; action payment suspension. 3) Specialty-program premium: on facility NPI x quarter, compute the share of claims billed at the veteran-specialised rate whose records show identical content to standard-rate cases; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus contracted peers; action documentation request (ADR).

119.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the restricted-formulary NDC is paid with no approved diagnosis code present on the claim or in the beneficiary's other claims. No treatment authorisation request appears in the DHCS prior-authorisation file for fills lacking an approved diagnosis. The dispensing pharmacy's rate of restricted-drug claims without diagnosis documentation exceeds chain peers. Diagnosis codes submitted on restricted-drug claims never appear in the beneficiary's medical claim history from any prescriber. Chain-level override or bypass codes are used at a rate above the pharmacy's own trailing baseline.
119.features_to_create: 1) Diagnosis substantiation: on claim line, compare the diagnosis code on a restricted-formulary NDC against the program's approved diagnosis list and the beneficiary's medical claim history; fires on absence or exact mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Missing authorisation: on beneficiary x NDC, compute whether an approved treatment authorisation request exists in the payer prior-authorisation file for fills lacking an approved diagnosis; fires when none exists; action claim suspension. 3) Store-level bypass rate: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute restricted-drug claims paid without diagnosis substantiation divided by all restricted-drug claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus chain peers; action postpay audit.

120.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the attendant's home address in the enrollment packet sits hundreds of miles from the member's service address on the claim. EVV visit records show no GPS or telephony check-in matching the timesheet hours submitted for those dates of service. The consumer-directed enrollment form lists the same person as both employer of record and approver of the attendant's timesheets. Paid hours per attendant NPI or SSN per day exceed 24 when summed across all timesheets in the fiscal agent file. State vital and address registries show the attendant residing in a different locality than the plan of care service county.
120.features_to_create: 1) Attendant-member distance: on attendant ID x member ID, compute the road miles between attendant address in the fiscal agent enrollment file and member service address; fires when distance exceeds a same-program calibrated percentile without documented relocation; action prepay edit. 2) Self-approval loop: on timesheet record, compute a match count between the member/employer-of-record identifier and the approver identifier; fires when the identifiers are identical; action claim suspension pending documentation request (ADR). 3) EVV corroboration gap: on attendant ID x date of service, compute paid timesheet hours minus EVV-verified visit hours; fires when the gap is above zero for consecutive pay periods; action payment suspension.

121.ways_to_identify: At claim adjudication, timesheet hours for the attendant have no corresponding EVV check-in or check-out record for those dates of service. The attendant's residential address in the fiscal agent enrollment record is hundreds of miles from the member's service address. The same individual appears as both the consumer-employer approving hours and the beneficiary receiving personal care and respite. Cumulative paid hours per attendant across a year exceed plausible full-time limits set in the consumer-directed program rules. Respite hours are billed on the same dates and clock times as personal care hours for the same member.
121.features_to_create: 1) Zero-EVV payroll: on attendant ID x pay period, compute the ratio of EVV-verified minutes to timesheet-claimed minutes; fires when the ratio is below the calibrated program percentile; action claim suspension. 2) Annual hour ceiling: on attendant ID x rolling 12 months, compute the sum of paid personal care and respite hours; fires when the sum exceeds hours physically available given 24-hour days across all members served; action postpay audit and payment suspension. 3) Approver-recipient identity: on timesheet record, compute whether the approver identifier equals the member identifier in the fiscal agent file; fires on exact match; action prepay edit.

122.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, housing transition and sustaining claims list beneficiaries whose only other claims come from a single addiction treatment facility roster. Billed service units per staff NPI per day exceed the hours physically available in a 24-hour day. Newly enrolled provider entities reach top-decile monthly billing within months of their CMS-855 or state DHS enrollment date. Service notes produced under documentation request share identical text blocks across unrelated beneficiaries and dates of service. Payment bank accounts on the provider enrollment file are shared across several distinct provider TINs.
122.features_to_create: 1) Staff-day impossibility: on rendering staff ID x date of service, compute total billed service units converted to minutes across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 1440 minutes; action prepay edit. 2) New-enrollee ramp: on provider NPI x month, compute paid dollars divided by months since state enrollment effective date; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-service peers; action prior-authorisation requirement and site visit. 3) Shared payee graph: on bank account number, compute the distinct count of provider TINs and NPIs receiving remittance; fires when that count exceeds one; action payment suspension.

123.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this procurement matter. The nearest detection route is contract-level: compare delivered lot numbers against required military specification test certificates in the contractor's quality file. Government source inspection and DCMA acceptance records would show missing first-article and conformance test reports before invoice payment.
123.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on contract line item x delivery lot, require matching specification test certificate identifiers in the acceptance record before invoice release, with payment withheld on any lot lacking a certificate.

124.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point because the funds are SBA loans, not reimbursements. The nearest detection route is loan underwriting: match applicant payroll figures against IRS Form 941 and state wage filings before disbursement. Bank statements and tax transcripts submitted with applications can be verified directly with the IRS Income Verification Express Service.
