157.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside claims: on employer EIN x quarter, compute wages reported on employee W-2 and state wage files minus wages reported and deposited on Form 941; fires when the difference exceeds zero; action IRS employment-tax examination.

158.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, stated household income on ACA applications fails income verification against IRS and SSA data hub responses. One broker National Producer Number appears on applications for an implausible count of enrollees relative to peer brokers. The same mailing address or phone number recurs across many unrelated applicant households on the enrolment file. Applicants show projected income clustered just above the Medicaid threshold with zero subsequent utilisation claims. Applicant SSNs mismatch names in the SSA verification response yet the plan remains effectuated.
158.features_to_create: 1) Income-hub mismatch: on application, compute the difference between attested projected income and IRS or SSA reported income from the data hub; fires when attested income clears the subsidy threshold while verified income does not; action subsidy hold pending documentation. 2) Broker enrolment concentration: on broker NPN x month, compute the count of enrolments and the share with zero claims in the first 90 days; fires when both exceed the calibrated percentile versus peer brokers; action commission suspension and enrolment audit. 3) Shared contact graph: on mailing address or phone number, compute the distinct count of unrelated applicant households enrolled; fires when the count exceeds one without documented relationship; action enrolment verification and prepay subsidy edit.

159.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, an E/M code appears on the same date of service as an intravitreal injection CPT for the same beneficiary and rendering NPI. Modifier 25 is appended on nearly every such paired claim rather than exceptionally, visible in the claim line modifier field. The provider's rate of same-day E/M with injections exceeds same-specialty peer distributions in remittance history. Documentation submitted on ADR lacks a separately identifiable service beyond the injection's inherent evaluation. Bilateral injection modifiers and E/M pairing repeat across consecutive monthly visits for the same beneficiaries.
159.features_to_create: 1) Bundled same-day E/M: on claim line, compute whether an E/M code and a same-date injection CPT for the same beneficiary and rendering NPI both pay without a supported modifier 25 basis; fires on any such pairing; action prepay edit. 2) Modifier 25 saturation: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of injection encounters carrying a paired E/M with modifier 25; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Repeat pairing per beneficiary: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of consecutive months with both an injection and same-day E/M; fires when the count exceeds the provider's trailing baseline; action postpay audit.

160.ways_to_identify: This is an annual department-wide settlement round-up, not a single billing scheme with one claim stream to adjudicate.
160.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest route outside claims adjudication is routing each named resolution's underlying mechanic into the payer's edit backlog so component schemes get their own prepay controls.

161.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, amniotic membrane codes V2790 and CPT 65778 billed per beneficiary exceed the eye-surface anatomy plausible in the date-of-service series. Claim volume for a single high-cost graft HCPCS concentrates in one rendering NPI far above same-specialty peers in the state file. Purchase invoices and lot numbers for the amniotic tissue do not reconcile with the units billed on paid remittance history. Chart notes lack a documented corneal defect diagnosis on the ICD fields supporting membrane placement. Payments from the practice TIN to state officials appear in the CMS-855 ownership and managing-employee disclosures and in Open Payments-style vendor records.
161.features_to_create: 1) Tissue-product inventory reconciliation: on provider NPI x HCPCS x quarter, compute units billed for amniotic membrane codes minus units evidenced by supplier purchase invoices and lot numbers; fires when billed units exceed purchased units; action prepay edit. 2) Graft frequency per eye: on beneficiary x provider NPI, compute the count of amniotic membrane placements per laterality modifier in a rolling year; fires when count exceeds the documented defect episodes; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Single-code concentration: on provider NPI x quarter, compute the share of allowed dollars from the top one high-cost HCPCS; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

162.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, dates of service post-date the beneficiary's date on the Death Master File or fall inside a state incarceration roster window. Rendering NPIs appear on claims from a billing TIN with no employment or affiliation record in NPPES or the state provider file. Sentinel fictitious beneficiary identifiers created by investigators appear on submitted claims, an exact registry mismatch. High-complexity urine drug testing codes are billed alongside psychotherapy for nearly every beneficiary of one group. Service notes across a rendering NPI share identical text blocks and identical minute counts across dates of service.
162.features_to_create: 1) Ineligible-beneficiary status: on claim line, compute the gap in days between date of service and the Death Master File date or incarceration admission date; fires when the service date follows either date; action prepay edit. 2) NPI-borrowing detection: on rendering NPI x billing TIN, compute the count of claim lines where no NPPES affiliation or payroll record links the pair; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 3) Test-with-therapy pairing: on billing TIN x month, compute the ratio of definitive urine drug test claims to distinct psychotherapy beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

163.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, procedure claims using single-use device codes exceed the practice's documented device purchases on wholesaler and distributor pedigree records. One rendering NPI bills the same gynecologic procedure CPT for an implausible share of his panel per year. Device-supply HCPCS or revenue-code charges are absent on claims that require a disposable instrument, indicating no new unit consumed. Procedure counts per rendering NPI per date of service imply more room-minutes than a 24-hour day allows. State licence board file and accreditation survey records show unresolved infection-control deficiencies at the practice address.
163.features_to_create: 1) Disposable-device reconciliation: on provider NPI x quarter, compute procedures billed requiring a single-use instrument minus units purchased in distributor pedigree data; fires when billed procedures exceed purchases; action postpay audit plus site visit. 2) Procedure saturation per panel: on rendering NPI x year, compute the share of distinct beneficiaries receiving the target gynecologic CPT; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Day-capacity check: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of procedure typical-time minutes across all billed lines; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit.

164.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the same rendering NPI bills overlapping service minutes for different recipients at the same date and time across separate billing TINs. Claimed service dates fall inside international travel windows shown in border-crossing or payroll absence records. Daily billed service units for one staff member exceed 24 hours across all employers combined. EVV visit records or timesheets carry no GPS check-in matching the recipient address on the claim. Mental health skill-building units per recipient sit above the state service plan authorization on the prior-authorisation record.
164.features_to_create: 1) Cross-employer overlap: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute overlapping service minutes across all billing TINs using start and stop times; fires when any two lines overlap by more than zero minutes; action prepay edit. 2) Daily hour ceiling: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed units converted to hours; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) EVV corroboration: on claim line, compute the count of matching EVV visit records within the billed time window at the recipient address; fires when the count is zero; action documentation request (ADR).

165.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, prenatal care coordination claims lack any corresponding prenatal or obstetric claim from any provider for the same beneficiary. One provider NPI bills care coordination for a count of distinct pregnant enrollees far above same-specialty peers in the state. Care coordination encounter dates cluster on identical calendar days across many unrelated beneficiaries with identical unit counts. Beneficiary contact information on enrollment forms repeats one phone number or address across dozens of member records. Gift and incentive expenditures appear in the provider's cost reports without corresponding beneficiary-signed acknowledgement in the case files.
165.features_to_create: 1) Missing clinical anchor: on beneficiary x provider NPI, compute the count of prenatal or delivery claims from any provider within the coordination episode window; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit. 2) Enrollment identity reuse: on provider NPI, compute the distinct-beneficiary count sharing a single phone number or street address in enrollment records; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action site visit. 3) Coordination volume outlier: on provider NPI x month, compute care coordination units billed per distinct beneficiary; fires when above the provider's trailing baseline and the peer percentile; action payment suspension.

166.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed dates of service precede the beneficiary's enrollment date on the state care-coordination enrollment file. Claims are submitted in bulk with submission dates months after clustered backdated service dates. No prenatal or obstetric claim exists for the beneficiary anywhere in the payer's history during the billed coordination period. One provider NPI shows distinct-beneficiary counts and per-member unit counts above same-specialty peers statewide. Cash enrollment payments to members appear as undocumented 'client incentive' disbursements in the provider's bank and cost records.
166.features_to_create: 1) Backdating detection: on claim line, compute the gap in days between the date of service and the beneficiary's program enrollment date; fires when the service date precedes enrollment; action prepay edit. 2) Submission lag burst: on provider NPI x week, compute the count of claim lines whose date of service precedes submission by more than the provider's trailing median lag; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action claim suspension. 3) Pregnancy corroboration: on beneficiary x episode, compute the count of prenatal, delivery, or postpartum claims from any NPI; fires when the count is zero; action documentation request (ADR).

167.ways_to_identify: This is an office activity announcement with no named defendant, payer, service line, or claim to adjudicate. There is no claim field, code, or date of service to test at any point in the payment lifecycle.
167.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest route outside the claims system is tracking qui tam referral intake so kickback allegations reach credentialing and prepay edit teams once the underlying mechanic is disclosed.

168.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, CMS-855 and state ownership disclosures omit a co-owner who appears on the DHS exclusion list and OIG LEIE. At adjudication, one QSP diagnosing NPI qualifies nearly every child later billed by a single EIDBI provider. Billed ABA hours equal the maximum authorized units on the prior-authorisation record for almost every member every month. Behavioral technician rendering NPIs lack the required state credential or training registry entry on the licence board file. Provider and QSP signatures on treatment plans repeat as identical image files across unrelated member records.
168.features_to_create: 1) Hidden ownership screen: on provider NPI x owner SSN or EIN in CMS-855 disclosures, compute exact matches against OIG LEIE and the state exclusion file including prior addresses and affiliated entities; fires on any exact registry match; action claim suspension plus site visit. 2) Authorization-ceiling billing: on provider NPI x month, compute the share of members billed at exactly 100 percent of authorized ABA units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Single-diagnoser funnel: on diagnosing NPI x provider NPI, compute the share of that provider's members whose autism qualification originates from one assessor; fires when above the peer percentile; action prior-authorisation requirement.

169.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the CMS-855 authorized official's identity fails NPPES and licence board verification against the real physician's practice address and contact record. At adjudication, ordering NPIs on brace L-codes have no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary in claims history. One telemedicine ordering NPI signs DME orders for beneficiaries spread across many states within a single week. HRSA Uninsured Program and Provider Relief Fund payments route to a bank account whose name does not match the enrolled TIN. Controlled-substance dispensing records show hydromorphone withdrawals by one nurse without matching administration entries in the patient's medication record.
169.features_to_create: 1) Enrolment identity verification: on provider NPI at enrolment, compute exact match rate between the 855 authorized official's licence number, DOB, and address and the state board and NPPES records; fires on any mismatch; action claim suspension plus site visit. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that orderer and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 3) Payee mismatch: on bank account, compute the count of distinct enrolled TINs and the name-match score against each TIN's legal name; fires on any name mismatch or multiple unrelated TINs; action payment suspension.

170.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, NDC units billed to Part D and Medicaid exceed units purchased by the pharmacy in wholesaler pedigree and ARCOS acquisition data. Beneficiary refill claims lack any matching pickup signature log in the pharmacy's dispensing records. High-cost NDCs concentrate in a small number of prescriber NPIs whose patients live far from the pharmacy ZIP. Claim reversals for unclaimed prescriptions are absent in remittance history despite peer pharmacies reversing routinely. Days-supply sequences show early refills that overlap prior fills for the same beneficiary and NDC.
170.features_to_create: 1) Inventory-to-claims reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute units billed minus units acquired from wholesaler pedigree data; fires when billed units exceed acquisitions; action payment suspension. 2) Non-reversal rate: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of adjudicated claims never reversed compared with the pharmacy's trailing baseline and peer rate; fires when reversals fall below the calibrated peer percentile; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Refill overlap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute overlapping days-supply across sequential fills; fires when overlap exceeds the plan's early-refill threshold repeatedly; action prepay edit.

171.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, CGX panel claims carry an ordering NPI with no prior E/M or oncology encounter with that beneficiary. One ordering NPI signs hereditary cancer panels for beneficiaries across many distant states in a single week. Specimen collection ZIPs and beneficiary residence ZIPs sit far outside the laboratory's CLIA site service area. The beneficiary's claim history shows no cancer diagnosis or family-history counseling code supporting panel medical necessity. Laboratory payments to marketing entities are structured per reimbursed test in contracts and invoices disclosed at credentialing.
171.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M encounter between the orderer and beneficiary; fires when none exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the distinct count of beneficiary states and laboratory NPIs on CGX panels; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Per-test marketing compensation: on laboratory TIN x vendor, compute the correlation between monthly vendor invoice dollars and reimbursed test counts; fires when payments scale with reimbursed volume; action postpay audit.

172.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one billing agent's submitter ID transmits brace claims for many supplier NPIs sharing owners on CMS-855S disclosures. Ordering physician signatures repeat as identical images across orders for unrelated beneficiaries and different braces. The ordering NPI has no E/M claim with the beneficiary before the L-code date of service. Single beneficiaries receive back, knee, wrist, and shoulder braces within days from related supplier NPIs. Suppliers show near-zero baseline volume then peer-top-decile L-code volume after a PECOS ownership or billing-agent change.
172.features_to_create: 1) Submitter-cluster concentration: on billing submitter ID x month, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs and their shared owner identifiers from 855S disclosures; fires when shared ownership links suppliers above the peer percentile; action payment suspension. 2) Multi-brace saturation: on beneficiary x rolling 30 days, compute the count of distinct L-code brace categories paid across all supplier NPIs; fires when the count exceeds documented medical necessity episodes; action prepay edit. 3) Signature reuse: on ordering NPI, compute the distinct-hash count of signature images across submitted orders relative to order count; fires when one hash covers most orders; action documentation request (ADR).

173.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, CMS-855S owner, managing employee, and W-2 disclosures omit an individual matching an OIG LEIE exclusion record. The enrolled owner of record shares addresses, phone numbers, and bank accounts with a previously excluded individual in payer files. At adjudication, ordering NPIs on brace claims have no E/M encounter with the beneficiary in claim history. Call-center leads produce beneficiary residence ZIPs far outside the supplier's declared service area on the 855S. Supplier claim volume ramps from zero to peer-top-decile within weeks of initial PECOS approval.
173.features_to_create: 1) Exclusion linkage graph: on supplier NPI, compute graph degree linking owners, managing employees, addresses, phones, and bank accounts to any OIG LEIE or prior-revocation identity; fires on any exact registry match on a linked node; action claim suspension plus site visit. 2) New-enrollee ramp: on supplier NPI x week, compute paid L-code dollars against weeks since PECOS approval; fires when volume exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty new enrollees; action prepay edit. 3) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim with that beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists; action prior-authorisation requirement.

174.ways_to_identify: This scheme involves unreported cash payroll and understated workers' compensation exposure, so there is no health care claim and no adjudication point. Detection lives with IRS payroll filings and insurer premium audits rather than with any payer claims edit.
174.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is comparing check-cashing volume at a single casher against the employer's reported Form 941 wages and the workers' compensation payroll audit declaration.

175.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compounded cream claims carry ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary in claims history. A small set of telemedicine prescriber NPIs accounts for most high-cost compound NDC claims across many distant pharmacies. Compound claim ingredient NDCs and per-claim allowed amounts cluster at nearly identical high values across unrelated beneficiaries. Beneficiary residence ZIPs sit far outside the dispensing pharmacy's service area with no local pharmacy attempt in history. Pharmacy remittance history shows recurring payments to a marketing entity proportional to reimbursed compound dollars.
175.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x prescriber NPI, compute days since the last E/M encounter with the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber-pharmacy concentration: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the share of compound NDC claims and distinct pharmacy NPIs and beneficiary states; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Compound cost outlier: on pharmacy NPI x NDC, compute mean allowed dollars per compound claim against the trailing baseline and peer distribution; fires when above the calibrated percentile; action prior-authorisation requirement.

176.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, COVID test kit claims lack any ordering NPI encounter or beneficiary-initiated request record in prior claims history. One supplier NPI bills the same test kit HCPCS to beneficiaries scattered across many states within days. Beneficiary identifiers billed appear in bulk with sequential or purchased-list patterns absent from any other clinical claim history. Claim volume ramps from zero to peer-top-decile immediately after PECOS enrolment with a new bank account. Some billed beneficiaries have dates of service after their Death Master File date.
176.features_to_create: 1) Cold-beneficiary detection: on beneficiary x supplier NPI, compute the count of prior claims of any type linking that beneficiary to the supplier's ordering network; fires when zero and the kit HCPCS is billed; action prepay edit. 2) Geographic dispersion: on supplier NPI x week, compute the distinct count of beneficiary states on test kit claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Deceased and duplicate screen: on claim line, compute the gap between date of service and Death Master File date and the count of other suppliers billing the same kit HCPCS in 30 days; fires on a post-death date or more than one supplier; action claim suspension.

177.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, CMS-855S ownership disclosures omit a part-owner who also invoices the supplier as a marketing vendor. At adjudication, brace L-code claims carry ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Marketing invoice dollars from the supplier TIN track reimbursed claim counts rather than fixed hourly rates. Signed doctors' orders arrive from a lead vendor rather than the beneficiary's treating physician on record. Supplier billing concentrates in a handful of ordering NPIs supplying almost all beneficiaries.
177.features_to_create: 1) Owner-vendor overlap: on supplier NPI, compute exact matches between 855S owner or managing-employee identifiers and payee identifiers on marketing vendor invoices; fires on any match; action postpay audit plus site visit. 2) Per-claim marketing compensation: on supplier TIN x month, compute the ratio of vendor payments to reimbursed claim count and its variance across months; fires when payments scale linearly with reimbursed volume; action payment suspension. 3) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim with the beneficiary; fires when none exists in the lookback; action prepay edit.

178.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, brace L-code claims show ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Supplier proceeds move to bank accounts and TINs belonging to investors not listed on the CMS-855S ownership disclosure. Beneficiary refusal or return activity appears as unusually low reversal and replacement rates versus peer suppliers. Multiple unrelated supplier NPIs share one billing agent submitter ID and one deposit account. Supplier claim volume continues after affiliated principals appear on OIG LEIE or arrest-related enrollment actions.
178.features_to_create: 1) Payee network graph: on bank account, compute the distinct count of enrolled supplier TINs depositing to it and the count of undisclosed beneficial owners versus 855S disclosures; fires on any undisclosed payee; action payment suspension. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim with that beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists; action prepay edit. 3) Post-action continuity: on supplier NPI, compute paid dollars after any affiliated owner appears in LEIE or a revocation record; fires when paid dollars exceed zero after the registry date; action claim suspension.

179.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, brace claims carry ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary in Part B or plan history. One lead-generation source feeds identical beneficiary demographics into orders signed by a small pool of prescriber NPIs. The same beneficiary receives the same L-code from unrelated supplier NPIs across Part B and Medicare Advantage within a month. Physician signature and attestation files repeat identical hashes across unrelated beneficiary orders. Two supplier NPIs share one billing company submitter ID, one address, and one deposit account.
179.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M encounter with the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 2) Cross-payer duplicate device: on beneficiary x HCPCS, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs paid across Part B and Medicare Advantage in 30 days; fires when that count exceeds one without a documented replacement reason; action claim suspension. 3) Submitter and account clustering: on billing submitter ID, compute the distinct count of supplier NPIs sharing an address or deposit account; fires when clustering exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peer billing agents; action payment suspension.

180.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, L-code brace claims carry an ordering NPI with no prior evaluation-and-management claim for that beneficiary. One telemedicine ordering NPI signs orders for beneficiaries spread across dozens of states weekly. Beneficiary residence ZIPs sit far outside the service area on the supplier's CMS-855S enrolment record. Several unrelated supplier NPIs bill the same beneficiary the same brace HCPCS within one month. At enrolment, the CMS-855S owner listed is a nominee whose SSN and address match owners of other newly enrolled supplier NPIs in PECOS.
180.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim linking that ordering NPI to the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Telemedicine orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs on ordered DMEPOS lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Shared-owner supplier cluster: on CMS-855S owner SSN/address, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs enrolled within 12 months and their summed paid DMEPOS dollars; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer new enrollees; action site visit.

181.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim here and no adjudication point, since the money is trust principal rather than payer reimbursement. Detection sits with the trustee's bank and the pooled trust's annual accounting, where beneficiary sub-account balances should reconcile to custodial bank statements. Medicaid agencies reviewing pooled special needs trust filings can compare reported sub-account balances against independently obtained custodian statements.
181.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Trust reconciliation gap: on trust administrator TIN x quarter, compute the difference between summed reported beneficiary sub-account balances and the custodian bank statement total; fires when any non-zero unexplained difference exists; action postpay audit by the state Medicaid trust review unit.

182.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the trans-cranial doppler CPT lines carry cerebral artery occlusion or stenosis diagnosis codes on nearly every patient of one ordering NPI. Diagnosis code appears on the claim with a date of service preceding any interpreting radiologist report in the record. The ordering practice's payment history shows per-test remittance to an outside testing entity, visible in CMS-855B contracted-supplier and reassignment fields. Almost all downstream imaging referrals from the practice route to a single radiology group TIN. Test volume per beneficiary exceeds specialty peers with no confirmatory follow-up vascular study in the beneficiary's other claims.
182.features_to_create: 1) Pre-assigned diagnosis rate: on rendering NPI x CPT for cerebral doppler studies, compute the share of lines carrying occlusion/stenosis ICD-10 codes; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Referral concentration: on ordering NPI, compute the share of imaging referrals paid to a single radiology TIN and the graph degree of distinct receiving TINs; fires when concentration is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 3) Confirmation absence: on beneficiary x doppler CPT, compute the count of follow-up vascular or neurology claims within 180 days; fires when that count is zero for a provider whose positive-diagnosis rate is top-decile; action prepay edit.

183.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, nearly every trans-cranial doppler line from one practice carries the same cerebral occlusion or stenosis ICD-10 code. The qualifying diagnosis appears on claims dated before any interpreting report exists in the medical record produced on ADR. Per-test payments from the practice to an outside testing vendor appear in CMS-855B contracted-entity and reassignment disclosures. Downstream imaging referrals from the practice concentrate on one radiology group TIN in the beneficiary's other claims. Beneficiaries show no confirmatory carotid or cerebrovascular study after a positive doppler result.
183.features_to_create: 1) Diagnosis saturation: on rendering NPI x doppler CPT, compute the proportion of lines bearing occlusion/stenosis diagnosis codes; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Referral graph concentration: on referring NPI x quarter, compute the share of imaging dollars flowing to the single largest receiving TIN; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 3) Volume-based vendor payment exposure: on practice TIN, compute the ratio of paid doppler tests to distinct beneficiaries seen; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR).

184.ways_to_identify: At prior authorisation, the submitting fax number and IP on the Evzio PA form trace to the dispensing pharmacy NPI rather than the prescriber's office. The prescriber signature block on PA forms is identical in image across many different prescribing NPIs. Step-therapy attestation claims prior Narcan trial, yet the beneficiary's Part D history shows no naloxone NDC ever dispensed. One pharmacy NPI accounts for a dominant share of the plan's total Evzio NDC claims. Prescribing NPIs on those claims have no other dispensing relationship with that pharmacy in remittance history.
184.features_to_create: 1) PA origin mismatch: on prior-authorisation record, compare the submitting fax/NPI on the form against the prescriber NPI of record in NPPES; fires on exact mismatch to the dispensing pharmacy NPI; action prepay edit. 2) Step-therapy contradiction: on beneficiary x high-cost naloxone NDC, compute the count of prior naloxone NDC fills in the Part D claim history; fires when the PA asserts prior failure and that count is zero; action claim suspension. 3) Single-NDC concentration: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of paid dollars from one branded NDC and the count of distinct prescriber NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

185.ways_to_identify: At prior authorisation, Evzio PA forms arrive from a fax number and sender registered to the dispensing pharmacy, not the prescriber's practice address in PECOS. Identical prescriber signature images repeat across PA forms bearing different prescriber NPIs. The asserted prior Narcan failure is contradicted by the absence of any naloxone NDC in the beneficiary's Part D history. One pharmacy NPI submits an outsized share of a plan's PA requests for a single high-cost NDC. Prescribers named on PA forms disclaim any dispensing relationship when contacted during credentialing verification.
185.features_to_create: 1) Pharmacy-originated PA: on prior-authorisation record, compute whether the submitter identifier equals the dispensing pharmacy NPI rather than the prescriber NPI in NPPES; fires on exact mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Step-therapy evidence gap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute the count of prior naloxone fills in the 24-month Part D history; fires when the PA asserts prior failure and the count is zero; action claim suspension. 3) Signature reuse: on pharmacy NPI, compute the distinct-count of prescriber NPIs sharing one identical signature image hash on submitted PA forms; fires when that count exceeds one; action payment suspension.

186.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this scheme, only employer cash receipts. Detection belongs to the dealership's bank reconciliation, comparing deposit slips against posted customer deal jackets and receipts. Segregation-of-duties review would show one accountant both receiving cash and posting the offsetting journal entries.
186.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Deposit reconciliation gap: on employee ID x day, compute the difference between customer down payments recorded on deal jackets and the amounts deposited to the bank account; fires when any unexplained non-zero difference exists; action internal postpay audit.

187.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the CMS-855S managing owner's identifiers match those of a person with no DME industry history and multiple concurrent supplier applications in PECOS. Brace claims list ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Beneficiary residence ZIPs lie far outside the supplier's declared service area on the CMS-855S. Supplier billing rises from zero to peer-top-decile within weeks of initial PECOS enrolment. Beneficiary contact confirms no delivery, contradicting the proof-of-delivery documents supplied on ADR.
187.features_to_create: 1) Nominee-owner linkage: on CMS-855S owner SSN, compute the distinct-count of supplier NPIs where that person is listed as owner or officer in PECOS; fires when that count exceeds one for a new enrollee; action site visit before billing privileges activate. 2) New-supplier ramp: on supplier NPI x month since enrolment, compute paid DMEPOS dollars and distinct beneficiary count; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-vintage peers; action prepay edit. 3) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days to the nearest prior E/M claim with that beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action claim suspension.

188.ways_to_identify: At prior authorisation, the diagnosis code on the PA request does not appear anywhere in the beneficiary's prior claim history from that prescriber. A single PA-submission vendor identifier appears across requests for multiple unrelated pharmacy NPIs. Compound drug PA approval rates for that submitter far exceed peer submitters for the same drug classes. The prescriber NPI on the PA form has no other claim contact with the beneficiary near the request date. Diagnosis codes on PA forms shift to covered indications immediately after a plan coverage policy change.
188.features_to_create: 1) PA diagnosis corroboration: on prior-authorisation record, compute whether the asserted diagnosis code appears in the beneficiary's claim history within the lookback window; fires on exact absence; action prepay edit. 2) Submitter concentration: on PA submitter identifier, compute the distinct-count of pharmacy NPIs and the approval rate for compounded NDCs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer submitters; action claim suspension. 3) Prescriber-beneficiary linkage: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary, compute the count of encounters within 90 days of the PA date; fires when that count is zero; action documentation request (ADR).

189.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, brace claims for one supplier NPI show no ordering NPI encounter with the beneficiary in the claim history. Many billed beneficiaries share a common enrolment or address cluster inconsistent with the supplier's CMS-855S service area. Beneficiaries appear on this supplier's claims while showing no other Medicare utilisation for years. Some dates of service post-date the beneficiary's date in the Death Master File. Proof-of-delivery documents supplied on ADR share identical signature images across different beneficiaries.
189.features_to_create: 1) Dormant-beneficiary billing: on beneficiary x supplier NPI, compute the count of other Medicare claims in the 12 months before the brace date of service; fires when that count is zero; action prepay edit. 2) Post-death service: on claim line, compute days between date of service and Death Master File date; fires when the service date is on or after death; action prepay edit. 3) Delivery-proof reuse: on supplier NPI, compute the distinct-count of beneficiaries sharing one identical proof-of-delivery signature image hash; fires when that count exceeds one; action payment suspension.

190.ways_to_identify: In PDMP and Part D data, one prescriber NPI writes Schedule II opioids with benzodiazepine overlap at rates above same-specialty peers. Controlled-substance prescriptions issue on dates with no corresponding E/M claim for the same beneficiary. Urine drug screen results in the record show illicit substances or absent parent drug, yet opioid fills continue afterwards. Beneficiaries travel unusually long distances from residence ZIP to the clinic's practice address in NPPES. High-MME prescriptions cluster on days where the prescriber's billed encounter count exceeds feasible clinic hours.
190.features_to_create: 1) Prescription without encounter: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary x fill date, compute days to the nearest E/M claim by that prescriber; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit on the pharmacy claim. 2) Opioid-benzodiazepine overlap: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the share of patients with overlapping Schedule II opioid and benzodiazepine days supply and mean daily MME; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Encounter-hours feasibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed typical-time minutes of billed E/M codes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension.

191.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since the loss is unremitted employment tax. Detection sits with IRS matching of Forms W-2 withholding totals against Forms 941 filed and deposits actually made. A second route is matching W-2 wage reporting for a named officer against the absence of a filed Form 1040 for the same years.
191.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Withholding remittance gap: on employer EIN x quarter, compute the difference between W-2 reported withholding and Form 941 deposits received; fires when the difference is positive for consecutive quarters; action IRS trust fund recovery examination.

192.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point here, only unpaid payroll trust fund taxes. Detection belongs to IRS reconciliation of Form W-2 withholding totals against Form 941 filings and actual deposits for the same EIN. Officer non-filing is detectable by matching reported W-2 officer wages to the absence of a Form 1040 for those tax years.
192.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Trust fund shortfall: on employer EIN x quarter, compute W-2 withholding reported minus federal tax deposits received; fires when positive across consecutive quarters; action IRS trust fund recovery penalty assessment.

193.ways_to_identify: There is no provider claim and no payer adjudication point, since disbursements came directly from a self-funded trust bank account. Detection belongs to the plan's TPA reconciliation, comparing trust account disbursements against adjudicated claim payments and premium remittances. Checks payable to individuals or to insurers unrelated to the plan, such as a long-term care carrier, have no matching adjudicated claim record.
193.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Unmatched trust disbursement: on health benefit trust bank account x month, compute the sum of debits with no corresponding adjudicated claim or premium invoice identifier; fires when any unmatched debit exists; action postpay audit and dual-signature requirement on the account.

194.ways_to_identify: There is no claim submitted and no adjudication point, as funds were drawn straight from a self-funded benefit trust account. Detection sits in reconciling trust account check registers against the third-party administrator's paid-claims file and carrier premium invoices. Federal grant single-audit testing of allowable fringe benefit costs would surface payees unrelated to any plan participant claim.
194.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payee registry mismatch: on trust account disbursement, compute whether the payee matches an enrolled participant, provider NPI, or contracted carrier on the plan roster; fires on exact registry mismatch; action postpay audit and payment suspension on the account.

195.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, buprenorphine prescriptions carry a prescriber DEA/NPI with no corresponding E/M or OTP encounter claim for that beneficiary. Definitive urine drug testing panels bill a high distinct-analyte CPT count on every patient at every visit. Presumptive and definitive drug testing codes are billed together routinely rather than on confirmatory exception. The clinic's ownership disclosed on CMS-855B lists no licensed practitioner among managing controllers. Testing dollars per patient encounter far exceed same-specialty pain and addiction clinic peers.
195.features_to_create: 1) Prescription without visit: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary x prescription date, compute days to the nearest billed encounter by that prescriber; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Definitive testing intensity: on clinic TIN x beneficiary x month, compute the count of definitive drug test analytes billed and the ratio of definitive to presumptive tests; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Reflex-testing violation: on claim line, compute whether a definitive test line has a paired presumptive result documented as positive; fires when definitive testing is billed on every encounter regardless of presumptive result; action postpay audit.

196.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one rendering NPI's summed community support unit-minutes on a single date of service exceed 24 hours. Encounter notes submitted on ADR repeat identical narrative text across different beneficiaries and dates. Billed service dates fall while the beneficiary has an inpatient or institutional claim elsewhere. The worker's billed hours exceed payroll timesheet hours held by the employing provider agency. Beneficiaries show no corroborating clinical contact from the agency, such as an assessment or treatment plan update, near the billed dates.
196.features_to_create: 1) Hours-per-day feasibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed billed units converted to minutes across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 2) Note text duplication: on rendering NPI, compute the share of encounter notes whose text hash matches another note for a different beneficiary; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus agency peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Conflicting-location overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between community support units and any inpatient or residential claim span; fires when overlap exceeds zero minutes; action prepay edit.

197.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since these are SBA loan and grant applications. Detection sits with cross-application matching at the SBA, comparing applicant EIN, address, and bank account across multiple PPP and EIDL submissions. IRS Form 941 and W-2 filings for the claimed EIN would contradict the asserted payroll and employee counts. Secretary of State registration dates would show entities formed after the eligibility reference period.
197.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Cross-application identity linkage: on applicant SSN and deposit bank account number, compute the distinct-count of PPP and EIDL applications and the summed requested amount; fires when the count exceeds program limits or the account is shared across unrelated EINs; action disbursement hold pending IRS payroll verification.

198.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on genetic testing and DMEPOS claims has no E/M encounter claim with the beneficiary. Electronic signature audit logs show seconds between order open and signature across hundreds of pre-populated orders. One ordering NPI orders for beneficiaries clustered in a state distant from the practice address in NPPES. The same ordering NPI appears across multiple unrelated laboratory and supplier NPIs in a short window. No follow-up claim from the ordering NPI appears after the ordered test or device.
198.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the nearest E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Signature velocity: on ordering NPI x day, compute the count of signed orders and the median seconds between order open and e-signature in the portal audit log; fires when order count is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Orderer-supplier fan-out: on ordering NPI x month, compute the distinct-count of billing laboratory and supplier NPIs and distinct beneficiary states; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

199.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, as the conduct is destruction of government records. Detection belongs to the agency's mobile device management and retention system, where message backups and deletion events are logged. Court-ordered production compliance can be tested by comparing carrier metadata records against the messages actually produced.
199.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Retention deletion audit: on government device ID x custodian, compute the count of message deletion events occurring after a litigation hold date recorded in the case management system; fires when that count exceeds zero; action internal affairs referral.

200.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, controlled-substance prescriptions carry a prescriber DEA number whose dispensing dates fall on days with no clinic encounter claim by that NPI. PDMP records show the same prescriber writing scheduled drugs to persons sharing the clinic's employer address in payroll or NPPES practice-location files. The National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners shows DOT examination certificates issued without matching electronic transmission of CMV driver exam results. Pharmacy claims show identical drug, strength and quantity across multiple patients on one prescription date, consistent with pre-signed blanks. Prescriber's PDMP scheduled-drug patient count exceeds peers of the same specialty with no corresponding office-visit claim volume.
200.features_to_create: 1) Prescription-without-encounter rate: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the share of PDMP controlled-substance prescriptions with no paid E/M claim for that patient within the lookback window; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit on that prescriber's pharmacy claims. 2) Staff-to-prescriber prescribing loop: on prescriber NPI, compute the count of distinct controlled-substance recipients whose address or employer matches the practice location in NPPES or payroll files; fires when the count exceeds zero; action postpay audit. 3) Same-day script clustering: on prescriber NPI x date of service, compute the count of controlled-substance prescriptions sharing identical NDC, strength and quantity; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR).

201.ways_to_identify: There is no health-care claim and no adjudication point; the loss is embezzlement from a nonprofit plus unremitted trust-fund payroll tax. The nearest detection route is IRS matching of employee Forms W-2 withholding totals against the employer's filed Forms 941 deposits. A second route is the nonprofit's Form 990 showing officer-controlled disbursements without independent board or dual-signature approval. Bank records showing entity checks payable to the executive director are visible to the organization's auditor, not to a payer.
201.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) W-2 to 941 reconciliation: on employer TIN x quarter, compute the difference between aggregate employee withholding reported on W-2s and trust-fund tax deposited per Form 941; fires when the gap exceeds zero for consecutive quarters; action postpay audit referral.

202.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the veteran's self-reported unemployment contradicts federal payroll and SSA wage records showing full-time employment. Caregiver stipend tiers assume full-time aide hours that overlap the veteran's own recorded work hours on the same days. The veteran's other medical claims show no encounters documenting dependence in dressing, grooming or other activities of daily living. Caregiver and veteran share a residential address and household bank account in the benefit application file. Reassessment records repeat identical functional scores across years with no clinical claim supporting decline.
202.features_to_create: 1) Employment-versus-dependency contradiction: on beneficiary, compute the overlap in hours between employer-reported paid work hours and the stipend-assumed caregiver assistance hours per day; fires when overlap exceeds zero hours on the same calendar day; action payment suspension. 2) Clinical corroboration gap: on beneficiary x benefit year, compute the count of paid claims containing ADL-dependency diagnoses or functional assessments; fires when the count is zero while a high-tier caregiver stipend is paid; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Household relationship linkage: on beneficiary x caregiver, compute the count of shared address and shared deposit-account matches across application and payment files; fires when both match and no independent reassessment exists; action site visit.

203.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the rendering NPI on home visit claims has no active state medical licence on the licence board file for the date of service. Rendering NPIs appear in NPPES with foreign medical school credentials but no state licence or residency training record. Visit volume attributed to a single supervising physician NPI exceeds feasible hours per day across dispersed home addresses. Payroll and timesheet records list clinicians who never appear as rendering NPIs on submitted claims. CMS-855 enrolment lists no supervising physician relationship for the unlicensed personnel performing the visits.
203.features_to_create: 1) Licence-on-date-of-service match: on claim line, compute an exact match of the rendering NPI to an active, unexpired state licence in the board file covering the date of service; fires on any registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Supervision hour feasibility: on supervising physician NPI x date of service, compute total attributed home-visit minutes plus estimated travel minutes between beneficiary addresses; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Payroll-to-claim identity reconciliation: on provider NPI x month, compute the count of rendering NPIs on claims absent from the agency's payroll and timesheet files; fires when the count exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

204.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a tight closed set of unrelated provider NPIs shares an unusually high proportion of the same beneficiary panel. Beneficiaries in that panel share a common recruiter-linked address or phone number captured in enrolment and claim demographic fields. Referral graph degree shows one non-clinical entity's associated NPIs directing beneficiaries only to a fixed group of billing providers. Beneficiaries receive duplicate diagnostic and behavioural services from multiple NPIs within days without any documented ordering encounter. Provider bank deposits and CMS-855 ownership disclosures show payments to a common management entity tied to per-patient volume.
204.features_to_create: 1) Closed referral clique: on beneficiary cohort, compute the Jaccard overlap of beneficiary panels across provider NPI pairs and the graph degree of shared beneficiaries; fires when overlap is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 2) Shared contact-detail cluster: on address or phone value, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries sharing it across enrolment and claim demographics; fires when the count exceeds a household-plausible level versus the calibrated percentile; action site visit. 3) Duplicative service saturation: on beneficiary x 30 days, compute the count of distinct NPIs billing the same CPT service category; fires when the count exceeds one without a documented ordering encounter; action prepay edit.

205.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the pharmacy's oxycodone NDC dispensed units far exceed same-volume peer pharmacies in ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree data. Dispensing claims cluster on a handful of prescriber DEA numbers writing high-dose immediate-release oxycodone to cash-adjacent patients. Beneficiary residence ZIPs on claims lie far outside the pharmacy's normal service radius on its enrolment file. PDMP records show early refills and identical quantity-per-fill patterns across unrelated patients at one store. DEA closing inventory reconciliation against acquisition and dispensing records leaves an unexplained pill shortfall.
205.features_to_create: 1) Opioid acquisition-dispensing reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute wholesaler-acquired oxycodone dosage units minus units dispensed on claims and PDMP records plus inventory change; fires when the unexplained difference exceeds zero units; action payment suspension. 2) Controlled-substance mix concentration: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the ratio of Schedule II opioid units to total dispensed units and the share from the top three prescriber DEA numbers; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-size peers; action prepay edit. 3) Patient travel radius: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of opioid claims where beneficiary ZIP distance exceeds the pharmacy's trailing median service radius; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR).

206.ways_to_identify: There is no health-care claim and no adjudication point; this is pandemic loan fraud against SBA programs. The nearest route is matching the payroll figures on loan applications against IRS Forms 941 and state unemployment wage filings for the same employer TIN. A second route is deduplicating applications by TIN, bank account and applicant identity across PPP and EIDL portals before disbursement. Post-disbursement, tracing loan proceeds to real-property and vehicle purchases shows no payroll use.
206.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payroll attestation reconciliation: on employer TIN, compute the difference between application-claimed monthly payroll and IRS 941 plus state wage-file reported wages; fires when the claimed amount exceeds filed wages; action prepay edit at loan disbursement. 2) Deposit-account concentration: on bank account number, compute the count of distinct borrower entities receiving disbursements; fires when the count exceeds one; action payment suspension.

207.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one ordering NPI accounts for nearly all transcranial doppler CPT volume billed by a single mobile diagnostic supplier. Ordering diagnoses on the claims are boilerplate cerebrovascular codes absent from the beneficiary's prior claim history. Place of service on the scan claims is a physician office rather than a facility with vascular ultrasound accreditation. Scan volume per beneficiary repeats at fixed intervals with no follow-up neurology or treatment claim after abnormal findings. The ordering physician's TCD ordering rate per 100 beneficiaries far exceeds internal medicine peers in the same state.
207.features_to_create: 1) Orderer-supplier dependency: on ordering NPI x supplier NPI, compute the share of that supplier's TCD CPT volume attributable to one orderer and the orderer's share of ordered tests going to that supplier; fires when both shares are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Diagnosis-history mismatch: on claim line, compute whether the ordering diagnosis appears in the beneficiary's prior 12 months of paid claims; fires when it is absent for all listed diagnoses; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Post-test action gap: on beneficiary x TCD test, compute days to any subsequent neurology, imaging or treatment claim; fires when no such claim exists within the clinical follow-up window; action postpay audit.

208.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one internist's ordering NPI supplies a disproportionate share of a mobile diagnostic company's transcranial doppler claims. The ordering diagnosis codes on scan claims do not appear anywhere in the beneficiary's prior claim history. Scan CPT volume per ordering NPI exceeds same-specialty peers per 100 attributed beneficiaries. Beneficiaries receive repeat scans at fixed intervals with no subsequent treatment or specialist claim. The supplier's CMS-855 enrolment lists mobile units serving locations far from the ordering physician's practice address.
208.features_to_create: 1) Single-orderer concentration: on supplier NPI x quarter, compute the share of TCD CPT lines originating from the top ordering NPI; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-service peers; action claim suspension. 2) Unsupported ordering diagnosis: on claim line, compute the presence of the ordering diagnosis in the beneficiary's 12-month claim history; fires on absence; action prepay edit. 3) Repeat-test cadence: on beneficiary x CPT, compute the count of paid scans in a rolling 12 months and days between them; fires when the count exceeds the coverage-policy frequency limit; action prior-authorisation requirement.

209.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on L-code brace claims has no prior in-person or evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiary. Telehealth encounter records tied to the order show call durations far below any plausible examination time. One ordering NPI signs brace orders for beneficiaries across many states within a single week. Multiple distinct supplier NPIs bill the same beneficiary for overlapping orthotic HCPCS within one month. Order documents share identical templated text and diagnosis codes across hundreds of unrelated beneficiaries.
209.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the brace date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Telehealth duration feasibility: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute total billed or logged telehealth minutes divided by count of signed DMEPOS orders; fires when minutes per order fall below the minimum documented examination time; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Orderer geographic dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs on ordered DMEPOS claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

210.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, claim lines report unit counts for an injection HCPCS thousands of times the maximum medically unlikely edit value. Submitted charge per line exceeds the fee-schedule allowance by orders of magnitude with no pricing modifier. Dates of service on newly submitted claims precede the submission date and fall after the licence suspension date on the state board file. The rendering NPI's licence status in the board file and PECOS is suspended for the billed service dates. Controlled-substance prescriptions carry a DEA registration number registered to a different prescriber NPI in the DEA file.
210.features_to_create: 1) Unit ceiling edit: on claim line, compute billed units against the medically unlikely edit maximum for the HCPCS; fires when units exceed the MUE value; action prepay edit. 2) Licence-effective-date check: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute whether the service date falls inside an active licence period in the state board and PECOS files; fires on any registry mismatch, including backdated service dates; action claim suspension. 3) DEA-to-prescriber binding: on prescription record, compute an exact match between the DEA registration number and the prescriber NPI in the DEA registrant file; fires on mismatch; action prepay edit on the associated pharmacy claim.

211.ways_to_identify: There is no health-care claim and no adjudication point; the loss is unremitted trust-fund employment tax across facilities. The nearest route is IRS matching of aggregate employee W-2 withholding to Form 941 deposits for each facility employer TIN under common ownership. A second route is DOL matching of Form 5500 filings against the plan sponsor list for 401K plans. Common ownership across states is visible in CMS-855A ownership disclosures, which links delinquent TINs to one operator.
211.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Common-owner tax delinquency linkage: on owning entity from CMS-855A ownership fields, compute the count of subsidiary employer TINs with W-2 withholding exceeding Form 941 deposits; fires when the count exceeds zero; action postpay audit and change-of-ownership scrutiny at re-enrolment.

212.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, definitive urine drug testing CPT codes are billed at every office visit for essentially all chronic opioid patients of one clinic. The ordering NPI and the performing laboratory NPI share ownership in the CMS-855B disclosure, indicating in-house self-referral. Tests per beneficiary per year far exceed the calibrated percentile for pain-management peers. Panel breadth in billed drug classes is identical across all patients regardless of prescribed medication or risk level. Provider relief fund attestation records conflict with the clinic's claim history showing no services after closure.
212.features_to_create: 1) Reflex testing rate: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of definitive urine drug test claims to office-visit claims for chronic opioid patients; fires when the ratio approaches one-to-one and is above the calibrated percentile versus pain-management peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Panel-uniformity index: on ordering NPI, compute the distinct-value count of drug-class code combinations billed across its beneficiaries; fires when a single combination covers a share above the calibrated percentile of tests; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Relief-fund activity check: on provider TIN, compute the count of paid claims with dates of service after the last relief-fund attestation period; fires when the count is zero while funds remain retained; action postpay audit and recoupment.

213.ways_to_identify: There is no health-care claim and no adjudication point; the conduct is obstruction by deleting consulting records. 214.ways_to_identify: There is no health-care claim and no adjudication point; the offence is destruction of consulting documents to impede an investigation. The nearest route is litigation-hold enforcement with device audit logs and mailbox retention records held by the employer. A second non-claims route is monitoring manufacturer targeting of high-volume opioid prescribers through Open Payments and dispensing data.
214.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Opioid prescriber growth surveillance: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the change in dispensed morphine-milligram-equivalents relative to the prescriber's own trailing baseline; fires when growth is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

215.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the claimed surviving-spouse status conflicts with the state vital records divorce decree on file. The applicant's name change postdates the veteran's death recorded in the Death Master File and state death index. The applicant had previously been removed as a dependent in the veteran's own benefit record, showing a prior status change. CHAMPVA medical claims are paid under a beneficiary identifier whose marital-status field was never re-verified against court records. Application signature dates cluster immediately after the veteran's date of death in the benefits file.
215.features_to_create: 1) Marital-status registry match: on claimant, compute an exact match of claimed marriage-until-death status against state vital records marriage and divorce filings; fires on any registry mismatch; action prepay edit on survivor benefit payments. 2) Prior-dependent removal contradiction: on veteran file x claimant identity, compute whether the claimant was previously removed as a dependent before the date of death; fires when removal exists without documented remarriage; action payment suspension. 3) Name-change timing: on claimant SSN, compute days between the surname change record and the veteran's date of death in the Death Master File; fires when the change follows death; action documentation request (ADR).

216.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a pediatric-specialty NPI writes controlled-substance prescriptions dispensed to adult beneficiaries far outside the specialty's age profile. Pharmacy claims list beneficiaries whose PDMP fill histories show identical prescriber, drug and quantity across ostensibly unrelated persons. Prescription fills occur for beneficiaries with no corresponding office-visit claim to that prescriber. Concurrent opioid, benzodiazepine and stimulant combinations appear across the prescriber's panel in PDMP records. Fill pickups are made by one common individual across several beneficiary identities per pharmacy signature logs.
216.features_to_create: 1) Specialty-age mismatch: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of controlled-substance fills for beneficiaries outside the specialty's expected age band from NPPES taxonomy; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-taxonomy peers; action prepay edit. 2) Prescription-without-visit rate: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary, compute days between each controlled-substance fill and the nearest paid E/M claim with that prescriber; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action claim suspension. 3) Shared-pickup identity: on pharmacy NPI x pickup signatory, compute the distinct count of beneficiaries whose controlled-substance fills that person collected; fires when the count exceeds household-plausible levels versus the calibrated percentile; action postpay audit.

217.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the optometry NPI bills eye examination and testing CPT volumes per beneficiary above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers. Beneficiaries appear on claims with recurring diagnostic tests but no corresponding refraction or treatment progression in their claim history. Rendering hours implied by billed procedure times exceed the practice's staffed clinic hours on given dates of service. An open audit case in the payer's integrity system is closed by administrative direction without documented sampling results. Settlement amount recorded in the remittance history is far below the extrapolated overpayment computed by the auditor.
217.features_to_create: 1) Service-time feasibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed typical procedure minutes for billed CPT lines; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the posted clinic hours; action claim suspension. 2) Audit-closure integrity: on audit case ID, compute the difference between the auditor's extrapolated overpayment and the final settled amount, together with the count of non-audit staff approvals; fires when the settlement discount is above the calibrated percentile of closed audits; action postpay audit re-opening. 3) Testing intensity ratio: on provider NPI x quarter, compute diagnostic test CPT lines per distinct beneficiary; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit.

218.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the practice bills eye examinations and diagnostic tests per beneficiary at rates above same-specialty peers in the state. Claim lines exist for dates of service when the beneficiary has other claims placing them elsewhere. Billed procedure minutes per rendering NPI per day exceed feasible clinic hours. Practice checks reimburse third-party payments to a public official, visible in the entity's bank records during an open audit. An open billing audit is administratively cancelled and settled far below the auditor's extrapolated exposure recorded in the case file.
218.features_to_create: 1) Phantom-visit conflict: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of claims from other providers whose service location conflicts with the optometry visit; fires when conflicting same-day claims exceed zero; action prepay edit. 2) Daily service-minute ceiling: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed typical minutes for all billed CPT lines; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Settlement discount outlier: on audit case ID, compute the ratio of settled amount to auditor-extrapolated overpayment; fires when the ratio is below the calibrated percentile of comparable closed audits; action postpay audit.

219.ways_to_identify: There is no health-care claim and no adjudication point; unapproved herbal vials were sold directly to consumers. The nearest route is FDA labeling surveillance matching product claims of prescription status against the NDC directory and approved drug listings. A second route is payer detection if any such product is ever submitted with an NDC absent from the FDA listing file.
219.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) NDC validity check: on claim line, compute an exact match of the billed NDC to an active FDA-listed approved product with matching prescription status; fires on any registry mismatch; action prepay edit.

220.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim here and no payer adjudication point, so no prepay edit can apply. The decisive signal is an IRS filing-versus-deposit mismatch: W-2 wage totals reported to SSA with no matching Form 941 for those quarters. Federal Tax Deposit records showing zero EFTPS deposits from an EIN whose payroll provider files continue is the nearest non-claims route. A registered agent or officer appearing on multiple EINs with the same 941 delinquency pattern extends the review.
220.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payroll withholding reconciliation: on EIN x quarter, compute the difference between SSA W-2/W-3 reported withholding and total EFTPS federal tax deposits plus filed Form 941 liability; fires when the gap is non-zero for consecutive quarters; action postpay audit (IRS trust fund recovery assessment).

221.ways_to_identify: No claim is submitted and there is no adjudication point, so a payer-side prepay control cannot reach this conduct. The nearest route is IRS matching of SSA-reported W-2 withholding against Form 941 filings and EFTPS deposits for the same EIN. Officer-level exposure is visible where the same responsible person appears on CMS-855 ownership fields or state corporate filings for multiple delinquent EINs. Large owner distributions from business accounts while trust fund deposits are zero is the corroborating bank-records signal.
221.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Trust fund gap by responsible officer: on EIN x responsible officer, compute the sum of W-2 withheld tax minus EFTPS deposits across quarters; fires when the cumulative gap is positive for two or more consecutive quarters; action postpay audit.

222.ways_to_identify: At facility audit, resident patient trust account ledger debits have no matching signed resident receipt or countersignature in the facility disbursement file. Check images from the facility bank account show a single employee as maker with a forged second signature on hundreds of sequential checks. Resident trust balances decline while the resident has no discharge, no personal spending pattern, and MDS shows immobility. IRS Economic Impact Payment deposits credited to resident trust accounts are withdrawn in cash within days. Continued payroll or trust deductions for a supplemental insurance policy already terminated in the carrier's cancellation file.
222.features_to_create: 1) Trust ledger disbursement concentration: on facility TIN x employee, compute the count and dollar sum of patient trust account checks where that employee is maker within a quarter; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer facilities of similar bed count; action postpay audit. 2) Unsupported cash debit: on resident x month, compute the sum of trust ledger debits lacking a scanned signed receipt; fires when that sum is above zero for consecutive months; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Dead-policy deduction: on resident x insurance policy number, compute the days between the carrier cancellation date and the latest deduction posted; fires when that gap is positive; action prepay edit.

223.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the compounded-drug claim's prescription image shows ingredient or quantity fields in different handwriting or font from the prescriber block. Fax header transmitting station ID and timestamp on the received prescription do not match the prescriber's registered practice fax on NPPES. The prescriber NPI's compound prescribing volume for that pharmacy is far above the same-specialty peer baseline. The same beneficiary receives high-margin compound kits with no prior E/M encounter with the ordering NPI. Prescriber attestation letters returned on ADR contradict the pharmacy's retained hardcopy for the same Rx number.
223.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber-source mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact match test between the originating fax number or e-prescribe origin ID and the prescriber's NPPES and DEA registered practice location; fires on registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Compound concentration by prescriber: on prescriber NPI x pharmacy NPI x month, compute the count of high-cost compound claims and its ratio to that prescriber's total prescriptions; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Alteration audit: on pharmacy NPI, compute the share of sampled compound Rx images whose quantity or ingredient field differs from the prescriber-confirmed original; fires when that share exceeds zero; action payment suspension.

224.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point; the payer is a loan program, not a claims system. The decisive route is SBA cross-matching applicant IRS Form 941 and W-2 payroll data against the stated average monthly payroll on the PPP application. Duplicate EIDL and PPP awards to related applicants sharing a bank account, address, or phone across applications are visible in the loan intake file. Post-disbursement bank monitoring showing proceeds moved to boat, vehicle, and real estate purchases rather than payroll is the nearest downstream control.
224.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payroll attestation mismatch: on applicant EIN, compute the ratio of claimed average monthly payroll to IRS Form 941 reported wages for the same period; fires when the ratio exceeds one by more than rounding; action claim suspension before disbursement. 2) Applicant clustering: on bank account number x address, compute the distinct count of EIDL and PPP applications submitted; fires when that count exceeds one without documented affiliation disclosure; action documentation request.

225.ways_to_identify: There is no adjudicated health care claim; the products sold were unlicensed insurance and a sham retirement plan. The nearest route is state department of insurance verification that the certificate of insurance's named carrier and policy number exist in the carrier's own policy file. DOL Form 5500 filings absent for a plan collecting employee 401(k) deferrals is the second registry check. Any entity marketing ACA hardship exemptions can be matched against the CMS exemption issuance file, which contains only government-issued certificate numbers.
