225.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Certificate registry verification: on certificate of insurance, compute an exact match of the named carrier NAIC code and policy number against that carrier's in-force policy file; fires on registry mismatch; action claim suspension and referral to the state insurance regulator. 2) Deferral-without-plan check: on employer EIN x plan year, compute the sum of employee 401(k) deferrals withheld per payroll records minus deposits reported on Form 5500; fires when the gap is positive; action postpay audit.

226.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Schedule II stimulant fills continue for beneficiaries whose date of death appears in the Death Master File. Prior-authorisation records assert prior non-stimulant trials and urine drug screens with no corresponding pharmacy NDC history or CPT 80305-80307 claims for that beneficiary. Rendering NPIs bill initial psychiatric evaluations (CPT 90792) at durations implying more encounters than fit in 24 hours. The same telehealth TIN shows near-universal stimulant prescribing with no follow-up E/M claim after the initial visit. Refills issue on exact monthly cadence with no interval telehealth encounter claim from any rendering NPI.
226.features_to_create: 1) Decedent dispensing: on claim line, compute the gap in days between the fill date and the Death Master File date of death; fires when the fill date is after the death date; action prepay edit. 2) Prior-auth assertion verification: on prior-authorisation request, compute the count of beneficiary claims matching the asserted urine drug screen CPT and prior non-stimulant NDC in the lookback; fires when that count is zero while the request asserts them; action prior-authorisation requirement with documentation request (ADR). 3) Prescriber stimulant throughput: on rendering NPI x day, compute total billed encounter minutes and the count of distinct beneficiaries receiving Schedule II stimulants; fires when billed minutes exceed 24 hours or the count is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

227.ways_to_identify: No health care claim is adjudicated; the product sold was a discount plan, so there is no payer claim lifecycle. The nearest route is state insurance department producer licence file matching of the selling agent name against the National Insurance Producer Registry. Repeat cancellations and rewrites of the same consumer within months are visible in the plan administrator's enrolment and billing file. Duplicate monthly ACH debits to one consumer from two plan IDs appear in the merchant processor chargeback record. Payroll withholding versus Form 941 deposit mismatch on the call centre EIN is the separate IRS route.
227.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Unlicensed seller check: on enrolment record x selling agent, compute an exact match of the agent name and NPN against the state producer licence file for the consumer's state; fires on registry mismatch; action claim suspension of commission payment. 2) Churn and double-bill: on consumer x plan administrator, compute the count of distinct policy IDs billed within a rolling 12 months and the count of overlapping active billing periods; fires when overlap exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

228.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the CMS-855A owner listed holds a recent visa or foreign passport identity that appears as owner on several unrelated hospice applications sharing an address. At adjudication, hospice election periods exist for beneficiaries whose other Part B claims show active curative treatment from unrelated physicians. Attending physician NPI on the hospice certification has no prior claim history with the beneficiary in the payer's remittance file. Hospice routine home care days are billed with no corresponding nurse or aide visit line for weeks at a time. Payments from multiple hospice PTANs route to bank accounts sharing one EFT routing and account number on CMS-588.
228.features_to_create: 1) Straw-owner graph: on owner SSN or ITIN from CMS-855A, compute the count of distinct enrolled provider PTANs sharing that owner, address, or CMS-588 bank account; fires when that count exceeds one; action site visit before enrolment approval. 2) Election-versus-curative conflict: on beneficiary x hospice election period, compute the count of paid curative or aggressive-treatment claims from unrelated NPIs during the period; fires when that count is above zero; action prepay edit. 3) Service-absent hospice days: on beneficiary x hospice NPI x month, compute the ratio of billed routine home care days to documented nurse or aide visit lines; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus peer hospices; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension.

229.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on the L-code brace claim has no prior E/M encounter with that beneficiary in the payer's claim history. One telemedicine ordering NPI signs brace orders for beneficiaries across many states within a single week. Three supplier PTANs share a common CMS-855S contact person, address, or CMS-588 bank account while billing the same L-codes. Beneficiary residence ZIPs sit far outside each supplier's declared service area on its enrolment record. Beneficiaries deny contact when surveyed, and no delivery proof of delivery exists on ADR response.
229.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs on ordered DMEPOS claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Supplier common-control graph: on CMS-588 bank account x address, compute the count of distinct DMEPOS PTANs billing overlapping L-codes; fires when that count exceeds one; action site visit.

230.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, claims carry an ordering physician NPI whose own claim history shows no beneficiary contact and whose specialty never orders that test. Beneficiary date of death in the Death Master File precedes the date of service on OTC COVID test and lab claims. Physical therapy units are billed for minutes overlapping the same claimant's surgical anesthesia time on another claim. Genetic testing panels bill for beneficiaries with no cancer diagnosis code and no prior oncology encounter. Payments described as loans, medical directorships, or consulting fees flow from the lab TIN to referring NPIs on the same providers' 1099 and bank records.
230.features_to_create: 1) Impossible concurrency: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlapping billed minutes across all rendering NPIs including anesthesia and facility times; fires when overlapping minutes exceed zero or total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Decedent service: on claim line, compute the gap in days between date of service and the Death Master File date of death; fires when service date follows death; action prepay edit. 3) Orderer-specialty implausibility: on ordering NPI x HCPCS, compute the count of ordered genetic or DME claims and the share with no prior E/M between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when that share is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

231.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Schedule II opioid dosage units per prescriber NPI per month sit far above same-specialty peers in PDMP and Part D data. Beneficiaries travel long distances from residence ZIP to the clinic and then to one dispensing pharmacy, visible in claim addresses. Office visit E/M claims supporting the prescriptions are billed at a per-day count exceeding a plausible clinic day. Patients share a common recruiter-linked address or phone across enrolment records at the same clinic. Cash-pay visit fees precede insured claims for maintenance drugs with no diagnostic imaging or urine screening history.
231.features_to_create: 1) Opioid MME concentration: on prescriber NPI x month, compute total Schedule II morphine milligram equivalents dispensed and the ratio of opioid to non-opioid prescriptions; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriber-pharmacy-beneficiary triangle: on prescriber NPI x pharmacy NPI, compute the count of shared beneficiaries and the median beneficiary-to-clinic distance; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Visit-day throughput: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries with E/M claims and implied total minutes; fires when implied minutes exceed 24 hours; action prepay edit.

232.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one certifying physician NPI signs terminal-illness certifications for a share of a hospice's admissions far above same-specialty peers. Beneficiaries remain on hospice past two benefit periods with live-discharge rates above peer hospices in the payer's remittance history. Referral source addresses cluster on a handful of group home addresses in the beneficiary enrolment file. Hospice patients simultaneously receive curative Part B services from unrelated NPIs during the election period. After a payer action, new hospice PTANs enrol at the same address or bank account with different CMS-855A straw owners.
232.features_to_create: 1) Certifier concentration: on certifying physician NPI x hospice PTAN, compute the count of terminal-illness certifications and its share of that hospice's admissions; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Non-terminal indicator: on beneficiary x election period, compute the count of live discharges plus paid curative claims from unrelated NPIs during the period; fires when that count is above zero; action prepay edit. 3) Successor-entity linkage: on address x CMS-588 bank account x phone, compute the count of distinct hospice PTANs enrolled within 24 months; fires when that count exceeds one; action site visit and payment suspension.

233.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, controlled substance claims carry a prescriber DEA number whose dispensed volume in PDMP far exceeds that physician's own trailing baseline. Prescriptions are written for individuals with no prior encounter claim at the prescriber's practice TIN. Prescription pad serial numbers or signature images differ from the prescriber's file exemplars held by the pharmacy. Multiple beneficiaries share a pickup address, phone, or cash payment pattern across pharmacies for the same DEA number. Prescriber attestation on ADR shows the physician did not authorise the prescriptions for those names.
233.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber baseline break: on prescriber DEA x month, compute hydrocodone and oxycodone dosage units dispensed and the ratio to that prescriber's trailing twelve-month mean; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit and prescriber alert. 2) No-encounter dispensing: on prescription x prescriber NPI, compute the count of prior E/M encounters between that NPI and the named patient; fires when that count is zero; action claim suspension. 3) Pickup clustering: on address or phone x pharmacy NPI, compute the count of distinct patient names filling Schedule II prescriptions from one DEA number; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action postpay audit.

234.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Schedule II volume attributed to one DEA registration jumps far above that prescriber's own trailing baseline in PDMP data. Named patients have no encounter history with the prescriber's practice TIN and some do not exist in the payer's eligibility file. One person picks up prescriptions for many unrelated patients, recorded in pharmacy pickup logs and signature files. Adderall prescriptions issue to persons sharing the practice's staff addresses in NPPES and payroll records. Cash payment with no insurance adjudication dominates fills tied to that DEA number.
234.features_to_create: 1) DEA volume break: on prescriber DEA x month, compute dispensed Schedule II dosage units versus that prescriber's trailing twelve-month mean; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit and prescriber verification. 2) Phantom-patient check: on prescription, compute an exact match of the patient name and date of birth against the practice's encounter roster and the payer eligibility file; fires on registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Pickup agent degree: on pickup signer x pharmacy NPI, compute the distinct count of patients whose controlled substances that signer collected in 90 days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action postpay audit.

235.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed NDC quantities exceed the pharmacy's documented wholesaler purchases in ARCOS and 340B or wholesaler pedigree data. Beneficiaries show refills on exact schedule with no corresponding prescriber encounter or diagnosis in their other claims. Refill claims continue after the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File. High-cost NDC mix at these PTANs is far above same-specialty peer pharmacies of similar script count. Common ownership across five pharmacy PTANs is visible in CMS-855B ownership fields and shared CMS-588 bank accounts.
235.features_to_create: 1) Purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed units minus wholesaler acquisition units from pedigree and ARCOS data; fires when billed exceeds purchased; action payment suspension. 2) Unclaimed-refill check: on beneficiary x NDC, compute the count of paid fills with no matching prescriber encounter claim or prescription record in the lookback; fires when that count is above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Common-ownership aggregation: on owner TIN or bank account, compute summed high-cost NDC billing across linked pharmacy PTANs and its growth versus trailing baseline; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit.

236.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compound claim dollars concentrate in a small set of referring NPIs whose compound share far exceeds same-specialty peers. Average paid amount per compound claim at this pharmacy is far above peer pharmacies for the same J- and NDC-level ingredients. Referring providers receive marketer payments recorded as commissions on the pharmacy's 1099s and bank transfers. Beneficiaries have no prior E/M encounter with the referring NPI before the compound prescription date. Claims cluster in DOL-OWCP and TRICARE lines with no comparable commercial volume for the same drugs.
236.features_to_create: 1) Referrer compound concentration: on referring NPI x pharmacy NPI x month, compute compound claim dollars and their share of that prescriber's total prescribing; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Ingredient cost outlier: on claim line, compute paid amount per compound claim against the peer median for the same ingredient NDC set; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action prepay edit. 3) Marketer payment linkage: on pharmacy TIN x payee NPI, compute the dollar sum of outbound payments to entities whose principals also appear as referring NPIs; fires when that sum is above zero; action payment suspension.

237.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed brand Adderall NDCs are not present in the pharmacy's wholesaler purchase pedigree for the same period. Dispensed Schedule II units in ARCOS exceed the sum of units supported by valid prescriber-originated prescriptions. Claims carry a prescriber NPI who has no PDMP record of writing for that beneficiary. Refill claims exist for beneficiaries with no encounter or eligibility activity in their other claims. A reported theft or robbery filed with DEA on Form 106 coincides with a purchase-to-dispense shortfall in the same NDCs.
237.features_to_create: 1) Brand-versus-stock mismatch: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x month, compute billed brand units minus wholesaler-acquired brand units from pedigree data; fires when the difference is positive; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber origin verification: on claim line, compute an exact match of the prescriber NPI and DEA against the state PDMP record for that prescription number; fires on registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Diversion shortfall: on pharmacy NPI x controlled NDC x quarter, compute ARCOS receipts minus billed dispensed units minus reported losses on DEA Form 106; fires when the unexplained gap is above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action postpay audit.

238.ways_to_identify: At credentialing, the applicant's nursing programme appears on a state board list of closed or sanctioned schools with disputed transcripts. Transcript-issuing institution and clinical hour records fail to match the school's registrar file held by the state education agency. Licence lookup shows NCLEX eligibility approved on a diploma issued within an implausibly short enrolment span. Clusters of licensees from one school share consecutive certificate numbers and identical clinical rotation sites and dates. Employer credentialing files show no verifiable clinical preceptor contact for those rotations.
238.features_to_create: 1) School-source cluster: on nursing school code x graduation cohort, compute the count of licensees whose transcripts list identical clinical sites and dates; fires when duplicate site-date tuples exceed one per preceptor capacity; action claim suspension of credentialing approval. 2) Enrolment-duration impossibility: on licensee, compute the gap in days between programme start date and diploma date against the board-required minimum programme length; fires when the gap is shorter than the regulatory minimum; action documentation request to the state board. 3) Registry verification: on rendering NPI, compute an exact match of licence number and status against the state licence board file and OIG LEIE at each claim; fires on registry mismatch or revocation; action prepay edit.

239.ways_to_identify: No health care claim exists; the payer is a state unemployment agency, so the control point is benefit claim intake, not adjudication of a medical claim. The decisive signal is claimant wage records absent from the state's quarterly UI wage base for the named employer. Many claims filed from one IP address, device fingerprint, email domain, or routed to one bank account are visible in the NCDES intake log. Employer identity on the claim can be exact-matched against the state's registered employer account file.
239.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Wage-record verification: on claimant SSN x employer account, compute the difference between claimed wages and state quarterly UI wage records; fires when no wage record exists for the named employer; action claim suspension before first payment. 2) Filer clustering: on IP address or bank account number, compute the distinct count of unemployment claims filed within 90 days; fires when that count exceeds one household plausibility threshold; action payment suspension and identity documentation request.

240.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare rendering NPI dates of service against that clinician's absence from any other claim activity nationwide during the same span. Count timed-therapy units billed under one rendering NPI per date of service and convert to treatment hours. Cross-check CPT 97110, 97140 and 97530 units against the clinic's staff roster and licence file for a second qualified renderer. Test whether every claim in the period carries the same single rendering NPI despite multi-therapist appointment volume. Match dates of service to passport or vessel manifest records obtained during investigation of clinician-absence tips.
240.features_to_create: 1) Impossible therapy day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total timed units for CPT 97110, 97112, 97140 and 97530 multiplied by 15 minutes; fires when the total exceeds a physically workable day of 24 hours or the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Sole-renderer concentration: on billing TIN x month, compute the share of therapy lines carrying one rendering NPI divided by all therapy lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Renderer continuity gap: on rendering NPI x week, compute the count of consecutive service days billed with zero corroborating co-signature or supervising NPI on the claim; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action postpay audit.

241.ways_to_identify: At enrolment and credentialing, compare hospital CMS-855A ownership and financial-relationship disclosures against Stark exception documentation for EHR subsidies to referring physicians. Compute each referring physician's share of admissions to one hospital system from Medicare Part A and Part B claim linkage. Compare physician bonus payments reported in the system's clinical-integration ledger against that physician's referral volume. Check whether subsidised EHR and equipment recipients are precisely the top-referring NPIs in the claims file. Review Open Payments and the hospital's vendor expense records for meals and entertainment concentrated on referring NPIs.
241.features_to_create: 1) Referral-payment correlation: on referring NPI x hospital TIN x year, compute the correlation between dollars paid to the physician and the paid amount of that physician's referred inpatient and outpatient claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 2) Subsidy-referral concentration: on referring NPI, compute the share of total Medicare admissions directed to the subsidising system; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline after the subsidy start date; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Disclosure mismatch: on hospital TIN, compute the count of physicians receiving in-kind support who are absent from CMS-855A financial-relationship disclosures; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action payment suspension.

242.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count skin-substitute application CPT 15271-15278 lines per rendering NPI per date of service and convert to clinician hours. Compare graft square-centimetre units billed against wholesaler purchase pedigree invoices for that product's Q-code. Test whether the rendering NPI appears on other claims at a different place of service during the same application dates. Check the state licence board file and NPPES for the individual physically documented as performing the application in the chart. Compare the supplier's Q-code acquisition volume against paid application volume for the same beneficiary panel.
242.features_to_create: 1) Graft day impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of CPT 15271-15278 applications multiplied by typical procedure minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Product-to-claim reconciliation: on billing NPI x Q-code x quarter, compute billed square centimetres minus wholesaler-invoiced square centimetres; fires when billed exceeds purchased; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension. 3) Unlicensed applier exposure: on claim line, compute a match of the documented performing individual's name against the state licence board file and NPPES; fires on exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension.

243.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count skin-substitute application CPT 15271-15278 lines under one rendering NPI per date of service across all places of service. Compare billed graft units against the practice's wholesaler pedigree and Q-code purchase invoices. Verify the individual named in the operative note against the state licence board file and NPPES at the credentialing stage. Test whether payments received by the billing TIN are promptly transferred to a supplier bank account matching the graft vendor. Compare per-beneficiary graft reapplication frequency to same-specialty peers for the same wound diagnosis.
243.features_to_create: 1) Renderer capacity ceiling: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total skin-substitute applications and multiply by minimum documented procedure minutes; fires when the total exceeds a 24-hour day; action prepay edit. 2) Purchase-versus-bill gap: on billing TIN x Q-code x quarter, compute billed units divided by invoiced units from wholesaler pedigree data; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action postpay audit. 3) Payment passthrough: on bank account x month, compute the share of payer remittances forwarded to a single vendor account within seven days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

244.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare the prescriber NPI on oxycodone and hydrocodone NDC fills against that prescriber's own claim history for the beneficiary. Count controlled-substance fills per prescriber NPI at one pharmacy NPI and compare to PDMP prescriber totals. Compute the pharmacy's ratio of Schedule II opioid dispensed dosage units to all dispensing using ARCOS purchase data. Check beneficiary travel distance between residence ZIP and pharmacy ZIP on high-dose opioid fills. Test for repeated identical quantity, day-supply and directions across prescriptions from multiple unrelated prescriber NPIs.
244.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber attribution mismatch: on prescriber NPI x pharmacy NPI x month, compute opioid fills at that pharmacy minus opioid prescriptions recorded for the prescriber in the state PDMP; fires on any positive difference; action prepay edit. 2) Opioid concentration: on pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute Schedule II dosage units dispensed divided by total dosage units, using ARCOS receipts as denominator control; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Template prescription clustering: on pharmacy NPI x week, compute the count of distinct prescriber NPIs sharing an identical NDC, quantity and day-supply string; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action site visit.

245.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check whether the certifying NPI on the home health face-to-face certification has any prior E/M claim with that beneficiary. Count distinct home health agency billing NPIs relying on one certifying physician NPI within a quarter. Compare certification dates on the plan of care against the physician's own claim calendar for patient-contact activity. Test OASIS assessment homebound findings against the beneficiary's concurrent outpatient and therapy claims showing mobility. Compare the certifying physician's G-code certification billings to same-specialty peers at claim adjudication.
245.features_to_create: 1) Certifier-encounter gap: on beneficiary x certifying NPI, compute days between the certification date and the nearest E/M claim between them; fires when no encounter exists within the required face-to-face window; action prepay edit. 2) Certifier fan-out: on certifying NPI x quarter, compute the count of distinct home health agency NPIs and beneficiaries certified; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Homebound contradiction: on beneficiary x episode, compute the count of outpatient or ambulatory claims inconsistent with the OASIS homebound field; fires when the count exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

246.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim and no adjudication point here because the failure is a DEA recordkeeping and inventory obligation, not a billing act. The nearest detection route is reconciling ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree receipts of oxycodone and alprazolam against the pharmacy's dispensing records and biennial inventory. A second route is DEA registrant inspection of the perpetual controlled-substance log against staff pharmacist dispensing under each pharmacist licence number.
246.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on pharmacy DEA registration x quarter, compute ARCOS-reported receipts of a given NDC minus dispensed dosage units plus inventory, and refer any unexplained shortage to DEA for inspection.

247.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check whether the ordering NPI on CGx and PGx CPT codes had any treating relationship claim with the beneficiary before the order date. Count distinct beneficiary states and distinct laboratory NPIs tied to one telemedicine ordering NPI per week. Compare beneficiary residence ZIPs to clusters at nursing facilities, malls and churches sharing identical collection dates. Test whether test results are followed by any therapy change in the beneficiary's subsequent Part B or Part D claims. Compare per-beneficiary genetic panel dollars against same-specialty peer laboratories at claim adjudication.
247.features_to_create: 1) Order without treating relationship: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M encounter between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Telehealth orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and distinct billing lab NPIs on genetic-test orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Collection-site clustering: on laboratory NPI x collection date, compute the count of beneficiaries sharing an identical address or facility identifier; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR).

248.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, verify that the ordering NPI on CGx claims has prior evaluation-and-management claims with the same beneficiary. Compute the number of distinct laboratory NPIs billing the same beneficiary for overlapping genetic panels within 90 days. Compare marketing-entity payments described as hourly consulting against the count of specimens delivered in the same period. Test whether a small set of ordering NPIs accounts for most of a lab's genetic-test revenue. Check bank-account linkage between the laboratory TIN and recruiter entities during enrolment ownership review.
248.features_to_create: 1) Duplicate panel saturation: on beneficiary x CPT panel, compute the count of distinct laboratory NPIs paid within a rolling 90 days; fires when the count exceeds one without a documented repeat indication; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer concentration: on laboratory NPI x quarter, compute the share of paid genetic-test dollars attributable to the top ordering NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Per-specimen payment pattern: on laboratory TIN x month, compute vendor payments divided by specimens received; fires when the quotient is near-constant across months despite varying invoiced hours; action postpay audit.

249.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, compare disclosed owners and managing employees on the provider application against criminal-history and OIG LEIE screening for undisclosed controlling parties. Check whether beneficiaries billed for counseling have any corroborating claim history with other providers in the plan file. Count encounters billed per rendering NPI per date of service and convert to clinician hours. Compare beneficiary enrolment records for AHCCCS ID numbers issued near the provider's first billing date at shared addresses. Test whether the new provider's paid dollars ramp from zero to peer-top-decile within months of enrolment.
249.features_to_create: 1) Hidden-owner screen: on provider TIN, compute the count of controlling individuals found in bank signatory or corporate registry records but absent from the enrolment ownership disclosure; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension and site visit. 2) Counselor capacity ceiling: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute billed therapy units multiplied by code-defined minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 3) New-enrollee ramp: on billing NPI x month, compute paid dollars divided by the provider's first-quarter trailing baseline; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

250.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, screen every CMS-855A disclosed owner, spouse and family member against OIG LEIE and prior exclusion records for straw-owner patterns. Compare hospice length of stay and live-discharge rate against same-specialty peers using paid claim history. Check whether certifying physician NPIs have any prior encounter claim with the enrolled beneficiary. Count beneficiaries whose terminal diagnosis lacks supporting hospital, imaging or oncology claims in the beneficiary's other claims. Test marketer payments recorded in the hospice's ledger against per-patient enrolment counts.
250.features_to_create: 1) Excluded-party ownership link: on provider TIN, compute the count of disclosed owners sharing an address, surname or bank account with an OIG LEIE-excluded individual; fires on any exact registry match; action claim suspension. 2) Live-discharge and long-stay rate: on hospice NPI x quarter, compute live discharges plus beneficiaries exceeding 180 days divided by total beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Terminality corroboration: on beneficiary x election period, compute the count of supporting diagnostic or hospital claims in the twelve months before election; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit.

251.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point because this is federal ship-repair contracting, not payer billing. The nearest detection route is comparing the prime contractor's subcontractor ownership disclosures against its own employee roster for conflicted insiders. A second route is matching subcontractor payroll against E-Verify and Form I-9 records for work authorisation on the government contract.
251.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on prime contract x subcontractor TIN, compute a match of subcontractor principals against the prime's employee and officer roster, and refer any exact match to contracting-officer conflict review before invoice approval.

252.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check whether the ordering NPI on urine drug testing claims has any encounter claim with the beneficiary near the specimen date. Contact-verify ordering physicians whose NPI appears on lab claims from an entity they have no contract with. Compute the share of one laboratory's testing volume referred by a single treatment-clinic owner or address. Compare definitive drug testing frequency per beneficiary per month against same-specialty peer laboratories. Trace payments from the laboratory TIN to the referring clinic's bank account during ownership and financial-relationship review.
252.features_to_create: 1) Unauthorised orderer use: on ordering NPI x laboratory NPI x month, compute the count of ordered lines lacking any encounter claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when above zero for a majority of lines; action prepay edit. 2) Referral concentration: on laboratory NPI x quarter, compute the share of paid urine-drug-test dollars from one referring facility address; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Testing frequency: on beneficiary x month, compute the count of definitive drug test claims across all laboratory NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-diagnosis peers; action postpay audit.

253.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute the laboratory's share of definitive high-analyte-count drug testing codes versus presumptive screening codes. Check whether each definitive test claim follows a presumptive screen with an unexpected or inconsistent result in the beneficiary's claim history. Compare analyte classes billed against the ordering diagnosis on the claim for clinical relevance. Count identical definitive panels repeated per beneficiary per month regardless of treatment stage. Compare the lab's average paid amount per beneficiary encounter against same-specialty peer laboratories.
253.features_to_create: 1) Definitive-tier skew: on laboratory NPI x quarter, compute definitive testing lines at the highest analyte tier divided by all drug-testing lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Reflex justification gap: on claim line, compute whether a paid presumptive screen with an abnormal result exists for the same beneficiary within the preceding days; fires when no such screen exists; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Panel repetition: on beneficiary x laboratory NPI x month, compute the count of identical highest-tier panels; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-diagnosis peers; action postpay audit.

254.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, test whether billed beneficiaries have any other claim linking them to the billing entity's county or referring clinicians. Compare specimen and office-visit dates against the beneficiary's concurrent claims placing them elsewhere. Count claims per beneficiary from a newly enrolled billing NPI with no prior remittance history. Verify the ordering NPI's awareness by contacting prescribers whose identifiers appear on high-volume test claims. Compare paid dollars to enrolled staffing and site capacity recorded on the enrolment application and a site visit.
254.features_to_create: 1) Orphan-beneficiary billing: on beneficiary x billing NPI, compute the count of paid lines where no other claim ties the beneficiary to that provider's referral network or geography; fires when the count is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 2) Startup revenue ramp: on billing NPI x month, compute paid dollars divided by the provider's trailing three-month baseline since enrolment; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers of the same enrolment age; action payment suspension and site visit. 3) Beneficiary claim density: on beneficiary x billing NPI x year, compute the count of urine drug test and E/M lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

255.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check for any prior encounter or referral claim tying each billed beneficiary to the billing entity. Compare paid urine drug screen volume to the enrolled site's equipment and CLIA certificate scope. Count repeat claims for the same beneficiary within short intervals lacking any treatment diagnosis in other claims. Compare the new billing NPI's payment ramp against its own trailing remittance history since enrolment. Verify physical laboratory operations and staffing against the CMS-855B enrolment address through a site visit.
255.features_to_create: 1) CLIA scope mismatch: on claim line, compute a match of the billed CPT to the laboratory's CLIA certificate-permitted test complexity; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Unlinked beneficiary rate: on billing NPI x month, compute the share of billed beneficiaries with no corroborating encounter claim from any provider in the same region; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Revenue acceleration: on billing NPI x month, compute paid dollars divided by the provider's trailing baseline; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers of equal enrolment age; action site visit.

256.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point because this is a pandemic business-loan certification, not a payer billing event. The nearest detection route is aggregating employee counts across commonly owned applicants using shared EIN officers, addresses and payroll filings before forgiveness. A second route is comparing certified employee headcount against state unemployment wage records for all affiliated entities.
256.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on applicant group keyed by shared owner and address, compute the summed employee count from state payroll filings and block forgiveness when the affiliated total exceeds the programme size standard.

257.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare submitted attendant timesheet hours against EVV visit records with matching telephony or GPS check-in and check-out. Count total paid attendant hours per attendant identifier per day across all consumers. Test whether the same submitter account created, approved and edited both the consumer and attendant portal records. Check attendant identities against the state licence or registry file, the Death Master File and duplicate Social Security numbers. Compare the consumer's authorised service plan units in the prior-authorisation record against billed units.
257.features_to_create: 1) Attendant day impossibility: on attendant identifier x date of service, compute total paid personal-care and respite hours summed across all consumers; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) EVV corroboration gap: on claim line, compute paid units minus units supported by a matching EVV visit record; fires when the difference is above zero; action claim suspension. 3) Self-approval concentration: on portal user account x month, compute the count of distinct consumers and attendants whose timesheets that account both submitted and approved; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-programme peers; action postpay audit and site visit.

258.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count power wheelchair repair and replacement-part HCPCS lines per beneficiary per year against the base K-code delivery date. Compute paid dollars per beneficiary for the supplier and compare to same-specialty DMEPOS peers. Test whether replacement claims for the same part exceed the device's expected lifetime service intervals. Check for prior-authorisation records and physician orders supporting each repair episode. Compare the supplier's distinct beneficiary count against total billed dollars on its remittance history.
258.features_to_create: 1) Repair frequency ceiling: on beneficiary x supplier NPI x part HCPCS x year, compute the count of paid replacement lines; fires when the count exceeds the manufacturer-supported replacement interval for that item; action prepay edit. 2) Revenue per beneficiary: on supplier NPI x quarter, compute paid dollars divided by distinct beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Order corroboration: on claim line, compute the presence of an ordering NPI encounter and a signed repair order within the lookback window; fires when absent; action documentation request (ADR).

259.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare billed home health visit units against EVV records and payroll timesheets for the named field staff. Count visits per rendering aide or nurse identifier per date of service and convert to hours. Compare the agency's visits per episode against the plan of care units in the prior-authorisation record. Test whether beneficiaries billed have concurrent inpatient or nursing facility claims on the same dates. Compare the agency's paid dollars per beneficiary against its own trailing baseline and same-specialty peers.
259.features_to_create: 1) Staff day impossibility: on rendering staff identifier x date of service, compute billed visit minutes summed across beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) EVV and payroll reconciliation: on agency NPI x week, compute billed visit hours minus payroll hours paid to field staff; fires when billed exceeds payroll; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension. 3) Overlapping institutional stay: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of home health lines coinciding with an inpatient or SNF claim; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension.

260.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, psychotherapy CPT 90834/90837 claims carry rendering NPIs whose portal submission IP and device fingerprint match a provider suspended in the payer's enrolment file. The suspended individual appears as an owner or managing employee on the billing entity's CMS-855 ownership fields shared with the billing NPIs. Claim dates of service fall on federal holidays and weekends at rates far above same-specialty peers in remittance history. Summed session minutes for a rendering NPI on one date of service exceed 24 hours. Two billing NPIs submit identical beneficiary panels and identical session times, indicating one person performing under borrowed numbers.
260.features_to_create: 1) Suspended-party submission linkage: on billing NPI x submitter credential, compute the count of claims whose submitter login, IP, or 855 associated-person matches an NPI under payment suspension or LEIE exclusion; fires on exact registry match; action claim suspension. 2) Impossible therapy day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed timed-unit minutes from CPT 90832/90834/90837 modifiers; fires when total exceeds 24 hours or documented clinic hours; action prepay edit. 3) Holiday and panel-overlap pattern: on rendering NPI x month, compute the share of sessions dated on federal holidays plus the Jaccard overlap of beneficiary panels with any other rendering NPI; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

261.ways_to_identify: At enrolment and plan oversight, the Medicare Advantage organization's vendor ledger shows per-lead payments to clinical or administrative staff at referring practices. Flat $2,500 'coordination of care' advances to physicians appear with no deliverable or encounter data supporting the service in claims. Enrollment files show beneficiary clusters where one practice TIN accounts for an outsized share of a plan's new enrollments in a month. Capitation payment records show new enrollees whose prior claims history is concentrated in practices receiving plan payments. Marketing 'permission to contact' card volumes reconcile poorly with CMS scope-of-appointment documentation retained by the plan.
261.features_to_create: 1) Enrollment source concentration: on plan contract x referring practice TIN x month, compute the share of new MA enrollments whose prior-year claims history maps to that TIN; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer plans in the same county; action postpay audit. 2) Payment-to-referrer linkage: on physician NPI, compute the sum of plan vendor payments coded as care coordination divided by the count of coordination encounters submitted; fires when encounters are zero while payments are positive; action payment suspension. 3) Lead-purchase ledger match: on plan x payee bank account, compute the count of payees whose tax ID matches staff at practices sending enrollments; fires on exact registry match; action site visit.

262.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, ordering-NPI concentration shows one laboratory receiving nearly all toxicology and blood panel orders from a small set of practices. The laboratory's ledgers show rent, phlebotomy, and processing payments to those same ordering physicians' TINs, tracked against fair-market-value benchmarks. Per-beneficiary toxicology panel breadth from those ordering NPIs exceeds same-specialty peers on definitive drug testing G-codes. Marketer commission payments in lab records scale with the dollar value of Medicare and TRICARE claims generated. Ordering physicians show no corresponding E/M encounter or documented medical-necessity indication before the panel dates of service.
262.features_to_create: 1) Referral-source exclusivity: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute the share of lab claims routed to a single laboratory NPI plus the count of distinct labs used; fires when exclusivity is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Payment-linked ordering: on laboratory TIN x ordering NPI, compute the ratio of lab-to-physician payments (rent, phlebotomy, processing) to allowed charges from that orderer; fires when the ratio is nonzero and volume rose above the orderer's trailing baseline; action payment suspension. 3) Panel breadth without encounter: on ordering NPI x HCPCS, compute the mean count of definitive drug test analytes per beneficiary and the days to the nearest E/M claim; fires when analytes exceed the peer percentile with no E/M in the lookback; action prepay edit.

263.ways_to_identify: There is no clinical claim here and no adjudication point; the false statement sits in an annual contractor compliance certification to the Defense Health Agency. The nearest detection route is contract administration: reconcile certified vulnerability-scan and patch cadence against the contractor's own scanner logs and third-party audit reports. Independent IV&V or DCAA-style audits of access control, firewall, and password policy artifacts would surface the gap before the next certification payment.
263.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on contractor contract x reporting period, require submission of raw scanner and patch-remediation export files and compare the count of open critical vulnerabilities past the contractual remediation window against the certified figure, withholding contract payment on mismatch.

264.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a handful of ordering NPIs send nearly all their toxicology and clinical chemistry orders to one out-of-area laboratory NPI. Laboratory financial records show space rental, phlebotomy, and processing fees flowing to those same ordering practices' TINs. Marketer entities receive commissions proportional to billed lab dollars, visible in lab ledgers requested at credentialing or audit. Beneficiary distance from the laboratory's CMS-855B service area exceeds the norm for same-specialty peers. Ordered panels lack any preceding E/M encounter between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary in claims history.
264.features_to_create: 1) Single-lab funnel: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute the share of ordered lab allowed dollars going to one laboratory NPI; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Remuneration-to-volume ratio: on laboratory TIN x ordering practice TIN, compute the sum of lease, phlebotomy, and commission payments divided by allowed charges generated; fires when nonzero and the orderer's volume is above its trailing baseline; action payment suspension. 3) Geographic implausibility: on laboratory NPI x beneficiary, compute the distance from beneficiary ZIP to the 855B enrolled service area; fires when the distance is above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action prepay edit.

265.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one aide's rendering NPI or employee ID shows overlapping service minutes for different beneficiaries at different addresses on the same date. EVV visit records show clock-in GPS coordinates inconsistent with travel time between consecutive beneficiary addresses. Summed timesheet hours submitted across multiple employer agencies for one aide exceed 24 hours in a day. Telephonic community-support claims and in-person personal care claims for the same worker occupy identical clock intervals. Aide-submitted timesheets lack matching EVV telephony call-origin numbers for the beneficiary's registered phone.
265.features_to_create: 1) Cross-employer overlap: on aide identifier x date of service, compute overlapping service minutes across all employing agency claims using start and end times; fires when overlapping minutes exceed zero or total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Travel infeasibility: on aide identifier x consecutive visit pair, compute the gap in minutes between visits minus the driving time between EVV-captured addresses; fires when the gap is negative; action claim suspension. 3) EVV-to-timesheet reconciliation: on beneficiary x aide x date, compute the count of billed units without a matching EVV check-in or telephony origin record; fires when unmatched units exceed zero; action documentation request (ADR).

266.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point; the products were sold cash-and-carry to retail shops and consumers outside any payer network. The nearest detection route is FDA import screening: entry lines from unregistered foreign drug establishments declared as dietary supplements but containing PDE5 inhibitors. State board of pharmacy wholesale-distributor licensure files and DSCSA pedigree records would show no licensed distributor behind these shipments.
266.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on importer of record x entry line, compare the declared foreign manufacturer against the FDA drug establishment registration file and the consignee against state wholesale distributor licences, detaining entries with no registry match.

267.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, inpatient E/M claims (99221-99233) carry a facility CCN and place of service 21 for dates after that facility's Medicare certification was terminated. Summed typical-time minutes for the rendering NPI on a single date of service exceed 24 hours. Beneficiaries on the inpatient claims have concurrent skilled nursing facility or long-term care claims covering the same dates. Dates of service fall after the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File and CMS enrollment records. No corresponding facility inpatient stay exists for the beneficiary in Part A claims for those dates.
267.features_to_create: 1) Facility-status mismatch: on claim line, compare the date of service against the billed facility CCN's termination or closure date in the CMS provider-of-service file; fires on any date after closure; action prepay edit. 2) Impossible provider day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed CPT typical-time minutes across all professional claims; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Setting and vitality conflict: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of inpatient professional claims with no matching Part A inpatient stay, or with a date after the Death Master File date of death, or overlapping an SNF stay; fires when the count exceeds zero; action prepay edit and postpay audit.

268.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point; this is identity-based bank and consumer credit fraud against an individual and a company. The nearest detection route is financial institution monitoring: repeated transfers from personal and business accounts into an accounts-payable clerk's own accounts. Credit bureau new-account alerts and lender identity verification against SSA and issuing-authority records would surface the impersonation at loan origination.
268.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on originating business account x beneficiary bank account, compute the count and sum of transfers to accounts titled to an authorized signer or bookkeeper and hold when the count is above the account's trailing baseline.

269.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, admitted patients cluster from out-of-state ZIPs far from the facility, all holding recently issued individual PPO policies. Facility vendor ledgers show fixed-fee 'marketing' contracts whose actual payments track billable treatment days per admitted patient. Definitive urine drug testing claims per patient per week exceed same-specialty peers, and positive results follow admission timing suspiciously. Level-of-care billing (H0010/H0018 residential vs outpatient) shifts upward immediately after admission with no matching ASAM assessment documentation. The same patient identifiers recycle through multiple admissions across affiliated facility TINs within short intervals.
269.features_to_create: 1) Broker payment per admission: on facility TIN x marketing vendor, compute vendor payments divided by the count of new admissions attributable to that vendor; fires when the per-admission amount varies with billed treatment days rather than a fixed contract rate; action payment suspension. 2) Patient-origin dispersion: on facility NPI x month, compute the count of distinct out-of-state beneficiary ZIPs and the mean policy age in days at admission; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Level-of-care and testing intensity: on beneficiary x admission, compute definitive drug-test claims per week and days billed at the highest level of care without a dated ASAM assessment; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR).

270.ways_to_identify: On ADR response, physician and nurse signatures on plans of care are pixel-identical images reused across different beneficiaries and dates. Signing nurse NPIs remain on submitted 485s and visit notes after their state licence board file shows separation or lapsed licence. Certifying physician NPIs show no face-to-face encounter claim with the beneficiary within the required window before episode start. One certifying physician NPI signs an outsized share of a single agency's episodes relative to same-specialty peers. Documents produced in response to records requests bear creation metadata dated after the payer's request.
270.features_to_create: 1) Signature-image reuse: on agency NPI, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries whose submitted plan-of-care signature images hash-match another document; fires when the count exceeds one for any hash; action claim suspension and postpay audit. 2) Signer licence validity: on rendering or signing clinician NPI x date of service, compare the date against state licence board effective and end dates plus the agency's payroll roster; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 3) Certifier concentration and face-to-face gap: on certifying NPI x agency NPI, compute the share of the agency's episodes certified and the days between the face-to-face E/M claim and episode start; fires when the share is above the calibrated percentile versus peers or no encounter exists; action prior-authorisation requirement.

271.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed RN-rate procedure codes are paired with rendering staff whose state licence board record shows LPN licensure only. Dates of service fall after the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File or after Medicaid eligibility termination in the state eligibility file. Aide hours billed per beneficiary per week exceed the units authorized on the prior-authorisation and plan of care. Summed staff hours across the owner's three agency NPIs exceed 24 hours per day per worker. All claims for three agency TINs are submitted from a single out-of-state IP address tied to the common owner in CMS-855A ownership fields.
271.features_to_create: 1) Licence-tier mismatch: on claim line, compare the skill level implied by the billed HCPCS (RN vs LPN vs aide) against the rendering clinician's licence class in the state board file; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Eligibility and vitality screen: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of billed units dated after the Death Master File date of death or outside the Medicaid eligibility span; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 3) Authorization overage across commonly owned agencies: on beneficiary x week, compute billed hours summed across all agency NPIs sharing an 855A owner minus prior-authorised hours; fires when the difference is positive; action prepay edit.

272.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, G0156 home health aide units are billed by staff whose training certificates are absent from the agency's personnel file at credentialing. The rendering worker identifier on G0156 lines does not appear on the state home health aide certification registry. The agency's ratio of G0156 units to non-skilled personal care units is far above same-specialty peers in the same state. Beneficiaries on G0156 claims lack a matching skilled nursing or therapy visit establishing a home health plan of care. OASIS assessments do not document any aide-level skilled need corresponding to the billed G0156 units.
272.features_to_create: 1) Aide certification match: on rendering worker identifier x claim line for G0156, compare the worker against the state home health aide certification registry and agency training file; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Skilled-rate mix outlier: on agency NPI x quarter, compute G0156 units divided by total aide-and-personal-care units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Plan-of-care anchor: on beneficiary x episode, compute the count of G0156 units with no skilled nursing or therapy visit and no OASIS assessment in the episode window; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension and postpay audit.

273.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, imaging claims billed under a hospital NPI with place of service 22 originate from equipment and addresses on a separate freestanding imaging center's 855B enrolment. Service facility address on the claim does not match any provider-based department listed on the hospital's CCN attachment in PECOS. Beneficiaries billed as hospital outpatients have no other claims from that hospital before or after the imaging date. Technical-component volume under the hospital NPI jumps above its trailing baseline right after a management or lease agreement date. Revenue-share ledgers show a fixed percentage of imaging collections retained by the hospital for NPI use.
273.features_to_create: 1) Service-address to provider-based match: on claim line, compare the service facility address and NPI against the hospital CCN's registered provider-based department list in PECOS; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Orphan hospital outpatient: on beneficiary x hospital CCN, compute the count of imaging claims where the beneficiary has no other encounter with that CCN within the lookback window; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 3) Technical-component surge: on hospital NPI x month x imaging CPT family, compute technical-component units versus the facility's trailing twelve-month baseline; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-size hospital peers; action postpay audit.

274.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, CPT 64553/64555 neurostimulator electrode implantation is billed with place of service 11 rather than an operating room or ASC. No matching facility claim, anesthesia claim, or implantable-device HCPCS appears for the same beneficiary and date of service. The same rendering NPI reports implantation volumes per day above the calibrated percentile versus neurosurgery and pain-medicine peers. Device invoices and DSCSA-style supplier records show purchases of auricular electro-acupuncture kits, not implantable pulse generators or leads. No subsequent programming or pulse-generator insertion claims follow the alleged implants in beneficiary claims history.
274.features_to_create: 1) Setting-and-device coherence: on claim line for neurostimulator implantation CPT codes, compute the count of same-beneficiary same-date facility, anesthesia, and implantable-device claims; fires when that count is zero or place of service is office; action prepay edit. 2) Implant volume implausibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of implantation procedures and derived operative minutes; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers or exceeding available clinic hours; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Absent follow-through: on beneficiary x implant date, compute the days to any subsequent generator insertion or electronic analysis claim; fires when none exists within the expected window; action postpay audit.

275.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, neurostimulator electrode implantation CPT codes appear with place of service 11 and no facility or anesthesia claim for the same beneficiary date. Device acquisition records show auricular electro-acupuncture units rather than implantable leads for the billed HCPCS. The rendering NPI's implantation counts per week far exceed same-specialty peers in the same locality. No pulse-generator insertion or device programming claim ever follows the alleged electrode implants in beneficiary claim history. The specialty on the rendering NPI's PECOS enrolment does not include surgical privileges consistent with implantation.
275.features_to_create: 1) Implant-without-operative-context: on claim line, compute the count of matching same-date facility, anesthesia, or device HCPCS claims for the beneficiary; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit. 2) Peer volume outlier: on rendering NPI x week, compute the count of neurostimulator implantation procedures per enrolled specialty; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Downstream device silence: on beneficiary x implantation claim, compute the gap in days to any generator insertion or analysis-programming claim; fires when no such claim exists in the expected window; action documentation request (ADR).

276.ways_to_identify: The pills were sold for cash to traffickers, so no claim reaches a payer and there is no adjudication point. The decisive non-claims route is ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree data: controlled-substance purchases far exceeding the pharmacy's dispensing volume. State prescription drug monitoring program filings showing near-zero dispensed schedule II opioids against large wholesale acquisitions expose the gap directly. Bank structuring patterns in cash deposits and Suspicious Activity Reports provide a second, financial route.
276.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on pharmacy DEA number x month, compute ARCOS-reported hydrocodone and oxycodone dosage units acquired minus PDMP-reported dispensed units plus payer-claimed units, and refer for DEA administrative action when the unexplained difference is above the calibrated percentile versus same-size pharmacy peers.

277.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point; this is employment tax withholding theft and unfiled returns. The nearest detection route is IRS matching of Forms W-2 and W-3 wage withholding totals against Forms 941 filed and trust fund deposits actually made. Repeated nonfiling by a business with active payroll registration and state unemployment wage filings is visible without any payer involvement.
277.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on employer EIN x quarter, compute reported W-2 withheld Social Security and Medicare tax minus Form 941 deposits received, and open a trust fund recovery examination when the difference is positive and recurs across quarters.

278.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point; this is employee embezzlement from a private construction company. The nearest detection route is bank and card monitoring: company payments routed to a personal credit card account held by the bookkeeper. Payroll system audit logs showing duplicate payroll checks and self-approved hour and bonus edits would surface it internally.
278.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on employee ID x pay period, compute the count of payroll disbursements and the sum of hour, bonus, and accrual adjustments made by the same user who approves them, and require dual authorization when the count exceeds one per period.

279.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the applicant's name, SSN, and date of birth combination fails SSA Enumeration Verification System matching in the state Medicaid eligibility file. Citizenship and immigration status returns no match in the SAVE system despite an attested U.S. citizen declaration. The same SSN shows concurrent wage or identity activity inconsistent with the claimed disability status in SSA records. Address and contact data on the Medicaid application match records already tied to a different identity in the state's master person index. Long benefit tenure with no verified employment history or immigration record persists across annual redetermination files.
279.features_to_create: 1) Identity verification gate: on applicant record at eligibility determination, compute the SSA EVS and SAVE match result across name, SSN, date of birth, and status fields; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension pending verification. 2) Duplicate-identity linkage: on SSN x master person index, compute the count of distinct beneficiary identities sharing SSN, address, or phone; fires when the count exceeds one; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Redetermination drift: on beneficiary x annual redetermination, compute the gap in days since the last successful SSA and SAVE re-verification; fires when the gap exceeds the redetermination cycle; action payment suspension.

280.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since the loss is unremitted payroll tax and understated workers' compensation premium. The nearest detection route is the carrier's premium audit comparing declared payroll on the policy application against certificates of insurance issued to unrelated contractors. State workers' compensation certificate-verification registries can be matched to check-cashing volume reported by the depository bank under BSA reporting. IRS Form 941 wage totals filed by the insured entity can be reconciled against 1099/bank deposit inflows for the same EIN.
280.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Premium-to-deposit divergence: on policy EIN x quarter, compute the ratio of bank deposits credited to the entity over declared payroll on the workers' compensation application and Form 941; fires when the ratio exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-class-code policyholders; action postpay audit.

281.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, home visit E/M codes 99341-99350 carry dates of service after the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File. Home visit place of service 12 overlaps an inpatient or SNF stay on the same beneficiary's Part A claims. The rendering NPI's daily home visit count implies travel and face-to-face time exceeding 24 hours. Beneficiary residence addresses in the enrolment file lie far outside the practice's service radius on CMS-855I. Home visit volume for the NPI jumps sharply above its own trailing monthly baseline without new staff on the enrolment record.
281.features_to_create: 1) Death and inpatient overlap: on claim line, compute whether the date of service falls after the Death Master File date or inside a paid Part A inpatient or SNF stay for the same beneficiary; fires on any overlap day; action prepay edit. 2) Home visit day capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of typical times for billed home visit codes plus inter-address travel minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Baseline break: on rendering NPI x month, compute home visit line count divided by the provider's trailing twelve-month mean; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

282.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, home visit CPT lines bear dates of service after the beneficiary's date of death recorded in the Death Master File. The same beneficiary has a concurrent paid inpatient or nursing facility Part A claim covering the home visit date. The rendering NPI bills more home visits per calendar day than travel between beneficiary addresses physically allows. No prior encounter history exists between the rendering NPI and the beneficiary in the payer's remittance history. Documentation returned on ADR shows identical narrative text across unrelated beneficiaries and dates.
282.features_to_create: 1) Decedent service edit: on claim line, compute the gap in days between date of service and the Death Master File date for the beneficiary; fires when the date of service is later; action prepay edit. 2) Concurrent institutional stay: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of paid Part A institutional days overlapping a place-of-service 12 professional line; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 3) Visit-day impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total billed home visit minutes plus geocoded travel minutes between service addresses; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action postpay audit.

283.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on L-code brace claims has no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary in claims history. A single ordering NPI signs brace orders for beneficiaries spread across many states within one week. The same beneficiary receives multiple distinct brace HCPCS from unrelated supplier NPIs within thirty days. At enrolment, the new supplier's CMS-855S owners, address or bank account match an entity already under payment suspension. Beneficiary telephone contact records show no request for the device before the order date.
283.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Suspended-entity re-enrolment link: on applicant NPI, compute the count of exact matches on CMS-855S owner SSN, practice address or bank routing/account against suppliers with active payment suspension; fires when the count exceeds zero; action site visit and prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Brace saturation: on beneficiary x brace HCPCS family, compute distinct paid supplier NPIs in a rolling 30 days; fires when the count exceeds one without a documented replacement reason; action claim suspension.

284.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, COVID-19 test claims under U0003/U0004/87635 exceed the lab's CLIA certificate instrument capacity for that date of service. Ordering NPIs on the claims have no other claim relationship with the tested beneficiaries in payer history. Beneficiary residence ZIPs cluster in states thousands of miles from the lab's CMS-855B service address. At enrolment, the listed owner on CMS-855B is a straw with no prior PECOS or NPPES laboratory history. Multiple lab NPIs share the same bank account, mailing address or authorised official across enrolment records.
284.features_to_create: 1) Capacity ceiling: on lab NPI x date of service, compute billed test line count divided by validated daily throughput for the analysers on the CLIA certificate; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action claim suspension. 2) Common-control graph: on TIN and bank account, compute the distinct count of enrolled lab NPIs sharing that account, address or authorised official in CMS-855B; fires when the count exceeds one; action site visit and prepay edit. 3) Orderer-beneficiary linkage: on claim line, compute the count of prior claims between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary in the lookback window; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit.

285.ways_to_identify: There is no billed claim and no adjudication point, because controlled substances were removed from facility emergency kits rather than billed. The nearest detection route is reconciliation of the facility's narcotic count sheets and e-kit pharmacy replenishment invoices against MAR administration entries. State PDMP and ARCOS distributor shipment data for the facility DEA number can be compared to documented resident administrations. Automated dispensing cabinet override and access logs identify one badge repeatedly opening carts outside administration windows.
285.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Kit reconciliation variance: on facility DEA number x drug NDC x month, compute wholesaler units received minus units documented on the MAR plus waste witnessed; fires when the unexplained variance exceeds zero units; action postpay audit and referral to the state board.

286.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, respiratory panel and COVID test lines carry dates of service after the beneficiary's Death Master File date. The referring NPI on the claim is deceased or retired per NPPES deactivation and PECOS status on the service date. No ordering physician encounter with the beneficiary exists anywhere in the payer's claim history. The lab's state test-site licence and CLIA certificate expiry date precede the billed dates of service. Payments deposited to the lab account are withdrawn in near-total lump sums within days of remittance.
286.features_to_create: 1) Dead-party edit: on claim line, compute whether the date of service postdates the beneficiary Death Master File date or the referring NPI's NPPES deactivation date; fires on either mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Licence validity: on lab NPI x date of service, compute the gap in days between the service date and the CLIA or state test-site licence expiry in the registry; fires when the service date is after expiry; action claim suspension. 3) Cash-out velocity: on provider bank account x week, compute withdrawals divided by Medicare remittances deposited in the trailing 30 days; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

287.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed test dates of service fall after the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File. The referring NPI listed on the claim was deceased or deactivated in NPPES on the service date. The lab's state test-site licence in the health department registry had expired before the billed dates. No prior encounter links the referring NPI to the beneficiary anywhere in claims history. Enrolment records show a foreign-resident authorised official with sole signature authority over the payment bank account.
