287.features_to_create: 1) Registry mismatch edit: on claim line, compute exact matches of date of service against beneficiary and referring-provider death or deactivation dates in the Death Master File and NPPES; fires on any service date later; action prepay edit. 2) Licence lapse hold: on lab NPI, compute days between date of service and the state test-site or CLIA expiry date; fires when the gap is positive; action payment suspension. 3) Referral concentration: on lab NPI x referring NPI, compute the share of the lab's billed lines attributable to referrers with zero other claims for those beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

288.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, respiratory pathogen panel CPT 0202U/87631-87633 lines appear for nearly every resident at a facility on the same collection date. The same specimen collection date shows an RPP billed without any corresponding COVID-19 test line. Ordering NPIs are facility physicians with no documented order in the lab requisition or the beneficiary's other claims. The lab's vendor ledger shows fixed monthly marketing payments to an entity that also controls specimen access at the referring facilities. Sales representative 1099 payments scale linearly with referred test volume, visible in the lab's own commission records.
288.features_to_create: 1) Facility-wide panel sweep: on referring facility CCN x collection date, compute the share of residents with an RPP line billed; fires when the share is above the calibrated percentile versus same-setting peers; action claim suspension. 2) Reflex mismatch: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of RPP lines with no COVID-19 test line on the same specimen date; fires when the count exceeds zero; action prepay edit. 3) Referral-source concentration: on lab NPI x referral-source entity, compute the share of billed lines originating from facilities served by one contracted marketing counterparty; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

289.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the declared value of the excluded automobile on the Medicaid asset schedule far exceeds NADA or Kelley Blue Book valuation for that year and model. State DMV title records show the vehicle transferred to the applicant's representative within the five-year lookback. Bank records disclosed on the application show a large check to the same attorney contemporaneous with the vehicle transfer. The vehicle registration record shows non-operable or salvage status inconsistent with the claimed appraisal. The submitted appraisal lacks an independent licensed appraiser identifier verifiable in state registry files.
289.features_to_create: 1) Vehicle valuation mismatch: on Medicaid application x excluded automobile, compute declared value minus published guide value for the VIN year, make and model; fires when the difference exceeds the guide value; action documentation request (ADR) before eligibility approval. 2) Transfer-window check: on applicant x asset, compute days between the DMV title transfer date and the application date; fires when inside the statutory lookback period; action claim suspension of eligibility pending review. 3) Representative concentration: on filing attorney or representative ID, compute the count of applications claiming a high-value automobile exclusion; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer filers; action postpay audit.

290.ways_to_identify: At pharmacy adjudication, the prescriber DEA number on Schedule II claims belongs to a hospital institutional registration rather than an individual practitioner. The prescriber name transmitted on the NCPDP claim does not match any individual in NPPES or the state licence board file. PDMP records show one DEA number writing oxycodone for a small closed set of patients at high dosage units. The prescribing address on the script does not match the DEA registrant's registered location in the DEA database. The prescriber has no NPI on any other medical claim for those same patients.
290.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber identity validation: on claim line, compute exact match of prescriber DEA number, name and NPI against the DEA registration file, NPPES and the state licence board file; fires on any mismatch or institutional-only registration; action prepay edit. 2) Institutional DEA misuse: on DEA number x month, compute the count of outpatient Schedule II claims written under a hospital registrant number by non-affiliated pharmacies; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 3) Concentrated opioid writer: on prescriber DEA x quarter, compute oxycodone dosage units divided by distinct patients; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension and board referral.

291.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, since the loss is nonprofit foundation funds paid on vendor invoices. The nearest detection route is accounts-payable matching of invoices to purchase orders, receiving records and contracts in the foundation's ERP. Vendor master file screening detects new payees whose bank account or address matches an employee record. Kickback flow is visible as vendor disbursements followed by deposits to the approving officer's personal account in bank records.
291.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Three-way match and payee-employee overlap: on vendor ID x invoice, compute the count of invoices approved by one officer with no purchase order or receiving record, plus exact matches of vendor bank account or address to employee HR records; fires when either count exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

292.ways_to_identify: This is a personnel announcement, not a fraud case, so there is no claim and no adjudication point. No payer data, provider NPI or service line is implicated anywhere in the item. The nearest non-claims route is simply routine tracking of district leadership announcements for enforcement liaison purposes.

293.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, brace L-code claims cite ordering NPIs whose only contact with the beneficiary is a brief telehealth code on the same day. Beneficiary states on the supplier's claims span far beyond its CMS-855S service area. Enrolment records list owners with no DMEPOS history whose identity documents match those on other suspended supplier applications. Multiple supplier NPIs share a payment bank account or authorised official in CMS-855S. Marketing vendor payments in the supplier's ledger track referral counts rather than fixed fees.
293.features_to_create: 1) Telehealth-only order: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the count of prior in-person or longitudinal encounters between orderer and beneficiary excluding a same-day brief telehealth code; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit. 2) Straw-owner and account linkage: on bank account and authorised official ID in CMS-855S, compute the distinct count of enrolled DMEPOS NPIs sharing them; fires when the count exceeds one; action site visit and prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Geographic dispersion: on supplier NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states on paid brace lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

294.ways_to_identify: On ADR response, physician and nurse signatures on plans of care appear as pasted images identical in pixel form across different beneficiaries and dates. The certifying physician NPI has no face-to-face encounter claim with the beneficiary within the required window. A signing nurse's licence in the state board file shows employment terminated before the documented visit dates. OASIS assessments transmitted to the state repository are missing or their dates conflict with billed visit dates. The certifying physician certifies for one agency at a rate far above same-specialty peers.
294.features_to_create: 1) Face-to-face linkage: on episode x certifying NPI, compute days between the certification date and the nearest E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter falls inside the required window; action prepay edit. 2) Signature reuse detection: on submitted document image, compute the count of byte- or perceptual-hash matches of the signature block across distinct beneficiaries; fires when the count exceeds one; action claim suspension and postpay audit. 3) OASIS-to-claim reconciliation: on episode, compute the count of billed visit dates with no matching OASIS assessment or with staff credential lapsed in the state licence file; fires when the count exceeds zero; action documentation request (ADR).

295.ways_to_identify: In PDMP data, one prescriber writes oxycodone and promethazine-with-codeine for patients residing across dozens of distant states. The prescriber's practice has almost no billed E/M claims corresponding to the dated prescriptions, indicating cash-only visits. Patients filling those scripts show high early-refill rates and long pharmacy travel distances in dispensing records. Medical records produced after a complaint carry creation timestamps postdating the documented visit dates. The prescriber's morphine-milligram-equivalents per patient sit far above same-specialty peers in the state's PDMP report.
295.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber geographic dispersion: on prescriber DEA x month, compute distinct patient states and mean patient-to-prescriber distance in PDMP fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit at the pharmacy and board referral. 2) Script-without-encounter: on prescriber NPI x patient, compute the count of controlled prescriptions with no billed or documented E/M encounter within the lookback; fires when the ratio exceeds the calibrated peer percentile; action postpay audit. 3) Record backdating: on chart document, compute the gap in days between electronic creation timestamp and the recorded visit date; fires when the gap exceeds the permitted late-entry window; action documentation request (ADR).

296.ways_to_identify: This is an enforcement-office expansion announcement rather than a single case, so there is no claim and no adjudication point. No provider NPI, service line or beneficiary is identified for any prepay edit. The nearest non-claims route is aligning payer data-sharing feeds with the strike force's regional analytics requests.
296.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Data-sharing agreements can route payer claim extracts to the regional strike force for targeting outside the adjudication system.

297.ways_to_identify: At pharmacy adjudication, claims for opioid, benzodiazepine and muscle relaxant NDCs overlap in days-supply for the same beneficiary. Refill claims arrive well before the prior fill's days supply is exhausted, visible in the payer's own remittance history. Single prescriptions exceed high morphine-milligram-equivalent daily thresholds computed from NDC strength and quantity. One prescriber DEA number accounts for an outsized share of a store's controlled dispensing in PDMP data. Beneficiaries fill controlled prescriptions at multiple pharmacies and prescribers within the same month.
297.features_to_create: 1) Trinity concurrency: on beneficiary x date, compute overlapping days-supply across opioid, benzodiazepine and skeletal muscle relaxant NDCs; fires when all three overlap on the same day; action prepay edit. 2) Early refill: on beneficiary x NDC, compute days between fill date and prior fill date minus prior days supply; fires when the gap is negative beyond the plan's permitted tolerance; action claim suspension. 3) Store-level red-flag rate: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of controlled claims with an early refill, trinity overlap or high MME; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-volume peer pharmacies; action postpay audit.

298.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, essentially all of the supplier's paid claims cite a single ordering NPI. That ordering physician has no E/M encounter history with the beneficiaries receiving the equipment. Delivery documentation requested on ADR lacks beneficiary-signed proof of delivery matching the billed dates. Beneficiary residence ZIPs are far outside the supplier's CMS-855S service area. Payment inflows are swept from the supplier account to unrelated entities within days of remittance.
298.features_to_create: 1) Single-orderer dependence: on supplier NPI x quarter, compute the share of paid dollars attributable to the top one ordering NPI; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line, compute days between date of service and the last E/M claim between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Proceeds sweep: on supplier bank account x week, compute outbound transfers to unrelated entities divided by Medicare deposits received; fires when the ratio exceeds the calibrated peer percentile; action payment suspension.

299.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a small closed set of beneficiaries receives the same diagnostic test panels repeatedly across the owner's several clinic NPIs. Those beneficiaries travel unusual distances past nearer providers to reach the clinics, visible in residence ZIP versus place of service. Test volume per beneficiary far exceeds same-specialty peer norms for the billed diagnosis codes. Multiple clinic NPIs share owners, address or bank account in CMS-855B enrolment records. Beneficiary cost-sharing is routinely waived or never collected, evident in absent secondary and patient-liability postings.
299.features_to_create: 1) Beneficiary recycling: on beneficiary x owning TIN, compute the count of distinct clinic NPIs under common ownership billing the same test HCPCS in a rolling 90 days; fires when the count exceeds one; action prepay edit. 2) Tests per beneficiary: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute diagnostic test lines divided by distinct beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Patient travel and cost-share: on claim line, compute beneficiary-to-clinic distance plus the share of claims with zero collected coinsurance; fires when both are above the calibrated peer percentile; action postpay audit.

300.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, clinic NPIs bill diagnostic tests to a beneficiary cohort whose home ZIPs cluster far from the clinic address on CMS-855B. The same beneficiary IDs appear across three commonly-owned clinic TINs receiving identical test panels within weeks. Beneficiaries show no prior E/M encounter with the rendering NPI before the ordered test dates of service. PECOS ownership fields link the three clinic enrolments to one managing owner with recent enrolment dates and immediate high volume. Beneficiary sharing across unrelated clinic NPIs, measured on paid claim history, exceeds normal referral overlap for the specialty.
300.features_to_create: 1) Shared-beneficiary ring: on beneficiary x owner entity from PECOS ownership fields, compute the count of distinct clinic NPIs billing the same CPT within 90 days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Testing without evaluation: on claim line, compute days between the diagnostic CPT date of service and the most recent E/M claim for that beneficiary at any commonly owned TIN; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action documentation request (ADR). 3) New-enrolment ramp: on provider NPI x month, compute paid dollars divided by the provider's trailing three-month baseline since PECOS enrolment date; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action site visit.

301.ways_to_identify: There is no claim and no adjudication point here, since this is a forfeiture and victim-remission announcement rather than a billing scheme. The nearest detection route is bank-side payment controls, where a payee-name mismatch on a large outbound wire against the vendor master file stops the transfer. Corporate treasury callback verification against previously validated insurer banking details catches altered wire instructions before funds leave.
301.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is a treasury rule on outbound wire, computing whether the beneficiary bank account differs from the vendor master account of record, holding the payment until callback verification.

302.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one ordering NPI signs DMEPOS, compounded cream and genetic test orders for beneficiaries spread across many states in a week. No E/M or telehealth encounter claim exists between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary before the order date of service. The same ordering NPI appears on claims from five unrelated supplier, pharmacy and lab TINs simultaneously. Ordered items span three unrelated benefit categories, which is implausible for one physician's specialty taxonomy in NPPES. Order counts per signing day exceed what a physician could evaluate within 24 hours.
302.features_to_create: 1) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states plus distinct billing supplier, lab and pharmacy TINs on ordered claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M or telehealth claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 3) Signing-rate impossibility: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries with orders divided by 24 hours; fires when implied minutes per patient fall below a clinically possible encounter length; action payment suspension.

303.ways_to_identify: In the automated dispensing cabinet log, one nurse's biometric withdrawals of hydromorphone are followed by cancel or null transactions at a rate far above unit peers. Cabinet withdrawals lack a matching medication administration record entry for the named patient in the EHR. Withdrawals are recorded under patient identifiers whose care assignment roster does not include that nurse for the shift. Waste events lack the required second-witness signature in the cabinet record. Vial-level ARCOS and pharmacy inventory reconciliation shows dispensed volume exceeding documented administered plus wasted volume.
303.features_to_create: 1) Cancel-rate outlier: on nurse ID x week, compute cancelled or nulled controlled-substance cabinet transactions divided by total withdrawals; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-unit peers; action postpay audit. 2) Withdrawal-without-administration: on nurse ID x date, compute the count of hydromorphone withdrawals with no matching MAR administration or witnessed waste within the shift; fires when the count exceeds zero; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Unassigned-patient access: on nurse ID x patient, compute the count of cabinet withdrawals where the patient is absent from that shift's assignment roster; fires when the count exceeds zero; action payment suspension.

304.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, because this is unremitted employment tax on a construction payroll. The nearest detection route is IRS matching of Forms W-2 wage and withholding totals against Forms 941 filed and deposits actually received. State unemployment insurance wage reports showing active payroll with no federal deposit trail provide a second non-claims signal.
304.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is an IRS reconciliation on employer EIN x quarter, computing withheld amounts reported on W-2 and 941 minus deposits received, escalating when the gap persists across consecutive quarters.

305.ways_to_identify: In risk-adjustment submissions, spinal enthesopathy and sacroiliitis ICD-10 codes appear at a rate far above same-region peers for the same provider group. Those diagnoses have no supporting treatment, imaging or specialist claim in the beneficiary's other encounter data. Retroactive additions of the codes arrive through supplemental chart-review submissions rather than the original encounter record. Radiology report creation timestamps postdate the MA plan's diagnosis query by weeks for the same beneficiary and date of service. The same two HCC-driving codes attach to a large share of one group's panel, with no deletions ever submitted.
305.features_to_create: 1) HCC code concentration: on provider group TIN x HCC diagnosis, compute the share of the attributed panel carrying that code in the encounter data submission; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty regional peers; action postpay audit. 2) Unsupported diagnosis: on beneficiary x HCC diagnosis year, compute the count of corroborating treatment, imaging or specialist claims within twelve months; fires when the count is zero; action documentation request (ADR) with medical record validation. 3) Late chart-review addition: on beneficiary x diagnosis, compute days between the encounter date of service and the supplemental submission or radiology report creation timestamp; fires when the report postdates the plan's query; action payment suspension of risk-adjusted amounts.

306.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the lab bills the highest-tier definitive urine drug testing CPT for nearly every specimen, with presumptive screens rarely preceding them. Ordering NPIs attached to the lab's claims show no corresponding office E/M claim on or near the specimen collection date of service. A small set of ordering NPIs accounts for nearly all of the lab's volume, indicating marketer-driven funneling. The lab's Form 1099 and vendor payments to marketing entities are percentage-based, visible in CMS-855B ownership and contractor disclosures. Definitive analyte counts per specimen sit at the panel maximum regardless of patient diagnosis on the claim.
306.features_to_create: 1) Panel-maximisation: on billing lab NPI x month, compute the share of definitive drug test claim lines billed at the top analyte tier, over total UDT lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Order concentration: on lab NPI, compute the Herfindahl concentration of paid volume across distinct ordering NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action documentation request (ADR) for signed physician orders. 3) Order without encounter: on claim line, compute days between specimen date of service and the nearest E/M claim linking that ordering NPI and beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action claim suspension.

307.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, high-dollar CGx panels are billed with an ordering NPI having no prior claim history with the beneficiary. One telemedicine ordering NPI signs genetic test orders for beneficiaries across many states within a single week. Beneficiary cohorts share collection dates and ZIP clusters matching health-fair and door-to-door recruitment rather than clinical referral patterns. The ordered panel is billed with cancer screening CPT stacks that lack any oncology diagnosis in the beneficiary's other claims. Lab payments to marketing entities appear as percentage-based contractor arrangements in CMS-855B disclosure and bank records.
307.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line, compute days between the genetic test date of service and the most recent E/M or telehealth claim between the ordering NPI and beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) Telemedicine orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct lab TINs on signed CGx orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Clinical-indication mismatch: on beneficiary x CGx CPT, compute the count of supporting oncology or hereditary-risk diagnoses in the prior twelve months of claims; fires when the count is zero; action prior-authorisation requirement.

308.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the lab's Part B claim date of service falls just past the 14-day window after the beneficiary's inpatient or outpatient discharge date on the hospital claim. The specimen collection date recorded on the lab claim precedes the billed date of service by more than two weeks. Order placement and cancel-resubmit timestamps in the lab information system cluster immediately before day fifteen. The same lab shows an unusual spike in claims with service dates on days 15 to 17 post-discharge relative to peers. The hospital's outpatient claim contains no corresponding pass-through charge for the same test.
308.features_to_create: 1) Fourteen-day rule edit: on claim line, compute days between the beneficiary's hospital discharge date and the lab claim date of service using the specimen collection date; fires when collection falls inside 14 days but billing date falls outside; action prepay edit. 2) Post-discharge day clustering: on lab NPI x month, compute the share of Part B claims with service dates on days 15 through 21 after a discharge; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action postpay audit. 3) Order-timestamp lag: on ordering NPI x lab accession, compute days between physician order timestamp and reported date of service; fires when the gap exceeds the specimen stability window; action documentation request (ADR).

309.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a small group of ordering physicians drives an outsized share of one lab's paid volume relative to their own patient panel size. Those same physicians appear as investors or members in MSO entities disclosed in CMS-855 ownership fields or state corporate registries. Beneficiary cost-sharing is systematically zero on the lab's remittance history, indicating routine copay and deductible waiver. Ordering physicians' test-per-patient counts exceed their specialty peers for cardiovascular and blood panels. Payments from the lab to physicians appear as consulting or processing fees in bank and 1099 records rather than fair-market service contracts.
309.features_to_create: 1) Referral concentration with ownership overlap: on ordering NPI x lab TIN, compute paid dollars share plus an exact match between the ordering NPI and any owner listed in CMS-855 or MSO registry filings; fires on registry match with share above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action payment suspension. 2) Copay waiver pattern: on billing lab NPI x quarter, compute the share of claim lines with zero patient responsibility collected in remittance history; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action postpay audit. 3) Ordering intensity: on ordering NPI x panel CPT, compute tests per distinct beneficiary per year; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit.

310.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, multiple beneficiaries are billed individual-ride procedure codes with identical pickup and drop-off times on the same date of service. Trip records show the same vehicle and driver ID assigned to overlapping trips billed separately at the higher rate. GPS or trip-log mileage for the claimed individual rides matches a single shared route across beneficiaries. The broker's authorization record specifies shared-ride mode while the submitted claim carries the individual-ride modifier. The provider's share of individual-ride codes exceeds same-market NEMT peers serving comparable destinations.
310.features_to_create: 1) Overlapping-trip detection: on vehicle ID x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between trips billed as individual rides; fires when any two individual-ride claims overlap in time; action prepay edit. 2) Mode mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact comparison between the billed ride-mode code and the mode on the transportation broker's prior-authorisation record; fires on mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Individual-ride share: on transportation provider NPI x month, compute individual-ride trips divided by total trips; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-market peers; action postpay audit.

311.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, two or more beneficiaries carry individual-ride codes with the same driver ID and overlapping pickup times on one date of service. Submitted trip mileage duplicates across beneficiaries, showing a single shared route billed multiple times at the solo rate. The claim's ride-mode code contradicts the mode recorded in the broker's trip authorization file. Signature logs or trip manifests list several riders for a trip billed as exclusive-use. The provider's individual-ride mix is far above same-market NEMT peers.
311.features_to_create: 1) Manifest rider count: on trip ID, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries on the manifest for trips billed with an individual-ride code; fires when the count exceeds one; action prepay edit. 2) Driver overlap: on driver ID x date of service, compute overlapping minutes across separately billed individual-ride claims; fires when overlap exceeds zero minutes; action claim suspension. 3) Authorization mode match: on claim line, compute exact equality of billed mode code and broker prior-authorisation mode; fires on mismatch; action postpay audit.

312.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the implanted neurostimulator electrode CPT is billed with office place of service 11 rather than a facility site. No facility, anesthesia or operating-room claim exists for the same beneficiary and date of service. The billing NPI's specialty in NPPES lacks surgical implantation privileges for the procedure billed. The same beneficiary receives repeated implantation codes at short intervals, inconsistent with a permanent implant's lifetime frequency. Supply and device invoices in the record match a single-use electro-acupuncture device with no covered HCPCS.
312.features_to_create: 1) Place-of-service impossibility: on claim line, compute whether the implantation CPT is billed with place of service 11 and no matching facility or anesthesia claim on the same date of service; fires when both conditions hold; action prepay edit. 2) Implant repeat frequency: on beneficiary x implantation CPT, compute the count of paid implantation events in a rolling twelve months against the device's expected lifetime frequency; fires when the count exceeds one without an explant claim; action claim suspension. 3) Specialty-privilege mismatch: on rendering NPI x CPT, compute exact match between NPPES taxonomy and the surgical specialties eligible to bill the code; fires on mismatch; action documentation request (ADR).

313.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, an owner or officer listed on the CMS-855 and state Medicaid disclosure matches a name on the state exclusion list or OIG LEIE. Rendering staff NPIs on psychotherapy claim lines have no active credential in the state licensing board file for the date of service. Billed service hours per rendering clinician per day exceed 24 hours. Beneficiaries billed for weekly counseling show no corresponding transportation, pharmacy or physician claim activity consistent with engagement. Group session rosters in the record repeat identical progress-note text across unrelated beneficiaries.
313.features_to_create: 1) Excluded-owner screen: on provider TIN, compute exact name and date-of-birth matches between CMS-855 owners and officers and OIG LEIE plus state exclusion files; fires on any match; action claim suspension and revalidation site visit. 2) Licence validity at service: on claim line, compute whether the rendering NPI held an active state licence spanning the date of service in the board file; fires on no active licence; action prepay edit. 3) Clinician hour impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed timed-unit minutes across all behavioral health CPTs; fires when total exceeds 24 hours; action payment suspension.

314.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, an unclassified biologic HCPCS is billed with no FDA approval or covered indication tied to the submitted diagnosis. The product's NDC does not appear in the payer's covered-drug file or the FDA licensed biologics list. The billing practice's units and dollars for the product jump from zero to top-decile within a quarter. In the hospital setting, controlled-substance cabinet withdrawals by one clinician lack matching administration records for the named patient. Cancelled or wasted narcotic transactions by that clinician exceed unit peers without a second witness.
314.features_to_create: 1) Non-covered biologic edit: on claim line, compute exact match of the billed NDC or HCPCS against the payer's covered-product file and FDA approval list; fires on no match; action prepay edit. 2) New-product ramp: on billing NPI x HCPCS x quarter, compute paid units divided by the provider's trailing baseline; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Diversion reconciliation: on clinician ID x week, compute controlled-substance withdrawals minus documented administrations and witnessed wastes; fires when the unreconciled count exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

315.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, psychotherapy add-on CPTs 90833, 90836 or 90838 are billed with an E/M code on nearly every encounter for the practice. Documented psychotherapy minutes are absent or duplicate the E/M time in the submitted record. Summed E/M plus psychotherapy minutes per rendering NPI per date of service exceed a plausible workday. The practice's add-on ratio far exceeds same-specialty psychiatric peers in the payer's remittance history. Internal compliance complaints and repeat identical time statements appear across unrelated beneficiary notes.
315.features_to_create: 1) Add-on ratio: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute psychotherapy add-on lines divided by total E/M lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Daily minute impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed E/M typical time plus billed psychotherapy minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the credentialed schedule; action claim suspension. 3) Distinct-time documentation: on claim line pairing E/M with an add-on, compute presence of a separately stated psychotherapy start and stop time in the record; fires when absent; action documentation request (ADR).

316.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one clinic NPI bills orthotic L-codes, timed physical therapy units and psychosocial rehabilitation for the same beneficiaries in one week. Summed timed therapy and behavioral health units per rendering NPI per date of service exceed 24 hours. Progress notes across unrelated beneficiaries contain byte-identical narrative strings, detectable by text hashing of submitted documentation. Beneficiaries billed for braces have no orthopedic diagnosis or prior evaluation in their other claims. Clinic bank deposits from multiple payers move promptly into personal accounts and vehicle purchases, visible in financial records.
316.features_to_create: 1) Cross-benefit stacking: on beneficiary x clinic NPI x week, compute the count of distinct benefit categories billed covering DMEPOS, therapy and behavioral health; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 2) Unit impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed timed units converted to minutes across all therapy and behavioral CPTs; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 3) Duplicate-note detection: on provider TIN, compute the share of submitted progress notes whose normalized text hash matches another beneficiary's note; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR), then payment suspension.

317.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the same beneficiaries receive brace L-codes, physical therapy and psychosocial rehabilitation from a single clinic NPI in one billing period. Timed units billed per rendering NPI per day exceed the hours available in a 24-hour day. Beneficiaries lack any prior evaluation or qualifying diagnosis supporting the ordered braces in their other claim history. Clinic payment volume rises sharply above its own trailing baseline across four payers simultaneously. Payer remittances flow into accounts that immediately disburse to personal asset purchases in bank records.
317.features_to_create: 1) Multi-payer volume ramp: on provider TIN x month, compute total paid dollars across payers divided by the provider's trailing six-month baseline; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 2) Daily unit impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed timed-unit minutes across therapy and behavioral CPTs; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 3) Brace without indication: on beneficiary x L-code, compute the count of qualifying musculoskeletal diagnoses and prior E/M encounters in the lookback; fires when the count is zero; action prior-authorisation requirement.

318.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, claims recur on a fixed weekly cadence for the same beneficiary with no gaps, matching a pre-booked schedule rather than delivered care. The rendering NPI on submitted lines shows no employment or credentialing record with the billing TIN for the date of service. Beneficiaries billed for ongoing visits have relocated or have no other claims in the region during the same period. Sign-in sheets or attendance records are absent for a large share of billed dates on ADR response. Billing continues under an NPI whose NPPES practice address no longer matches the billing site.
318.features_to_create: 1) Perfect-cadence billing: on beneficiary x provider TIN, compute the count of consecutive billed visit dates matching the scheduled interval with zero no-show gaps; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Rendering-NPI affiliation: on claim line, compute exact match between the rendering NPI and the TIN's credentialed staff roster and NPPES affiliation on the date of service; fires on no active affiliation; action prepay edit. 3) Beneficiary presence check: on beneficiary x month, compute the count of other claims within the service area during billed treatment months; fires when zero while visits continue to be billed; action payment suspension.

319.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, timed acupuncture and therapy units summed per licensed rendering NPI per date of service exceed 24 hours. Multiple clinic locations bill under the same borrowed licensed provider NPI on the same dates of service. Beneficiaries billed for repeated visits show no travel-consistent claim footprint and reside far from all three clinic addresses. Submitted treatment notes repeat identical text and identical measured findings across unrelated beneficiaries. Clinic enrolment records show licensed practitioners listed as supervising while payments flow to a non-licensed owner entity in bank records.
319.features_to_create: 1) Borrowed-licence detection: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct service locations billing under that NPI; fires when the count exceeds one at physically separated addresses; action claim suspension. 2) Timed-unit impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed acupuncture and therapy minutes from billed units; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 3) Beneficiary-distance and duplication: on beneficiary x clinic TIN, compute distance from residence ZIP to service address plus the count of notes with matching text hashes; fires when distance exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peers with duplicate notes present; action documentation request (ADR), then payment suspension.

320.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on DMEPOS, pharmacy and lab claims has no prior E/M encounter with that beneficiary. One telehealth ordering NPI appears on claims from unrelated supplier, pharmacy and laboratory NPIs across many beneficiary states weekly. Telehealth encounter claims show place-of-service 02 with unit times far below the billed CPT's required minutes. Beneficiaries receive braces, topical creams and cancer panels within days of each other from separate billing NPIs. Supplier remittance history shows volume jumping from near-zero to peer-top-decile within weeks of a marketing contract start date.
320.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim linking that ordering NPI to the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Shared-orderer graph degree: on ordering NPI x month, compute the count of distinct billing NPIs and distinct beneficiary states across DMEPOS, Part D and lab claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Cross-silo bundle: on beneficiary x 30 days, compute the count of distinct service silos (DME L-code, compounded drug NDC, genetic test CPT) traced to one ordering NPI; fires when that count exceeds one; action documentation request (ADR).

321.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed attendance days exceed signed daily sign-in-sheet records reconciled against the center's registration file. Enrolled recipients' residence addresses sit far outside the center's catchment on the Medicaid provider enrollment file. The same recipients simultaneously show personal care or home health visit claims overlapping the adult day care attendance hours. Enrollment surges cluster on marketer-linked recruitment dates rather than on assessment or care-plan dates. Ownership fields on the enrollment record link the day care TIN to a fiscal intermediary and a shell entity sharing one bank account.
321.features_to_create: 1) Attendance-versus-roster: on provider NPI x date of service, compute billed attendance units minus signed sign-in-sheet entries; fires when billed units exceed documented entries; action prepay edit. 2) Concurrent-service overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between adult day care units and home health or personal care visit records including EVV timestamps; fires when overlap exceeds zero minutes; action claim suspension. 3) Common-account cluster: on bank account, compute the count of distinct billing TINs receiving remittance deposits; fires when that count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership in enrollment records; action site visit and payment suspension.

322.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the applicant SSN and name mismatch the Social Security Administration and state vital records identity verification file. The same SSN appears on active enrollment in another beneficiary's Medicaid identity record. Claims and SNAP redemptions post in a geography inconsistent with the enrollee's address of record. The enrollee identity matches a Death Master File entry or an identity flagged in a prior fraud referral. Enrollment application signature and contact phone match those already used on other member records.
322.features_to_create: 1) Identity verification mismatch: on applicant record, compute the count of mismatched fields (SSN, date of birth, legal name) against SSA and state vital records; fires when any field mismatches exactly; action claim suspension pending eligibility review. 2) SSN reuse: on SSN, compute the distinct count of active member IDs across Medicaid and SNAP files; fires when that count exceeds one; action prepay edit. 3) Contact-point sharing: on phone number or mailing address, compute the count of distinct enrollee IDs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-region enrollees; action documentation request (ADR).

323.ways_to_identify: This is a personnel announcement, not a fraud matter, so no claim, no billing NPI and no adjudication point exists. There is nothing for a payer edit to evaluate at enrollment, prior authorisation or claim adjudication. The nearest non-claims route is routine tracking of Department of Justice press releases for later case linkage.
323.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system is maintaining a case-intake feed that ingests only actual charging or settlement documents for provider watchlisting.

324.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, summed timed psychotherapy CPT units for the rendering NPI exceed 24 hours on a single date of service. Dates of service fall on days the rendering NPI has no local activity while claims post continuously without any covering NPI. Beneficiaries have dates of service after the date recorded in the Death Master File. Patients with only one prior pre-surgical evaluation CPT show long ongoing 90837 series with no interval diagnosis change. Records supplied in response to claim inquiries were created after the payer's ADR date, per document metadata.
324.features_to_create: 1) Impossible day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed billed minutes from timed CPT codes 90832, 90834 and 90837; fires when total exceeds 24 hours or the provider's licensed practice hours; action prepay edit. 2) Post-mortem service: on claim line, compute days between date of service and the beneficiary's Death Master File date; fires when date of service is after date of death; action claim suspension. 3) Single-evaluation conversion: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the ratio of ongoing psychotherapy sessions to documented evaluation encounters; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR) then postpay audit.

325.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, remote patient monitoring CPT 99453/99454/99457 claims concentrate in beneficiary cohorts sourced from one marketing vendor rather than one clinic. Enrolled beneficiaries lack any prior treating-relationship E/M claim with the billing NPI. Device supply claims post monthly with transmission-day counts exactly at the minimum threshold for payment. The billing entity's cost data show flat per-referral marketing payments rather than fair-market fixed fees, visible in vendor contracts requested at audit. Enrollment growth spikes align with marketing campaign start dates rather than diabetes diagnosis incidence.
325.features_to_create: 1) Referral-source concentration: on billing NPI x month, compute the share of new RPM beneficiaries with no prior E/M claim to that NPI; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Threshold clustering: on beneficiary x month, compute the count of device transmission days billed under 99454; fires when the distribution mass sits exactly at the minimum payable day count above the provider's trailing baseline; action prepay edit. 3) Marketer graph: on marketing vendor TIN, compute the count of distinct billing NPIs whose RPM volume rose after contract start; fires when that count exceeds one; action postpay audit.

326.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, HCPCS E0601/E0470 claims are billed with new-equipment modifier NU while serial numbers match FDA recall listings for returned devices. Supplier acquisition records show purchases from online resellers rather than a manufacturer or authorized distributor pedigree. Device serial numbers on claims repeat across multiple beneficiaries over time. The supplier's CMS-855S enrollment lists no reprocessing or refurbishment capability at the site inspected. Beneficiary complaint and repair claim rates for the supplier exceed same-specialty peer rates.
326.features_to_create: 1) Recall serial match: on claim line, compare the reported device serial or model against the FDA recall registry for that HCPCS; fires on an exact registry match billed with modifier NU; action prepay edit. 2) Serial reuse: on device serial number, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries paid over the device lifetime; fires when that count exceeds one; action claim suspension. 3) Pedigree gap: on supplier NPI x HCPCS, compute paid units minus units traceable to authorized distributor invoices; fires when paid units exceed documented acquisitions; action site visit and postpay audit.

327.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim and no adjudication point here, since the loss is diverted grant-funded commodities, not billed services. Detection sits with grant commodity accounting, comparing shipped HIV test kit lot numbers against recipient warehouse receipt records. The nearest control is verifying distributor Letters of Authority directly with the manufacturer before sole-source award.
327.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system is a lot-level reconciliation on donated-commodity shipment ID, computing shipped units minus units receipted at the designated national authority, with award suspension when the gap is nonzero.

328.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, CPT 98940-98943 claims post on dates the rendering NPI was verifiably absent, evidenced by no other local activity and incarceration or travel records. Daily treatment counts for the solo rendering NPI exceed feasible hours given the timed service definitions. Members recruited at events show identical visit-frequency templates with no varying diagnosis or plan-of-care progression. Records produced during an insurer audit were written in a single hand across many patients and dated retroactively. Patients report no service when the payer sends explanation-of-benefit verification letters.
328.features_to_create: 1) Provider-absent dates: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of billed encounters on dates matched to absence records such as incarceration or license-board and travel evidence; fires when count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 2) Daily capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total encounters divided by feasible working hours using per-CPT service time; fires when implied hours exceed 24 or licensed practice hours; action prepay edit. 3) Member verification: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the rate of member survey denials of service among sampled paid claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

329.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, chiropractic manipulation CPT codes are billed where the rendering staff on the encounter record are licensed massage therapists, per the state licence board file. Claims post on dates the rendering NPI was out of the country or incarcerated with no covering provider on file. Nearly every new member's first visit follows a free-service promotion with identical coding patterns and no documented subluxation level. Audit-response records show uniform handwriting and creation dates after the ADR letter date. The same beneficiaries show high visit counts without any interim re-evaluation CPT.
329.features_to_create: 1) Licence-scope mismatch: on claim line, compare the rendering individual's licence type in the state board file against the scope required by the billed CPT; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Absence-date billing: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of encounters billed on documented absence dates; fires when count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 3) Promotion cohort intensity: on rendering NPI x member cohort, compute mean paid visits per member within 90 days of first visit; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

330.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Schedule II NDC fills carry a prescriber NPI with no corresponding E/M claim for that beneficiary in the lookback window. The prescriber's written dates cluster in batches while the prescriber holds concurrent full-time employment claims elsewhere on the same dates. PDMP and ARCOS data show morphine milligram equivalents per prescriber far above same-specialty peers. Prescriptions written by a hired practitioner carry an identical signature image across many patients. Prescriber's clinic bills no office visits while pharmacy claims volume rises, visible in remittance history.
330.features_to_create: 1) Prescription without encounter: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute days between the Part D fill date and the nearest E/M claim by that prescriber; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber MME intensity: on prescriber NPI x month, compute total morphine milligram equivalents dispensed from NDC and days-supply fields; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Batch-signing pattern: on prescriber NPI x written date, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries with controlled-substance prescriptions written that day; fires when implied minutes per patient fall below feasible visit length in a 24-hour day; action payment suspension.

331.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, DMEPOS claims cite ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Ordering physicians disavow the certificates of medical necessity when the payer sends verification letters to the NPPES address of record. One supplier NPI concentrates orders from a narrow set of ordering NPIs recruited by a single marketer. Beneficiary complaint volume against the supplier exceeds same-specialty peer rates in the payer's grievance file. Supplier billing jumps from near-zero to top-decile within weeks of enrollment approval on the CMS-855S.
331.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer concentration: on supplier NPI x quarter, compute the share of paid DMEPOS lines attributable to the top few ordering NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Complaint-adjusted ramp: on supplier NPI x month, compute paid amount growth versus the supplier's trailing baseline combined with the count of beneficiary complaints; fires when growth exceeds baseline while complaints exceed peer rate; action payment suspension.

332.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, hereditary cancer panel CPT and 81479 claims cite an ordering NPI whose telehealth encounter duration is under the billed code's minimum minutes. Ordered diagnosis codes are anatomically impossible for the beneficiary's sex recorded in the eligibility file. One nurse practitioner NPI orders panels for beneficiaries across many states within days. Ordering NPI has no oncology or genetics specialty taxonomy in NPPES for the tests ordered. Beneficiary has no prior cancer diagnosis or family-history counseling claim before the panel order.
332.features_to_create: 1) Sex-diagnosis conflict: on claim line, compare the ordering diagnosis code against the beneficiary sex in the eligibility file; fires on exact edit mismatch such as cervical cancer for a male beneficiary; action prepay edit. 2) Encounter-duration floor: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute encounter minutes divided by the count of orders signed that day; fires when implied minutes per patient are below the billed code's minimum; action claim suspension. 3) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct laboratory NPIs on ordered genetic tests; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

333.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, L-code brace claims cite an ordering NPI with no prior E/M encounter with that beneficiary. One nurse practitioner NPI signs orders for beneficiaries in many states within a single week. Certifications state assessment occurred while no telehealth encounter claim exists for that date of service. The same beneficiary receives multiple brace HCPCS spanning unrelated joints within one month. Ordering NPI appears across several unrelated supplier NPIs sharing marketing contracts, visible in claim-level orderer-supplier pairings.
333.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M or telehealth claim linking that NPI to the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) Signer volume: on ordering NPI x day, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries with signed DMEPOS orders; fires when implied assessment minutes exceed 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Multi-joint saturation: on beneficiary x 30 days, compute the count of distinct brace HCPCS across unrelated body regions; fires when that count exceeds clinically plausible one-per-region limits; action prior-authorisation requirement.

334.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, E/M claims list the physician NPI as rendering while the practice's schedule and payroll show a nurse practitioner performed the visit. Physician rendering-NPI volume exceeds feasible daily encounters given the number of clinicians actually on site. Claims lack the incident-to conditions since no physician encounter for the same problem exists in the lookback. Physician is billing on dates with no on-site presence, unsupported by any concurrent supervision record. The practice bills almost no claims under its enrolled nurse practitioner NPIs despite their PECOS enrollment.
334.features_to_create: 1) Unused midlevel NPI: on TIN x quarter, compute the ratio of E/M lines billed under physician NPIs to the count of enrolled nurse practitioner NPIs with near-zero billing; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 2) Physician capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total E/M encounters times typical code service time; fires when implied hours exceed 24 or documented on-site hours; action prepay edit. 3) Incident-to precondition: on beneficiary x TIN, compute days since the last physician-performed encounter for the same problem; fires when no qualifying physician encounter exists in the lookback; action documentation request (ADR).

335.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, orthotic brace claims cite ordering NPIs having no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. A single marketer-linked set of ordering NPIs supplies most of the supplier's paid volume. A new supplier NPI enrolls with a nominee owner while sharing address, phone or bank account with a supplier already under review, per CMS-855S fields. Beneficiaries already have a paid same-HCPCS brace within the reasonable-useful-lifetime window. Medicare Advantage and fee-for-service claims duplicate the same device for the same beneficiary.
335.features_to_create: 1) Successor-entity link: on bank account or practice address, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs enrolled, including those with prior payment suspension; fires when that count exceeds one across enrollment records; action site visit and prepay edit. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim with the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 3) Lifetime duplication: on beneficiary x HCPCS, compute months since the last paid same-code device across FFS and Advantage claims; fires when within the reasonable useful lifetime; action claim suspension.

336.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the certifying medical director NPI's monthly stipend tracks the count of patients that director referred, visible in cost report and contract records. A small set of medical director NPIs certifies most admissions for the agency. Certifying physicians also appear as referring NPIs on the same beneficiaries' prior claims, creating a closed referral loop. Live-discharge and long-length-of-stay rates exceed same-specialty peer rates in hospice claim history. Ownership and contractor disclosures on the CMS-855A do not list all compensated medical directors.
336.features_to_create: 1) Referral-linked compensation: on medical director NPI x month, compute the correlation between stipend amount in contract records and the count of certified admissions; fires when payment varies with referral count; action postpay audit. 2) Certifier concentration: on hospice NPI x quarter, compute the share of admissions certified by compensated medical director NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Disclosure mismatch: on hospice TIN, compute the count of compensated physician NPIs absent from CMS-855A disclosure fields; fires when that count exceeds zero; action prepay edit.

337.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, hospice election claims cite certifying physician NPIs with no other claim relationship to the beneficiary or the agency. Beneficiaries under the hospice benefit continue receiving curative and Part D claims inconsistent with terminal certification. Newly enrolled agencies list owners whose identity documents mismatch SSA and NPPES records on the CMS-855A. Multiple agency NPIs share one bank account and mailing address in enrollment and remittance data. Certifying physicians deny signing when the payer sends verification to the NPPES address of record.
337.features_to_create: 1) Certifier-relationship void: on beneficiary x certifying NPI, compute the count of prior claims linking that physician to the beneficiary before the hospice election date; fires when the count is zero; action claim suspension. 2) Non-terminal utilization: on beneficiary x hospice period, compute the count of curative treatment and Part D claims during election; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus hospice peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Shared-account cluster: on bank account, compute the count of distinct provider NPIs receiving Medicare deposits; fires when that count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership; action payment suspension and site visit.

338.ways_to_identify: At enrollment, the CMS-855S ownership fields name a purchaser whose funding and control documents conflict with the seller's continuing signature authority on the bank account. Two supplier NPIs share address, phone and bank account across enrollment and remittance records. Billed DMEPOS lines cite ordering NPIs with no encounter or any order record at all. Beneficiaries deny receipt when the payer mails delivery verification against the claim's delivery date. Cash withdrawals in large round amounts follow Medicare deposits, visible in financial institution reporting.
338.features_to_create: 1) Nominee-owner test: on supplier NPI, compute the count of mismatches between CMS-855S owners and bank account signatories plus prior-owner continuity; fires when any exact mismatch exists; action site visit before enrollment approval. 2) Delivery verification failure: on supplier NPI x month, compute the rate of beneficiary-denied deliveries among sampled paid claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Ramp anomaly: on supplier NPI x week, compute paid amount versus the supplier's trailing baseline and same-specialty peer median; fires when growth exceeds both thresholds; action prepay edit.

339.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim and no adjudication point, since the controlled substance was sold direct-to-consumer across borders for cash. No NDC, prescriber NPI or pharmacy billing record enters any payer system. The nearest detection route is customs parcel screening and payment-processor monitoring of recurring foreign merchant transactions mislabeled as cosmetics.
339.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system is import-manifest and payment-processor screening on merchant account, computing counts of small international parcels declared as cosmetics from repeat shippers, with referral to DEA and CBP.

340.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the CMS-855I and NPPES taxonomy claim a physician or ARNP credential absent from the state licence board file. The NPI was issued with no matching state licence number verifiable in the primary-source licensure registry. E-prescribing traffic shows a Schedule III prescription whose prescriber NPI conflicts with the DEA registrant name on the transaction. The new NPI writes controlled-substance prescriptions with no associated E/M claim history in payer remittance data. Prescriber address on the pharmacy claim matches no PECOS practice location for that NPI.
340.features_to_create: 1) Licence-registry mismatch at enrolment: on provider NPI, compute an exact match test between NPPES taxonomy plus licence number and the state board file record; fires when no active licence record exists for that name and taxonomy; action prepay edit on all claims citing that NPI as prescriber. 2) Prescriber-DEA identity conflict: on claim line, compute whether the prescriber NPI, DEA registrant name and pharmacy-reported prescriber name agree exactly across NPPES, the DEA registration file and the NCPDP claim; fires on any mismatch for a scheduled drug; action claim suspension. 3) Zero-encounter prescriber: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of controlled-substance prescriptions dispensed to E/M claims billed by that NPI; fires when the denominator is zero or the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

341.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on cancer-panel CPT lines has no prior E/M claim with that beneficiary. One telemedicine ordering NPI signs genetic-test orders for beneficiaries across many distant states weekly. Beneficiary residence ZIPs on the claim sit far outside the laboratory's CLIA and CMS-855B service area. The same beneficiary receives duplicate hereditary-cancer panels from unrelated laboratory NPIs within months. Laboratory volume for these CPTs jumps from near-zero to peer-top-decile after a new marketing contract or PECOS ownership change.
341.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Telehealth orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the distinct count of beneficiary states and distinct laboratory NPIs on ordered genetic-test claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Panel duplication: on beneficiary x CPT family, compute the count of distinct laboratory NPIs paid within a rolling 180 days for hereditary-cancer panels; fires when that count exceeds one; action prepay edit.

342.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, ordering physicians who hold MSO investment interests show lab-order volume far above same-specialty peers. Ownership and contract disclosures on the laboratory's CMS-855B omit the marketer entities collecting percentage-of-reimbursement commissions. A small set of ordering NPIs supplies most of a distant out-of-state laboratory's referral volume. Ordered test panels repeat the identical CPT bundle across unrelated beneficiaries of one clinic TIN. OIG LEIE and prior settlement lists tie marketer principals to multiple laboratory NPIs at enrolment.
342.features_to_create: 1) Referral concentration graph: on laboratory NPI, compute the share of paid lab claims attributable to the top ordering NPIs plus each orderer's distance in miles to the lab; fires when concentration and distance are both above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action postpay audit. 2) Orderer-versus-peer intensity: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute lab CPT claims per distinct beneficiary with an E/M encounter; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement for those panels. 3) Ownership-disclosure mismatch: on TIN, compute the count of common principals or addresses shared between marketer/MSO entities and enrolled laboratory NPIs in CMS-855 ownership fields; fires when any undisclosed shared principal exists; action claim suspension pending enrolment revalidation.

343.ways_to_identify: In the hospital's automated dispensing cabinet log, one nurse's fentanyl and hydromorphone withdrawals exceed unit peers per shift. Cabinet withdrawal events lack matching administration entries or waste witnesses in the eMAR record. Pain scores and reassessment documentation are missing for patients recorded as receiving the diverted doses. Discrepancy and override counts for that employee ID rise above the nurse's own trailing baseline. Pharmacy inventory reconciliation shows unresolved variances on the units and shifts that nurse worked.
343.features_to_create: 1) Dispense-to-administer gap: on rendering nurse ID x shift, compute the count of controlled-substance cabinet withdrawals minus matched eMAR administrations plus witnessed wastes; fires when the unmatched count exceeds zero repeatedly above the employee's trailing baseline; action postpay audit of associated claims. 2) Peer-shift opioid intensity: on nurse ID x unit x shift, compute milligram morphine equivalents withdrawn per assigned patient; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-unit peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Override rate: on nurse ID x week, compute cabinet override withdrawals divided by total withdrawals; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action site visit by pharmacy compliance.

344.ways_to_identify: Charge lines for fentanyl, hydromorphone and morphine post without corresponding eMAR administration timestamps in the patient record. One emergency-department nurse ID accounts for cabinet withdrawals per patient above same-unit peers. Billed drug units exceed dispensing-cabinet withdrawal quantities reconciled to the same encounter. Waste documentation lacks a second-witness signature on a large share of that nurse's controlled-substance events. The same nurse appears on diversion-relevant discrepancy logs at two facilities sharing the payer's remittance history.
344.features_to_create: 1) Billed-versus-administered reconciliation: on claim line x encounter, compute billed controlled-substance units minus eMAR-documented administered units; fires when the difference is greater than zero; action prepay edit. 2) Unwitnessed waste rate: on nurse ID x week, compute controlled-substance waste events without a second witness divided by total waste events; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-unit peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Cross-facility diversion linkage: on employee identity x quarter, compute the distinct count of facilities with unmatched withdrawal events for that person; fires when that count exceeds one; action postpay audit of drug charges.

345.ways_to_identify: In PDMP data, essentially every patient of one prescriber NPI receives a Schedule II opioid at each visit. Pharmacy claims show beneficiaries travelling hundreds of miles between home ZIP and the prescriber's PECOS practice address. Prescribed morphine milligram equivalents per patient per day exceed same-specialty peer distributions in dispensing records. The practice bills no insurer, so opioid volume appears only in PDMP and ARCOS pharmacy-level dispensing data. Multiple patients of that prescriber share identical drug, dose and quantity combinations on the same dates.
345.features_to_create: 1) Universal-opioid prescribing rate: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute distinct patients receiving a Schedule II opioid divided by distinct patients in PDMP records; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement for opioid fills from that prescriber. 2) Patient travel radius: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the median miles between patient residence ZIP and the prescriber practice ZIP on dispensed controlled-substance prescriptions; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit plus referral to the licence board. 3) MME intensity: on prescriber NPI x patient, compute average daily morphine milligram equivalents dispensed; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit on pharmacy claims.

346.ways_to_identify: E-prescribing enrolment records show a new account for an existing prescriber NPI opened from an unrecognised device and address. Pharmacy claims list a prescriber DEA number whose dispensing pattern jumps far above that prescriber's trailing baseline within days. Oxycodone and promethazine-with-codeine fills cluster at pharmacies far from the prescriber's NPPES practice location. Contact phone number on the prescriber account changed shortly before the surge, per credentialing and identity-verification logs. The same beneficiary identifiers appear at many unrelated pharmacy NPIs within a short window in dispensing history.
346.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber baseline break: on prescriber DEA/NPI x week, compute controlled-substance prescription counts versus that prescriber's trailing 26-week mean; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile of within-prescriber change; action claim suspension pending prescriber confirmation. 2) Geographic dispersion of fills: on prescriber NPI x week, compute the distinct count of pharmacy NPIs and states dispensing that prescriber's controlled-substance scripts; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 3) Credential-change velocity: on prescriber e-prescribing account, compute days between a change to phone number, address or device fingerprint and the next controlled-substance transmission; fires when that gap is short and volume exceeds baseline; action claim suspension.

347.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one community-support worker's billed service minutes per date of service exceed twenty-four hours. Encounter notes are submitted with identical narrative text across many beneficiaries and dates in the provider record. Billed units per beneficiary per month exceed the authorised amount on the Medicaid prior-authorisation record. Service dates fall on days the worker was not scheduled per agency timesheets and payroll files. Beneficiaries show no other claims or contact activity on the dates community support was billed.
347.features_to_create: 1) Impossible service day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed community-support units converted to minutes plus travel time; fires when total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Authorisation overrun: on beneficiary x rendering NPI x month, compute billed units minus units authorised on the prior-authorisation record; fires when the difference is above zero; action claim suspension. 3) Note-template duplication: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of encounter notes with text similarity above the calibrated duplicate threshold across distinct beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer workers; action documentation request (ADR) then postpay audit.

348.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, private duty nursing claim hours have no matching EVV clock-in and clock-out visit record. Aggregate billed hours per employee per day across beneficiaries exceed twenty-four hours in payroll-linked claim data. Nursing notes carry guardian signatures dated identically across many blank pre-signed forms in the medical record. Payments from the agency's bank account to beneficiary guardians appear alongside claims for those beneficiaries. Billed personal care and respite hours exceed the plan-of-care hours on the Medicaid service authorisation.
348.features_to_create: 1) EVV-to-claim reconciliation: on claim line, compute billed hours minus EVV-verified visit minutes for the same beneficiary, worker and date; fires when billed hours exceed verified minutes; action prepay edit. 2) Worker day impossibility: on rendering staff ID x date of service, compute summed billed hours across all beneficiaries; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Authorisation overrun: on beneficiary x agency NPI x month, compute billed private duty nursing, personal care and respite hours minus authorised plan-of-care hours; fires when positive; action documentation request (ADR) then postpay audit.

349.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one certifying physician NPI signs genetic-test orders for beneficiaries with whom she has no E/M claim. The signing NPI's ordered-test volume is far above same-specialty peers per week in claim data. Beneficiary residence states on ordered tests span the country while the physician has one PECOS practice location. Order signatures show identical timestamps in batches inconsistent with individual patient consultations in the laboratory requisition file. Multiple unrelated laboratory NPIs bill Medicare on orders bearing the same physician NPI within the same period.
349.features_to_create: 1) Certification without encounter: on ordering NPI x beneficiary, compute the count of E/M claims between them in the lookback window before the order date; fires when zero; action prepay edit on the laboratory claim. 2) Signature throughput: on ordering NPI x day, compute the count of distinct genetic-test orders signed divided by available clinical hours; fires when implied minutes per order fall below a physically plausible consultation time; action payment suspension. 3) Orderer-to-lab fan-out: on ordering NPI x month, compute the distinct count of billing laboratory NPIs and beneficiary states on ordered genetic tests; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

350.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim and no adjudication point, since the injections were cash-pay at an unenrolled med spa. The nearest detection route is the state licence board and medical spa registration file showing no prescriber licence at the business address. Wholesaler and import pedigree data show no lawful distribution of an FDA-approved botulinum toxin NDC to that facility. Public health botulism case reports linked to a single business address are the practical downstream signal.
350.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest outside control: on facility address, compare state licence board prescriber records and DSCSA wholesaler pedigree shipments of botulinum toxin NDCs; fires when injections are advertised at an address with no licensed prescriber and no lawful product pedigree; action state board site visit and FDA import referral.

351.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, sterilisation claims lack a Medicaid consent form dated at least thirty days before the procedure date.
