One operating surgeon's hysterectomy rate per thousand attributed patients exceeds same-specialty peers at that facility. Elective induction claims carry gestational-age diagnosis codes below thirty-nine weeks without a documented medical indication. Preoperative pathology and imaging claims supporting the surgical indication are absent from the beneficiary's claim history. A single surgeon NPI accounts for an outsized share of the facility's inpatient gynaecologic surgical revenue.
351.features_to_create: 1) Consent-form timing: on claim line for sterilisation procedures, compute days between the signed consent date and the date of service; fires when fewer than thirty days or no consent record exists; action prepay edit. 2) Surgeon procedure-rate outlier: on rendering NPI x facility x quarter, compute hysterectomies and other irreversible procedures per hundred attributed patients; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Indication support gap: on beneficiary x surgical claim, compute the count of supporting pathology, imaging or E/M claims in the preceding lookback window; fires when zero; action documentation request (ADR) then postpay audit of facility claims.

352.ways_to_identify: Wholesaler and ARCOS pedigree data show controlled-substance orders shipped to a practice address under a licensee who never placed them. TMS therapy claims list a rendering identity with no active nurse or medical assistant credential in the state licence board file. The same person appears as beneficiary on opioid and pain-pump claims while acting as biller for the ordering practice. Prescriptions self-directed to a practice employee show prescriber and patient sharing an address in NPPES and eligibility records. Ordering volume for opioid NDCs at that practice exceeds its own trailing baseline without matching patient census growth.
352.features_to_create: 1) Ordered-versus-dispensed drug reconciliation: on practice DEA registrant x month, compute wholesaler-shipped controlled-substance units minus units dispensed or administered on claims; fires when the unexplained surplus is above zero; action site visit. 2) Rendering-credential registry check: on claim line, compute an exact match of the rendering identity against the state licence board file for the credential required by the billed TMS CPT; fires on no active credential; action prepay edit. 3) Self-dealing overlap: on beneficiary identity, compute whether the same person appears as employee, biller or owner in the ordering practice's CMS-855 or payroll records; fires on any exact identity match with paid claims; action claim suspension and postpay audit.

353.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, claims are submitted under a physician NPI naming the billing agent himself as the beneficiary. Billed E/M level distribution for the practice shifts to higher levels above the practice's own trailing baseline. Service dates fall on days the rendering physician had no other facility or office activity in claim history. The billing agent's TIN and pay-to bank account appear across multiple unrelated practice NPIs on remittance records. Claim volume per rendering NPI per day exceeds physically plausible encounter counts given billed time-based codes.
353.features_to_create: 1) Biller-as-patient overlap: on claim line, compute an identity match between the beneficiary and any principal listed in the billing agent's TIN or the practice's CMS-855 contact fields; fires on exact match; action claim suspension. 2) Level-of-service drift: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of E/M claims at the two highest levels versus the provider's own trailing baseline and same-specialty peers; fires when above the calibrated percentile; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Rendering-day capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed typical minutes for all billed time-based codes; fires when total exceeds a physically plausible workday; action prepay edit.

354.ways_to_identify: In claim history, revision knee arthroplasty CPT codes cluster on beneficiaries whose implant model appears in device identifier fields. UDI device identifiers on implant claims map to catalogue numbers named in FDA recall and MAUDE adverse-event data. Time from index implant to revision for one manufacturer's device is shorter than for peer devices in longitudinal claims. Hospital-supplied implant charge lines continue after the manufacturer's own complaint files show elevated failure rates. Warranty and credit records show no manufacturer credit applied to the payer for premature device replacement.
354.features_to_create: 1) Device survival outlier: on device identifier (UDI) x manufacturer, compute the median days from index implant claim to revision arthroplasty claim across beneficiaries; fires when materially below the same-procedure peer-device distribution; action postpay audit and False Claims Act referral. 2) Recall-registry match: on claim line, compute an exact match between the billed UDI or catalogue number and the FDA recall and safety-communication file; fires on any match after the recall effective date; action prepay edit. 3) Replacement credit reconciliation: on beneficiary x revision claim, compute the manufacturer credit amount posted against the implant charge; fires when the credit is zero for a device replaced inside its expected service life; action claim suspension.

355.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, anorectal manometry and biofeedback claims post without a matching billed single-use catheter or sensor supply line. Supply purchase volume from the manufacturer is far below the number of procedures billed by the same practice NPI. Procedures per catheter purchased exceed one, contradicting the FDA single-use labelling in the device 510(k) record. Manufacturer shipment and distributor pedigree data show declining probe orders while provider procedure volume rises. Practices trained by that manufacturer share the same anomalous supply-to-procedure ratio in remittance history.
355.features_to_create: 1) Single-use supply reconciliation: on billing NPI x quarter, compute billed anorectal manometry and pelvic rehabilitation procedures divided by documented single-use catheter or sensor purchases from distributor records; fires when the ratio exceeds one per procedure; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Missing supply line: on claim line, compute whether the required single-use device HCPCS or supply charge appears on the same date of service for that beneficiary; fires when absent; action prepay edit. 3) Manufacturer-cluster ratio: on manufacturer customer list x provider NPI, compute the distinct count of NPIs with supply-to-procedure ratios above the calibrated percentile versus peers; fires when the cluster exceeds peer expectation; action postpay audit.

356.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, orthotic L-code claims have no prior E/M encounter between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary. Ordering physicians deny signing when contacted, and their NPIs show no other DMEPOS ordering in claim history. One supplier's beneficiaries span states far outside the service area on its CMS-855S enrolment. The same beneficiary receives back, knee and shoulder braces on identical dates from one supplier NPI. Multiple supplier NPIs share an owner, address or bank account in CMS-855S ownership and remittance fields.
356.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that orderer and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Multi-brace same-day bundle: on beneficiary x supplier NPI x date of service, compute the distinct count of orthotic L-code body regions billed; fires when the count exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peer suppliers; action claim suspension. 3) Common-control supplier cluster: on bank account and owner identity, compute the distinct count of enrolled supplier NPIs sharing it in CMS-855S; fires when greater than one with correlated billing spikes; action payment suspension and site visit.

357.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, DMEPOS claims carry ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Beneficiary attestation and delivery-proof documents are absent or template-identical across the supplier's claims. The supplier's paid volume rises from near-zero to peer-top-decile within weeks of enrolment. Two supplier NPIs share an owner, address or pay-to bank account in CMS-855S ownership fields. Payments to that bank account are swept out in large transfers immediately after remittance posting.
357.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the most recent E/M claim between orderer and beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) New-supplier ramp: on supplier NPI x week, compute paid dollars versus the supplier's own trailing baseline since enrolment; fires when growth is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension pending site visit. 3) Shared bank account degree: on bank account, compute the distinct count of supplier NPIs receiving remittance plus days from deposit to outbound transfer; fires when multiple NPIs share the account with rapid sweep-out; action claim suspension.

358.ways_to_identify: There is no health-care claim and no adjudication point, because the money came from an SBA loan programme, not billing. The nearest detection route compares the employee count and payroll certified on the PPP application against IRS Form 941 filings and state wage records. A second route compares the applicant's certified payroll against the payroll implied by its Medicare cost report or credentialed staff roster. Forgiveness applications listing far fewer employees than the loan application are checkable within SBA's own file.
358.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest outside control: on borrower EIN, compute certified PPP payroll and headcount minus IRS Form 941 reported wages and employee counts for the same quarters; fires when the certified figure exceeds filed wages; action forgiveness denial and SBA Office of Inspector General referral.

359.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, screening breast MRI CPT claims cluster at practices using one risk-calculator software version. Ordered breast MRI rates per thousand screened women exceed same-specialty peers for those ordering NPIs. Documented lifetime risk scores in prior-authorisation records exceed scores recomputed from the same patient inputs. Beneficiaries lack genetic-mutation or high-risk diagnosis codes that normally accompany supplemental MRI in claim history. The elevated ordering pattern starts sharply at a software installation date recorded in vendor deployment files.
359.features_to_create: 1) Risk-score recomputation: on prior-authorisation record, compute the difference between the submitted lifetime risk score and the score recomputed from the submitted Tyrer-Cuzick inputs; fires when the difference exceeds tolerance; action prepay edit. 2) MRI ordering rate: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute supplemental breast MRI orders divided by screening mammograms for the same panel; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Indication support: on beneficiary x MRI claim, compute the count of high-risk diagnosis or genetic-mutation codes in the preceding claim history; fires when zero and risk score is the sole justification; action documentation request (ADR).

360.ways_to_identify: At encounter data validation, compute the share of a group's members carrying M46.0 spinal enthesopathy or M46.1 sacroiliitis diagnoses versus same-region peers. Check whether each risk-adjusting diagnosis has any corresponding treatment, imaging or referral claim in the member's other claims history. Look for enthesopathy and sacroiliitis codes appearing only on addenda or chart-review submissions with no linked professional encounter claim. Compare radiology report dates in the imaging supplier's records against the date the MA plan queried the diagnosis, indicating back-dated reports. Track members whose HCC risk score jumps on capitation renewal without any new utilization in the payer's remittance history.
360.features_to_create: 1) Orphan HCC diagnosis rate: on rendering NPI x diagnosis code, compute the fraction of members with M46.0 or M46.1 having no follow-on treatment, imaging or specialist claim within the year; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit of encounter data. 2) Chart-review-only additions: on provider group TIN x member, compute the count of risk-adjusting diagnoses submitted solely through supplemental chart review with no matching encounter claim line; fires when above the group's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Retro report creation: on imaging NPI x member, compute the gap in days between date of service and report authorship timestamp in the submitted record; fires when the gap exceeds the report-signature window in the plan's credentialing policy; action claim suspension.

361.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare monthly capitation ESRD MCP codes 90957-90962 against the dialysis facility's own treatment records for the same beneficiary dates. Compute daily face-to-face visit counts per rendering NPI across all dialysis facilities billed that day. Compare travel distance between dialysis facility addresses billed by one physician on one date of service. Check whether the physician's MCP claims continue during periods the beneficiary shows inpatient or hospice claims elsewhere. Compare the ratio of billed visits per ESRD patient month against same-specialty nephrology peers in remittance history.
361.features_to_create: 1) Physician-day dialysis visit load: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct ESRD beneficiaries with face-to-face visit codes multiplied by minimum visit minutes; fires when the product exceeds 24 hours in a day; action prepay edit. 2) Facility cross-check: on beneficiary x month, compute the count of MCP visit tiers billed versus dialysis facility 72x claims documenting physician presence; fires when the billed tier exceeds documented visits; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Site dispersion: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct dialysis facility service addresses billed; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus nephrology peers; action postpay audit.

362.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, sum billed custodial care hours per beneficiary per calendar day across all claim lines from the agency. Compare billed hours against EVV clock-in and clock-out records and caregiver timesheets for the same dates. Compute per-caregiver daily hours across all beneficiaries served by the agency NPI. Check whether authorized hours on the plan's prior-authorization record match units billed per date of service. Compare the agency's payroll totals against total billed service hours for the same period.
362.features_to_create: 1) Round-the-clock billing: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the sum of custodial care units converted to hours across all claim lines; fires when the sum exceeds authorized hours on the prior-authorization record or exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) EVV-to-claim variance: on beneficiary x supplier NPI x week, compute billed hours minus EVV-verified visit minutes; fires when the variance exceeds zero for any day; action claim suspension. 3) Payroll coverage ratio: on provider NPI x month, compute total billed care hours divided by paid caregiver hours from payroll records; fires when the ratio is above one; action postpay audit.

363.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, match accreditation inspector identity against the CMS-855S owner, officer and managing-employee names for surname and address overlap. Compare the inspector's inspection date log against site-visit travel feasibility, counting distinct site addresses inspected per day. Check newly accredited supplier NPIs whose PECOS ownership changes hands within months of accreditation. Compare the enrolment address against other supplier NPIs sharing the same suite, phone and bank account. Compare time from accreditation application to award against the accreditor's own trailing baseline for that inspector.
363.features_to_create: 1) Inspector-owner kinship overlap: on supplier NPI, compute the count of exact matches between accrediting inspector name or address and CMS-855S owner, officer and managing-employee fields; fires when any exact registry match exists; action site visit before enrolment approval. 2) Inspection throughput: on inspector ID x date, compute the count of distinct supplier site addresses accredited; fires when count multiplied by minimum inspection duration exceeds an eight-hour workday; action claim suspension for suppliers in that batch. 3) Flip-after-accreditation: on supplier NPI, compute the gap in days between accreditation date and first PECOS ownership change; fires when the gap is below the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prior-authorisation requirement on all billing.

364.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count orthotic brace orders signed per ordering NPI per day against the number of billable telehealth minutes that NPI billed. Check whether any E/M or telehealth claim exists between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary before the L-code date of service. Compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs served by one ordering physician per week. Compare the ordering physician's state licence file against the beneficiary's state of residence in the eligibility record. Count distinct L-code braces per beneficiary within a rolling month across unrelated supplier NPIs.
364.features_to_create: 1) Signature throughput: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct DMEPOS orders signed divided by documented encounter minutes; fires when implied consult time per order falls below the minimum for a physical impossibility of 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the most recent E/M or telehealth claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action claim suspension. 3) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct billing supplier NPIs on ordered L-code claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

365.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare NDC-level dispensed quantities against wholesaler acquisition pedigree and ARCOS purchase data for the same pharmacy NPI. Compute the ratio of billed units of high-cost anticoagulants and inhalers to total prescription volume versus same-size pharmacy peers. Check whether the prescribing NPI on each claim has any office-visit claim with that beneficiary in the relevant period. Look for beneficiaries with no refill-adherence pattern yet continuous costly fills in remittance history. Compare pharmacy purchase invoices submitted at revalidation against total billed dispense quantity per NDC.
365.features_to_create: 1) Inventory reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed dispensed units minus wholesaler-documented acquired units; fires when billed exceeds acquired; action payment suspension. 2) High-cost NDC concentration: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of paid dollars from top-decile-cost NDCs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-region pharmacy peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Prescriber linkage: on claim line, compute days between fill date and nearest E/M claim between prescriber NPI and beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists within the lookback window; action prepay edit.

366.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare pharmacy adjudicated claims against point-of-sale pickup records to find scripts billed but never removed from will-call inventory and never reversed. Count opioid claims per prescriber NPI cross-referenced with manufacturer Open Payments speaker-fee records for the same drug. Compute monthly E/M visit levels per assisted-living facility resident per rendering NPI versus peer distributions. Check genomic test claims for an ordering NPI with no prior treating relationship in the beneficiary's claim history. Match hospital claim lines against ClinicalTrials.gov trial numbers and sponsor-funded item lists in the Medicare Advantage secondary payer file.
366.features_to_create: 1) Unclaimed prescription reversal: on pharmacy NPI x claim line, compute days between adjudication date and dispensing pickup timestamp; fires when no pickup is recorded past the return-to-stock window without a reversal; action prepay edit and postpay audit. 2) Speaker-payment-linked prescribing: on prescriber NPI x drug NDC, compute paid claim volume divided by trailing baseline, joined to Open Payments speaker fees from that manufacturer; fires when both volume and payments exceed the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Facility visit intensity: on rendering NPI x facility x month, compute visits per resident and the share coded at the two highest E/M levels; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers serving assisted living; action postpay audit.

367.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point in this investment scheme. Detection sits with bank anti-money-laundering monitoring of corporate accounts receiving pooled foreign investor wires. Securities regulators can match the entity against broker-dealer and commodity-trading registrations for unregistered offerings. Altered bank statements shown to investors are detectable by direct confirmation with the depository institution.
367.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: bank transaction monitoring on the business account, computing the count of inbound international wires from unrelated individuals followed by same-week transfers to the owner's personal account and mortgage servicer, escalated as a SAR.

368.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this commodity investment fraud. The nearest detection route is bank AML review of a trading company account funded by dozens of small foreign investor wires. Registration checks against commodity-broker and state securities registries would show no authority to solicit these investments.
368.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: on business bank account x month, compute the count of distinct inbound remitters and the ratio of funds transferred to the owner's personal account, escalating to a SAR when personal transfers dominate deposits.

369.ways_to_identify: At enrolment and credentialing, match the rendering provider name against the state BCBA licence board file and OIG LEIE for exclusion or absence of licensure. Compare billed ABA technician units against the agency's payroll records for any paid employee on those dates of service. Check for BCBA supervision code 97155 billed on dates with no corresponding 97153 technician code for the same beneficiary. Cross-check ABA dates of service against the beneficiary's inpatient hospital claims for overlapping days. Compare enrolled owner and officer names on the Medicaid provider agreement against prior state fraud convictions and pseudonym aliases.
369.features_to_create: 1) Licence and exclusion match: on rendering NPI x claim line, compute exact-match status against the state behavior-analyst licence file and OIG LEIE on the date of service; fires on any registry mismatch or exclusion hit; action prepay edit. 2) Supervision without service: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of 97155 supervision units where the count of 97153 technician units is zero; fires when greater than zero; action claim suspension. 3) Inpatient overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between billed outpatient ABA units and any inpatient facility stay span; fires when overlap exceeds zero; action prepay edit.

370.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, compare the supplier's CMS-855S practice location against shared virtual-office addresses used by other supplier NPIs. At adjudication, measure the distance between beneficiary residence ZIPs and the supplier's stated service area for nationwide orthotic billing. Check whether each L-code claim has an ordering NPI with any prior encounter claim for that beneficiary. Compare the supplier's payment bank account against outbound international wire activity flagged in the plan's vendor banking file. Compute time from first enrolment approval to peak billing volume against same-specialty supplier baselines.
370.features_to_create: 1) New-supplier velocity: on supplier NPI x week, compute paid orthotic claim dollars divided by weeks since PECOS enrolment approval; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus newly enrolled DMEPOS peers; action payment suspension pending site visit. 2) Geographic dispersion: on supplier NPI x month, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and mean beneficiary-to-supplier distance; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit. 3) Address and account sharing: on supplier NPI, compute the count of other supplier NPIs sharing the same 855S location, phone or payee bank account; fires when count exceeds zero without disclosed common ownership; action site visit.

371.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim adjudication point; this is contract procurement bribery on a federal services contract. Detection sits with contracting-officer conflict screening comparing vendor payment ledgers against government employee financial disclosure filings. Contract award pattern analysis can show one contracting official repeatedly steering awards or modifications to a single vendor.
371.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: on contracting official x vendor, compute the count and dollar share of awards and modifications approved plus any match between vendor disbursement payees and the official's OGE-278 disclosed income sources, referred to the Inspector General when a match exists.

372.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, run NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits on neurofeedback claim lines for mutually exclusive code pairs billed on the same date of service. Compute total timed-code minutes billed per rendering NPI per day from time-based CPT units. Compare the practice's code mix against same-specialty peers for use of codes inapplicable to neurofeedback. Check whether billing behavior changed after prior payer audit findings recorded in the payer's remittance and overpayment history. Compare billed service duration units against session logs and appointment schedules in requested documentation.
372.features_to_create: 1) Mutually exclusive pairing: on claim line pair per beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of NCCI PTP-conflicting neurofeedback code combinations without a valid modifier; fires when count exceeds zero; action prepay edit. 2) Timed-unit day load: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of time-based CPT units multiplied by their defined minutes; fires when the total exceeds a 24-hour day or the clinic's staffed hours; action claim suspension. 3) Post-audit persistence: on provider TIN x month, compute the rate of previously denied or audited code combinations resubmitted after the audit notice date; fires when the rate exceeds zero above the provider's own trailing baseline; action payment suspension.

373.ways_to_identify: There is generally no payer claim here because franchise buyers and cash patients, not insurers, funded the scheme. If clinics did bill, look for unlisted or miscellaneous electrical stimulation HCPCS codes tied to Alzheimer's and autism diagnoses lacking FDA-cleared indications. Device labels with removed manufacturer serial numbers are detectable through FDA UDI registry lookup at supplier accreditation. Franchise marketing claiming a 95 percent cure rate is actionable through FTC and state consumer-protection complaint records.
373.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: on supplier NPI x HCPCS, compute the count of claims for electrical stimulation devices whose UDI or serial number fails to match an FDA-registered manufacturer record, denying at prepay edit and referring to FDA.

374.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, compare CMS-855S owner, officer and managing-employee fields across supplier NPIs for shared addresses, phones and payee bank accounts revealing common control by straw owners. At adjudication, check whether the ordering NPI on each L-code claim has any prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs billing braces for the same beneficiary within a rolling month. Compare a single ordering NPI's order volume and beneficiary state dispersion against same-specialty peers. Compare each supplier's brace claim volume against the number of documented beneficiary contacts in submitted records.
374.features_to_create: 1) Common-control graph: on payee bank account and 855S address, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs sharing that node in PECOS; fires when count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership; action prior-authorisation requirement across the linked NPIs. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the nearest E/M claim between that NPI and beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 3) Beneficiary brace saturation: on beneficiary x L-code, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs paid within rolling 30 days; fires when count exceeds one without a documented replacement reason; action claim suspension.

375.ways_to_identify: There is a payer, but the fraud sits in eligibility determination rather than in a provider claim, so no adjudication edit catches it. The decisive check is at application and renewal: match self-reported household income against state wage-reporting and Department of Revenue business income files. Business ownership filings with the Secretary of State identify applicants who are officers of retail businesses while reporting minimal earnings. Federal data hub and IRS income verification at renewal would surface the same discrepancy.
375.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: on Medicaid applicant household, compute reported earned income minus wage and business income reported to the state revenue and Secretary of State files, referring for eligibility redetermination when the difference exceeds the program's reasonable-compatibility threshold.

376.ways_to_identify: At credentialing, verify the rendering provider's degree and BCBA certification directly against the BACB registry and state licence board file rather than the employer's attestation. At adjudication, sum all timed ABA units billed under one rendering NPI per date of service across beneficiaries. Compare the assessment and treatment-plan CPT codes billed against the credential level required by the state Medicaid provider manual. Check whether the rendering NPI in NPPES has a taxonomy authorizing behavior analysis services. Compare billed service hours against the employer's payroll and contractor timesheets for the same dates.
376.features_to_create: 1) Credential-to-code match: on claim line x rendering NPI, compute exact-match status between the provider's registry-verified credential and the credential required for the billed ABA CPT; fires on any registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Impossible day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of timed ABA units multiplied by their defined minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Payroll coverage: on provider NPI x pay period, compute billed service hours divided by paid staff hours in payroll records; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action postpay audit.

377.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check whether the ordering NPI on each cancer or cardiovascular panel CPT has any prior treating encounter with the beneficiary in claims history. Compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and lab NPIs served per telemedicine ordering NPI per week. Compare a lab's billed panel volume to its CLIA certificate scope and staffing declared at enrolment. Track abrupt shifts of the same ordering NPIs' volume from one lab NPI to a sibling lab NPI after audit contact. Match CMS-855B owner names against family surnames, shared addresses and payee bank accounts across the affiliated labs.
377.features_to_create: 1) Orderer-beneficiary relationship: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no treating encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit on genomic CPTs. 2) Lab-hopping continuity: on ordering NPI x month, compute the count of distinct billing lab NPIs and the share of volume migrating after a prior audit or denial event; fires when migration exceeds the ordering NPI's trailing baseline; action payment suspension across linked labs. 3) Ownership graph: on payee bank account x 855B address, compute the count of distinct lab NPIs and undisclosed common owners; fires when any exact registry mismatch with disclosed ownership exists; action site visit and prior-authorisation requirement.

378.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, verify whether the ordering NPI on each genomic panel claim has any prior encounter claim with that beneficiary. Count distinct beneficiaries and states per telemedicine ordering NPI per week on lab orders. Compare paid dollars per beneficiary for cancer and cardiovascular panels against same-specialty lab peers. Compare CMS-855B disclosed owners against family-member names, shared addresses and payee accounts across affiliated lab NPIs. Detect the same ordering physicians' volume shifting between sibling lab NPIs after denials appear in remittance history.
378.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the nearest treating E/M claim with the beneficiary; fires when none exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Telemarketed orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct billing lab NPIs on genomic CPT orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Sibling-lab migration: on lab NPI cluster keyed by shared bank account, compute the ratio of billing volume transferred between NPIs within 90 days of a payer audit or denial spike; fires when the ratio exceeds the cluster's trailing baseline; action payment suspension.

379.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, confirm each genomic test claim has an ordering NPI with a documented prior treating relationship in the beneficiary's claims. Compute per-ordering-NPI weekly counts of distinct beneficiaries against feasible consultation minutes. Compare CMS-855B ownership disclosures against relatives' names, shared addresses and shared payee bank accounts among affiliated labs. Compute the share of a lab's beneficiaries with no oncology or cardiology diagnosis history supporting the panel billed. Compare marketer payments in submitted contracts against per-test volume to detect volume-based compensation.
379.features_to_create: 1) Treating-relationship edit: on claim line, compute the gap in days between panel date of service and the nearest E/M claim linking ordering NPI and beneficiary; fires when no such claim exists; action prepay edit. 2) Ordering throughput: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiaries with signed genomic orders divided by billed consult minutes; fires when implied per-patient time is physically impossible within a 24-hour day; action claim suspension. 3) Hidden ownership match: on lab NPI, compute exact-match count between 855B owner fields and the payee bank account signatories or relatives listed on affiliated NPIs; fires on any registry mismatch; action site visit and payment suspension.

380.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim here and no adjudication point, so no payer edit could have stopped it. The nearest detection route is SBA loan-application screening comparing listed owners against felony-disclosure answers and state corporate registry officers. A second route is matching certified payroll headcount on the forgiveness application to IRS Form 941 and state unemployment wage filings. Bank monitoring of loan-account outflows to owner draws and a new unrelated trucking entity is the third route.
380.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Forgiveness payroll reconciliation: on borrower EIN, compute the difference between certified payroll spend and quarterly Form 941 wages plus state UI wage records; fires when certified spend exceeds reported wages; action postpay audit.

381.ways_to_identify: This is an individual income tax matter with no claim submitted to any health payer and no adjudication point. The nearest detection route is IRS return matching of reported income against Forms 1099 and payer remittance totals paid to the practice TIN. A second route is comparing the practice's deposited receipts in bank records to gross receipts reported on Schedule C.
381.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payer-to-return income match: on provider TIN x tax year, compute the gap between total remittances issued and income reported on the filed return; fires when the reported figure is below remittances issued; action postpay audit.

382.ways_to_identify: No health care claim exists, so no prepay adjudication control could apply to this loan forgiveness. The nearest detection route is SBA eligibility screening of the applicant's ownership field against foreign-government and affiliate ownership disclosures. A second route is affiliation-rule headcount testing using consolidated Form 941 employee counts across all commonly owned entities. Corporate registry and parent-company filings identify the sovereign owner at application, before disbursement.
382.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Sovereign and affiliate ownership screen: on borrower EIN, compute the count of disclosed owners matching foreign-government entities and the summed affiliate headcount from Form 941; fires when foreign-government ownership exists or headcount exceeds the program size standard; action prepay edit.

383.ways_to_identify: At pharmacy adjudication, one beneficiary fills high-strength oxycodone NDCs from multiple prescriber NPIs within overlapping days-supply windows. The state PDMP shows the same patient dispensed by several pharmacies with no gap between fills. Claim history shows no imaging, procedure, or chronic pain diagnosis supporting the billed high morphine-milligram-equivalent NDCs. Prescription fills are consistently paid cash at some pharmacies and billed at others, visible in switch and PDMP records. Distance between the beneficiary residence ZIP and the dispensing pharmacy ZIP far exceeds the plan network norm.
383.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber shopping: on beneficiary x rolling 30 days, compute the distinct count of prescriber NPIs and pharmacy NPIs on Schedule II opioid NDC fills; fires when both counts exceed the calibrated percentile versus plan peers; action prepay edit. 2) MME overlap: on beneficiary x date, compute total morphine milligram equivalents from all overlapping days-supply opioid claims; fires when daily MME exceeds the plan's calibrated high-dose threshold; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Prescriber diversion profile: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of that NPI's dispensed prescriptions that are Schedule II opioids at maximum strength; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

384.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, beneficiary attendance days per week at one SUD facility NPI cluster tightly at the maximum billable frequency across many unrelated patients. Definitive drug-testing claims from a single lab NPI accompany nearly every treatment day for the same referring facility NPI. Group session claims imply staff rendering NPI hours per date of service exceeding twenty-four hours. Ordering NPIs on brace and compression-device HCPCS have no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary in claim history. The same beneficiary receives duplicate L-code braces from several supplier NPIs within a rolling month.
384.features_to_create: 1) Attendance ceiling clustering: on facility NPI x beneficiary x week, compute the count of billed service days and the share of the facility's beneficiaries at the maximum billable days; fires when that share is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Lab-to-treatment coupling: on referring facility NPI x lab NPI x month, compute the ratio of definitive toxicology claim lines to treatment days and the share of the lab's volume from that one referrer; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action payment suspension. 3) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit.

385.ways_to_identify: No health care claim was submitted and there is no adjudication point in this payroll-tax and workers-compensation scheme. The nearest detection route is FinCEN currency transaction reports from the check casher matched to the contractor EIN's Form 941 wage filings. A second route is comparing certified payroll headcount on general-contractor project records to the subcontractor's reported employees and workers' compensation payroll audit.
385.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Cash-out to wage reconciliation: on employer EIN x quarter, compute the ratio of checks cashed at money service businesses to wages reported on Form 941; fires when cashed receipts exceed reported wages by more than the industry-calibrated ratio; action postpay audit.

386.ways_to_identify: At pharmacy adjudication, one dispensing NPI's Schedule II opioid claims concentrate on a handful of prescriber NPIs far beyond same-county pharmacy peers. Prescriber NPIs write opioid volumes implying patient encounters exceeding a plausible workday, visible in paid E/M dates of service. Beneficiaries on the opioid claims have no supporting diagnosis or facility encounter in their other claim history. Wholesaler ARCOS purchase quantities for the pharmacy DEA number fall far below or above dispensed NDC units billed. Nursing-home claims for skilled services persist while MDS assessments and staffing PBJ hours show no corresponding care delivered.
386.features_to_create: 1) Pharmacy-prescriber concentration: on pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute the share of Schedule II opioid claim lines attributable to the top three prescriber NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-county pharmacy peers; action prepay edit. 2) Dispense-to-purchase reconciliation: on pharmacy DEA number x month, compute billed NDC units minus ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree units received; fires when billed units exceed units acquired; action payment suspension. 3) Staffing-to-billing coverage: on nursing facility CCN x quarter, compute billed resident days divided by PBJ-reported nursing hours per resident day; fires when hours per resident day fall below the state minimum; action postpay audit.

387.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, CMS-855S owner identities on dozens of supplier NPIs resolve to foreign addresses, shared phone numbers, or one mail-drop practice location. At adjudication, catheter HCPCS A4351 through A4353 quantities per beneficiary far exceed a month's medically plausible units. Beneficiaries on the claims have no prior urology, hospice, or wound-care encounter with any provider in claim history. Newly enrolled supplier NPIs jump from zero to peer-top-decile billing within weeks of a PECOS ownership change. Beneficiary identifiers appear on claims from many unrelated supplier NPIs spread across states never visited, per beneficiary residence ZIP.
387.features_to_create: 1) Straw-owner graph: on CMS-855 enrolment record, compute the count of other enrolled NPIs sharing an owner SSN, bank account, address, or phone from PECOS; fires when that degree exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty enrollees; action site visit before billing privileges activate. 2) Catheter unit ceiling: on beneficiary x HCPCS x month, compute summed units and the distinct count of billing supplier NPIs; fires when units exceed the coverage-policy monthly maximum or supplier count exceeds one; action prepay edit. 3) New-supplier ramp: on supplier NPI x week, compute billed allowed amount divided by the provider's trailing twelve-week baseline since enrolment; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

388.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, genetic-testing CPT lines carry identical prepopulated diagnosis codes across nearly all beneficiaries of one ordering NPI. The ordering telemedicine NPI has no prior or subsequent E/M claim with the beneficiary and no in-state licence on the board file. Test results never appear to change care, since no follow-up oncology or pharmacogenomic-linked claim follows within months. OTC COVID-19 test HCPCS are billed for beneficiaries whose other claims show no contact with the billing supplier NPI. Performing laboratory CLIA number on the claim differs from the lab that actually holds the specimen contract, visible in referral-lab fields.
388.features_to_create: 1) Diagnosis-code uniformity: on ordering NPI x genetic-testing CPT, compute the share of claim lines carrying the single most frequent ICD-10 code; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty ordering peers; action prepay edit. 2) Telehealth order without encounter: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the test date of service and the nearest E/M or telehealth claim with that beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action claim suspension. 3) Unsolicited OTC test saturation: on beneficiary x HCPCS x month, compute billed test kit units and the distinct count of supplier NPIs; fires when units exceed the program monthly limit; action prepay edit.

389.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, HRSA Uninsured Program claims name beneficiaries who simultaneously have active Medicare or commercial coverage in eligibility files. Specimen collection dates cluster at volumes exceeding the lab CLIA site's physical capacity per day. Ordering NPIs are hospital-employed physicians submitting orders for patients with no encounter at any facility in their claim history. Supplier and lab NPIs share bank accounts and remittance addresses across the payer's own payment file. Beneficiary consent recordings supporting DME and test orders repeat identical audio characteristics, checkable against the payer's prior-authorisation document repository.
389.features_to_create: 1) Uninsured-program coverage crosswalk: on claim line, compute a match of the patient identifier against active Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial eligibility on the date of service; fires on any exact coverage match; action prepay edit. 2) Lab throughput impossibility: on performing CLIA number x date of service, compute the count of billed specimen tests divided by accessioning capacity implied by staffing on file; fires when tests per day exceed the calibrated peer capacity ceiling; action payment suspension. 3) Shared payment-instrument graph: on bank account, compute the distinct count of billing NPIs and TINs receiving remittances; fires when that count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership in PECOS; action payment suspension.

390.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, transcranial doppler CPT volume per ordering NPI rises in near-linear step with payments recorded to that NPI in vendor ledgers. Ordering physicians bill TCD studies for beneficiaries with no stroke, syncope, or cerebrovascular diagnosis on any claim. The mobile diagnostic entity's place-of-service code shows office testing at practices with no imaging equipment on their CMS-855 enrolment. A small set of ordering NPIs accounts for nearly all of the billing entity's TCD claims. Sham space and administrative agreements name physician landlords whose leased square footage does not appear in the practice's enrolment address record.
390.features_to_create: 1) Orderer concentration: on billing entity NPI x quarter, compute the share of TCD CPT claim lines contributed by the top five ordering NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty imaging peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Indication mismatch: on ordering NPI x CPT, compute the share of TCD studies with no cerebrovascular ICD-10 code in the beneficiary's twelve-month claim history; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit. 3) Per-test payment correlation: on ordering NPI x month, compute the correlation between ordered TCD counts and disclosed rental or administrative payments from the entity's financial-relationship disclosures; fires when ordered volume scales with payments; action postpay audit.

391.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a handful of ordering NPIs generate nearly all transcranial doppler CPT lines billed by one mobile diagnostic supplier. Beneficiaries receiving the scans carry no cerebrovascular or syncope diagnosis anywhere in their claim history. Ordered study counts per physician move in step with rental and administrative payments listed in Open Payments and vendor ledgers. Place-of-service on the claim is a physician office with no imaging modality declared on the CMS-855 enrolment record. Repeat TCD studies recur at fixed intervals per beneficiary with no interval change in diagnosis or treatment claims.
391.features_to_create: 1) Referral concentration: on supplier NPI x quarter, compute the Herfindahl concentration of TCD claim lines across ordering NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty imaging peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Unsupported indication rate: on ordering NPI x CPT, compute the share of TCD orders lacking any qualifying ICD-10 code in the beneficiary's prior twelve months of claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit. 3) Repeat-study cadence: on beneficiary x TCD CPT, compute the count of studies in a rolling year and the gap in days between them; fires when count exceeds the coverage-policy frequency limit; action claim suspension.

392.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, hospice election claims name beneficiaries whose other claims show active curative treatment and no terminal diagnosis. One certifying physician NPI signs terminal-illness certifications for beneficiaries clustered in a few group-home addresses. Skin-substitute HCPCS Q-codes are billed with no prior wound-care encounter or wound measurement documented in prior-authorisation records. Genetic testing CPT lines route through shell laboratory NPIs whose enrolment addresses match the ordering entity's address in PECOS. COVID Uninsured Program consultation claims name patients with concurrent active insurance coverage in eligibility files.
392.features_to_create: 1) Hospice certification concentration: on certifying physician NPI x quarter, compute the count of hospice elections and the distinct count of beneficiary residence addresses; fires when elections per address exceed the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Skin-substitute without wound: on beneficiary x Q-code claim line, compute days since the last wound-care E/M or debridement claim and the summed square centimetres applied; fires when no prior wound encounter exists or area exceeds the documented wound size; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Live-discharge and survival check: on hospice NPI x cohort year, compute the share of beneficiaries discharged alive or surviving beyond the benefit period; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state hospice peers; action postpay audit.

393.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, amniotic allograft Q-code claim lines bill square centimetres far exceeding the wound area recorded in prior-authorisation documentation. The rendering nurse practitioner NPI's allograft spend per beneficiary sits far above same-specialty wound-care peers. Beneficiaries have no prior debridement, wound culture, or vascular study claim preceding the graft application. Application dates repeat weekly per beneficiary with no wound-size reduction documented across serial claims. Place of service is a home or group-home setting while the graft HCPCS requires a documented clinical wound assessment.
393.features_to_create: 1) Graft area versus wound size: on claim line, compute billed square centimetres of Q-code product minus documented wound area from the prior-authorisation or ADR record; fires when billed area exceeds documented area; action prepay edit. 2) Allograft spend outlier: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute allowed amount for skin-substitute HCPCS per treated beneficiary; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty wound-care peers; action payment suspension. 3) Missing wound workup: on beneficiary x graft date of service, compute days since the nearest debridement or wound-assessment claim; fires when no such claim exists in the lookback window; action prior-authorisation requirement.

394.ways_to_identify: In PDMP data, one prescriber NPI's buprenorphine prescriptions cluster at maximum daily doses far above same-specialty peers. Dispensing records show most of this prescriber's patients paying cash while holding active insurance coverage in eligibility files. Prescribed dosage changes per patient correlate with payment status rather than any documented clinical assessment in records requested by ADR. Patient counts per prescriber NPI exceed the DATA-waiver or practice-capacity limits recorded with DEA registration. Visit intervals in PDMP show refills issued on dates with no corresponding E/M claim for that beneficiary.
394.features_to_create: 1) High-dose buprenorphine share: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of buprenorphine prescriptions at or above the maximum recommended daily dose; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Cash-pay divergence: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the share of dispensed prescriptions paid cash by patients with active coverage in eligibility files; fires when above the provider's trailing baseline and peer percentile; action postpay audit. 3) Refill without encounter: on beneficiary x prescription fill date, compute days since the nearest E/M claim from that prescriber; fires when no encounter exists within the plan's required visit interval; action prepay edit.

395.ways_to_identify: In PDMP records, the prescriber NPI issues Schedule II opioid prescriptions on dates with no corresponding E/M claim for that patient. The patient's residence ZIP in eligibility files lies hundreds of miles from both the prescriber and the dispensing pharmacy. The prescriber's practice location on the CMS-855 and NPPES record is a residential address without a registered clinical site. Multiple local pharmacies have refused fills, visible as reversed or rejected claims in switch and remittance history. No urine drug screen or treatment-plan claim accompanies chronic opioid prescribing for a patient with an opioid use disorder diagnosis.
395.features_to_create: 1) Prescription without encounter: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary x fill date, compute days since the last paid E/M claim between them; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Geographic implausibility: on claim line, compute the mileage between beneficiary residence ZIP, prescriber practice ZIP, and dispensing pharmacy ZIP; fires when all three distances exceed the calibrated peer travel percentile; action claim suspension. 3) Rejection-shopping: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the count of distinct pharmacies with rejected or reversed opioid claims preceding a successful fill elsewhere; fires when above the provider's trailing baseline; action postpay audit.

396.ways_to_identify: At pharmacy adjudication, claims pair an opioid, a benzodiazepine, and a muscle relaxant NDC with overlapping days supply for one beneficiary. A single prescriber NPI accounts for a dominant share of one pharmacy NPI's controlled-substance claim lines. Benzodiazepine daily doses billed exceed maximum labelled dosing across most of the prescriber's panel in PDMP data. Office-visit E/M claims occur on exactly the same cadence as controlled-substance refills with no varying diagnoses. Requested progress notes contain no vital signs or mental-status findings supporting the billed E/M level.
396.features_to_create: 1) Trinity combination: on beneficiary x date, compute overlapping days supply across opioid, benzodiazepine, and carisoprodol NDCs; fires when all three overlap on the same day; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber-pharmacy pair concentration: on prescriber NPI x pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute that pair's share of the pharmacy's controlled-substance claim lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-county pairs; action payment suspension. 3) Refill-locked E/M: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary, compute the share of E/M claims falling within days of a controlled-substance fill; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

397.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, CMS-855S records for many supplier NPIs share addresses, bank accounts, phones, or authorised officials pointing to one hidden principal. New supplier NPIs begin billing brace L-codes at peer-top-decile volume within weeks of activation, then cease abruptly after an ADR. Ordering NPIs on the brace claims have no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary in claim history. Beneficiary residence ZIPs lie far outside the supplier's declared service area on the enrolment record. The same beneficiary receives duplicate L-code braces from multiple unrelated supplier NPIs within a rolling month.
397.features_to_create: 1) Common-principal graph: on bank account and enrolment address, compute the distinct count of supplier NPIs sharing that identifier in PECOS and payment files; fires when the count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership; action site visit before privileges activate. 2) Ramp-then-stop pattern: on supplier NPI x week, compute weekly allowed amount divided by the provider's trailing baseline and the days between activation and peak billing; fires when peak occurs above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Order-encounter gap and duplication: on beneficiary x L-code, compute days since the ordering NPI's last E/M claim and the count of distinct paying supplier NPIs in thirty days; fires when no encounter exists or supplier count exceeds one; action prepay edit.

398.ways_to_identify: In PDMP data, the prescriber NPI's oxycodone prescription count per month far exceeds same-specialty peers in the state. Prescription and E/M dates of service fall on days when the beneficiary was incarcerated or hospitalised per other claims and correctional rosters. Progress notes returned on ADR lack vital signs and repeat identical boilerplate text across different beneficiaries. Billed E/M and counseling units per rendering NPI per date imply more than twenty-four hours of patient contact. Promethazine with codeine NDC fills accompany oxycodone fills for the same beneficiaries at abnormal frequency.

402.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, claims carry the owner-physician's rendering NPI on dates his airline or hotel records place him out of state. 403.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, NDC-level units billed exceed units the pharmacy purchased per wholesaler pedigree and 340B/ASP acquisition files. 404.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed units of the single high-cost NDC exceed all wholesaler acquisition recorded in pedigree and 867 purchase data. 407.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, ordering NPIs on L-code brace claims have no prior evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiary. 412.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on brace and CGx claims has no prior evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiary. Payment flows show suppliers remitting per-order fees to a common marketing TIN and bank account.
431.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the last E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 2) Shared-orderer supplier graph: on ordering NPI, compute the graph degree of distinct billing supplier NPIs and distinct beneficiary states per week; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Multi-brace saturation: on beneficiary x 30 days, compute the count of distinct brace L-codes and distinct supplier NPIs paid; fires when distinct suppliers exceed one without documented replacement reason; action prepay edit.

432.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the pharmacy NPI's paid dollars concentrate in a handful of high-reimbursement non-contracted generic NDCs far above peer mix. Claim volume for those NDCs surges immediately after the prior-authorisation suspension effective date in the plan rule file. Dispensed NDC quantities exceed the pharmacy's wholesaler acquisition units in DSCSA pedigree data for the same period. Prescribing NPIs on the fills show no prior encounter claims with those beneficiaries. Beneficiaries have no refill continuity or matching diagnosis for an over-the-counter vitamin billed at high cost.
432.features_to_create: 1) Acquisition-to-dispensing reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x month, compute units billed minus units purchased per wholesaler pedigree records; fires when billed units exceed purchased units; action payment suspension. 2) Post-policy surge on narrow NDC set: on pharmacy NPI x week, compute the share of paid dollars from the top five NDCs versus the provider's trailing baseline; fires when the share rises above the trailing baseline and above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Prescriber-encounter gap: on claim line, compute days between fill date and last encounter claim between the prescribing NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit.

433.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, because the loss is unpaid payroll tax and workers' compensation premium. The nearest detection route compares certificate-of-insurance payroll exposure filed with the carrier against check volume deposited to the policyholder's bank account. A second route matches state unemployment wage filings for the EIN against gross contractor payments made to that EIN. A third route flags one policy's certificates issued to dozens of unrelated contractors within a year.
433.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Premium-to-cashflow mismatch: on policy EIN x year, compute deposited contractor payments divided by payroll exposure declared on the workers' compensation policy; fires when the ratio exceeds one materially; action carrier premium audit and state referral.

434.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the facility's mix is dominated by the 45-minute psychotherapy CPT with near-absent shorter-duration codes versus same-specialty peers. Summed session minutes per counselor per date of service exceed the counselor's feasible working hours. Beneficiary throughput per rendering NPI per day exceeds what 45-minute sessions physically allow in 24 hours. The CMS-855B enrolment omits an owner or managing employee identified in state corporate registry and bank signatory records. Disclosed ownership fields conflict with an existing federal conviction record checked against OIG LEIE and court data at enrolment.
434.features_to_create: 1) Session minutes impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total minutes implied by billed timed counseling CPT units; fires when the sum exceeds available hours in 24; action prepay edit. 2) Duration code skew: on provider NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of 45-minute session claims to all timed counseling claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR) then postpay audit. 3) Undisclosed principal: on enrolling TIN, compute the count of officers, signatories or registry principals absent from CMS-855 ownership and managing-employee fields; fires when the count exceeds zero; action enrolment site visit and payment suspension.

435.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the CMS-855B owner listed has no verifiable industry history and appears as sole signatory on the receiving bank account. Remittance payments for one laboratory NPI route to a bank account whose signatory differs from the disclosed owner in enrolment records. The nominal owner appears as owner on multiple unrelated enrolments within a short window across payers. Laboratory test volume ramps from zero to peer-top-decile within weeks of PECOS approval. Ordering NPIs on the lab's claims are geographically distant from the lab's enrolled service address.
435.features_to_create: 1) Nominee-owner detection: on enrolling NPI, compute the count of distinct provider enrolments sharing the same disclosed owner SSN, address or phone in PECOS; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action enrolment site visit. 2) Payee-owner mismatch: on bank account, compute the count of distinct provider NPIs receiving remittances and whether the account signatory matches the CMS-855 disclosed owner; fires on exact mismatch; action payment suspension. 3) Post-enrolment volume ramp: on provider NPI x month, compute paid dollars versus the provider's trailing baseline since enrolment; fires when growth exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty new enrollees; action prepay edit.

436.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no clinical adjudication, because the instrument is a WIC food voucher redeemed by a retail vendor. The nearest detection route compares each vendor's redeemed voucher dollars against wholesale purchase invoices for WIC-eligible foods stocked. A second route compares average redemption per voucher across vendors of the same size and peer group. A third route matches redemption spikes to store inventory capacity observed at authorization site visits.
436.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Redemption-to-inventory ratio: on vendor ID x quarter, compute redeemed WIC dollars divided by documented wholesale purchases of WIC-eligible items; fires when the ratio exceeds one or is above the calibrated percentile versus peer vendors; action redemption hold and site visit.

437.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, ordering NPIs on brace L-codes have no prior evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiaries. Ordering NPIs appear on claims from supplier NPIs in states where those practitioners have never billed any other service. The same practitioner NPI is used across suppliers under common ownership per CMS-855S disclosure fields. Beneficiaries receive multiple brace L-codes within thirty days from suppliers sharing one bank account. Supplier marketing payments are structured as flat fees but scale linearly with monthly order counts in ledgers.
437.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 2) NPI misuse detection: on ordering NPI x supplier NPI, compute the count of ordered claims where the ordering NPI has no other billing activity in that beneficiary's state; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension with documentation request (ADR). 3) Common-ownership supplier cluster: on bank account or TIN, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs paid and their shared ordering-NPI overlap; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action payment suspension.

438.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, brace L-code claims carry ordering NPIs with no prior evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiary. Marketing contracts obtained on ADR show flat fees while payment ledgers scale with order counts month over month. Practitioner NPIs used on orders show no telehealth or office claim for those beneficiaries on any date. Beneficiary residence ZIPs fall far outside the supplier's service area declared on the CMS-855S. Several supplier NPIs sharing one owner submit claims citing the same small pool of ordering NPIs.
438.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the date of service and the most recent encounter claim linking that ordering NPI to the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer concentration: on supplier NPI x month, compute the share of paid brace claims attributable to the top three ordering NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Service-area breach: on claim line, compute the distance between the beneficiary residence ZIP and the supplier's enrolled service area on CMS-855S; fires when outside the declared area; action claim suspension.

439.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, weekly HCBS residential claims attest required staffing ratios while payroll and timesheet records show fewer staff hours than residents billed. EVV or shift records show no staff clock-ins covering hours billed as staffed residential support. State licensing inspection files record unsanitary or unsafe conditions at addresses still billing full waiver units. The same staff member's hours across group home addresses exceed 24 hours on a single date. The representative-payee provider receives beneficiary Social Security funds while also billing waiver units for the same residents.
439.features_to_create: 1) Staffing-ratio attestation test: on group home site x week, compute total paid staff hours from payroll or EVV divided by billed resident-days times the waiver-required ratio; fires when the computed ratio falls below the program-required minimum; action payment suspension. 2) Staff hour impossibility: on staff ID x date of service, compute total hours claimed across all sites; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 3) Licensing-deficiency crosswalk: on provider NPI x site address, compute the count of open state health or safety citations during the billed service week; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension with site visit.

440.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, cross-match every CMS-855A owner, officer and managing-employee SSN against the OIG LEIE and state exclusion list. Compare the disclosed owners in PECOS against state corporate filings to expose a concealed principal behind a nominee. At adjudication, overlap home health visit dates against the beneficiary's inpatient claims for the same dates of service. Compare billed visit units to EVV check-in and check-out records for the same aide, date and beneficiary. Screen every employee NPI or payroll record against the state criminal-background-check registry required for direct-care staff.
440.features_to_create: 1) Excluded-principal match: on provider NPI x disclosed owner SSN, compute exact-match count against OIG LEIE and state exclusion files at CMS-855 screening and revalidation; fires when any exact registry match exists; action claim suspension. 2) Inpatient overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of home health visit lines whose service date falls inside a paid inpatient admission span; fires when that count exceeds zero; action prepay edit. 3) EVV-to-claim gap: on rendering aide NPI x date of service, compute billed units minus EVV-verified visit minutes divided by 15; fires when billed units exceed EVV minutes; action payment suspension.

441.ways_to_identify: There is no claim and no adjudication point here, since the violation is controlled-substance recordkeeping rather than billing. The nearest detection route is DEA inspection comparing ARCOS purchase data against the pharmacy's biennial inventory and dispensing logs. A second route is auditing the electronic pseudoephedrine logbook required by the Combat Methamphetamine Epidemic Act for missing purchaser certifications.
441.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: on pharmacy DEA number x NDC x quarter, compute ARCOS-reported units received minus units dispensed in the pharmacy dispensing file; fires when the unexplained gap exceeds the pharmacy's trailing baseline; action site visit.

442.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, match every trip date of service against the Death Master File date of death for the beneficiary. Compare trip dates against the beneficiary's inpatient and incarceration eligibility spans in the Medicaid eligibility file. Check whether the beneficiary has any same-day treatment claim from the destination clinic NPI on the trip date. Compare the pickup address on the claim to the address of record in the eligibility file to detect mileage inflation. Count distinct beneficiaries whose trips all originate from one carrier and terminate at the same three clinic NPIs.
442.features_to_create: 1) Decedent and custody trips: on claim line, compute whether the date of service falls after the Death Master File date of death or inside an inpatient or incarceration eligibility span; fires when either condition is true; action prepay edit. 2) Destination-encounter match: on beneficiary x trip date, compute the count of treatment claims from the destination provider NPI within the trip date; fires when that count is zero; action claim suspension. 3) Address-mileage mismatch: on claim line, compute the mileage implied by the eligibility-file residence ZIP minus billed loaded mileage; fires when billed mileage exceeds the geocoded distance; action prepay edit and postpay audit.

443.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute the share of the pharmacy's Part D dollars concentrated in compounded topical cream NDCs and high-cost bulk ingredient codes. Measure the road distance between beneficiary residence ZIP in eligibility data and the mail-order pharmacy's CMS-855S practice location. Check whether prescribing NPIs on those creams have any prior evaluation-and-management claim with the same beneficiary. Count how many prescribers concentrate a majority of their compound scripts in this one pharmacy chain's NPIs. Compare marketing or consulting payments disclosed in Open Payments against prescriber referral volume into the pharmacy.
443.features_to_create: 1) Compound concentration: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the ratio of compounded topical cream NDC paid dollars to total paid dollars; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriber-pharmacy exclusivity: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of compound claims routed to a single pharmacy TIN; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Orderer-encounter gap: on claim line x prescriber NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between prescriber and beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit.

444.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count distinct L-code braces billed to one beneficiary across all supplier NPIs within a rolling period. Check whether the ordering telemedicine NPI has any prior evaluation-and-management or telehealth encounter claim with that beneficiary. Count distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs served by one ordering NPI in a week. Compare CMS-855S disclosed owners across suppliers for shared addresses, bank accounts and nominee officers indicating common control. Compare supplier volume after a PECOS ownership change against its own trailing baseline.
444.features_to_create: 1) Brace saturation: on beneficiary x rolling 90 days, compute the count of distinct orthotic L-codes and distinct supplier NPIs paid; fires when multiple braces are paid without a documented replacement reason; action prepay edit. 2) Telehealth orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs on ordered DMEPOS claims plus the count with no prior E/M; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Common-control cluster: on bank account and remittance address across CMS-855S records, compute the graph degree of linked supplier NPIs; fires when degree exceeds one undisclosed link; action site visit.

445.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, because the loss is a forgiven SBA loan rather than a paid claim. The nearest detection route is matching payroll figures on the loan application against IRS Forms 941 and state wage filings for the same quarters. A second route is comparing bank statements submitted with forgiveness applications against lender-held originals for altered balances.
445.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payroll attestation match: on borrower EIN x quarter, compute claimed payroll dollars on the loan and forgiveness applications minus IRS Form 941 reported wages; fires when the difference exceeds the filed amount; action postpay audit by the lender and SBA.

446.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, since the funds were SBA-guaranteed loan proceeds rather than payer reimbursements. The nearest detection route is cross-matching application payroll and headcount against IRS Form 941 and state unemployment insurance wage records. A further route is checking whether multiple loans were issued to related entities sharing one owner, address or bank account.
446.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Related-borrower cluster: on bank account and owner SSN across loan applications, compute the count of distinct borrower EINs sharing the identifier; fires when the count exceeds one undisclosed affiliate; action postpay audit before forgiveness.

447.ways_to_identify: At credentialing, verify each rendering NPI on therapy claims against the state physical therapy licence board file for an active licence. At adjudication, compare the rendering NPI on 97110 and 97140 lines against the clinic's roster of licensed therapists on file.
