Compute total timed therapy units billed per rendering NPI per day and convert to hours to test physical possibility. Check whether the same licensed therapist NPI appears as renderer at two clinic locations during overlapping treatment minutes. Compare the clinic's paid therapy minutes to its licensed full-time-equivalent staffing reported at enrolment.
447.features_to_create: 1) Licence verification: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute whether the NPPES taxonomy and state licence board file show an active therapy licence covering that date; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Impossible therapy day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of timed CPT units multiplied by 15 minutes; fires when total exceeds a physically possible workday; action claim suspension. 3) Capacity ratio: on provider NPI x week, compute paid therapy minutes divided by licensed therapist full-time-equivalents on the enrolment roster; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

448.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare the rendering physician NPI on claims against that physician's own reassignment records in PECOS for the billing TIN. Contact-verify billed rendering NPIs against NPPES practice address and the physician's other claim footprint in a different market. Compute the share of one clinic group's total claim dollars attributed to a single rendering NPI. Compute daily service counts and units under that rendering NPI to test physical possibility of one physician's workday. Check whether the physician's signature-bearing documentation matches a signature log or attestation on file at credentialing.
448.features_to_create: 1) Reassignment mismatch: on claim line, compute whether an active CMS-855R reassignment links the rendering NPI to the billing TIN on the date of service; fires on any exact PECOS mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Single-renderer concentration: on billing TIN x month, compute the share of paid dollars carried by the top rendering NPI plus that NPI's daily encounter count; fires when both exceed the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Physician workday: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed service time implied by billed CPT codes; fires when it exceeds 24 hours or a physically possible day; action payment suspension.

449.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, because the loss is unremitted employment and meals taxes. The nearest detection route is comparing IRS Form 941 reported wages against point-of-sale gross receipts and bank cash deposits for the same period. A second route is matching state meals tax collected on register data against monthly returns filed with the state revenue department.
449.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Receipts-to-return gap: on business EIN x month, compute point-of-sale taxable sales multiplied by the meals tax rate minus tax remitted on the filed return; fires when the shortfall exceeds zero; action state revenue audit.

450.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, match the dispensed NDC and serial number against DSCSA transaction history to confirm an unbroken pedigree from the labeler. Check whether the upstream wholesaler on the pedigree holds an active state wholesale distributor licence for the shipping period. Compare a pharmacy's high-cost HIV NDC acquisition volumes against its dispensing claim volume for the same NDCs. Detect beneficiaries with repeated early refills of high-value antiretrovirals that never appear in adherence or lab monitoring claims. Count complaint reports of wrong-drug or tampered bottles tied to one wholesaler across pharmacy NPIs.
450.features_to_create: 1) Pedigree break: on claim line x NDC serial number, compute whether a continuous DSCSA transaction chain exists back to the labeler; fires on any missing or unlicensed upstream node; action prepay edit. 2) Buy-back refill pattern: on beneficiary x antiretroviral NDC, compute days between fills divided by days supply; fires when refills occur before the prior supply is exhausted repeatedly; action claim suspension and postpay audit. 3) Supply-dispense imbalance: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute dispensed units minus units acquired from licensed distributors per pedigree data; fires when dispensed exceeds documented acquisitions; action site visit.

451.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare billed private duty nursing units against EVV check-in and check-out records for the same nurse, beneficiary and date. Compute nursing hours billed per rendering NPI per day to test physical possibility across concurrent beneficiaries. Compare billed hours against the hours authorised on the prior-authorisation and plan-of-care record for that beneficiary. Verify each rendering nurse NPI against the state nursing board licence file for an active licence on the service date. Detect nursing notes with identical signature dates or template text across different beneficiaries in ADR-returned documentation.
451.features_to_create: 1) EVV shortfall: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute billed nursing units minus EVV-verified minutes divided by the unit length; fires when billed exceeds verified; action prepay edit. 2) Authorisation overage: on beneficiary x authorisation period, compute paid hours minus prior-authorised hours; fires when paid exceeds authorised; action claim suspension. 3) Impossible caregiver day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed billed hours across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or overlapping visit minutes occur; action payment suspension.

452.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare CPT codes billed against the licensed disciplines on the clinic's credentialing roster and rendering NPI taxonomies. Check whether acupuncture and therapy lines carry a rendering NPI with the corresponding state licence in the board file. Compute the ratio of therapy and E/M lines billed per beneficiary visit day against same-specialty peers. Detect identical daily CPT bundles repeated for every beneficiary regardless of diagnosis in remittance history. Compare beneficiary-reported service via post-payment questionnaires against E/M visits with no supporting chart entry.
452.features_to_create: 1) Taxonomy-service mismatch: on claim line, compute whether the rendering NPI taxonomy and state licence permit the billed CPT on that date; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Cloned visit bundle: on provider NPI x beneficiary x date, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries receiving the identical CPT combination that day divided by total beneficiaries seen; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Unstaffed modality volume: on provider NPI x month, compute paid units of therapy codes with no correspondingly licensed staff on the credentialing roster; fires when units exceed zero; action payment suspension.

453.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute the count of definitive urine drug test panels per beneficiary per month billed by an in-house lab under the same TIN. Compare presumptive and definitive test pairs on the same specimen date for duplicative billing. Compute the share of the clinic's lab claims referred by ordering NPIs within its own ownership group per PECOS. Compare Schedule II prescription dispensing dates against the prescriber's documented presence, using absence of any same-day E/M claim. Check whether nurse practitioners issued opioid prescriptions under the physician's DEA number outside supervision records.
453.features_to_create: 1) UDT frequency: on beneficiary x ordering NPI x month, compute the count of definitive drug test HCPCS units and analyte counts; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Duplicative confirmation: on specimen date x beneficiary, compute the count of presumptive plus definitive tests billed for the same analytes; fires when confirmation occurs without a discordant presumptive result; action prepay edit. 3) Prescriber-presence gap: on prescribing NPI x date of service, compute the count of Schedule II prescriptions attributed on days with zero claims or encounters by that prescriber; fires when the count exceeds zero; action documentation request (ADR) and postpay audit.

454.ways_to_identify: At adjudication of Foreign Medical Program claims, verify the billing provider's foreign licence and registration against the host country regulator file. Compare submitted invoices for the same veteran across providers for duplicate dates of service and identical line items. Compute per-veteran annual paid dollars and encounter counts against the FMP peer distribution in that country. Compare dispensed medication quantities to the veteran's documented diagnoses and prior FMP pharmacy history. Detect clusters of unrelated provider claims sharing one bank account or remittance address in the payment file.
454.features_to_create: 1) Foreign licence verification: on billing provider ID, compute whether an active host-country licence and registration exist for each date of service; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 2) Veteran utilisation outlier: on veteran x year, compute paid FMP dollars and distinct encounter count; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus in-country peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Shared payee cluster: on bank account in the FMP payment file, compute the count of distinct provider IDs receiving deposits; fires when the count exceeds one undisclosed affiliate; action payment suspension.

455.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, because the loss is withheld employment taxes diverted by a payroll agent. The nearest detection route is reconciling client employees' Forms W-2 withholding totals against Forms 941 filed by the agent for the same EINs. A second route is IRS notice matching of EFTPS deposits against reported liabilities per quarter per client EIN.
455.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) W-2 to 941 reconciliation: on client EIN x quarter, compute summed W-2 federal withholding minus withholding reported and deposited on Form 941; fires when the shortfall exceeds zero; action IRS examination of the third-party payroll agent.

456.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute overlapping service minutes for one rendering aide NPI across different beneficiaries on the same date. Compare EVV geolocation stamps against the beneficiary's address of record in the eligibility file. Sum all billed units per rendering worker per day across both personal care and behavioral health programs to test the 24-hour limit. Measure travel time implied between consecutive visit locations versus the gap between claimed shift end and start. Detect one worker billing under two different program provider NPIs for the same hours.
456.features_to_create: 1) Overlapping shift detector: on rendering worker NPI x date of service, compute overlapping minutes across all beneficiary visit spans including other program lines; fires when overlap exceeds zero minutes; action prepay edit. 2) EVV geofence mismatch: on visit record, compute distance between the EVV check-in coordinates and the beneficiary's eligibility-file address; fires when distance exceeds the geofence radius; action claim suspension. 3) Daily hour ceiling: on rendering worker NPI x date of service, compute summed billed units converted to hours across all payer programs; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or an impossible shift; action payment suspension.

457.ways_to_identify: Match Open Payments speaker fee and meal records to each prescriber's Part D claim volume for the promoted NDC. Compute the prescriber's share of the drug written before and after the first speaker payment date. Detect repeat programs where the same speaker NPI and same attendee NPIs recur across sessions in the manufacturer's transparency file. Identify attendees who are the speaker's practice colleagues under the same TIN in NPPES and PECOS. Compare per-attendee meal spend against fair-market-value thresholds in the payments file.
457.features_to_create: 1) Payment-to-prescribing lift: on prescriber NPI x NDC, compute paid Part D claim counts in the 12 months after the first Open Payments speaker fee minus the 12 months before; fires when the lift is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 2) Repeat-attendee graph: on speaker NPI x program series, compute the count of repeat attendee NPIs and attendees sharing the speaker's TIN; fires when repeats exceed the calibrated percentile versus peer programs; action postpay audit. 3) Brand concentration: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the promoted NDC's share of that prescriber's claims in its therapeutic class; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

458.ways_to_identify: Link Open Payments speaker honoraria and meal transactions to each recipient prescriber's subsequent Part D claims for the promoted NDC. Compute the change in that prescriber's brand share before and after the first honorarium date. Count sessions with an identical program topic and speaker NPI repeated within the manufacturer's transparency reporting. Identify attendee NPIs sharing a group practice TIN or surname with the paid speaker in NPPES records. Compare per-head meal spend on program records against documented educational content and attendance need.
458.features_to_create: 1) Honorarium-prescribing correlation: on prescriber NPI x NDC, compute the ratio of post-payment to pre-payment paid claim counts using Open Payments dates; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 2) Sham-program detector: on speaker NPI x program topic, compute the count of repeat sessions and the count of attendees under the speaker's TIN; fires when both exceed peer program norms; action postpay audit. 3) High-cost brand share: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute promoted NDC paid dollars divided by class dollars; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement.

459.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check every TIRF fentanyl NDC claim for a cancer diagnosis on the beneficiary's other claims within the lookback period. Verify prescriber and beneficiary enrolment in the TIRF REMS registry before payment of the Part D claim. Link Open Payments speaker and advisory board payments to each prescriber's TIRF volume. Compare the prescriber against DEA action lists and state board discipline files for diversion findings. Detect prior-authorisation submissions routed through a manufacturer-funded reimbursement hub rather than the prescriber's office.
459.features_to_create: 1) Off-label TIRF edit: on claim line, compute whether the beneficiary has any malignancy diagnosis code on claims within the lookback window; fires when no cancer diagnosis exists; action prepay edit. 2) REMS registry match: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary, compute enrolment status in the TIRF REMS registry at the fill date; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Sponsored-prescriber concentration: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute TIRF claim counts alongside Open Payments dollars from the manufacturer; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement.

460.ways_to_identify: At Part D adjudication, TIRF fentanyl NDCs appear for beneficiaries with no cancer diagnosis on any prior medical claim. The prescribing NPI's TIRF volume sits far above same-specialty peers in the payer's prescriber profile file. Open Payments records show speaker and advisory payments from the labeling manufacturer to the same prescribing NPIs. Prior-authorisation packets for these NDCs are submitted by a manufacturer-funded hub rather than the prescriber's own office fax or portal. Some prescribing NPIs carry state board sanctions or DEA registration actions visible at credentialing.
460.features_to_create: 1) Off-label TIRF indication check: on claim line x beneficiary, compute the count of oncology diagnosis codes on that beneficiary's medical claims in the prior 12 months for TIRF NDCs; fires when the count is zero; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriber TIRF concentration: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute TIRF NDC claim count and its share of that prescriber's total Part D opioid claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Sponsored-prescriber overlay: on prescriber NPI x NDC, compute the sum of Open Payments speaker and consulting dollars from the NDC's labeler in the prior year; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers and TIRF volume also exceeds peer baseline; action prepay edit.

461.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed NDC units exceed the pharmacy's documented wholesaler acquisition units for the same NDC in the invoice and pedigree file. Dispensed quantities of high-cost antipsychotics and inhalers exceed peer pharmacies of the same script volume in the payer's remittance history. Beneficiaries billed for these NDCs have no matching office-visit or diagnosis claims supporting the therapy. Refill intervals are shorter than days-supply on the prior fill, indicating fills never taken. Audit responses across two related pharmacy NPIs share identical inventory documents and common ownership on CMS-855B filings.
461.features_to_create: 1) Purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed units minus wholesaler-invoiced units acquired; fires when billed units exceed acquired units; action claim suspension then postpay audit. 2) High-cost NDC concentration: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the ratio of paid dollars for the top five NDCs to total paid dollars; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-region peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Common-owner aggregation: on TIN x owner SSN from CMS-855B, compute the sum of purchase-to-dispense shortfall units across all linked pharmacy NPIs; fires when any linked NPI shows a shortfall; action site visit.

462.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a small set of prescriber NPIs accounts for nearly all of the pharmacy's compounded-drug claims despite being far from the pharmacy. Compound claims carry high-cost bulk ingredient NDCs with per-claim paid amounts above same-state pharmacy peers. Beneficiary residence ZIPs are hundreds of miles from the dispensing pharmacy's 855B practice location. The pharmacy's general ledger and 1099 filings show large payments to marketing entities not enrolled as providers. Refill counts continue after the beneficiary has no further contact claims with the prescriber.
462.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber concentration graph: on pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute the share of compounded-drug paid dollars from the top ten prescriber NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state pharmacy peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Distance anomaly: on claim line, compute miles between beneficiary ZIP and pharmacy 855B service address for compound HCPCS/NDC claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action prepay edit. 3) Compound cost outlier: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute mean paid dollars per compound claim; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers or above the pharmacy's trailing twelve-month baseline; action payment suspension.

463.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the prescriber NPI on the claim has no other prescribing activity for that beneficiary in any payer claim history. Prescriber NPIs used are inactive, retired, or in NPPES specialties that never prescribe the billed drug class. A single pharmacy NPI accounts for an outsized share of one prescriber's total Medicaid scripts. Prescriber-attested outreach letters go unanswered or are disclaimed by the physician's office. Fill dates fall outside the prescriber's licensed practice dates on the state board file.
463.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber-beneficiary linkage: on claim line, compute the count of medical encounter claims between the listed prescriber NPI and the beneficiary in the prior 12 months; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit. 2) Single-pharmacy prescriber capture: on prescriber NPI x pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute the pharmacy's share of that prescriber's total dispensed claims; fires when the share is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR) to the prescriber. 3) Registry status mismatch: on claim line, compare prescriber licence status and DEA registration on the state board file at the date of service; fires on exact mismatch such as expired, retired, or deceased; action claim suspension.

464.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed NDC units exceed the pharmacy's wholesaler acquisition units in invoice and pedigree data. Prescriber NPIs on the claims have no encounter claims with the billed beneficiaries. Prescription images produced in audit share identical handwriting or signature bitmaps across different prescriber NPIs. Three pharmacy NPIs with common ownership on CMS-855B show the same NDC mix and the same top prescribers. Beneficiaries have no diagnosis on file supporting the dispensed drug class.
464.features_to_create: 1) Purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed units minus wholesaler-invoiced units; fires when billed exceeds acquired; action claim suspension. 2) Orphan-prescriber rate: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of claims whose prescriber NPI has no encounter claim with the beneficiary in 12 months; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-region pharmacy peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Common-ownership cluster: on owner identifier from CMS-855B, compute the count of linked pharmacy NPIs sharing the same top-five prescriber NPIs; fires when overlap exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peers; action site visit.

465.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, high-cost medicated scar-pad NDCs are billed for beneficiaries with no surgical, burn, or wound diagnosis in prior claims. Paid amount per unit is extreme relative to the state's average pharmacy claim, visible in remittance history. All such claims trace to one pharmacy NPI and a handful of prescriber NPIs. Beneficiaries have no encounter claim with the listed prescriber near the fill date. There are no refills or follow-up wound-care claims, which is inconsistent with genuine therapy.
465.features_to_create: 1) Indication gap for high-cost topical NDCs: on claim line, compute the count of wound, burn, or post-surgical diagnosis codes on the beneficiary's claims in the prior 180 days; fires when zero; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Per-claim cost outlier: on pharmacy NPI x NDC, compute mean paid dollars per claim against the state pharmacy distribution; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action claim suspension. 3) Prescriber-contact check: on claim line, compute days since the beneficiary's most recent encounter with the listed prescriber NPI; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action documentation request (ADR).

466.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed NDC units exceed units the pharmacy purchased per wholesaler invoices and drug pedigree records. The pharmacy's paid dollars per prescription exceed same-state peers in the payer's remittance history. Beneficiaries billed for chronic-therapy NDCs show no supporting diagnosis or prescriber encounter claims. Refill timing is inconsistent with days-supply on the prior fill for the same NDC. The pharmacy's dispensing volume rose sharply above its own trailing baseline without any enrolment change in PECOS.
466.features_to_create: 1) Inventory reconciliation edit: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed units minus wholesaler-acquired units; fires when the difference is positive; action claim suspension then postpay audit. 2) Early-refill density: on beneficiary x NDC x pharmacy NPI, compute the count of fills whose gap from the prior fill is less than the prior days-supply; fires when the count exceeds the pharmacy's trailing baseline percentile versus peers; action prepay edit. 3) Volume step change: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute paid dollars divided by the trailing twelve-month mean; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action documentation request (ADR).

467.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Part D billed units for specific NDCs exceed wholesaler-invoiced acquisition units for the same pharmacy NPI. The pharmacy's high-cost NDC mix diverges sharply from same-state pharmacies of similar script count. Beneficiaries lack diagnosis or prescriber encounter claims supporting the dispensed drugs. Fill patterns show automatic monthly refills with no beneficiary cost-share collection recorded. Rapid growth in paid dollars occurs against the pharmacy's own trailing baseline in remittance history.
467.features_to_create: 1) Purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed units minus wholesaler-invoiced units; fires when billed exceeds acquired; action claim suspension. 2) High-cost mix divergence: on pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute the share of paid dollars from NDCs above the state cost-per-claim median; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Auto-refill without contact: on beneficiary x NDC, compute the count of consecutive fills with no intervening prescriber encounter claim; fires when the count exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit.

468.ways_to_identify: At adjudication and in PDMP data, the pharmacy dispenses Schedule II opioids almost entirely as cash transactions with no insurance adjudication record. ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree data show opioid purchase volumes far above same-size pharmacy peers. Prescriptions carry prescriber NPIs whose PDMP history shows no other activity in that state. Patient cohorts share long travel distances, identical drug cocktails, and same-day fills at one pharmacy. The owner's disability benefit application conflicts with payroll and business income records held by the agency.
468.features_to_create: 1) Controlled-substance acquisition outlier: on pharmacy DEA number x quarter, compute morphine-milligram-equivalent units purchased from ARCOS divided by total prescriptions dispensed; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-size peers; action site visit. 2) Cash-fill share: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of Schedule II fills in PDMP with no corresponding payer adjudication record; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus state peers; action prepay edit on that pharmacy's remaining claims plus referral. 3) Prescriber-identity validation: on prescription record x prescriber NPI, compute whether the prescriber's DEA registration, state licence, and NPPES address match the prescription face; fires on exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension.

469.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, specialty NDC billed units exceed the pharmacy's wholesaler acquisition and cold-chain purchase records for those products. Refill claims continue with no shipment tracking numbers matching the carrier manifest supplied at PBM audit. A handful of prescriber NPIs generate nearly all high-cost specialty scripts routed to two commonly owned pharmacy NPIs. Beneficiaries lack hepatitis C, Crohn's, or rheumatoid arthritis diagnoses and lab monitoring claims consistent with therapy. Pharmacy payroll records show staff placed inside a referring physician's office, visible in 1099 and payment ledgers.
469.features_to_create: 1) Specialty inventory reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed units minus wholesaler-invoiced units for specialty NDCs; fires when billed exceeds acquired; action payment suspension. 2) Refill without clinical footprint: on beneficiary x NDC, compute the count of paid refills with zero supporting diagnosis or monitoring lab claims in the prior 180 days; fires when the count exceeds one; action prepay edit. 3) Referral concentration: on prescriber NPI x pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute the pharmacy's share of that prescriber's specialty scripts and the prescriber's share of the pharmacy's specialty dollars; fires when both exceed the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR).

470.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed brand NDC units exceed brand units the pharmacy purchased, while generic purchases of the same molecule dominate wholesaler invoices. Brand-versus-generic dispensing ratio for Schedule II opioids sits far above same-state pharmacy peers. Returned-to-stock inventory entries have no corresponding reversal transaction in the payer's remittance history. Some billed prescriptions have no matching PDMP dispensing record for the beneficiary. Beneficiaries show gaps between claimed days-supply and next-fill dates inconsistent with actual pickup logs.
470.features_to_create: 1) Brand-billed versus brand-purchased: on pharmacy NPI x molecule x quarter, compute billed brand NDC units minus wholesaler-invoiced brand units; fires when billed exceeds acquired; action claim suspension. 2) Unreversed return detection: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the count of fills with a return-to-stock inventory entry but no claim reversal in remittance history; fires when the count is above zero; action postpay audit. 3) PDMP-to-claim match: on claim line for Schedule II NDCs, compute whether a PDMP dispensing record exists with matching beneficiary, NDC, and fill date; fires on exact mismatch; action prepay edit.

471.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, home health visit claims have no matching EVV check-in and check-out record for the beneficiary and caregiver. Billed aide hours exceed the payroll and timesheet hours the agency reports to the state wage system. Rendering caregiver identifiers are absent from the state registry or duplicated across simultaneous visits. The agency's Medicaid billing volume grew from near zero with no plan-of-care or supervisory visit claims. Provider bank account and TIN match those used in unrelated benefit applications flagged in fraud-file cross-checks.
471.features_to_create: 1) EVV-to-claim reconciliation: on claim line, compute billed service minutes minus matched EVV verified minutes for that beneficiary, caregiver, and date; fires when unmatched minutes are above zero; action prepay edit. 2) Payroll capacity ratio: on provider NPI x quarter, compute billed aide hours divided by hours reported on state payroll filings; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action payment suspension. 3) New-agency ramp: on provider NPI x month, compute paid dollars divided by trailing three-month mean for agencies enrolled under two years; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action site visit.

472.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the applicant's SSN does not match the name and date of birth in the SSA numident verification response. Multiple approved cases share one mailing address, one phone number, and one bank account across different applicant identities. Submitted birth certificates for dependents have no corresponding record in the state vital records file. The photograph on the driver's licence submitted matches images on other applications under different names. Issued SNAP EBT cards are redeemed almost entirely at a single retailer in high-value even-dollar transactions.
472.features_to_create: 1) Identity verification mismatch: on benefit application, compute the SSA numident match result across name, SSN, and date of birth; fires on any exact mismatch; action claim suspension of the eligibility determination pending documentation request. 2) Household collision graph: on address, phone, or bank account, compute the count of distinct approved case identifiers sharing that value; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-county caseload; action site visit. 3) Dependent vital-records match: on each listed dependent, compute whether a state vital records birth entry matches name and date of birth; fires on exact mismatch; action prepay edit on benefit issuance.

473.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim here and no payer adjudication point, so no prepay or postpay control applies. The theft involves parcel cargo and is detected through carrier facility access logs, door-forcing alarms, and parcel scan gaps. The nearest detection route is reconciling last-scan location against delivery exceptions for high-value electronics shipments.
473.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is a carrier-side check on facility x night that counts high-value parcels with a terminal scan but no outbound scan and escalates when the count exceeds the facility's trailing baseline.

474.ways_to_identify: At eligibility determination, the SSN on the application fails the SSA numident match against submitted name and date of birth. One residential address, phone number, or payee bank account appears across several approved cases with different identities. Dependent birth certificates submitted have no matching entry in the state vital records registry. The same facial image appears on identity documents filed under multiple applicant names. EBT redemptions concentrate at one retailer in round-dollar amounts inconsistent with household size.
474.features_to_create: 1) Numident mismatch edit: on benefit application, compute the SSA verification result across SSN, name, and date of birth; fires on exact mismatch; action claim suspension pending documentation request. 2) Shared-attribute degree: on address, phone, or bank account, compute the distinct count of approved case identifiers linked to that value; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-county caseload; action site visit. 3) Retailer concentration: on EBT card x month, compute the share of redemption dollars at a single retailer FNS number; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-county households; action postpay audit.

475.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the rendering NPI's billed time-based units for one date of service exceed the hours physically available in a workday. Documented start and end clock times overlap across different beneficiaries for the same rendering NPI. Claims for the same rendering NPI on one date carry two different service facility locations minutes apart. Nearly all med-check claims bill the same time-based CPT unit count, with no distribution across shorter codes. Encounter counts per provider day exceed same-specialty peers in the payer's remittance history.
475.features_to_create: 1) Impossible-day check: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed time-based CPT units multiplied by their code-defined minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the calibrated peer workday percentile; action prepay edit. 2) Overlapping-time detection: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of documented start-end intervals that overlap another beneficiary's interval; fires when overlapping minutes are above zero; action claim suspension. 3) Multi-site same-day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the distinct count of service facility addresses and the drive-time between them versus interval spacing; fires when travel time exceeds the documented gap; action documentation request (ADR).

476.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point in this extortion scheme, so no prepay or postpay claims control applies. Detection sits with network telemetry: intrusion logs, ransomware note artefacts, and darknet leak-site monitoring. The nearest financial route is tracing ransom cryptocurrency wallet clusters through blockchain analytics and exchange KYC records.
476.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest control outside the claims system is a security-operations check on provider network x day counting anomalous outbound data-transfer volume against the site's trailing baseline, with escalation to incident response.

477.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the medical licence number on the CMS-855I does not match any active record in the state licensing board file. NPPES taxonomy claimed as general practitioner conflicts with the physician assistant credential on the state registry. No ECFMG or USMLE verification record supports the submitted score reports at credentialing. Reassignment of benefits to a group is requested with no prior residency or hospital privileging verifiable at primary source. Enrolment application address and dates conflict with employment records at the named hospital.
477.features_to_create: 1) Licence primary-source match: on CMS-855I application, compute an exact match of licence number, name, and issue date against the state board file; fires on any mismatch; action claim suspension of enrolment plus site visit. 2) Taxonomy-credential consistency: on provider NPI, compute whether the NPPES taxonomy requires a credential the applicant holds in the state registry; fires on exact mismatch such as physician assistant billing as physician; action prepay edit on all claims. 3) Post-enrolment claim block: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute whether the date falls within a verified active licence period; fires when the date lies outside it; action claim suspension.

478.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, controlled-substance prescriptions and same-day dispensing claims share one owner TIN across prescriber and pharmacy NPIs. Every opioid claim for a beneficiary is accompanied by additional non-controlled NDCs from the same in-house pharmacy on the same date. The prescription record shows an intern or unlicensed writer while the prescriber NPI is the supervising physician. Beneficiaries have no diagnosis supporting the bundled ancillary medications in their prior claim history. Opioid tablet quantities per beneficiary exceed same-specialty prescriber peers in PDMP and Part D data.
478.features_to_create: 1) Self-referral bundle: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of NDCs dispensed by a pharmacy sharing the prescriber's owner TIN alongside a Schedule II fill; fires when the count exceeds one without a supporting diagnosis; action prepay edit. 2) Writer-prescriber mismatch: on prescription record, compute whether the individual documented as writing the order holds an active licence and DEA registration; fires on exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Opioid quantity outlier: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute total morphine-milligram-equivalents dispensed per beneficiary; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

479.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on high-cost genetic CPT claims has no prior evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiary. Requisition forms show identical prepopulated diagnosis codes across large numbers of unrelated beneficiaries. One telemedicine ordering NPI orders panels for beneficiaries spread across many distant states in a week. The same specimen and beneficiary are billed by two lab NPIs under a pass-through arrangement within days. Lab claim volume rises sharply against its own trailing baseline following an ownership change filed in PECOS.
479.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the genetic test date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 2) Diagnosis-template uniformity: on ordering NPI x CPT, compute the share of ordered claims carrying the single most frequent diagnosis code; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Pass-through duplication: on beneficiary x CPT x 30 days, compute the distinct count of billing lab NPIs paid for the same test; fires when the count exceeds one; action claim suspension.

480.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count NDC fills per beneficiary from pharmacies sharing a PECOS owner with the prescribing NPI on the claim. Oxycodone NDC quantities per prescriber on Part D PDE data sit far above same-specialty peers for nine beneficiaries. Prescription images show one pre-signed prescriber signature with different handwriting on drug and quantity fields. Ordering NPI on the claim belongs to a physician while the state licence board file shows the writer is an unlicensed intern. Beneficiary receives multiple high-cost non-controlled NDCs on the same date as each opioid fill, a bundled dispensing pattern.
480.features_to_create: 1) Owner-linked pharmacy loop: on prescriber NPI x pharmacy NPI, compute the share of that pharmacy's paid claims written by prescribers listed in its CMS-855 or PECOS ownership records; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Opioid-plus-bundle co-fill: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of distinct non-controlled NDCs paid alongside a Schedule II opioid NDC from the same pharmacy; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Prescriber daily impossibility: on prescriber NPI x date of service, compute total controlled-substance dosage units plus the count of distinct patients; fires when patient count exceeds what 24 clinic hours permit; action payment suspension.

481.ways_to_identify: In PDMP data, one prescriber NPI writes controlled-substance scripts for patients whose residence ZIPs span dozens of states. Pharmacy claims show the same prescriber NPI dominating oxycodone and promethazine-with-codeine NDC fills with no paid E/M claim for the patient. Cash-pay dispensing share for that prescriber's scripts is extreme in PBM and pharmacy remittance records versus peers. Patient identity fields on scripts fail SSN and date-of-birth matching against the payer's eligibility file and NPPES-verified demographics. Chart entries produced under ADR carry creation timestamps after the Board of Health complaint date but bear earlier service dates.
481.features_to_create: 1) Opioid geographic dispersion: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the count of distinct patient states on filled oxycodone and promethazine-codeine NDCs in PDMP and pharmacy claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Script without encounter: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary, compute the days between the controlled-substance fill date and the nearest paid E/M claim by that NPI; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action claim suspension. 3) Backdating detector: on claim line, compute the gap in days between the electronic record creation timestamp supplied under ADR and the billed date of service; fires when the record postdates service beyond the documentation window; action postpay audit.

482.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, presumptive and definitive UDT CPT codes appear on the same date of service for nearly every patient of an ordering NPI. The ordering practice's requisition forms obtained under ADR show pre-checked panels identical across all beneficiaries of that TIN. Urine hormone and specimen-validity CPT lines are billed separately alongside UDT codes already inclusive of validity testing. A single laboratory NPI receives orders from a handful of ordering NPIs whose UDT rate far exceeds same-specialty peers. Collection staff placed in the practice appear as the lab's employees in CMS-855B enrolment records while ordering under the practice's NPI.
482.features_to_create: 1) Reflex-to-definitive ratio: on ordering NPI x month, compute the share of presumptive UDT claims followed by definitive UDT CPT lines on the same date of service; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Bundled validity unbundling: on claim line, compute the count of specimen-validity and urine hormone CPT codes billed with a UDT code on the same date of service for the same beneficiary; fires when that count exceeds zero against NCCI bundling rules; action prepay edit. 3) Order concentration: on laboratory NPI, compute the share of UDT revenue attributable to the top ordering NPIs and the distinct-beneficiary uniformity of ordered panels; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR), then postpay audit.

483.ways_to_identify: Payroll-Based Journal staffing hours reported to CMS exceed hours supported by the facility's payroll register and tax filings for the same quarter. Named staff on submitted staffing sheets hold no active licence in the state nurse aide registry or licence board file. Individuals counted as direct care appear in job-code fields as kitchen, laundry or administrative staff in payroll records. Reported nursing hours per resident day sit just above the state minimum ratio in every reporting period with implausibly low variance. Staffing spikes reported to the Pennsylvania Department of Health cluster on survey dates recorded in the state inspection file.
483.features_to_create: 1) PBJ-payroll reconciliation: on facility CCN x quarter, compute the difference between direct-care hours reported in Payroll-Based Journal and paid hours in the payroll register by job code; fires when the reported hours exceed payroll hours; action postpay audit. 2) Ghost staff registry match: on facility CCN x reported staff name, compute the count of listed direct-care individuals with no active record in the state nurse aide or licence board file; fires when that count exceeds zero on an exact registry mismatch; action site visit. 3) Survey-day staffing spike: on facility CCN x date, compute the ratio of reported nursing hours per resident day on inspection dates to the facility's own trailing non-survey baseline; fires when above that baseline by the calibrated percentile versus state peers; action site visit.

484.ways_to_identify: Member-submitted reimbursement invoices name a dental practice whose NPI and TIN do not match NPPES or the plan's provider file. No corresponding dental encounter claim exists from that practice for the member on the invoiced dates of service. Invoice numbers, fonts and totals repeat across multiple submissions from the same member in the fund's imaged claim records. Reimbursement payments route to a bank account already tied to the member in the fund's payment file rather than a provider account. The member's out-of-pocket reimbursement dollars far exceed same-plan peers within the benefit year.
484.features_to_create: 1) Provider existence check: on member reimbursement claim line, compute the exact match of the invoiced provider name, NPI and TIN against NPPES and the state dental licence file; fires on registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Encounter corroboration: on member x invoiced date of service, compute the count of corroborating provider-submitted dental claims or eligibility-verified encounters; fires when that count is zero; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Member reimbursement velocity: on member x benefit year, compute the count and dollar sum of self-submitted out-of-pocket invoices; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-plan peers; action claim suspension, then postpay audit.

485.ways_to_identify: Enrollment applications report projected household income sitting narrowly inside the fully-subsidized band while IRS and state wage data show far lower income. One broker NPN or agent ID appears on enrollments spanning thousands of consumers across unrelated addresses in the marketplace enrollment file. Applicant Social Security numbers and dates of birth fail SSA verification in the marketplace identity-proofing record. Enrollee mailing addresses resolve to shelters, mail drops or addresses reused across dozens of unrelated applications. Enrolled members generate no claims at all in the insurer's remittance history while premium subsidies pay monthly.
485.features_to_create: 1) Income-band clustering: on broker NPN x month, compute the share of enrollments with attested income inside the fully-subsidized band and the mismatch rate against IRS and wage-data trusted sources; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer brokers; action payment suspension of commissions. 2) Address and identity reuse: on application, compute the distinct count of unrelated applicants sharing the same mailing address plus the count of SSA verification failures; fires when reuse exceeds a household-plausible count or verification fails; action prepay edit on subsidy payment. 3) Zero-utilization subsidy: on enrollee x plan year, compute the sum of advance premium tax credit dollars paid against the count of paid medical and pharmacy claims; fires when subsidy dollars accrue with zero claims beyond the calibrated percentile duration; action documentation request (ADR), then postpay audit.

486.ways_to_identify: At marketplace application, attested household income sits just above the Medicaid floor for fully subsidized plans across an implausible share of one agent NPN's book. The Federal Data Services Hub returns an income data-matching inconsistency against IRS and SSA records for those same applications. Many applications from one agent NPN share a single mailing address, phone or bank routing detail in the enrollment record. Enrollees show zero paid medical or pharmacy claims after effectuation despite full-year APTC payments to the issuer. Special enrollment periods are claimed by loss-of-Medicaid attestation with no corresponding state Medicaid denial record on file.
486.features_to_create: 1) Income-floor clustering: on agent NPN x plan year, compute the share of submitted applications with attested household income within one FPL point above the subsidy minimum, over marketplace application income fields; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-market agent peers; action prepay edit on APTC effectuation plus documentation request (ADR). 2) Identity-element reuse: on agent NPN, compute the distinct-value count of enrollees divided by the distinct count of addresses, phones and SSN-prefix groups in the enrollment file; fires when the ratio exceeds one household per address beyond the agent's trailing baseline; action claim suspension of APTC and site visit. 3) Zero-utilization subsidy: on enrollee x issuer, compute the sum of APTC paid months minus months with any paid medical or pharmacy claim; fires when APTC months exceed zero and claim months equal zero for a full policy year; action postpay audit with agent commission recoupment.

487.ways_to_identify: At Medicaid eligibility determination, the employment verification letters submitted by multiple applicants are near-identical in wording, layout and employer letterhead fields. The signer named on those letters matches a record in the Death Master File with a death date preceding the letter date. Attested wages on the Medicaid application contradict quarterly wage data for the same SSN in the state wage-match and IRS income file. Worker SSNs listed on city shelter-contract invoices belong to individuals with no state wage record for that employer or quarter. The contractor's invoiced material costs exceed vendor pedigree and purchase-order documentation held by the contracting agency.
487.features_to_create: 1) Deceased signer check: on eligibility case, compute the match between the verification letter signer's name and SSN and the Death Master File death date versus the document date; fires on an exact registry match with death preceding the document; action claim suspension of eligibility and postpay audit. 2) Template letter reuse: on employer TIN x quarter, compute the count of distinct Medicaid applicants submitting employment letters with identical text hash and signature block; fires when that count exceeds one; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Wage-match gap: on applicant SSN, compute attested monthly income minus state quarterly wage-file income divided by wage-file income; fires when the negative gap exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-program applicants; action prepay edit on benefit issuance.

488.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim here and no adjudication point, so no payer-side edit applies. The nearest detection route is municipal accounts-payable matching of subcontractor invoices to retailer receipts and pedigree documentation. Vendor beneficial-ownership disclosures compared against state corporate registries would expose shell intermediaries sharing the prime's bank account.
488.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on vendor TIN x bank account, compute the count of distinct city vendors depositing to one account and the markup ratio of invoiced price to retailer receipt price, and refer accounts above the calibrated percentile to procurement audit.

489.ways_to_identify: At benefit adjudication, the claimed combat deployment has no matching record in DMDC deployment files or the veteran's DD-214 foreign service block. The service treatment record contains no in-theater injury entry or line-of-duty determination for the asserted blast event. Personnel records show non-deployable status during the exact date range asserted in the compensation application. The PTSD stressor statement lacks any corroborating unit record, casualty report or award citation in the personnel file. The claimed diagnosis rests solely on self-report captured in a single VA clinician note with no prior treatment history in the health record.
489.features_to_create: 1) Deployment registry mismatch: on claimant file, compute the overlap in days between asserted deployment dates on the compensation application and DMDC deployment and DD-214 foreign service dates; fires when overlap equals zero; action claim suspension pending documentation request (ADR). 2) Stressor corroboration gap: on claimant x claimed stressor event, compute the count of independent corroborating records in personnel, casualty and line-of-duty files; fires when that count equals zero; action prepay edit before rating decision. 3) Self-report-only diagnosis: on rendering NPI x claimant, compute the count of prior encounters documenting the claimed condition before the compensation application date; fires when that count equals zero and the rating rests on one encounter; action postpay audit.

490.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, dates of service fall on days when the rendering NPI's own claims cluster in a different state, evidenced by other payers' place-of-service and location data. Billed office visit and counseling units on a single date exceed the hours the rendering NPI could physically work in 24 hours. Smoking cessation counseling CPT codes are billed for beneficiaries whose claim history shows no tobacco-use diagnosis. Every licensed prescriber on the group TIN has zero prescription fills in state PDMP records on the billed treatment dates. Encounter volume for office-based opioid treatment is uniform day to day, unlike the provider's own trailing appointment pattern.
490.features_to_create: 1) Impossible service day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of time-based CPT unit minutes across all payers and MCOs; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours or exceeds clinic operating hours; action prepay edit and payment suspension. 2) Absent-provider day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of billed encounters on dates with no PDMP dispensing, no EVV record and no facility badge or travel corroboration; fires when the count is above zero on more than the provider's trailing baseline of such days; action documentation request (ADR) then postpay audit. 3) Unsupported counseling code: on claim line, compute whether a tobacco-use or opioid-use diagnosis appears on the beneficiary's claim history within the lookback; fires on an exact absence of any supporting diagnosis; action prepay edit.

491.ways_to_identify: There is no insurance claim and no adjudication point here, since the controlled substances were bought from a wholesaler and never billed to a payer. The nearest detection route is ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree data showing hydrocodone and oxycodone purchases far above same-species veterinary practice norms for the DEA registration. A second route is the DEA registrant biennial inventory and dispensing log reconciliation, where purchased units minus documented dispensed and destroyed units leaves a large unaccounted balance.
491.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Wholesaler purchase outlier: on DEA registrant number x quarter, compute the sum of Schedule II and III dosage units purchased from ARCOS and distributor pedigree files; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-registrant-class veterinary peers; action site visit by the state board and DEA inspection referral. 2) Inventory reconciliation gap: on DEA registrant number x audit period, compute purchased units minus dispensed, destroyed and on-hand inventory units from the required DEA records; fires when the unaccounted balance exceeds zero; action postpay audit of licensure and administrative inspection warrant.

492.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, so no payer-side prepay edit exists here. The nearest route is regulator-side verification of certified small-entity status against SAM.gov, IRS receipts data and corporate parent filings. Ownership change filings showing acquisition by a larger holding company should void prior small-entity fee certifications automatically.
492.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on licensee entity EIN, compute the count of affiliated entities sharing a common parent in SAM.gov and Dun & Bradstreet, and refer certifications where the aggregated receipts exceed the regulatory size standard to fee recovery.

493.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, orthotic L-code claims carry an ordering NPI with no prior E/M encounter with that beneficiary. One ordering NPI signs brace orders for thousands of distinct beneficiaries across many states in a quarter. Behavioral health claims list rendering staff whose NPI and state licence board file show no credential on the date of service. Beneficiary identifiers appear on counseling claims whose service dates conflict with the same beneficiary's inpatient or facility claims. Pharmacy claims show controlled-substance NDCs from one prescriber NPI at morphine-equivalent volumes above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers.
493.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim linking that NPI and beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Signer dispersion: on ordering NPI x month, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries and distinct beneficiary states on DMEPOS orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Rendering credential mismatch: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute an exact match of the NPI against the state licence board file and OIG LEIE effective dates; fires on any registry mismatch; action claim suspension.

494.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, residential and IOP per-diem claims exceed the facility's licensed bed count on the same date of service. Group therapy HCPCS units billed per counselor NPI per day exceed feasible clinical hours in 24 hours. Dispensed buprenorphine or methadone NDC quantities exceed the facility DEA registrant's ARCOS purchase totals for the same period. Beneficiary attendance rosters requested by ADR are absent for a large share of billed session dates. Beneficiaries show billed treatment days overlapping paid inpatient or incarceration-period claims in the payer's own remittance history.
494.features_to_create: 1) Bed-capacity overflow: on facility NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries with paid per-diem residential lines divided by licensed beds on the state licence file; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action prepay edit. 2) Counselor hour impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed therapy units converted to minutes across all group and individual codes; fires when total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Dispense-versus-pedigree gap: on facility DEA registrant x quarter, compute dispensed controlled-substance units from claims minus ARCOS wholesaler acquisition units; fires when dispensed exceeds acquired; action site visit.

495.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, RPM CPT 99454 device-supply lines appear with no matching device supply or DME acquisition record for that beneficiary. Billed 99457 treatment-management minutes per rendering NPI per day exceed feasible staffed hours in 24 hours. The 99454 line is billed in a 30-day period without the required 16 days of transmitted readings documented on ADR. Beneficiaries have no prior E/M encounter with the billing NPI establishing the monitored chronic condition. The practice's RPM volume rises from near-zero to peer-top-decile within weeks of a PECOS ownership or specialty change.
495.features_to_create: 1) Device-supply substantiation: on beneficiary x billing NPI x 30-day period, compute the count of documented transmission days supporting CPT 99454; fires when fewer than the 16 days the code requires; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Monitoring minute impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of 99457 and 99458 minutes across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) RPM volume ramp: on billing NPI x month, compute paid RPM line counts versus that NPI's trailing twelve-month baseline; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit.

496.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the share of the surgeon's female patients receiving hysterectomy or sling CPT codes exceeds same-specialty peer rates. Urodynamic study CPT 51728 and pelvic ultrasound units per beneficiary per year exceed the provider's own trailing baseline. Diagnosis codes supporting incontinence surgery appear first on the claim dated the same day as the surgical booking. Prior-authorisation submissions repeat identical symptom narratives verbatim across unrelated beneficiaries. Post-operative complication and readmission claims for this rendering NPI's patients exceed peer rates in the payer's remittance history.
496.features_to_create: 1) Surgical propensity outlier: on rendering NPI x year, compute the ratio of major gynecologic surgery claims to the count of distinct female patients with any E/M claim; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Diagnostic workup stacking: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of urodynamic and pelvic ultrasound units billed within 90 days before a surgical CPT; fires when above the provider's trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Harm signal rate: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the rate of post-surgical complication or readmission claims per 100 operated beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

497.ways_to_identify: At enrolment and adjudication, the rendering NPI on psychotherapy claims matches an active entry on the OIG LEIE exclusion file. The individual appears as employed staff on the group's CMS-855B managing-employee fields despite exclusion. Billed psychotherapy CPT 90837 minutes per rendering NPI per day exceed feasible hours in 24 hours. Telehealth session claims lack corresponding platform connection logs when requested by documentation request. NPPES shows the rendering NPI enumerated in a state distant from all billed beneficiaries' residence ZIPs.
497.features_to_create: 1) Exclusion registry match: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute an exact match against OIG LEIE names, NPIs and exclusion effective dates; fires on any active exclusion covering the service date; action claim suspension. 2) Staff roster screen: on group TIN x quarter, compute the count of CMS-855B listed owners, managing employees and rendering NPIs matching LEIE or state licence-board sanction files; fires when the count exceeds zero; action payment suspension. 3) Therapy hour impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of psychotherapy CPT time-code minutes across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit.

498.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, presumptive and definitive urine drug codes 80305-80307 and G0480-G0483 repeat on a fixed weekly cadence per beneficiary for months. The ordering NPI on the requisition has no corresponding office or telehealth encounter claim near most collection dates of service. Definitive testing is billed on the same date of service as a presumptive screen without a documented abnormal presumptive result. One residential treatment facility address supplies nearly all beneficiaries on a single lab NPI's toxicology claims. Ordering NPI signature dates on the lab's requisition and standing-order forms precede dates of service by up to a year.
498.features_to_create: 1) Standing-order cadence: on beneficiary x lab NPI, compute the count of distinct toxicology dates of service per week for 80305-80307 and G0480-G0483 over a rolling 90 days; fires when the weekly count is constant and above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Orderless requisition: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the days between the toxicology date of service and the nearest E/M or behavioral health encounter claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Reflex-without-trigger and facility concentration: on lab NPI x facility address, compute the ratio of definitive G0480-G0483 lines to presumptive lines with a documented abnormal result, plus the share of beneficiaries sharing one residential address; fires when either exceeds the provider's own trailing baseline and peer percentile; action payment suspension.

499.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, summed timed psychotherapy units for CPT 90832, 90834 and 90837 on one rendering NPI exceed 16 service hours in a day. The same rendering NPI bills 90837 for nearly every encounter, far above the 90834 share seen in peer remittance history. Claim dates of service fall on dates the beneficiary has inpatient or other facility claims that preclude an outpatient therapy session. Beneficiary rosters show identical session lengths and start times repeated across unrelated patients on the same date of service. Requested progress notes are near-verbatim duplicates across beneficiaries, with no signature or licence number matching the state board file.
499.features_to_create: 1) Impossible clinician day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total therapy minutes implied by CPT 90832, 90834, 90837 and 90853 units; fires when the total exceeds 16 hours in a 24-hour day; action prepay edit. 2) Highest-intensity code share: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of 90837 lines to all psychotherapy lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers and above the provider's trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Conflicting-location overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of outpatient psychotherapy lines overlapping an inpatient or facility stay on the beneficiary's other claims; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension.

500.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, definitive urine drug testing G-codes carry an ordering NPI that has no E/M or counseling claim with that beneficiary. A single substance use clinic NPI accounts for nearly all of one lab's presumptive and definitive UDT referral volume. Definitive testing panels bill the maximum drug-class tier on nearly every specimen with no presumptive screen first. Beneficiaries show weekly UDT claims far exceeding the frequency in their treatment plan documented on prior-authorisation records. The lab's CMS-855B ownership and PECOS records show payments or common addresses linking it to the referring clinic's owner.
500.features_to_create: 1) Referral concentration: on laboratory NPI x quarter, compute the share of UDT claim lines whose ordering NPI belongs to a single clinic TIN; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit and payment suspension. 2) Order without encounter: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between UDT date of service and the nearest E/M or SUD treatment claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 3) Definitive tier saturation: on laboratory NPI x month, compute the ratio of highest-tier definitive UDT lines to total UDT lines and the presumptive-to-definitive ratio; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action documentation request (ADR).

501.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed personal care and respite units for the attendant NPI exceed 24 hours on given dates of service. EVV visit records show no check-in or check-out matching the billed units on those dates. Submitted timesheets carry signatures dated after the billing date on the payer's remittance history. Two beneficiaries are billed by the same attendant for overlapping minutes at different service addresses. Billed hours exceed the authorised hours on the Medicaid service plan and prior-authorisation record.
501.features_to_create: 1) Attendant hour ceiling: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of personal care and respite units converted to hours across all beneficiaries; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours or overlapping visit minutes occur at distinct addresses; action prepay edit. 2) EVV reconciliation: on claim line, compute the difference between billed units and EVV-verified visit minutes for the same beneficiary, attendant and date; fires when no matching EVV record exists or the gap is nonzero; action claim suspension. 3) Authorisation overrun: on beneficiary x attendant NPI x week, compute billed hours minus prior-authorised hours; fires when the difference is positive; action prepay edit.

502.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, J0600 edetate calcium disodium claims carry no lead poisoning ICD-10 diagnosis, or carry one unsupported by any prior encounter. The billing NPI shows lead-poisoning diagnoses on a share of its panel far above same-specialty peers. Beneficiaries have no blood lead level laboratory claim preceding the chelation infusion date of service. The same beneficiary receives repeated chelation infusion lines across months without any interval lead testing claim. Infusion administration codes are billed in office place of service at volumes above the provider's own trailing baseline.
502.features_to_create: 1) Lead diagnosis without test: on beneficiary x billing NPI, compute the count of J0600 chelation lines with a lead toxicity diagnosis but zero blood lead level laboratory claims in the lookback window; fires when the count is above zero; action prepay edit. 2) Diagnosis prevalence outlier: on billing NPI x year, compute the share of distinct beneficiaries carrying heavy-metal toxicity diagnoses; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Repeat infusion series: on beneficiary x HCPCS J0600, compute the count of infusion dates over twelve months without an intervening lead level result; fires when the count exceeds the labelled treatment course; action prior-authorisation requirement.

503.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point here, since the theft is card data captured at retail point of sale. The nearest detection route is EBT processor monitoring for card-present transactions clustering at terminals previously used by other compromised cards. Card networks' common point of purchase analysis on settlement files identifies the specific store terminals where the compromised accounts overlap.
503.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on merchant terminal ID x week, compute the count of distinct EBT accounts later reporting disputed transactions, and refer terminals above the calibrated threshold for physical inspection.

504.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since the loss is unremitted employment tax on cash wages. The nearest detection route is IRS matching of Forms 941 wage totals against bank cash withdrawal volumes reported on currency transaction reports. State workers' compensation payroll filings compared with the same employer's federal wage returns show the same understatement.
504.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on employer EIN x quarter, compute the ratio of aggregate cash withdrawals in CTR filings to wages reported on Form 941 and refer ratios above the calibrated percentile versus same-industry peers.

505.ways_to_identify: At Medicaid eligibility determination, the applicant's declared income has no matching wage or 1099 record in the state new hire and income verification files. Business registration and contractor licence records list the applicant as owner of an active roofing entity absent from the eligibility application. The mailing address on the eligibility file resolves to a commercial mailbox rather than a residence in the postal address file. Asset and check-casher currency transaction data show deposits far above the declared household income for the eligibility period. Names and Social Security numbers on associated Forms 1099 belong to relatives rather than the actual payee in IRS matching.
505.features_to_create: 1) Income declaration mismatch: on beneficiary Medicaid case, compute declared annual household income minus the sum of IRS and state wage, 1099 and business receipt records for the same year; fires when the gap exceeds the eligibility threshold; action claim suspension and eligibility redetermination. 2) Hidden ownership screen: on applicant SSN, compute the count of active business entities listing that person as officer in the secretary of state and contractor licence files; fires when the count is above zero and unreported; action documentation request. 3) Commercial address flag: on eligibility case address, compute an exact match against the USPS commercial mail receiving agency file; fires on exact registry match; action site visit.

506.ways_to_identify: At Medicaid eligibility determination, declared income is contradicted by state and federal wage, 1099 and business receipt files for the same tax year. Secretary of state and contractor licence registries show the applicant owning an active paving business not disclosed on the application. The residence address on the eligibility record matches a commercial mail receiving agency in the USPS file. Check-casher currency transaction reports show deposit volumes incompatible with the declared low-income status. Forms 1099 tied to the business carry relatives' taxpayer identification numbers rather than the actual earner in IRS matching.
506.features_to_create: 1) Income verification gap: on Medicaid case x benefit year, compute declared income minus summed IRS, state wage and 1099 amounts; fires when the difference exceeds the program income limit; action claim suspension and redetermination. 2) Undisclosed business ownership: on applicant SSN, compute the count of active entity registrations and contractor licences naming that individual; fires when that count is above zero with no disclosed self-employment income; action documentation request. 3) Address registry mismatch: on case mailing address, compute exact match to the commercial mail receiving agency file; fires on exact registry match; action site visit.

507.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the same COVID-19 test CPT for the same beneficiary and specimen date appears on claims to Medicare, the state program and a commercial payer. Claim lines bill high-complexity or add-on test codes on specimens with no corresponding collection or accession record in the lab's submitted logs. Test volume per day at the lab NPI exceeds the instrument throughput declared on its CMS-855B enrolment. Beneficiaries on the claims have residence ZIPs with no other encounter linking them to that laboratory. Billed test counts exceed reagent and supply purchases in wholesaler pedigree data for the same period.
507.features_to_create: 1) Cross-payer duplicate: on beneficiary x test CPT x date of service, compute the count of distinct payers billed by the same laboratory NPI; fires when that count exceeds one without a coordination-of-benefits indicator; action prepay edit. 2) Throughput impossibility: on laboratory NPI x date of service, compute total billed tests divided by declared instrument capacity and staffed hours; fires when the implied run rate exceeds physical capacity; action claim suspension. 3) Reagent-to-claim ratio: on laboratory NPI x month, compute billed test count minus test kits purchased in wholesaler pedigree data; fires when the difference is positive; action postpay audit.

508.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, electrical stimulation codes are billed with acute pain or neuropathy diagnoses outside the device's covered indications in the national coverage determination. The same beneficiary receives stimulation, vitamin injection and ENFD punch biopsy lines on the same date of service in a repeating bundle. Provider adoption clusters sharply by distributor territory, with new billers appearing in cohorts after a single marketing contact. Ownership fields on CMS-855 filings show treating providers holding equity in the distributorship supplying the device. One laboratory receives nearly all ENFD biopsy referrals from that same provider cohort.
