508.features_to_create: 1) Non-covered indication edit: on claim line, compute whether the electrical stimulation HCPCS and diagnosis pair matches an indication listed in the coverage determination; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Bundled triad velocity: on rendering NPI x month, compute the share of beneficiaries receiving stimulation, vitamin injection and ENFD biopsy within seven days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Distributor-owner overlap: on rendering NPI, compute graph degree linking its CMS-855 owners to distributor and laboratory TINs receiving its referrals; fires when any shared owner exists; action postpay audit.

509.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, DME claims carry no ordering physician NPI with a prior face-to-face encounter for that beneficiary in the lookback window. Rental line items continue after the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File or after equipment pickup. Massage and therapy claims pair mutually exclusive E/M codes on the same date of service, tripping NCCI edits. Telehealth place-of-service and modifier combinations conflict with in-person therapy codes billed the same day. Wheelchair-related therapy codes appear for beneficiaries with no wheelchair HCPCS in their claim history.
509.features_to_create: 1) Order authorisation check: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the count of face-to-face E/M claims between that NPI and the beneficiary before the DME date of service; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit. 2) Mutually exclusive pairing: on rendering NPI x beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of code pairs violating NCCI mutually exclusive and telehealth place-of-service rules; fires when the count is above zero; action claim suspension. 3) Equipment-dependent therapy: on beneficiary, compute whether a device-specific therapy code is billed with zero prior claims for that device HCPCS; fires on exact absence; action documentation request (ADR).

510.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, hospice election periods extend far beyond six months with no documented decline in the certification of terminal illness. Live discharge rates at the hospice NPI are above the calibrated percentile versus peer hospices. Beneficiaries on the hospice benefit continue to have curative treatment or hospital claims from other providers. Face-to-face recertification encounters required at the third benefit period are missing from the attending NPI's claim history. The certifying physician's NPI signs terminal illness certifications for a share of the hospice's census far above peers.
510.features_to_create: 1) Long-stay concentration: on hospice NPI x quarter, compute the share of beneficiaries with cumulative hospice days beyond two benefit periods and no hospitalisation; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer hospices; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Live discharge rate: on hospice NPI x year, compute live discharges divided by total discharges from claim status codes; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action postpay audit. 3) Recertification encounter gap: on beneficiary x benefit period, compute days between the recertification date and the nearest face-to-face encounter claim by the attending or hospice physician; fires when no encounter exists within the required window; action prepay edit.

511.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since the money came from private investors rather than a benefit program. The nearest detection route is verifying the claimed purchase orders directly with the named hospital or provider purchasers before funding. State securities regulators can match the promoter's promissory note offerings against bank records showing gambling and investor-to-investor transfers.
511.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on lender or investor bank account, compute the share of incoming funds paid out to earlier investors within thirty days and refer accounts above the calibrated threshold to securities regulators.

512.ways_to_identify: There is no benefit claim and no adjudication point, since the violation is controlled substance recordkeeping at a registered site. The nearest detection route is DEA comparison of ARCOS distributor shipment data to the registrant against the site's biennial inventory and dispensing logs. Registrant-level purchase volumes of contrast-sedation controlled substances can be compared with imaging procedure volumes billed under the site's NPI.
512.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on DEA registration number x year, compute ARCOS units received minus units documented as dispensed, wasted or on hand, and schedule an inspection when the unexplained difference is above zero.

513.ways_to_identify: At payment reconciliation, the capitation rate on submitted invoices does not match the rate in the contracting agency's approved rate schedule. Per-member-per-month amounts paid diverge from the actuarially certified rate file for the same enrolment month. Enrolment counts on the invoice exceed the eligibility file's member months for that plan and period. Retained credit balances persist on the plan's ledger beyond the sixty-day overpayment return deadline. Identical rate variances appear simultaneously across all plans under the same program, indicating a shared rate error.
513.features_to_create: 1) Rate schedule match: on plan TIN x month, compute invoiced per-member-per-month rate minus the contracted rate in the approved rate file; fires on any nonzero difference; action prepay edit. 2) Member month reconciliation: on plan TIN x month, compute invoiced member months minus eligibility file member months; fires when the difference is positive; action claim suspension. 3) Overpayment retention clock: on plan TIN, compute days since identification of a credit balance or rate variance; fires when days exceed the statutory sixty-day return deadline; action payment suspension and postpay audit.

514.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since the loss is diverted trust and Social Security funds. The nearest detection route is Social Security representative payee change monitoring when benefits redirect to a third-party account. Bank anti-money-laundering review can compare fiduciary account outflows to a church or personal accounts against the trust's stated purpose.
514.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on beneficiary Social Security account, compute the count of payee or direct-deposit account changes within twelve months and require identity verification when above the calibrated threshold.

515.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim for the street sales themselves, but the upstream office visits and fills are visible. At adjudication, oxycodone fills concentrate among a small set of prescriber NPIs with short-interval repeat visits from the same beneficiaries. Prescription drug monitoring program data show beneficiaries filling at multiple pharmacies with overlapping days supply. Cash-pay fills of the same prescriber's oxycodone appear alongside insured fills, hiding volume from the payer.
515.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber opioid concentration: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute total oxycodone morphine milligram equivalents dispensed per distinct patient from PDMP and pharmacy claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Overlapping fill days: on beneficiary x opioid NDC, compute overlapping days supply across distinct dispensing pharmacy NPIs; fires when overlap days are above zero; action prepay edit and pharmacy lock-in.

516.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, CPT 93922, 93923 and 93924 are billed by providers whose only vascular equipment is a photoplethysmography device not performing ankle brachial index measurement. Providers newly billing these codes cluster by device distributor territory and start dates. Non-invasive physiologic vascular study volume per provider is far above same-specialty peers with no vascular specialty on NPPES taxonomy. The same beneficiary receives repeat vascular studies at short intervals with no intervening abnormal finding or treatment claim. Submitted study reports lack segmental pressures and waveform documentation required by the coverage determination.
516.features_to_create: 1) Specialty-code mismatch: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the count of 93922-93924 lines where the NPPES taxonomy is non-vascular and no vascular procedure claims exist; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Device-code eligibility: on claim line, compute whether the vascular study code is supported by a documented ankle brachial index measurement in the ADR response; fires when documentation shows photoplethysmography only; action prepay edit. 3) Repeat study interval: on beneficiary x CPT, compute days between successive vascular study claims; fires when the gap is below the coverage determination's minimum interval; action claim suspension.

517.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since the losses are unemployment benefits, real property and trust funds. The nearest detection route is cross-state unemployment claim matching on Social Security number, bank routing and debit card mailing address. County recorder deed filings can be matched against the owner of record and require notarised identity verification before recording.
517.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on unemployment claimant SSN, compute the count of distinct states with active claims and the count of claims sharing one mailing address, and suspend disbursement when either exceeds one.

518.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, prescriptions from one clinic NPI dispense at pharmacies hundreds of miles away in multiple states within the same week. Patient identities on the prescriptions have no other claim history and addresses that fail USPS validation. Promethazine-codeine and Tussionex volumes per prescriber are far above same-specialty peers in PDMP dispensing data. Multiple patients on the same prescriber's controlled substance prescriptions share a single address or telephone number in the pharmacy record. Fills are predominantly cash-pay despite the patients holding coverage in the eligibility file.
518.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber geographic dispersion: on prescriber NPI x week, compute the count of distinct pharmacy states and the median miles from clinic to dispensing pharmacy; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Ghost patient screen: on patient record x prescriber NPI, compute the count of prior claims and the exact match of the address to USPS validated addresses; fires when zero prior claims and address validation fails; action claim suspension and site visit. 3) Shared identifier cluster: on prescriber NPI, compute the count of distinct controlled substance patients sharing one address or phone number in pharmacy records; fires when the count exceeds a household size; action postpay audit.

519.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since the losses are unpaid payroll taxes and an SBA loan. The nearest detection route is IRS matching of Forms W-2 withholding totals against Form 941 deposits for the same quarter. SBA underwriting can verify PPP payroll certifications against filed 941s and state unemployment wage reports before disbursement.
519.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on employer EIN x quarter, compute withheld tax reported on W-2 and 941 filings minus deposits received, and hold loan disbursement when the difference is positive.

520.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare EIDBI and Housing Stabilization service dates against the beneficiary's Death Master File and Medicaid eligibility span. Sum billed service units per rendering technician NPI per day to expose totals exceeding 24 hours across clients. Check each billed behavioral technician against the DHS provider registry and state EIDBI qualification roster for a credential on the date of service. Compare Housing Focused Plan signatures and staff signature blocks across agencies for identical fabricated names appearing at unrelated TINs. Compare billed units to the DHS prior-authorization amount, since billing exactly to the authorized ceiling every month signals fabricated encounters.
520.features_to_create: 1) Impossible staff day: on rendering staff ID x date of service, compute summed billed service minutes across all beneficiaries and agencies; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours or overlapping visit minutes exist; action prepay edit. 2) Deceased or ineligible service date: on claim line, compute the gap in days between date of service and the beneficiary's Death Master File or eligibility termination date; fires when the service date is after that date; action claim suspension. 3) Authorization-ceiling saturation: on provider NPI x beneficiary x month, compute billed units divided by the DHS prior-authorized units; fires when the ratio equals one for a share of beneficiaries above the calibrated percentile versus same-program peers; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension.

521.ways_to_identify: On MDS assessments, compute the share of Medicare stays coded Ultra-High RUG and compare to same-state SNF peers. Check therapy minutes recorded on MDS against the therapy logs and staffing hours reported on the facility cost report. At adjudication, compare outpatient individual therapy CPT 97110 volume against group therapy CPT 97150 at the same site and hour. Verify a physician-signed plan of care exists in the medical record for each outpatient therapy episode before the certification period lapses. Look for therapy minutes clustering just above the Ultra-High RUG threshold in the payer's own remittance history.
521.features_to_create: 1) RUG concentration: on facility NPI x quarter, compute the fraction of Part A days billed at Ultra-High RUG over total days from MDS-linked claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state SNF peers; action documentation request (ADR) then postpay audit. 2) Individual-versus-group impossibility: on rendering therapist NPI x date of service, compute summed individual therapy minutes from timed CPT units plus concurrent group sessions; fires when the sum exceeds available clinical minutes in the shift; action prepay edit. 3) Missing plan-of-care certification: on claim line, compute presence of a signed plan of care with a physician NPI and signature date within the certification window; fires when no matching certification exists; action claim suspension.

522.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check whether the referring NPI on OTC COVID test kit claims has any other claim relationship with the beneficiary. Compare the billing chiropractic taxonomy in NPPES against the HCPCS billed, since test-kit supply is outside that scope. Count distinct beneficiary states per billing NPI per week on kit claims and compare to the enrolled service area. Query the referring NPI's own claim submissions, since a credential used only as referrer with zero rendering activity signals misappropriation. Compare per-beneficiary kit quantities against the program's per-month allowance in the payer's remittance history.
522.features_to_create: 1) Referrer-without-relationship: on claim line x referring NPI, compute the count of prior encounters between that referring NPI and the beneficiary in the lookback; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit. 2) Taxonomy-scope mismatch: on billing NPI x HCPCS, compute an exact match between the NPPES primary taxonomy and the allowed specialty list for the code; fires on registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Kit quantity and dispersion: on billing NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiaries billed the kit HCPCS and distinct beneficiary states; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers or per-beneficiary allowance is exceeded; action payment suspension.

523.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check for any evaluation-and-management or telehealth claim by the ordering NPI for the beneficiary before the CGx date of service. Count distinct beneficiaries and distinct states on CGx orders per ordering NPI per week against same-specialty peers. Compare the ordering physician's state licences in the state board file to the beneficiary residence states on the claims. Compute the share of that ordering NPI's total Medicare activity that is CGx orders routed to a small set of lab TINs. Check the beneficiary's diagnosis history for a cancer or hereditary-risk diagnosis supporting the 81400-series codes billed.
523.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between CGx date of service and the most recent E/M or telehealth claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct lab billing NPIs on CGx orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension. 3) Licence-state mismatch: on claim line, compute exact match between beneficiary residence state and the ordering NPI's active state board licences; fires on registry mismatch; action claim suspension.

524.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, verify a prior E/M or telehealth encounter between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary before the CGx test date. Count distinct beneficiaries per ordering NPI per week on CGx orders versus same-specialty peers. Match beneficiary residence states to the ordering physician's licences in the state board file. Compute the concentration of one orderer's CGx volume into a handful of laboratory TINs. Check whether the beneficiary has any oncology or family-history diagnosis in prior claims supporting the panel billed.
524.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the CGx date of service and the nearest prior E/M claim linking that NPI and beneficiary; fires when none exists in the lookback; action prepay edit. 2) Lab-orderer graph concentration: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute the share of ordered CGx claims paid to the single top laboratory TIN and the count of distinct beneficiaries; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action payment suspension. 3) Diagnosis support: on claim line, compute the count of supporting oncology or hereditary-risk ICD-10 codes in the beneficiary's 12-month claim history; fires when zero; action documentation request (ADR).

525.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point in this loan-eligibility case. The nearest detection route is cross-matching SBA second-draw applications to corporate affiliation, using EIN and common ownership recorded in SBIC portfolio filings. A second route is summing all PPP loans across affiliated borrowers sharing an ultimate parent before forgiveness is granted.
525.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on ultimate parent entity, compute the sum of second-draw PPP loan amounts across all EINs linked by ownership filings and fire before forgiveness when the sum exceeds the statutory group cap.

526.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim adjudication step in this PPP eligibility case. The nearest detection route is linking each borrower EIN to common owners disclosed on CMS-855A ownership and PECOS affiliation records for the facility chain. A further route is summing employee counts across commonly owned facility EINs from payroll tax filings before forgiveness of the loan.
526.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on ultimate owner identified in CMS-855A ownership fields, compute total employees across all commonly owned facility EINs and fire when the total exceeds the 500-employee small-business certification made on the application.

527.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this grant construction case. The nearest detection route is matching each invoice line certifying installed drainage systems and sump pumps to a dated inspection record and photograph in the grantee's file. A second route is comparing supplier purchase and delivery records for sump pump units against the number of homes invoiced.
527.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on invoice line x property address, compute the count of matching independent inspection sign-offs and material receipts for the certified component and withhold payment when the count is zero.

528.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare respiratory pathogen panel dates of service to the Death Master File date of death for each beneficiary. Check whether an ordering NPI on the panel claim has any treating relationship with the nursing home resident in prior claims. Compute the ratio of RPP CPT 87633 claims to COVID-only 87635 claims per laboratory NPI versus peer labs. Count distinct facility ZIPs and states served by one lab NPI in a week against its CMS-855B enrolment service area. Compare specimen collection dates on claims against facility visitor and staffing logs obtained during a site visit.
528.features_to_create: 1) Deceased-beneficiary testing: on claim line, compute days between the specimen date of service and the Death Master File date of death; fires when service date is after death; action prepay edit. 2) Reflex panel ratio: on laboratory NPI x month, compute RPP CPT units divided by COVID-only test units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty laboratory peers; action payment suspension. 3) Orderer relationship: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the count of prior encounters between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when zero for a facility-wide batch of same-day specimens; action documentation request (ADR).

529.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, match respiratory pathogen panel service dates against the Death Master File date of death. Verify the ordering NPI has a prior treating encounter with the nursing home resident in the beneficiary's claim history. Compute the share of a lab's volume in high-reimbursement panel codes versus single-target COVID codes relative to peer labs. Count distinct facilities and states billed by one lab NPI per week against its CMS-855B enrolled service area. Compare billed specimen counts against courier and reagent purchase records collected on a site visit.
529.features_to_create: 1) Post-death service date: on claim line, compute the gap in days between date of service and Death Master File date of death; fires when positive; action prepay edit. 2) Panel-versus-single ratio: on laboratory NPI x month, compute panel CPT units divided by total respiratory test units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Batch orderer anomaly: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute distinct beneficiaries with same-day panel orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers with no prior encounter on file; action documentation request (ADR).

530.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check for a preceding diagnostic angiogram or non-invasive vascular study claim before each angioplasty CPT on the beneficiary. Compute angioplasties per rendering NPI per year against same-specialty peers in the payer's remittance history. Check the beneficiary's diagnosis history for peripheral arterial disease or critical limb ischemia codes supporting intervention. Compute the rate of repeat angioplasties on the same vessel territory per beneficiary within short intervals. Compare procedures per operator per day against realistic procedure room minutes recorded on the facility claim.
530.features_to_create: 1) Missing diagnostic workup: on claim line x beneficiary, compute the count of qualifying non-invasive vascular study or diagnostic angiography claims in the lookback before the angioplasty date; fires when zero; action prepay edit. 2) Operator volume outlier: on rendering NPI x year, compute angioplasty CPT counts divided by distinct beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 3) Repeat intervention rate: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of angioplasties on the same limb within a rolling year; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline and peer rate; action documentation request (ADR).

531.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check the beneficiary's prior claims for any terminal diagnosis or declining-status utilization before the hospice election date. Compare the certifying physician NPI on the CMS hospice certification against that physician's own claim history with the beneficiary. Compute the share of the hospice's patients with live discharges or stays exceeding the six-month benchmark. Count distinct beneficiaries recruited from the same retirement home address across the hospice's admissions file. Verify the certifying physician's signature on documentation returned to an ADR against the state board licence file and PECOS.
531.features_to_create: 1) Certifier-relationship gap: on hospice election x certifying physician NPI, compute the count of prior encounters between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when zero; action prepay edit. 2) Long-stay live-discharge rate: on hospice NPI x quarter, compute the share of beneficiaries with stays beyond 180 days or discharged alive; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state hospice peers; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension. 3) Address clustering: on hospice NPI x residential address, compute distinct beneficiaries admitted within a rolling 90 days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action site visit.

532.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute daily morphine milligram equivalents per beneficiary from NDC, strength and days supply on pharmacy claims. Detect overlapping opioid and benzodiazepine fills from the same prescriber NPI in the beneficiary's pharmacy claim history. Compute the gap in days between successive fills of the same NDC to identify early refills against days supply. Compare the distance between beneficiary residence ZIP and prescriber practice ZIP in NPPES for long-distance patient patterns. Compare cash-paid fills reported in the state PDMP against the beneficiary's active insurance coverage.
532.features_to_create: 1) High-MME prescriber: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of patients whose daily MME from NDC strength and days supply exceeds the CDC threshold; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Dangerous combination: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute overlapping days supply of opioid and benzodiazepine or carisoprodol NDCs; fires when overlap days are above zero repeatedly; action prepay edit. 3) Early refill gap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute days between fill date and prior fill date minus prior days supply; fires when negative; action claim suspension.

533.ways_to_identify: In the state PDMP, compute oxycodone and oxymorphone pill counts dispensed per prescriber NPI per month against same-specialty peers. Compute the share of that prescriber's prescriptions paid in cash despite the patient holding active coverage. Compute the distance from prescriber practice address in NPPES to patient residence ZIPs on dispensed prescriptions. Check whether the prescriber submits any E/M claims corresponding to the visits that supposedly generated the prescriptions. Compare the prescribing address to the CMS-855I practice location, since a warehouse site indicates no clinical facility.
533.features_to_create: 1) Opioid volume outlier: on prescriber NPI x month, compute total oxycodone and oxymorphone dosage units dispensed from PDMP NDC and quantity fields; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriptions without encounters: on prescriber NPI x month, compute dispensed controlled prescriptions divided by billed E/M encounters; fires when the ratio far exceeds one against peer baseline; action payment suspension. 3) Patient travel radius: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the median miles between practice ZIP and patient ZIP on controlled fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action site visit.

534.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute definitive urine drug testing units per patient per week against clinical guideline frequency for the treatment level billed. Verify the ordering NPI on urinalysis claims was actively affiliated with the facility on the date of service using NPPES and payroll rosters. Match new-enrollee applications against reported qualifying life events and income, since clustered enrollments from one facility address signal broker activity. Compare patient residence states to the facility state to identify brokered out-of-state admissions in the eligibility file. Compute marketing payments per admitted patient recorded in the facility's contractor invoices against admissions volume.
534.features_to_create: 1) Urinalysis frequency: on beneficiary x facility TIN x week, compute definitive drug test panel units billed; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-modality treatment peers; action prepay edit. 2) Ordering-provider validity: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute whether the date of service falls inside that provider's active affiliation and licence dates in NPPES and the state board file; fires on exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Enrollment clustering: on facility address x plan enrollment month, compute distinct new marketplace enrollees sharing that mailing address or contact phone; fires when above one household equivalent; action payment suspension.

535.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this disaster loan case. The nearest detection route is matching EIDL disbursement bank accounts to subsequent vehicle title and real property deed records in the borrower's name. A second route is comparing certified working-capital use on the loan application against the borrower's business bank statements before further draws.
535.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on borrower bank account, compute the share of loan proceeds transferred within 90 days to titled vehicle purchases or real estate escrow and refer when that share is above zero for prohibited categories.

536.ways_to_identify: In the state PDMP, compute overlapping days supply of opioid, benzodiazepine, sedative and carisoprodol NDCs per patient for one prescriber. Compute daily morphine milligram equivalents from NDC strength, quantity and days supply on each patient's dispensing history. Compute the count of distinct controlled substance schedules prescribed to the same patient in a rolling month. Compare the prescriber's controlled prescription count per patient against same-specialty peers in the dispensing file. Check for early refills using the gap between fill date and the prior fill's exhaustion date.
536.features_to_create: 1) Quadruple-therapy overlap: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute overlapping days supply across opioid, benzodiazepine, sedative and carisoprodol NDC classes; fires when three or more overlap on the same day; action prepay edit. 2) MME concentration: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of patients above the CDC daily MME threshold; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Early refill gap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute fill date minus prior fill date minus prior days supply; fires when negative repeatedly for the same prescriber; action postpay audit.

537.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this employee card embezzlement. The nearest detection route is reconciling corporate card transaction files against approved vendor lists and expense receipts each month. A second route is comparing per-cardholder monthly spend to that cardholder's own trailing baseline in the card issuer statement file.
537.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on cardholder account x month, compute the sum of transactions lacking a matched receipt or approved vendor code and escalate when that sum exceeds the cardholder's trailing baseline.

538.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this corporate card embezzlement. The nearest detection route is monthly reconciliation of card transaction files to receipts and merchant category codes by someone other than the cardholder. A second route is trending each cardholder's spend against their own prior-year baseline in the issuer statement file.
538.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on cardholder account x month, compute unreceipted spend and personal merchant category spend as a share of total charges and escalate when above the cardholder's trailing baseline.

539.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this trust fund tax case. The nearest detection route is comparing wages and withholding reported on Forms W-2 and W-3 against Form 941 deposits actually received by the IRS. A second route is flagging employers filing 941s while making no corresponding EFTPS deposits over consecutive quarters.
539.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on employer EIN x quarter, compute withheld tax reported on Form 941 minus deposits received through EFTPS and open a trust fund recovery inquiry when the difference is positive across consecutive quarters.

540.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare the rendering NPI on E/M claims against travel or absence evidence such as out-of-state card and claim activity on the same dates. Count services billed under one supervising NPI per day and divide by a physically possible workday of 24 hours. Check the state medical board collaborative practice arrangement file for assistant physician names not matching any rendering NPI on submitted claims. Match the practice service location on the CMS-855B against the HRSA medically underserved area file required for assistant physician supervision. Screen every individual furnishing services at the TIN against OIG LEIE and state Medicaid suspended-provider lists at credentialing.
540.features_to_create: 1) Solo-rendering impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total billed E/M time-equivalent minutes across all service locations; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours or overlapping minutes occur at two locations; action prepay edit. 2) Supervision registry mismatch: on rendering NPI x practice TIN, compute an exact match rate between billed rendering NPIs and the state board collaborative practice arrangement roster plus the HRSA underserved-site list; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension and site visit. 3) Excluded furnisher linkage: on practice TIN, compute the count of payroll or credentialed clinicians appearing on OIG LEIE or state suspension files; fires when the count exceeds zero; action payment suspension.

541.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute the share of urine drug testing claims whose ordering NPI has a PECOS or CMS-855 ownership link to the billing laboratory. Compare annual wellness visit claims billed as in-person place of service 11 against telecom-only documentation and absent telehealth modifiers. Match rendering NPI dates of service against border-crossing or out-of-country evidence and same-day claims in another jurisdiction. Verify the prescriber on controlled-substance claims holds an active DEA registration at the NDC dispensing date in the DEA registrant file. Count patients with controlled-substance prescriptions but no prior in-person E/M encounter with the prescribing NPI in the payer's own claim history.
541.features_to_create: 1) Self-referral share: on ordering NPI x laboratory TIN, compute the proportion of the lab's toxicology claims traceable to orderers with PECOS ownership or compensation links; fires when the proportion exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit and postpay audit. 2) DEA registry mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact match of prescriber NPI to an active DEA registration covering the billed NDC schedule on the fill date; fires on any mismatch or expired registration; action prepay edit. 3) Absent-clinician billing: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of face-to-face place-of-service 11 services on days with documented absence or with claims filed in a distant state; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension.

542.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check each long-term care pharmacy claim for a prescriber NPI, written date, and prescription number linked to a valid original or refill authorization. Compute the days between the fill date and the last valid prescription expiration or last authorized refill on the pharmacy's own dispensing records. Compare the residence facility type on the beneficiary's claim to the drug's authorization source, since assisted living residents lack a chart-order equivalent. Count dispensings continuing after the prescriber NPI shows no encounter with that beneficiary for the diagnosis in the payer's claim history. Sample cycle-fill records against the pharmacy's electronic prescription files at audit rather than accepting attestation.
542.features_to_create: 1) Refill authorization expiry: on beneficiary x NDC x pharmacy NPI, compute days between fill date and the expiration of the last documented prescription authorization; fires when the gap is positive with no new authorization on file; action prepay edit. 2) Order-source mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact match between the residence facility type and the presence of a prescriber-signed prescription record rather than a facility chart order; fires on mismatch for assisted living or residential settings; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Prescriber-contact gap: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute months since the last paid encounter with that prescriber while chronic fills continue; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-setting peers; action postpay audit.

543.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, verify the entity's legal name, TIN, and address in NPPES against state licensure and secretary-of-state incorporation records for early intervention providers. At adjudication, count therapy claims whose rendering clinician NPI has no active state licence in the licensing board file. Compare claimed session dates for each child against the beneficiary's other claims showing school, hospital, or travel conflicts. Compute the ratio of billed charges to any prior remittance history for a newly enrolled entity with no ramp period. Check whether multiple provider entities submit for the same children from one bank account or shared address in the payer's payment file.
543.features_to_create: 1) New-entity billing ramp: on billing NPI x month, compute total billed charges divided by the provider's trailing baseline since enrolment; fires when a first-year entity exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit and site visit. 2) Unlicensed renderer: on claim line, compute an exact match between rendering NPI and an active state therapy licence covering the date of service; fires on any registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Shared-payment cluster: on bank account, compute the count of distinct billing NPIs and distinct entity names receiving remittances; fires when the count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership on enrolment forms; action payment suspension.

544.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim and no adjudication point here, since the harm is importation and resale of misbranded devices rather than billing. The nearest detection route is customs entry data and FDA import records compared against the distributor's domestic sales invoices and device labeling. A payer-side proxy exists only if such devices later appear on DMEPOS claims with serial or lot numbers absent from the manufacturer's U.S. distribution pedigree.
544.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Pedigree mismatch: on supplier NPI x HCPCS, compute the count of dispensed device serial or lot numbers absent from the manufacturer's authorized U.S. distribution file; fires when the count exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

545.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute the share of the practice's E/M claims billed at the two highest levels against same-specialty peer distributions. Count endometrial ablation and biopsy CPT claims per 100 female beneficiaries relative to obstetrics-gynecology peers in the same state. Compare telehealth-modifier visits billed at high complexity levels with the total minutes claimed by that rendering NPI per day. Check for repeat ablation claims on the same beneficiary, since the procedure is not normally repeated at short intervals. Cross-check STD and blood panel orders against any documented diagnosis code supporting screening in the beneficiary's other claims.
545.features_to_create: 1) High-level E/M concentration: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of level 4 and 5 E/M lines to all E/M lines for both in-person and telehealth places of service; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit and documentation request (ADR). 2) Procedure saturation: on rendering NPI, compute ablation and biopsy CPT counts per 100 attributed female beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Repeat-ablation impossibility: on beneficiary x CPT, compute the gap in days between successive endometrial ablation claims; fires when a second claim occurs within the clinically implausible window; action claim suspension.

546.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare billed personal care units per resident per day against the authorized units on the state prior-authorization and person-centered service plan record. Compute total direct-care staff hours from payroll and EVV records versus billed units for the same week. Check the billed procedure and modifier against the resident's assessed level of need in the state assessment file to detect a higher-paying tier. Match dates of service against hospital or emergency inpatient claims in the resident's other claims showing absence from the facility. Verify representative payee status and Social Security benefit flows against the provider's room-and-board charges at enrolment.
546.features_to_create: 1) Authorization overage: on beneficiary x provider NPI x week, compute billed units minus prior-authorized units from the state service plan; fires when the difference is positive; action prepay edit. 2) Staffing capacity: on provider NPI x week, compute billed service hours divided by payroll and EVV-documented direct-care hours; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action payment suspension and site visit. 3) Tier upcoding: on beneficiary x claim line, compute an exact match between the billed level-of-need modifier and the tier in the state assessment record; fires on mismatch; action claim suspension.

547.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute the share of a pharmacy's compound cream claims traceable to a single marketing entity's referring prescriber cluster. Compare average paid amount per compound NDC combination against the same drug class across peer pharmacies. Check whether prescriber NPIs on the compound claims are geographically distant from the pharmacy and from beneficiary residence ZIPs. Review the pharmacy's disclosed contracts and ownership on enrolment forms for percentage-of-revenue marketing arrangements. Count beneficiaries receiving high-cost scar and pain creams with no prior related diagnosis in their other claims.
547.features_to_create: 1) Marketer funnel concentration: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of compound claims from the top prescriber cluster and the distinct-referrer graph degree; fires when concentration exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action prepay edit. 2) Compound price outlier: on claim line, compute the paid amount per compound prescription against the same-ingredient distribution across peer pharmacies; fires when above the calibrated percentile; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Distance implausibility: on pharmacy NPI x prescriber NPI, compute the mean miles between prescriber practice address in NPPES and beneficiary residence ZIP; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR).

548.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, verify the foreign treating facility's name and address against recognized international provider directories before paying out-of-network reimbursement. Compare claimed treatment dates abroad with the member's domestic claims, pharmacy fills, and card activity in the same window. Count distinct member reimbursement requests sharing one mailing address, bank account, or submitter email in the payer's payment file. Check submitted invoices and police reports for identical templates, fonts, or sequential document numbers across unrelated members. Compute each member's out-of-network foreign reimbursement total against the plan's trailing baseline for that member.
548.features_to_create: 1) Domestic-presence conflict: on beneficiary x claimed foreign service date, compute the count of domestic claims or pharmacy fills on overlapping dates; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 2) Submitter cluster: on bank account, compute the distinct count of members, foreign facilities, and claim submissions received; fires when the count exceeds one member without a documented family relation; action payment suspension. 3) Unverifiable facility: on claim line, compute an exact match of the foreign provider name and address to a recognized international facility registry; fires on mismatch; action documentation request (ADR) before payment.

549.ways_to_identify: At credentialing, screen every rendering and supervised clinician NPI and SSN against the OIG LEIE and the state Medicaid exclusion list. At adjudication, match each claim's rendering NPI to the exclusion file effective date range for the date of service. Compare the entity's payroll and contractor roster on the CMS-855 disclosure against the clinicians actually named on claims. Recheck exclusion status monthly, since exclusions are added after initial enrolment. Count claims billed under a supervising NPI whose session notes name a different, non-enrolled counselor.
549.features_to_create: 1) Exclusion match at adjudication: on claim line, compute an exact match of rendering, supervising, and ordering NPI or SSN to OIG LEIE and state exclusion files for the date of service; fires on any match; action prepay edit. 2) Roster refresh: on provider TIN x month, compute the count of disclosed employees or contractors newly appearing on LEIE since the last screening; fires when the count exceeds zero; action payment suspension. 3) Substitute-renderer gap: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute billed session counts minus sessions attributable to that NPI in the entity's scheduling records; fires when the difference is positive; action documentation request (ADR).

550.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, sum the minimum minutes implied by time-based psychotherapy CPT codes per rendering NPI per day and compare with 24 hours. Compare each session's billed code to the telehealth platform connection log duration retained by the provider. Compute the share of sessions billed at the longer time-based code versus same-specialty peers in the same setting. Check for back-to-back session start times per rendering NPI that leave no gap for documentation. Count nursing facility beneficiaries receiving weekly psychotherapy without a supporting behavioral diagnosis in their other claims.
550.features_to_create: 1) Daily minute impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of minimum minutes required by each billed time-based psychotherapy code; fires when the sum exceeds a physically possible workday or sessions overlap in minutes; action prepay edit. 2) Long-code concentration: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of longer-duration psychotherapy codes to all psychotherapy lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR) for platform connection logs. 3) Facility saturation: on facility x provider TIN x month, compute sessions per resident; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer facilities; action postpay audit.

551.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check whether the ordering NPI on CGx claims has any prior evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiary in the payer's claim history. Count distinct beneficiary states per ordering NPI per week on genetic testing orders. Compare the beneficiary's cancer diagnosis and family history codes in other claims against the medical necessity criteria for hereditary cancer panels. At enrolment, verify all owners with 5 percent or greater interest on the CMS-855B against SSN, PECOS, and identity verification records. Compute the count of beneficiaries receiving the same CGx panel from more than one laboratory NPI within a year.
551.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that orderer and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct laboratory NPIs on CGx orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Ownership identity verification: on billing TIN, compute an exact match of each disclosed 5 percent owner's name and SSN to identity and PECOS records including prior exclusions; fires on mismatch or undisclosed nominee; action claim suspension and site visit.

552.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, match each beneficiary on COVID test kit claims against the Death Master File for a date of death preceding the date of service. Check whether the ordering NPI has any prior encounter with the beneficiary in claim history before the mailed test kit. Count distinct beneficiaries per laboratory NPI per week whose residence ZIPs lie far outside the lab's enrolled service area. Compare the lab's weekly claim volume against its own trailing baseline since PECOS enrolment. Examine authorization records produced during audit for identical signatures or metadata across unrelated beneficiaries.
552.features_to_create: 1) Deceased beneficiary edit: on claim line, compute days between date of service and the Death Master File date of death; fires when the service date follows death; action prepay edit. 2) Unsolicited mailing pattern: on laboratory NPI x week, compute the share of test kit claims with no prior E/M or order-linked encounter for the beneficiary; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action payment suspension. 3) Volume ramp: on billing NPI x week, compute claim counts divided by the provider's trailing 12-week baseline; fires when the ratio exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension and site visit.

553.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, since the fraud is sale of fabricated commercial receivables to banks. The nearest detection route is receivables-auction underwriting comparing invoice counterparties, shipping and rail bills of lading, and tax filings for the purported ethanol deliveries. A second route is concentration analysis showing nearly all receivables flowing between two affiliated counterparties with circular payment timing.
553.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Counterparty circularity: on obligor pair, compute the share of auctioned receivables between the same two entities and the count lacking independent delivery documentation; fires when concentration exceeds the platform's calibrated percentile; action funding suspension pending documentation.

554.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute the share of a rheumatologist's panel carrying a rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis relative to same-specialty peers in the same state. Count infusion and injection J-code units per attributed beneficiary per year against peer distributions. Check whether serologic testing such as rheumatoid factor or anti-CCP appears in the beneficiary's claim history before biologic infusion claims begin. Compare imaging volume, including MRI and diagnostic ultrasound, per beneficiary against peer rheumatologists. Detect identical ultrasound image files or duplicate report text across different beneficiaries during documentation review.
554.features_to_create: 1) Diagnosis prevalence outlier: on rendering NPI x year, compute the share of attributed beneficiaries with a rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis code; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Infusion without confirmatory testing: on beneficiary x provider NPI, compute the count of biologic infusion lines preceded by zero rheumatoid serology claims in the lookback; fires when the count exceeds zero; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Duplicate-documentation detection: on provider NPI, compute the distinct-hash count of submitted imaging files divided by the count of imaging claims; fires when the ratio falls below one; action payment suspension and postpay audit.

555.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare the beneficiary residence ZIP and referring physician address against the rural hospital's service area for outpatient lipid panel claims. Compute the share of a critical access hospital's outpatient lab revenue derived from specimens not collected on its own campus. Check whether the reference laboratory performing the test is the entity of record versus the hospital billing under outpatient rates. Cross-reference referring physician NPIs against ownership or investment interests in management services organizations disclosed on enrolment and Open Payments. Compute the ratio of lab lines to face-to-face encounters for each referring NPI at that hospital.
555.features_to_create: 1) Pass-through lab detection: on hospital NPI x month, compute the share of outpatient lab claims where the beneficiary has no same-facility encounter within the surrounding days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer hospitals; action prepay edit. 2) Non-local referral geography: on referring NPI x hospital NPI, compute the mean distance between referring practice address in NPPES and the hospital's enrolled location; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer referral patterns; action claim suspension. 3) Investment-linked referral: on referring NPI, compute the count of lab lines billed to hospitals sharing an MSO payment relationship in disclosure or Open Payments records; fires when the count exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

556.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, since this is pandemic loan fraud using fabricated payroll for nonexistent businesses. The nearest detection route is lender comparison of applicant payroll schedules against IRS Form 941 filings and state unemployment insurance wage records before disbursement. A second route is cross-application matching of listed employee SSNs appearing simultaneously on unrelated applicants and on the broker's insurance client rosters.
556.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payroll verification mismatch: on loan application EIN, compute the difference between claimed monthly payroll and IRS 941 plus state wage-record payroll for the same quarters; fires on any material mismatch or absent filings; action disbursement hold pending verification.

557.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, match the prescriber DEA number on controlled-substance claims to the registrant's registered state and practice address in the DEA file. Check whether the presenting beneficiary identifier exists in the payer's eligibility file and matches name and date of birth. Count distinct pharmacies in distinct states filling schedule prescriptions under one prescriber DEA number within days via the PDMP. Compare the prescribed codeine NDC and quantity against that prescriber's own trailing prescribing baseline. Detect sequential or duplicated prescription serial numbers presented at multiple pharmacies in the same chain's dispensing records.
557.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber geographic dispersion: on prescriber DEA number x week, compute the count of distinct dispensing pharmacy states in PDMP and claims data; fires when the count exceeds the prescriber's trailing baseline or peer percentile; action prepay edit and prescriber verification call. 2) Eligibility identity mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact match of member ID, name, and date of birth to the eligibility file; fires on any mismatch for a controlled-substance NDC; action claim suspension. 3) Prescriber baseline break: on prescriber DEA x NDC schedule, compute weekly dispensed quantity divided by the trailing 12-week baseline; fires when the ratio exceeds the calibrated percentile; action payment suspension.

558.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute the paid amount per compounded cream prescription against ingredient acquisition cost benchmarks and peer pharmacy distributions. Count the share of a pharmacy's workers' compensation claims originating from a small set of prescriber NPIs. Compare prescriber payments recorded in the pharmacy's disclosed contracts, Open Payments, and shell-company remittances against referral volume. Check whether each injured worker had a documented failure of standard oral analgesics in the claim history before compound approval. Detect refills authorized without any intervening prescriber encounter in the workers' compensation claim record.
558.features_to_create: 1) Cost-to-charge outlier: on claim line, compute billed amount divided by benchmark ingredient cost for the compound NDC set; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer compounding pharmacies; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriber concentration and payment link: on pharmacy NPI x prescriber NPI, compute referred claim dollars alongside dollars paid to that prescriber or affiliated entity from the pharmacy's bank accounts; fires when both exceed the calibrated percentile versus peers; action payment suspension. 3) Step-therapy gap: on beneficiary x compound claim, compute the count of prior paid oral analgesic fills in the lookback; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit.

559.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, since funds were diverted by impersonating a vendor in email rather than by billing. The nearest detection route is accounts-payable verification of any bank-account change request through a callback to the vendor contact of record, not the requesting email. A second route is matching the new beneficiary bank account and routing number against the vendor master file and against accounts newly opened in unrelated names.
559.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Vendor bank-change verification: on vendor master record, compute the count of payment-instruction changes with no out-of-band callback confirmation and the days since the account was opened; fires when a change is unverified or the account is newly opened; action payment hold pending verification.

560.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, bilateral knee patients show right and left injection CPT 20610/20611 lines on separate dates instead of one date with modifier 50. The rendering NPI's ratio of split-date bilateral injections to same-date RT/LT pairs far exceeds same-specialty peers in remittance history. JW-modifier discarded milliliters on the contrast NDC exceed what one single-use vial per patient can yield. Billed drug volume per quarter exceeds vials acquired per wholesaler pedigree and purchase invoices. Repeat E/M and facility visit counts per beneficiary per year sit above orthopedic peer norms.
560.features_to_create: 1) Bilateral split-visit ratio: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of beneficiaries with right-knee and left-knee injection CPT lines on different dates within 30 days divided by same-date RT/LT pairs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit on the second date of service. 2) Discard-to-vial reconciliation: on rendering NPI x HCPCS x month, compute total JW discarded units divided by administered units against labeled single-use vial size for the NDC; fires when discard exceeds one vial per patient physically allows; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Purchase-versus-billed volume: on TIN x NDC x quarter, compute billed milliliters minus milliliters evidenced in wholesaler acquisition records; fires when billed exceeds acquired; action payment suspension.

561.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare the supplier's submitted charge for HCPCS E0603 breast pumps against its charges to state Medicaid for the same code. Check whether accessory HCPCS lines (A4281-A4286) are billed on the same date as the pump kit already containing them. Look for accessory lines coded as replacement parts with no prior pump dispense date in the beneficiary's claim history. Compare the supplier's charge-to-allowed spread against same-code peers in the DMEPOS remittance file. Verify the product model billed against the manufacturer kit contents listed on the CMS-855S product line at enrolment.
561.features_to_create: 1) Dual fee schedule differential: on supplier NPI x HCPCS, compute the submitted charge to this payer minus the same supplier's submitted charge to other payers for the identical code and date window; fires when the differential exceeds zero after allowed rounding; action prepay edit. 2) Kit component unbundling: on claim line, compute the count of accessory HCPCS codes billed on the same date of service as the pump base code that are listed as included kit contents; fires when that count is above zero; action prepay edit. 3) Phantom replacement: on beneficiary x supplier NPI, compute days between the accessory 'replacement' line and the earliest paid pump dispense; fires when no prior pump dispense exists; action claim suspension.

562.ways_to_identify: At enrolment and monthly, match every CMS-855 owner, officer and managing-employee SSN against OIG LEIE and state exclusion lists. Compare the named President on the 855S against bank signature cards and beneficial-ownership filings for the same TIN. At adjudication, check brace HCPCS claims for beneficiaries whose ordering NPI has no prior encounter claim. Compare the ordering physician NPI's own claim submissions and NPPES contact data against the volume of orders attributed to that NPI. Screen pharmacy claims for NDCs whose lot pedigree does not appear in ARCOS or licensed wholesaler purchase records.
562.features_to_create: 1) Exclusion match on ownership: on TIN x disclosed individual, compute exact match of name, date of birth and SSN against OIG LEIE and state exclusion files at enrolment and each revalidation; fires on any exact registry match; action payment suspension and enrolment revocation. 2) Straw-owner divergence: on supplier NPI, compute the count of distinct individuals appearing as payment-account signatories or wire beneficiaries who are absent from the CMS-855 ownership section; fires when that count is above zero; action site visit. 3) Order without encounter: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the most recent E/M or telehealth encounter claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit.

563.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare the high-reimbursement metabolic formula HCPCS (B4157 enteral, inborn-error formula codes) against the beneficiary's diagnosis history for an inherited metabolic disorder ICD-10 code. Check whether any claim from a metabolic specialist or geneticist NPI appears in the beneficiary's other claims. Reconcile units of specialty formula billed against the supplier's wholesaler purchase invoices for those NDCs. Look for a single TIN operating under several DBA names and NPIs at the same service address in PECOS. Compare the supplier's share of inborn-error formula codes to statewide DME peers in remittance history.
563.features_to_create: 1) Formula-diagnosis mismatch: on claim line, compute whether a qualifying inherited metabolic disorder ICD-10 code appears on the beneficiary's paid claims in the prior 12 months; fires when no such diagnosis exists for a specialty metabolic formula HCPCS; action prepay edit. 2) Product acquisition reconciliation: on supplier NPI x HCPCS x quarter, compute billed units minus units evidenced by wholesaler or manufacturer purchase records for that formula NDC; fires when billed exceeds purchased; action payment suspension. 3) Specialty formula concentration: on supplier NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of inborn-error formula units to total enteral nutrition units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

564.ways_to_identify: There is no clinical claim and no adjudication point here, since the payment flows from plan to broker outside the claims system. The nearest detectable route is comparing plan-to-broker payments in the MA bid and administrative-cost filings against CMS broker compensation caps for the plan year. Enrollment files can be tested for the disabled-under-65 share of each broker's enrollments versus that broker's overall book.
564.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Broker compensation cap test: on plan contract ID x broker TIN x plan year, compute total payments reported in administrative cost and marketing filings divided by enrollments attributed to that broker, compared to the published CMS compensation limit; fires when per-enrollee payment exceeds the limit; action postpay audit and referral. 2) Disability steering skew: on broker TIN x plan contract ID x quarter, compute the share of new enrollees with an original-reason-for-entitlement disability indicator relative to the county eligible population share; fires when below the calibrated percentile versus peer brokers in the same counties; action postpay audit.

565.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compute daily billed psychotherapy minutes per rendering NPI from CPT 90837, 90834 and 90853 units against a 24-hour day. Compare the rendering NPI's counseling dates of service against beneficiary claims showing inpatient stays or out-of-area services the same day. Check for identical session-note text and identical start times across many beneficiaries in ADR-returned documentation. Look for beneficiaries with no other behavioral health claims from any provider surrounding the billed episode. Compare the solo licensee's annual paid encounter count against state licence board scope and same-specialty peer volume.
565.features_to_create: 1) Impossible clinician day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total service minutes implied by billed psychotherapy CPT time units; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the provider's own trailing baseline by the calibrated margin; action prepay edit. 2) Patient corroboration gap: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of other providers' claims within 90 days of the billed counseling episode; fires when zero corroborating claims exist and session count is above the peer percentile; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Note duplication: on rendering NPI, compute the distinct-value count of session-note text hashes divided by the number of billed sessions in ADR responses; fires when the ratio falls below the calibrated threshold; action payment suspension.

566.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, total billed psychotherapy time units per rendering NPI per day from CPT 90834, 90837 and 90853 exceed a physically possible workday. Beneficiaries billed for counseling show no other claims from any provider around those dates of service. ADR-returned progress notes repeat identical narrative text and identical start times across unrelated patients. The solo licensee's paid encounter volume sits far above same-specialty peers in the payer's remittance history. Some billed dates fall on days the beneficiary has an inpatient or out-of-state claim elsewhere.
566.features_to_create: 1) Impossible clinician day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total minutes implied by timed psychotherapy CPT units; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours or the provider's trailing baseline by the calibrated margin; action prepay edit. 2) Documentation duplication: on rendering NPI, compute the distinct-value count of progress-note text hashes divided by billed session count in ADR responses; fires when below the calibrated threshold; action payment suspension. 3) Isolation of encounter: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of claims from other NPIs within 90 days of the billed sessions; fires when zero and session volume is above the peer percentile; action documentation request (ADR).

567.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, match the prescriber DEA number on the pharmacy claim against the DEA registration file for schedule authority, address and expiry. Compare the prescriber's practice ZIP in NPPES to the dispensing pharmacy ZIP and the member's residence ZIP. Count distinct beneficiaries receiving promethazine-with-codeine or hydrocodone NDCs from one prescriber DEA in a rolling week. Check whether the prescriber has any prior claim relationship with the beneficiary in the payer's claim history. Compare pharmacy dispensed controlled-substance volume against ARCOS and wholesaler purchase records for the same NDCs.
567.features_to_create: 1) DEA registry validation: on claim line, compute exact match of prescriber DEA number, schedule authority and registration status against the DEA file on the fill date; fires on any mismatch or expired registration; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber-pharmacy distance and burst: on prescriber DEA x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries and distinct pharmacies for controlled-substance NDCs plus median miles between prescriber and pharmacy ZIPs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty prescribers; action claim suspension. 3) No prior relationship: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute days since the last paid encounter claim between them; fires when no encounter exists before a schedule II or III fill; action prior-authorisation requirement.

568.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, validate the prescriber DEA number, schedule authority and registration status on each controlled-substance claim against the DEA registration file. Compare the prescriber's NPPES practice address to the dispensing pharmacy address and beneficiary residence ZIP. Count distinct beneficiaries and distinct pharmacies per prescriber DEA per week for promethazine-with-codeine and hydrocodone NDCs. Check for any prior paid encounter between the prescriber NPI and the beneficiary before the fill date. Reconcile pharmacy dispensed quantities against ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree purchases, including inventory reported after a reported burglary.
568.features_to_create: 1) DEA registry validation: on claim line, compute exact match of prescriber DEA number and schedule authority against the DEA file as of the fill date; fires on any mismatch, expiry or schedule not authorised; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber dispersion burst: on prescriber DEA x week, compute distinct beneficiary count and distinct pharmacy count for controlled-substance fills against the prescriber's trailing baseline; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty prescribers; action claim suspension. 3) Dispense-versus-acquisition gap: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute dispensed units minus units purchased in wholesaler pedigree records; fires when dispensed exceeds purchased; action payment suspension.

569.ways_to_identify: At credentialing, compare the rendering NPI's date of birth and NPPES record against active practice indicators such as recent continuing-education or other payer claims. At adjudication, count daily billed encounters and buprenorphine prescriptions under one prescriber DEA against a physically possible workday. Check whether the credentialed rendering NPI ever appears on facility sign-in, EVV or timesheet records returned under ADR. Compare the clinic's mix of high-complexity E/M and OTP bundle codes against opioid treatment program peers. Screen owners and managing employees on the CMS-855 against state board discipline files and OIG LEIE.
569.features_to_create: 1) Ghost prescriber load: on prescriber NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries with billed encounters or buprenorphine prescriptions divided by available clinical hours; fires when implied minutes per patient fall below a physically possible visit length; action prepay edit. 2) Credential substitution: on clinic TIN x rendering NPI x month, compute the ratio of claims billed under the highest-volume rendering NPI to that NPI's documented on-site hours in timesheets; fires when billed encounters exceed documented hours; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension. 3) Complexity drift: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of level-4 and level-5 E/M plus high-intensity counseling codes; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus opioid treatment program peers; action postpay audit.

570.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, because the money came from a loan program rather than a payer. The nearest detection route is matching payroll figures on the loan application against IRS Form 941 filings and state wage reports for the same EIN. Bank statements submitted with the application can be verified directly with the depository institution before disbursement.
570.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payroll attestation reconciliation: on EIN x application, compute claimed monthly payroll minus wages reported on filed Forms 941 and state unemployment wage reports for the same quarters; fires when the difference exceeds allowed rounding; action prepay edit at loan disbursement. 2) Shared-application graph: on bank account and applicant identifier, compute the count of distinct business entities sharing the same account, address or IP across applications; fires when above one without documented affiliation; action claim suspension of disbursement.

571.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim mechanic here, since the harm is device misbranding rather than billing, so adjudication offers no hook. The nearest route is the FDA Medical Device Reporting database showing complaint clusters for one device model against the manufacturer's own submitted correction reports. Laboratory proficiency-testing results filed under CLIA can be compared across analyzers for systematic low bias on venous specimens.
571.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Device complaint divergence: on device model x quarter, compute the count of MDR complaints and CLIA proficiency-testing failures citing low venous results divided by installed base, versus the manufacturer's reported corrections; fires when complaint rate exceeds the calibrated percentile versus comparable assay platforms; action site visit by the regulator. 2) Confirmatory retest discordance: on laboratory CLIA number x quarter, compute the share of venous blood lead results later contradicted by a reference-method retest; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer laboratories; action postpay audit of the testing program.

572.ways_to_identify: There is no claim and no adjudication point, because the conduct is device misbranding and false statements to the FDA rather than billing. The nearest non-claims route is comparing MDR complaint clusters for the analyzer model against the manufacturer's timeline of internal defect discovery documents. Proficiency-testing and reference-method confirmation data held under CLIA can reveal systematic low bias on venous specimens.
572.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Confirmatory discordance rate: on device model x quarter, compute the share of venous blood lead results contradicted by reference-method retesting across reporting laboratories; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus comparable platforms; action site visit by the regulator. 2) Complaint-to-correction lag: on manufacturer x device model, compute days between the earliest internal complaint or investigation record and the first filed correction or MDR report; fires when the gap exceeds the statutory reporting window; action postpay audit and referral.

573.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count distinct pharmacy NPIs filling for the same Medicaid ID across states within a short window. Compare the member's residence ZIP on the eligibility file with the dispensing pharmacy ZIP and the prescriber's NPPES address. Check whether the prescriber NPI on the fill has any prior encounter claim with that member. Match delivery or courier transportation claims to a pharmacy pickup rather than an authorized medical appointment in the trip record. Look for repeated same-day fills of high-value NDCs for members with no supporting diagnosis in claim history.
573.features_to_create: 1) Cross-state pharmacy dispersion: on beneficiary Medicaid ID x rolling 30 days, compute the count of distinct pharmacy NPIs and distinct states with paid fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-plan members; action claim suspension. 2) Prescriber relationship gap: on claim line, compute days since the last paid encounter between the prescriber NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists before a high-cost NDC fill; action prepay edit. 3) Trip-destination mismatch: on transportation claim line, compute whether the trip destination address matches an enrolled medical facility in PECOS rather than a pharmacy or residence; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit.
