574.ways_to_identify: There is no patient claim and no adjudication point, because the loss ran through vendor invoicing at a grant-funded clinic. The nearest route is matching vendor payee TINs on the entity's accounts-payable ledger against officers and family members disclosed on IRS Form 990 Schedule L related-party filings. Grant cost reports can be tested by comparing invoiced vendor prices against the underlying subcontractor invoices for the same work order.
574.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Related-party payee match: on payee TIN x fiscal year, compute exact match of the payee's registered officers against the organization's officers and Form 990 disclosures; fires on any exact registry match not disclosed as a related-party transaction; action postpay audit of cost reports. 2) Markup spread: on vendor invoice, compute invoiced amount minus the underlying subcontractor invoice for the same work order divided by that cost; fires when the markup exceeds the calibrated percentile versus comparable service contracts; action documentation request. 3) Percentage kickback pattern: on contracted third party x year, compute the share of received fees transferred out to a single affiliated entity; fires when that share approaches a fixed split of total fees; action postpay audit.

575.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, compare billed private duty nursing and personal care units against EVV visit records for the same beneficiary and date of service. Compute daily and weekly billed service hours per caregiver NPI or employee ID against a 24-hour day. Check that the nurse listed on the visit note holds an active licence on the state board file for that date. Compare respite and personal care hours billed against the units authorized in the prior-authorisation record and plan of care. Look for nursing notes returned under ADR with pre-signed guardian signatures and identical handwriting or entries across dates.
575.features_to_create: 1) EVV-to-claim reconciliation: on beneficiary x date of service x agency NPI, compute billed units minus units supported by matched EVV check-in and check-out records; fires when billed units exceed verified units; action prepay edit. 2) Caregiver hour impossibility: on caregiver identifier x week, compute total billed service hours across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours in any day or the hours reported on payroll timesheets; action claim suspension. 3) Authorization overage: on beneficiary x service HCPCS x authorization period, compute cumulative paid units divided by prior-authorised units; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action prepay edit.

576.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, compare the officer named on the CMS-855S against bank signature cards, lease documents and beneficial-ownership filings for the same TIN. At adjudication, check whether beneficiaries receiving braces have any prior encounter with the ordering NPI. Count denied claims resubmitted with altered HCPCS, diagnosis or ordering NPI from the same supplier within days. Compare beneficiary residence states against the supplier's declared service area and the geography of its lead sources. Trace outbound payments from the supplier's payment account to shell entities absent from the enrolment ownership disclosure.
576.features_to_create: 1) Denial-resubmission churn: on supplier NPI x claim control number family, compute the count of resubmissions where the HCPCS, diagnosis or ordering NPI changed after a medical-necessity denial; fires when the churn rate is above the calibrated percentile versus DMEPOS peers; action payment suspension. 2) Straw-officer divergence: on supplier TIN, compute the count of individuals on bank signature cards or wire beneficiary records who do not appear in the CMS-855S ownership and managing-employee sections; fires when above zero; action site visit. 3) Order without encounter and geographic spread: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states on ordered DMEPOS claims plus the share lacking any prior E/M with that NPI; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit.

577.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, reconcile dispensed NDC units against the pharmacy's wholesaler pedigree and purchase invoices for the same drugs. Verify the prescriber NPI and DEA on each claim have a documented injury-claim relationship in the workers' compensation case file. Count distinct claimants per prescriber and per pharmacy relative to the size of the local injured-worker population. Compare average paid amount per prescription for compounded and high-cost NDCs against peer pharmacies in remittance history. Check refill intervals and quantities against the days-supply already paid on prior fills for the same claimant.
577.features_to_create: 1) Dispense-versus-acquisition gap: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed units minus units evidenced in wholesaler pedigree purchase records; fires when billed exceeds purchased; action payment suspension. 2) Prescription validity linkage: on claim line, compute whether the prescriber NPI appears as a treating provider on the claimant's accepted injury case file and has a paid encounter within the lookback; fires on registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 3) Cost-per-script outlier: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute mean paid amount per prescription and the share of top-cost NDCs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies serving the same program; action prior-authorisation requirement.

578.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, check whether the prescriber has any prior paid encounter with the beneficiary before a high-cost compounded prescription. Compute the share of one prescriber's compounded scripts routed to a single pharmacy NPI. Compare average paid amount per compounded prescription against the prescriber's own trailing baseline and family-practice peers. Count authorized refills billed against the refill count on the original prescription record obtained at audit. Look for beneficiaries residing far outside the prescriber's NPPES practice service area.
578.features_to_create: 1) No-relationship compound script: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute days since the last paid E/M encounter before the compounded drug fill; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriber-pharmacy channel concentration: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of compounded prescriptions dispensed by a single pharmacy NPI and the mean paid amount per script; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 3) Refill overrun: on prescription number, compute the count of paid refills minus refills authorized on the original order; fires when the difference exceeds zero; action claim suspension.

579.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count component molecular CPT codes (87631 series and individual 87xxx targets) billed on the same specimen date where a panel code exists. Compute the summed allowed amount of component lines versus the bundled panel rate for the same date and beneficiary. Check whether the ordering diagnosis on respiratory or urinary panel claims supports multi-target testing rather than a single Covid-19 test. Compare each ordering NPI's panel-to-single-test ratio against urgent care peers in remittance history. Verify the laboratory's CLIA certificate covers high-complexity molecular testing for the codes billed.
579.features_to_create: 1) Panel unbundling detector: on beneficiary x specimen date x laboratory NPI, compute the count of component molecular CPT lines that map to an existing panel code and the summed allowed amount versus that panel rate; fires when component count exceeds the panel threshold or summed allowed exceeds the panel rate; action prepay edit. 2) Diagnosis-to-panel support: on claim line, compute whether the submitted ICD-10 codes match the payer's covered indication list for the multi-target panel; fires on exact policy mismatch; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Ordering intensity outlier: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of multi-target panel tests to single-target tests per patient encounter; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus urgent care peers; action postpay audit.

580.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, count the component CPT codes on one claim that together match an existing NAAT respiratory or UTI panel code. Same beneficiary, same date of service, same rendering NPI shows multiple single-target PCR lines instead of one panel code. The clinic's paid-per-encounter amount for respiratory testing sits far above same-specialty urgent care peers in remittance history. Large panels are billed on encounters whose only diagnosis code is a COVID-19 symptom code with no other indication. Panel-to-single-test ratio for this NPI jumped sharply above its own trailing baseline after a fee schedule change.
580.features_to_create: 1) Panel rebundling detector: on beneficiary x date of service x rendering NPI, compute the count of component PCR CPT lines that map to a single multiplex panel code; fires when that count meets the panel's component threshold without the panel code billed; action prepay edit. 2) Panel intensity outlier: on provider NPI x month, compute the ratio of paid dollars for respiratory or UTI molecular testing to total encounters; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Indication mismatch: on claim line, compute the share of large-panel claims whose diagnosis set contains only COVID-19 symptom codes; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action postpay audit.

581.ways_to_identify: At enrolment processing, count Medicare Advantage enrolment transactions submitted by one agent or plan NPI within a single day. Compare beneficiary-signed scope-of-appointment records against CMS online enrolment submissions for the same HICN or MBI. Cross-check enrolling beneficiary contact data against pharmacy dispensing records held by the same corporate TIN for common source of demographics. Track beneficiary-initiated disenrolment and rapid-disenrolment complaint rates per agent identifier in the plan's CTM file. Compare pharmacy payments in the plan's vendor ledger against the count of enrolments referred by those same pharmacy NPIs.
581.features_to_create: 1) Enrolment burst: on agent identifier x day, compute the count of distinct beneficiary enrolment transactions submitted to CMS; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer agents; action claim suspension of the enrolment batch pending beneficiary verification. 2) Consent-record gap: on enrolment record, compute the presence of a matching dated scope-of-appointment or recorded call before the submission timestamp; fires when no matching record exists; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Referral-payment coupling: on pharmacy NPI, compute the correlation between dollars paid from the plan's vendor ledger and the count of enrolments attributed to that NPI; fires when payment per enrolment exceeds zero for any referral-linked pharmacy; action payment suspension and site visit.

582.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim here and no adjudication point, so no payer edit applies. Detection sits with IRS revenue officers comparing Forms 1099-K and 1120 gross receipts against bank deposits for successor entities sharing an owner. State corporate registry and DOT operating-authority filings showing new entities at the same address with the same principal are the nearest lead.
582.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest outside control: on taxpayer identification number, compute the count of successor entities sharing officer, address or vehicle title records while a prior entity carries unpaid trust-fund liability; fires on any match; action IRS collection referral.

583.ways_to_identify: In Part D PDE data, compute the share of this prescriber's fills that are Schedule II amphetamine NDCs versus same-specialty peers. Compare prescribed amphetamine days-supply against any office visit E/M claim between prescriber NPI and beneficiary in the lookback period. Check PDMP records for beneficiaries filling stimulants from multiple prescribers within overlapping days-supply windows. Compare beneficiary residence ZIP distance to the practice address on the CMS-855I enrolment record. Track the prescriber's stimulant volume growth against its own trailing baseline in remittance history.
583.features_to_create: 1) Stimulant concentration: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of Schedule II stimulant claims to total prescription claims using NDC and days supply; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) No-encounter prescribing: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary, compute days between the controlled-substance fill date and the most recent E/M claim between the pair; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 3) Patient dispersion: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries receiving stimulants who live beyond the practice service radius on CMS-855I; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action postpay audit.

584.ways_to_identify: There is no medical claim and no clinical adjudication point, but the state agency does adjudicate benefit claims and can control there. Adjudicator user IDs in the UI claims system can be grouped to show approvals concentrated in one examiner without wage-record support. Cross-matching claimant SSNs against state quarterly wage files and the National Directory of New Hires exposes ineligible approvals before payment. Bank routing and account numbers repeating across unrelated claimant records point to a single beneficiary of the payments.
584.features_to_create: 1) Examiner override rate: on adjudicator user ID x week, compute the share of approved claims lacking matching quarterly wage records; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer adjudicators; action claim suspension pending second-level review. 2) Shared deposit account: on bank account number, compute the count of distinct claimant SSNs receiving benefit deposits; fires when that count exceeds one without a documented representative payee; action payment suspension. 3) Self-touch approvals: on adjudicator user ID, compute the count of approved claims whose address, phone or account matches the adjudicator's HR record; fires on any exact match; action payment suspension and referral.

585.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim in this scheme because buyers paid by wire and cash, so no adjudication edit fires. The nearest route is customs and import screening of parcels from India against FDA registered-importer lists and DSCSA pedigree requirements. Payment-processor and money-remitter reports showing repeated consumer wires to one foreign beneficiary for named drug products are the second route. Payers can still watch for oncology drug NDCs appearing in patient records with no matching specialty pharmacy dispensing claim.
585.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest outside control: on shipper or consignee identifier, compute the count of inbound parcels declaring non-drug contents that test positive for pharmaceutical packaging in FDA-CBP screening; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer shippers; action import alert and seizure referral.

586.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, neurostimulator implant CPT and L-code lines appear with place of service office and no facility or anesthesia claim on the same date. The rendering or supervising NPI's taxonomy in NPPES is chiropractic, which cannot perform a surgical implant. No operative report or implant device serial number is present in the prior-authorisation or ADR record for the implant code. The same beneficiary has repeat implant claims within intervals shorter than any device lifetime, consistent with disposable auricular devices. Referring physician NPIs sending patients to this supplier receive payments recorded in Open Payments or the supplier's vendor ledger.
586.features_to_create: 1) Implant without surgical footprint: on claim line, compute the count of same-date facility, anesthesia or operating-room claims for the beneficiary when a neurostimulator implant code is billed; fires when that count is zero with place of service office; action prepay edit. 2) Taxonomy-procedure mismatch: on rendering NPI x CPT, compute an exact match between NPPES taxonomy and the specialties permitted to bill implantation codes; fires on registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Implant frequency impossibility: on beneficiary x implant HCPCS, compute the gap in days between paid implant claims; fires when the gap is shorter than the device's expected lifetime without a documented revision; action postpay audit.

587.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the CMS-855A owner listed for the hospice shares an address, phone or bank account with other newly enrolled hospice NPIs. The attending or certifying physician NPI on the hospice election appears in the Death Master File or has no other Medicare billing activity. Beneficiaries on hospice claims continue receiving curative Part A and Part B services from unrelated providers during the election period. The hospice bills routine home care days with no NOE-consistent face-to-face encounter documentation and no OASIS or clinical record on ADR. Payment deposits route to a bank account opened weeks before enrolment under a foreign national's identity documents.
587.features_to_create: 1) Dead or dormant certifier: on certifying physician NPI, compute an exact match to the Death Master File date or a zero count of other paid claims in the prior year; fires on any match; action prepay edit and payment suspension. 2) Concurrent curative care: on beneficiary x hospice election period, compute the count of paid non-hospice acute or specialist claims during the election; fires when that count is above zero without a revocation record; action claim suspension. 3) Common-control cluster: on bank account and address in CMS-855A, compute the graph degree of distinct hospice NPIs sharing that node; fires when degree exceeds one; action site visit before first payment.

588.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, OTC COVID test kit HCPCS lines are billed for beneficiaries with a Death Master File date preceding the date of service. One lab NPI bills the kit code to a count of distinct beneficiaries spread nationwide far beyond its enrolled service area on CMS-855B. Beneficiaries have no ordering encounter and no prior claim relationship with the billing lab NPI. The billing NPI's volume rose from zero to peer-top-decile within weeks of a PECOS ownership change to a recently arrived owner. Beneficiary lists overlap heavily with other unrelated lab NPIs billing the same kit code in the same period, indicating a purchased list.
588.features_to_create: 1) Deceased beneficiary edit: on claim line, compute the difference between date of service and the Death Master File date of death; fires when service date follows death; action prepay edit. 2) Kit saturation: on beneficiary x HCPCS, compute the count of distinct supplier or lab NPIs paid for the OTC test code in a rolling month plus total units against the per-month coverage limit; fires when units exceed the limit or suppliers exceed one; action prepay edit. 3) New-owner volume spike: on provider NPI x week, compute paid claim count divided by the provider's trailing 12-week baseline since the PECOS ownership change date; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension and site visit.

589.ways_to_identify: At credentialing, the individual controlling the billing entity is absent from the state licence board file for BCBA or behavior analysis. Cross-check owners and managers named on the Medicaid provider enrolment against the OIG LEIE and state exclusion list for prior program convictions. At adjudication, ABA service dates fall on days when the entity's payroll and EVV records show no technician clock-in. BCBA supervision codes are billed on dates with no corresponding behavior technician direct-service line for the same recipient. Recipients have concurrent inpatient hospital claims spanning the outpatient ABA service dates.
589.features_to_create: 1) Exclusion and licence match: on enrolled TIN and each listed owner or manager, compute exact-name and SSN matches against OIG LEIE, state exclusion list and the licence board file; fires on any match or missing licence; action claim suspension and enrolment revocation. 2) Supervision without service: on recipient x date of service, compute the count of technician direct-service lines when a BCBA supervision code is billed; fires when that count is zero; action prepay edit. 3) Inpatient overlap: on recipient x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between paid outpatient ABA units and any inpatient admission span; fires when overlap is above zero; action prepay edit, then postpay audit.

590.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a small set of high-cost compound NDC ingredient combinations accounts for nearly all of the pharmacy's paid dollars. Average paid amount per compound claim for this pharmacy NPI is far above same-specialty peers in remittance history. Prescribing NPIs on the compound claims have no other claim relationship with the beneficiary and are clustered in distant states. Reversal-and-rebill patterns show repeated test submissions varying ingredient quantities for the same beneficiary within minutes. Beneficiary demographics on new compound claims exactly match records from older unrelated prescriptions at the same pharmacy, indicating reuse of stored data.
590.features_to_create: 1) Reimbursement-tuned formula: on pharmacy NPI x compound ingredient set, compute the paid dollars share and the average paid per claim versus same-specialty peers; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Claim-probing behavior: on pharmacy NPI x beneficiary x day, compute the count of reversed then re-adjudicated compound claims with changed ingredient quantities; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action prepay edit. 3) No-encounter prescriptions: on prescriber NPI x beneficiary, compute days between compound fill date and the nearest E/M claim between the pair; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action documentation request (ADR) and payment suspension.

591.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering telehealth NPI on brace and CGM claims has no prior evaluation-and-management encounter with that beneficiary. One ordering NPI writes DMEPOS orders for beneficiaries across dozens of states within a single week. Beneficiary ZIPs fall far outside the supplier's declared service area on its CMS-855S enrolment record. Several supplier NPIs sharing owners, address or bank account on CMS-855S bill the same L-codes for overlapping beneficiary sets. CGM claims lack any diabetes diagnosis or insulin fill in the beneficiary's other claims history.
591.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim between ordering NPI and beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs on ordered DMEPOS claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) CGM clinical support: on beneficiary x HCPCS, compute the count of diabetes diagnosis claims or insulin NDC fills in the prior year; fires when that count is zero; action prior-authorisation requirement.

592.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, advanced lipid panel CPT codes are billed under a critical access hospital NPI while the specimen was collected far from the hospital service area. Referring physician ZIPs on hospital outpatient lab claims cluster in metropolitan areas hundreds of miles from the rural facility. The hospital's outpatient lab revenue share jumps above its own trailing baseline while inpatient volume stays flat. Referring physicians appear as investors in management services organizations disclosed in Open Payments or hospital vendor ledgers. Reference-lab pass-through arrangements are absent from the hospital's CMS-855A reported contractual and ownership fields.
592.features_to_create: 1) Non-local reference testing: on hospital NPI x month, compute the share of outpatient lab lines whose referring NPI practice ZIP lies beyond the facility's service radius; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus rural hospital peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Lab revenue shift: on hospital NPI x quarter, compute outpatient lab paid dollars divided by total paid dollars against the facility's trailing four-quarter baseline; fires when the ratio rises above baseline while inpatient claim counts are flat; action postpay audit. 3) Investor-referrer link: on referring NPI, compute the count of paid lab lines routed to a facility whose MSO investor list or Open Payments record includes that NPI; fires when count is above zero; action payment suspension.

593.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the practitioner bills telehealth E/M codes with no matching audio-video or interactive encounter record on ADR. One practitioner NPI signs DMEPOS orders for a count of distinct beneficiaries impossible within the E/M minutes billed that day. Ordered brace claims carry no prior treating-relationship claim between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary. Total billed E/M time for a rendering NPI on a date of service exceeds 24 hours. Beneficiary residences span dozens of states inconsistent with the practitioner's licence board file coverage.
593.features_to_create: 1) Time impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed typical minutes for all billed E/M and telehealth codes; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Order-to-visit ratio: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of signed DMEPOS orders divided by the count of billed patient encounters; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Licence-state mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact match between beneficiary state and the states on the rendering NPI's licence board file; fires on mismatch; action claim suspension.

594.ways_to_identify: In the VA purchasing system, the count of purchase orders routed to one newly created vendor by a single contracting employee spikes above peers. Vendor registration records show an address, phone or bank account matching a VA employee's HR record. Unit prices paid for surgical supply SKUs exceed the Federal Supply Schedule or prevailing market benchmark on the same items. Employee financial disclosure filings omit an ownership interest in a vendor receiving payments. Quantities ordered exceed the surgical case volume recorded for the same period in facility case logs.
594.features_to_create: 1) Buyer-vendor concentration: on employee user ID x vendor TIN, compute the share of that employee's approved purchase orders going to one vendor; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer buyers; action payment suspension pending contracting review. 2) Insider linkage: on vendor bank account and address, compute exact matches against employee HR and ethics disclosure records; fires on any match with no disclosed interest; action payment suspension and site visit. 3) Price and quantity variance: on purchase order line, compute unit price against the Federal Supply Schedule rate and quantity against recorded surgical case counts; fires when price exceeds schedule or quantity exceeds cases; action prepay edit.

595.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, high-cost HIV NDC claims carry prescriber NPIs whose specialty in NPPES never prescribes those agents. Prescriptions originate from e-prescribing platform sessions whose IP address and device fingerprint differ from the prescriber's registered credentials. Patients receiving the antiretrovirals have no prior HIV diagnosis, lab claim or prior fill history with any payer. Copay assistance card enrolments cluster on beneficiaries sharing addresses, phone numbers or dates of birth. One prescriber's monthly high-cost specialty volume rises far above their own trailing baseline within days.
595.features_to_create: 1) Credential-use anomaly: on prescriber NPI x e-prescribing session, compute the count of distinct IP addresses or device identifiers used against the prescriber's trailing baseline; fires when a new device issues prescriptions above baseline; action claim suspension. 2) Therapy-history gap: on beneficiary x NDC class, compute the count of prior HIV diagnosis claims, viral-load lab claims or prior fills; fires when that count is zero for a new antiretroviral fill; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Sham-patient clustering: on address and phone in member enrolment, compute the count of distinct patient identities using copay assistance for the same NDC; fires when count exceeds one household size; action prepay edit and postpay audit.

596.ways_to_identify: There is no health insurance claim here, since a hospital bought supplies directly, so no adjudication edit applies. The nearest control is procurement verification of the NIOSH Certified Equipment List approval number against the exact model and manufacturer on the invoice. Supplier registration in FDA's establishment database and in GSA SAM exclusion records gives a second pre-purchase check. Independent filtration efficiency testing on a sampled lot compared to the 95 percent N95 requirement confirms misrepresentation before wide distribution.
596.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest outside control: on purchase order line, compute an exact match between the model and approval number on submitted NIOSH documentation and the NIOSH Certified Equipment List entry for that manufacturer; fires on any mismatch; action hold payment and lot testing before acceptance.

597.ways_to_identify: DSCSA transaction history for high-cost NDCs traces back to distributors absent from the manufacturer's authorized trading partner list. Serial numbers and lot codes on received bottles repeat across multiple pharmacies or fail manufacturer verification requests. Wholesaler licence status in the state board of pharmacy file is expired or the entity is unregistered in ARCOS reporting. Purchase invoice prices for specialty drugs fall far below wholesale acquisition cost benchmarks. Pharmacy dispensing volume for these NDCs exceeds documented purchases from authorized wholesalers in the pedigree file.
597.features_to_create: 1) Pedigree authenticity: on NDC serial number, compute the count of verification failures or duplicate serials against manufacturer product identifiers; fires on any duplicate or unverifiable serial; action claim suspension for dispensed units. 2) Purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute dispensed units minus units purchased from authorized wholesalers per DSCSA records; fires when the difference is above zero; action prepay edit and postpay audit. 3) Unauthorized supplier: on distributor identifier, compute an exact match against state board of pharmacy licensure and the manufacturer's authorized distributor list; fires on registry mismatch; action payment suspension and site visit.

598.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one prescriber NPI writes oxycodone 30 mg 30-day supplies at a rate far above same-specialty peers in PDMP and claim data. Nearly all of that prescriber's fills route to a small set of pharmacy NPIs sharing owners on state licence records. Beneficiaries filling the oxycodone have no imaging, procedure or E/M claim supporting a chronic pain diagnosis. Prescriptions are signed on dates when the prescriber has no billed encounter for that beneficiary. Beneficiaries travel unusually long distances between residence ZIP, practice ZIP and dispensing pharmacy ZIP.
598.features_to_create: 1) High-dose opioid concentration: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the share of claims that are oxycodone 30 mg at 30-day supply and the average daily morphine milligram equivalents; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriber-pharmacy channeling: on prescriber NPI, compute the share of opioid fills going to the top one or two pharmacy NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit and payment suspension. 3) Distance triangle: on claim line, compute summed miles between beneficiary ZIP, prescriber practice ZIP and dispensing pharmacy ZIP; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer opioid claims; action documentation request (ADR).

599.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, one pharmacist licence number appears as pharmacist-in-charge across many pharmacy NPIs in the state board of pharmacy file. Those pharmacies' oxycodone 30 mg purchase volumes in ARCOS exceed peer pharmacies of similar prescription count. A single pill-mill practice NPI accounts for most controlled-substance fills across that pharmacy network. Beneficiaries on the prescriptions have no examination claim from the prescribing NPI on or before the written date. Patient identities on fills recur with mismatched dates of birth or addresses against payer eligibility files.
599.features_to_create: 1) Common-control pharmacy network: on pharmacist licence number and bank account, compute the graph degree of distinct pharmacy NPIs sharing that node in board and enrolment records; fires when degree exceeds one without disclosed chain ownership; action site visit and payment suspension. 2) ARCOS-to-claims mismatch: on pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute oxycodone units purchased in ARCOS minus units dispensed on adjudicated claims; fires when the difference is above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action postpay audit. 3) Identity verification failure: on claim line, compute exact matches of member name, date of birth and address against the payer eligibility file and Death Master File; fires on any mismatch; action prepay edit.

600.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, claims billed under one NPI carry dates of service when that physician's own travel and other-state claims place him elsewhere. Telephone-only contacts are billed as annual wellness visits G0438 and G0439 without the required in-person place of service or telehealth modifier. The rendering NPI on the claim differs from the clinician documented in the encounter note obtained through documentation request. Urine specimen volume from one referring practice NPI to one laboratory NPI rises sharply against the lab's trailing baseline. Controlled-substance prescriptions written under the prescriber NPI show no companion E/M claim for the beneficiary in the lookback window.
600.features_to_create: 1) Provider-absence conflict: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of in-person place-of-service 11, 21 or 22 lines on dates where that NPI also has claims in a distant state or no local activity; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 2) Wellness-visit modality mismatch: on claim line, compute presence of G0438 or G0439 with place of service 11 alongside any telephone CPT 99441-99443 for the same beneficiary and date; fires on exact code-modality mismatch; action prepay edit. 3) Referral-concentration surge: on referring NPI x laboratory NPI x month, compute the count of urine drug test specimens and its ratio to that referrer's total lab orders; fires when above the referrer's trailing baseline and peer percentile; action postpay audit.

601.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim here and no adjudication point, because the product is a dietary supplement sold to commercial customers rather than billed to a payer. The nearest detection route is verifying GMP certificates and FDA Certificates of Free Sale directly with the issuing auditor and FDA export-certification system. Ownership overlap between the certifying consultancy and the manufacturer is visible in state corporate registry and beneficial-ownership filings.
601.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on certificate issuer entity, compute the count of certificates naming clients whose corporate registry shows shared officers or addresses with the issuer; fires when any shared-control match exists; action referral to FDA and customer notification.

602.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, hospice election periods end near six months with live discharge, visible in the revocation and discharge status codes. A single nurse practitioner NPI signs the face-to-face encounter for beneficiaries whose diagnoses lack any supporting hospitalisation or treatment claims. Beneficiaries discharged from hospice appear immediately on home health claims from a commonly owned NPI shown in CMS-855A ownership fields. Marketer payments appear as per-patient monthly amounts in the provider's own books, matching admission counts obtained on site visit. Beneficiaries show no prior narcotic, oxygen or hospital claims consistent with a six-month terminal prognosis.
602.features_to_create: 1) Live-discharge rate: on hospice NPI x quarter, compute the share of elections ending in live discharge and the median length of stay from election and discharge dates; fires when the live-discharge share is above the calibrated percentile versus peer hospices; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Certifier concentration: on certifying NPI x hospice NPI, compute the count of certifications and the share of the hospice's admissions signed by that one clinician; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit on new elections. 3) Common-ownership recycling: on beneficiary, compute days between hospice discharge date and the next home health start of care from an NPI sharing an owner TIN in PECOS; fires when the gap is under one billing cycle; action postpay audit and site visit.

603.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, telehealth E/M claims cluster on beneficiaries whose only companion claims are hereditary cancer panel CPT 81162 and 8140x lines. The ordering NPI has no prior or subsequent encounter with the beneficiary in the payer's remittance history. One telehealth NPI orders genetic panels for beneficiaries spread across dozens of states within a single week. Telehealth encounter durations billed as 99442 or 99443 are implausible against the clinician's daily total minutes. The CMS-855B enrolment names owners and managers who do not match ownership records or hide a person with a bank fraud conviction.
603.features_to_create: 1) Consult-to-panel coupling: on ordering NPI x week, compute the share of that NPI's telehealth encounters followed within 14 days by a hereditary cancer panel 81162 or 8140x order; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) No-treatment-relationship gap: on beneficiary x ordering NPI, compute the count of prior and subsequent E/M claims between them outside the single telehealth date; fires when that count is zero; action prepay edit. 3) Enrolment identity mismatch: on TIN x CMS-855 record, compute the count of listed owners and managing employees not matching PECOS, NPPES or LEIE identity and exclusion records; fires on exact registry mismatch; action site visit, then payment suspension.

604.ways_to_identify: At prior authorization, the submitted cancer diagnosis code is absent from every other claim in the beneficiary's history. At adjudication, the transmucosal fentanyl NDC is billed for beneficiaries with no oncology encounter or chemotherapy claim. A small set of prescriber NPIs accounts for an outsized share of that NDC's paid volume in Part D PDE data. Those same prescriber NPIs appear as paid speaker-program recipients in Open Payments records for the labeling manufacturer. Dose escalation per beneficiary rises across successive fills faster than the prescriber's own trailing baseline for the same NDC.
604.features_to_create: 1) Off-label indication mismatch: on beneficiary x NDC, compute the count of claims carrying an active malignancy diagnosis in the 12-month claim history across all payers; fires when the count is zero for a REMS cancer-pain-only NDC; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriber concentration plus payments: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the paid volume share of the rapid-onset fentanyl NDC and the summed Open Payments dollars from its manufacturer; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Dose escalation slope: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute the change in daily morphine-milligram-equivalent across consecutive fills of the same NDC; fires when the slope exceeds the prescriber's trailing baseline for the same NDC; action documentation request (ADR).

605.ways_to_identify: This is an annual collections round-up rather than a single scheme, so there is no single claim stream and no adjudication point. The nearest detection routes are co-pay foundation data reconciliation and SBA loan-forgiveness file review outside the claims system. Manufacturer donations to patient assistance foundations matched against the foundation's grant lists reveal drug-specific steering.
605.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on manufacturer x foundation fund, compute the correlation between donation amounts and grants awarded to patients using that manufacturer's drug; fires when the fund is effectively single-product; action referral for False Claims Act review.

606.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the CMS-855A ownership and Stark disclosure fields list physician-group owners whose referrals dominate the hospital's inpatient and surgical claim volume. Hospital claims show rendering NPIs from two group TINs accounting for an outsized share of designated health services. Physician-group compensation reported in the hospital's cost report exceeds fair-market-value benchmarks for the same specialty and region. Referral volume from those two TINs rises sharply in the quarter following the dated financial arrangement in the ownership file. The pandemic relief attestation on file names a payroll figure inconsistent with the TIN's reported wages.
606.features_to_create: 1) Owner-referral concentration: on hospital NPI x referring TIN, compute the share of designated-health-service claim lines whose referring NPI maps to a disclosed owner in CMS-855A; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-size peer hospitals; action postpay audit. 2) Compensation-to-referral ratio: on physician NPI, compute the ratio of hospital-paid compensation reported on the cost report to that physician's referred DHS payments; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Post-arrangement referral step change: on referring NPI x quarter, compute referred inpatient claim counts to the disclosing hospital against the referrer's own trailing baseline; fires when the post-arrangement quarter exceeds baseline beyond the calibrated percentile; action prepay edit.

607.ways_to_identify: This is an annual collections announcement covering unrelated matters, so there is no identifiable claim, provider or adjudication point. The nearest detection route is program-level recovery reporting rather than a prepay control.

608.ways_to_identify: This document announces an interagency working group meeting, so no claim, provider NPI or payment decision exists to adjudicate. The nearest detection route is the tip intake and referral channels the release publicises.

609.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, skin-substitute Q-code units billed per beneficiary encounter far exceed the wound surface area documented in the paired CPT application code. Application CPT 15271-15278 is billed in place of service 12 or 32 rather than a facility wound clinic. A single rendering nurse NPI applies allografts to more beneficiaries per day than working hours physically allow. Nearly all allograft product NDCs and Q-codes trace to one distributor per wholesaler pedigree data despite multiple billing TINs. Beneficiaries have no prior wound-care evaluation claim from any ordering NPI before the first graft date of service.
609.features_to_create: 1) Units-to-wound-area mismatch: on claim line, compute billed square centimetres on the Q-code against the wound area implied by the paired 152xx application CPT; fires when billed centimetres exceed the coded area band; action prepay edit. 2) Applier day capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries with allograft application CPTs multiplied by the code's typical service minutes; fires when the product exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Distributor-applier concentration: on rendering NPI, compute the distinct-value count of allograft manufacturers and the share of paid dollars tied to one distributor's Q-codes; fires when the share is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

610.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, prescriber-level Part D volume for the branded HIV NDCs rises sharply in the quarters after the first Open Payments speaker honorarium. The same prescriber NPI appears as a paid speaker on hundreds of events with repeat attendee rosters in the manufacturer's transparency file. Honoraria and meal transfers of value per prescriber exceed same-specialty peer distributions in Open Payments general-payment records. Branded NDC share versus generic alternatives for the prescriber exceeds peer infectious-disease prescribers in the payer's remittance history. Event locations reported in the transparency file are resort destinations rather than clinical venues.
610.features_to_create: 1) Honorarium-to-prescribing lift: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute paid claim counts for the manufacturer's HIV NDCs against the prescriber's own pre-honorarium trailing baseline using Open Payments dates; fires when the post-payment quarter exceeds baseline above the calibrated percentile; action postpay audit. 2) Transfer-of-value outlier: on prescriber NPI x year, compute summed speaker honoraria plus meal and travel value from Open Payments divided by the prescriber's total transfers; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Branded-share concentration: on prescriber NPI x drug class, compute the ratio of branded manufacturer NDC claims to all HIV-regimen claims in the payer's remittance history; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit on subsequent claims.

611.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the days-of-supply field on the insulin NDC claim equals the plan's benefit maximum exactly rather than the metric quantity dispensed divided by the sig daily dose. Metric decimal quantity on the claim reflects a full five-pen carton while reported days-of-supply is capped below it. The refill claim's date of service falls before the prior fill's quantity would have been exhausted at the prescribed daily dose. Repeated fills for the same beneficiary and NDC show identical truncated days-of-supply values across many pharmacy NPIs in one chain TIN. No plan override or prior-authorisation record exists for the quantity exceeding the days-of-supply limit.
611.features_to_create: 1) Days-supply arithmetic mismatch: on claim line, compute metric decimal quantity divided by the sig daily dose and subtract the reported days-of-supply field; fires when the difference is positive and the reported value equals the plan maximum; action prepay edit. 2) Premature refill gap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute the gap in days between consecutive fill dates of service minus the quantity-derived true days-of-supply; fires when the gap is negative without a documented override record; action claim suspension. 3) Chain truncation rate: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of insulin NDC lines whose reported days-of-supply exactly equals the plan cap while quantity implies more; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-chain peers; action postpay audit.

612.ways_to_identify: At claim adjudication, oncology claims cite a referring NPI whose group holds a hospital medical-directorship contract lacking supporting time records. The hospital's disclosed financial relationships on its Stark self-disclosure and contract register show payment dates after the written agreement expiry date. Referral concentration from one oncology TIN to one hospital TIN rises sharply in the payer's own remittance history after the contract start date. Directorship compensation per hour on the contract file exceeds fair-market-value benchmarks for that specialty and locality. Physician-owned entity disclosures on the hospital's CMS-855A ownership fields omit the paid oncology practice as a financial relationship.
612.features_to_create: 1) Expired-arrangement referral flow: on referring NPI x hospital TIN, compute the count of paid inpatient and outpatient oncology claims with dates of service after the contract expiry date on the disclosed arrangement register; fires when that count exceeds zero; action postpay audit. 2) Referral concentration shift: on referring NPI x hospital TIN x quarter, compute the share of that physician's total referrals going to the contracted hospital versus his pre-contract trailing baseline; fires when the share rises above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Undocumented directorship pay: on physician TIN x month, compute the ratio of directorship dollars paid to logged director hours on submitted time records; fires when logged hours are zero or the implied hourly rate exceeds the fair-market benchmark; action postpay audit.

613.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the pharmacy's paid NDC claims lack a matching dispensing event in the pharmacy management system fill and pickup logs. Prescriptions billed then reversed and rebilled without a new fill show refill-too-soon patterns in the payer's own remittance history. Dispensed quantity summed by NDC exceeds the pharmacy's wholesaler acquisition volume in pedigree and ARCOS purchase data. Ingredient average wholesale prices reported by the compounding supplier exceed published pricing compendia benchmarks for the same NDC. Laboratory referral volume from one physician group rises after payments recorded in the hospital's disclosed financial arrangement register.
613.features_to_create: 1) Dispense-without-pickup: on beneficiary x NDC x fill date, compute the gap in days between the paid claim date of service and the recorded pickup or delivery confirmation in the pharmacy dispensing log; fires when no pickup record exists within the return-to-stock window; action prepay edit. 2) Purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute the ratio of units billed to units acquired per wholesaler pedigree and ARCOS data; fires when billed units exceed acquired units; action payment suspension. 3) AWP outlier: on NDC x reporting supplier, compute the ratio of reported average wholesale price to the compendia median for the same ingredient; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus peer ingredients; action prepay edit.

614.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, nerve-block CPT lines carry a drug or device with no FDA-approved NDC or HCPCS, visible in the claim's drug fields. Ultrasound-guidance CPT is billed on nearly every procedure line by one rendering NPI without a stored image report. Group-home residential day claims overlap inpatient hospital stay dates for the same beneficiary in the payer's other claims. Rendering NPIs listed on hyperbaric therapy claims have no NPPES address or credentialing link to the billing TIN. Controlled-substance waste and administration records in the automated dispensing cabinet log do not reconcile with the fentanyl units billed on patient accounts.
614.features_to_create: 1) Non-covered device masquerade: on rendering NPI x CPT, compute the share of procedure lines whose paired drug NDC or device HCPCS is absent from the FDA approved product file; fires when the share exceeds zero; action prepay edit. 2) Residential-inpatient overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of residential or group-home per-diem units billed on dates falling inside a paid inpatient, incarceration or hospice claim span; fires when that count exceeds zero; action prepay edit. 3) Unauthorised rendering identity: on rendering NPI x billing TIN, compute the count of paid claims where no credentialing or CMS-855 reassignment link exists between that NPI and the TIN; fires on exact registry mismatch in PECOS; action claim suspension.

615.ways_to_identify: This is a personnel announcement with no claim, provider or payment decision, so there is no adjudication point. The nearest non-claims route is routine agency press monitoring, which yields no detection signal.

616.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, chelation J-code and infusion CPT lines lack any claim-history diagnosis of heavy-metal poisoning for that beneficiary. No laboratory claim for blood or urine heavy-metal testing precedes the chelation administration date for the same beneficiary. One rendering NPI's chelation infusion units per beneficiary per year exceed the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers. Repeat chelation sessions continue for months with no interval toxic-level laboratory result in the beneficiary's other claims. The practice's share of total billing concentrated in chelation drug and infusion codes far exceeds its own trailing baseline.
616.features_to_create: 1) Missing toxicity indication: on claim line, compute the count of heavy-metal poisoning diagnosis codes on the chelation claim and in the beneficiary's 12-month diagnosis history; fires when that count is zero; action prepay edit. 2) Pre-treatment lab absence: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the gap in days between the chelation date of service and the most recent paid heavy-metal laboratory test; fires when no such test exists in the lookback window; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Chelation intensity outlier: on rendering NPI x year, compute chelation infusion units per treated beneficiary over J-code and CPT units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

617.ways_to_identify: This is a resignation announcement, containing no claim, no billing provider and no payment decision to adjudicate. The nearest non-claims route does not apply because no scheme is described.

618.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, DMEPOS claims name an ordering NPI with no prior evaluation-and-management encounter with that beneficiary in claim history. A small set of ordering NPIs signs certificates of medical necessity for an implausibly large distinct-beneficiary count in one week. Beneficiary complaint records in the payer's contact-center file name the same supplier NPI repeatedly before payment. Beneficiary residence ZIPs sit far outside the service area declared on the supplier's CMS-855S enrolment record. Signature dates on submitted certificates of medical necessity precede the recorded physician-beneficiary encounter date on any claim.
618.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the days between the DMEPOS date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) CMN signer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the distinct-beneficiary count and distinct supplier-NPI count on signed certificates of medical necessity; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Complaint-linked supplier: on supplier NPI x month, compute the count of beneficiary complaints in the contact-center file per hundred paid DMEPOS claims; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action site visit.

619.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, because the false submissions were employee travel and time vouchers on a federal contract. The nearest detection route is contractor expense-voucher auditing against badge access, hotel folios and airline records. Claimed labour hours can be reconciled against timekeeping and facility entry logs.
619.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on employee ID x travel voucher, compute claimed work hours and expense dates against badge-access and receipt records; fires when claimed hours occur on dates with no corroborating record; action contractor audit and suspension of reimbursement.

620.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the prescribing DEA number on the Schedule II claim belongs to a veterinarian not enrolled to treat human beneficiaries in PECOS. The patient name on the pharmacy claim has no matching Medicaid member ID or date of birth in eligibility files. Fill dates fall after the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File. The dispensing pharmacy's controlled-substance acquisitions in ARCOS fall short of the Schedule II quantities dispensed under that DEA number. The same beneficiary's stimulant prescription is filled and billed by a pharmacist NPI who is also the listed patient.
620.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber-scope mismatch: on claim line, compare the prescriber DEA registration business activity and state licence board file specialty against human-patient eligibility; fires on exact registry mismatch for a veterinary registrant; action prepay edit. 2) Ghost patient identity: on claim line, compute the match rate of billed patient name, date of birth and member ID against the Medicaid eligibility and Death Master File records; fires when no exact match exists or fill date follows date of death; action claim suspension. 3) Dispenser self-fill and inventory gap: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x month, compute dispensed units minus ARCOS wholesaler acquisition units, plus the count of fills where dispensing pharmacist equals the patient; fires when the difference is positive or that count is above zero; action postpay audit.

621.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, an owner or managing employee listed on the facility's CMS-855A ownership fields matches an individual on the OIG LEIE exclusion file. Bank account and pay-to address on the CMS-588 EFT record match those previously used by an excluded provider's prior entity. PECOS shows the excluded individual's home address or phone reused as the new entity's correspondence contact. At adjudication, counseling H-code units billed per rendering NPI per day exceed the hours available in a 24-hour workday. Beneficiary rosters overlap heavily with the excluded owner's prior billing entity in the payer's own remittance history.
621.features_to_create: 1) Exclusion graph match: on TIN x owner SSN, compute the count of CMS-855A owners, managing employees and authorized officials matching OIG LEIE or state exclusion records; fires on any exact registry match; action payment suspension. 2) Shared-identifier successor: on bank account, compute the distinct count of billing TINs sharing that EFT account, address or phone with a previously excluded entity; fires when that count exceeds one; action site visit. 3) Counselor day impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total billed counseling minutes from H0004/H0015 units; fires when total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit.

622.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, G0438 or G0439 is billed without any documented health risk assessment element in the encounter record supporting the wellness visit. The same beneficiary shows G0438 initial wellness visits billed more than once in a lifetime across the payer's claim history. G0439 subsequent wellness visits appear at intervals shorter than the 11 full months required by the benefit rule. Wellness visit volume per rendering NPI per day exceeds the visit minutes physically available in that provider's scheduled hours. The rendering NPI on the wellness claim is a non-physician whose specialty in PECOS was not supervised or enrolled during the service period.
622.features_to_create: 1) Lifetime and interval rule: on beneficiary x HCPCS, compute the count of paid G0438 lines lifetime and the month gap between consecutive G0439 dates of service; fires when G0438 count exceeds one or the gap is under 11 months; action prepay edit. 2) Wellness visit day capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of G0438/G0439 lines multiplied by the typical visit minutes; fires when the product exceeds 24 hours; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Wellness billing rate outlier: on provider NPI, compute the ratio of G0438/G0439 lines to total E/M lines against the provider's trailing 24-month baseline; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

623.ways_to_identify: This entry is an annual collections announcement covering several unrelated matters, so there is no single claim stream or adjudication point to edit. The nearest non-claims route is tracking each underlying civil settlement and judgment through the office's debt and lien files. A secondary route is matching settling provider TINs to active enrolment records so future billing is monitored under integrity agreements.
623.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on settling TIN, compute whether the entity remains active in PECOS after judgment entry and route active ones to revalidation review.

624.ways_to_identify: The release reports only asset sale proceeds applied to a prior civil settlement, with no billing mechanic and no claim to adjudicate. There is no prepayment decision point because the conduct was already resolved civilly. The nearest non-claims route is the Financial Litigation Unit's asset and lien tracking against the judgment debtor.
624.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on judgment debtor TIN, compute open judgment balance against recorded real-property liens and refer unsecured balances for collection.

625.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on DMEPOS and diagnostic lab claims has no prior E/M encounter with that beneficiary. One staffing-agency-placed ordering physician signs orders for beneficiaries across many states within a single week. The same beneficiary receives an identical L-code brace and a large panel lab test ordered by the same NPI on the same date. Ordering volume for a physician jumps from near-zero to peer-top-decile immediately after a locum tenens contract start recorded in PECOS reassignment fields. Multiple unrelated supplier and laboratory NPIs submit claims citing the identical ordering NPI and identical diagnosis code strings.
625.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that ordering NPI and beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the distinct count of beneficiary states, supplier NPIs and laboratory NPIs on ordered claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Paired DME-lab bundle: on beneficiary x ordering NPI x date of service, compute the count of DMEPOS L-code lines co-occurring with high-value diagnostic panel lines; fires when that count exceeds the provider's trailing baseline rate; action documentation request (ADR).

626.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, telehealth psychotherapy units billed per rendering NPI per date of service exceed the minutes available in 24 hours. Psychotherapy CPT 90837 lines lack any documented session start and stop times in the encounter record supporting the 60-minute threshold. The same beneficiary receives duplicate telehealth counseling claims from several unrelated group TINs on the same date of service. Dental claims cluster around a small set of beneficiary addresses and phone numbers repeated across unrelated NPPES beneficiary records, indicating recruiter steering. Marketing or recruiter payments appear as contracted managing entities on the practice's CMS-855 ownership and managing-employee fields.
626.features_to_create: 1) Telehealth minute impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total psychotherapy minutes implied by 90832/90834/90837 units plus place-of-service 02/10 lines; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Duplicate session overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlapping billed session minutes across distinct rendering NPIs and TINs; fires when overlapping minutes exceed zero; action claim suspension. 3) Recruiter address concentration: on dental practice NPI, compute the distinct-beneficiary count sharing a single address or phone number in claim demographic fields divided by total beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action site visit.

627.ways_to_identify: This item is a debt-collection recap of restitution already ordered, so there is no pending claim and no adjudication point remaining. The nearest non-claims route is financial: Treasury Offset Program and lien filings matched to the defendant's TIN and bank accounts. The nearest forward-looking route is enrolment screening, checking OIG LEIE and CMS-855 ownership fields before any affiliated entity bills TRICARE, VA or Medicare.
627.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Affiliation carryover: on provider NPI x owner SSN/TIN from CMS-855 ownership fields, compute the count of matches to OIG LEIE and convicted-party restitution lists; fires when the match is an exact registry hit; action prepay edit.

628.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, claims cite beneficiary IDs whose access came from an employee account with no corresponding encounter in the practice's other claims history. A single rendering NPI shows a sudden burst of new beneficiaries never previously seen in the payer's remittance history. Billed beneficiaries' residence ZIPs on the eligibility file lie far outside the billing provider's service area. Payment goes to a bank account on the CMS-855 EFT page that recently changed and is shared with unrelated billing TINs. Beneficiaries deny service when surveyed, and no ordering NPI or prior-auth record supports the dates of service.
628.features_to_create: 1) New-beneficiary burst: on provider NPI x week, compute the count of beneficiaries with no prior paid claim to that NPI divided by total beneficiaries billed; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action claim suspension. 2) Shared payee account: on bank account number from the CMS-855 EFT record, compute the distinct count of billing TINs receiving remittance; fires when that count exceeds one without documented common ownership; action payment suspension. 3) Orphan-encounter check: on claim line, compute the days between date of service and the nearest other claim for that beneficiary with the same TIN; fires when no supporting encounter exists in the lookback window; action documentation request (ADR).

629.ways_to_identify: This is an annual district collections total spanning unrelated contract, estate-theft and lender-fraud matters, with no health care claim and no adjudication point. The nearest non-claims route is contract-level verification of deliverables before federal grant or contract invoices are paid. A second route is Financial Litigation Unit asset tracing against sentenced defendants.
629.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on federal contract invoice, compute whether required deliverable artifacts such as security test reports were filed before payment release.

630.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, Payroll-Based Journal nurse hours per resident day fall below the state minimum for the facility CCN's census on the same dates billed as skilled RUG/PDPM days. MDS assessments record new Stage 2+ pressure ulcers, UTIs and falls acquired after admission at rates above same-state peers. The PDPM nursing case-mix component billed implies staffing intensity the PBJ file cannot support for those dates of service. Hospital claims for the same beneficiaries show emergency transfers for sepsis or fracture within days of the billed SNF days. State survey deficiency citations for staffing overlap the same billing periods on the CMS-2567 record.
630.features_to_create: 1) Staffing-to-billing mismatch: on facility CCN x day, compute PBJ total nurse hours divided by resident census and compare to the state minimum hours per resident day; fires when the ratio falls below the regulatory minimum on days billed as skilled; action prepay edit. 2) Acquired-harm rate: on facility CCN x quarter, compute the count of MDS-coded facility-acquired pressure ulcers, UTIs and falls divided by resident days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action postpay audit. 3) Case-mix versus hours: on facility CCN x month, compute mean PDPM nursing component index minus PBJ-implied staffing index; fires when the gap is above the facility's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR).

631.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, EVV visit records place the rendering aide's GPS location away from the client's address on the billed dates of service. Two personal care or community support claim lines for the same rendering NPI show overlapping service minutes for different beneficiaries. Summed billed units per rendering NPI per day exceed the hours physically available in 24 hours. Disability and medical-excuse documentation carries a physician NPI that never submitted any claim for that patient on the stated treatment dates. The same attending physician signature and note template appear across unrelated claimants in the same employer group.
631.features_to_create: 1) EVV geofence mismatch: on claim line, compute the distance between the EVV check-in coordinates and the beneficiary's address on the eligibility file; fires when the distance exceeds the geofence radius for that visit; action prepay edit. 2) Aide overlap: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total overlapping billed service minutes across distinct beneficiaries; fires when overlapping minutes exceed zero or daily units exceed 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Phantom-certifier check: on certifying physician NPI x claimant, compute the count of that physician's paid encounter claims for the claimant within the certified treatment window; fires when that count is zero; action documentation request (ADR).

632.ways_to_identify: This is an annual roundup of more than twenty unrelated civil recoveries, so there is no single claim stream or adjudication point. The nearest non-claims route is tracking each settlement separately through the district's civil recovery and debt files. Individual mechanics such as inflated price reporting and non-terminal hospice would each need their own control if pursued as separate cases.
632.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on reported Average Wholesale Price submissions, compute variance against wholesaler acquisition cost files and refer outliers to the pricing compendia auditor.

633.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, E/M and procedure claims list a rendering NPI on dates when passport or travel records place that physician outside the country. Rendering NPI daily billed time across all payers exceeds the hours available in 24 hours at that place of service. Controlled-substance prescriptions under one prescriber DEA number show high-dose opioid and benzodiazepine combinations across a wide beneficiary radius in PDMP data. Visit intervals per beneficiary cluster at the minimum refill spacing with identical CPT levels every encounter. Incident-to claims lack any supervising-physician presence documented in the practice's schedule or timesheets.
633.features_to_create: 1) Impossible-day rendering: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total CPT-implied service minutes summed across all claim lines and payers; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or falls on documented absence dates; action claim suspension. 2) Prescriber concentration: on prescriber DEA/NPI x month, compute the count of beneficiaries receiving opioid plus benzodiazepine on overlapping days divided by panel size; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Cloned-visit ratio: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of E/M claims at a single CPT level with identical diagnosis code sets; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR).

634.ways_to_identify: This is an annual statistical release of district collection totals with no named defendant, payer or billing scheme. There is no claim and no adjudication point to control. The nearest non-claims route is case-level tracking of the underlying False Claims Act and Controlled Substances Act penalty matters as they are individually resolved.
634.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on each resolved provider judgment, compute remaining balance and enrolment status to trigger revalidation review.

635.ways_to_identify: At each compensation payment cycle, match the claimed dependent spouse SSN on Form CA-1032 against the Social Security Death Master File. Compare the dependent's name on the augmented-rate benefit record to state vital-records divorce decree files. Check whether the dependent spouse appears on any beneficiary's other claims or tax filings after the stated marriage date. Compute the elapsed years since the last signed CA-1032 dependency recertification on the claimant's case file. Flag augmented-rate cases where no dependent has appeared as an enrolled dependent in the payer's own health-benefit enrolment file.
635.features_to_create: 1) Dependent death match: on beneficiary x payment cycle, compute a match of the dependent SSN and date of birth on Form CA-1032 against the Death Master File; fires when an exact registry match with a death date before the payment date exists; action payment suspension. 2) Augmentation recertification gap: on beneficiary, compute the days between the payment date and the most recent signed CA-1032 dependency attestation; fires when the gap exceeds the program's annual recertification interval; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Marital-status conflict: on beneficiary, compute the count of state vital-records divorce or remarriage events dated after the dependency attestation date; fires when that count is at least one; action claim suspension, then postpay audit.

636.ways_to_identify: This is a loan-eligibility certification scheme, so there is no health care claim and no adjudication point in the payer's system. The nearest non-claims route is comparing each applicant entity's certified headcount to commonly owned affiliate structures. CMS-855A ownership and managing-control disclosures identify the affiliated chain that defeats the small-business certification.
636.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on applicant EIN, compute the total employee count across all entities sharing owners, officers or managing control in CMS-855A and state licence filings, and fires when the affiliated total exceeds the program size standard.

637.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, billed units of an NDC exceed the pharmacy's wholesaler pedigree and ARCOS acquisition quantities for the same period. Refill intervals on chronic NDCs are shorter than the prior fill's days supply for many beneficiaries. Beneficiaries billed by the pharmacy have no matching prescriber encounter claim from the listed prescriber NPI. High-cost NDC volume jumps far above the pharmacy's own trailing baseline without any change in unique beneficiary count. Beneficiary ZIP codes on paid claims cluster far outside the pharmacy's CMS-855B service area.
637.features_to_create: 1) Inventory reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x month, compute billed dispensed units minus purchased units from wholesaler pedigree and 340B or ARCOS records; fires when billed exceeds purchased; action payment suspension. 2) Early refill accumulation: on beneficiary x NDC, compute the gap in days between consecutive fill dates minus the prior days supply; fires when the gap is negative on a count of fills above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action prepay edit. 3) Orphan prescription: on claim line, compute the count of encounter claims between the listed prescriber NPI and the beneficiary in the lookback window; fires when that count is zero; action documentation request (ADR).

638.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on CGX panel CPT codes has no prior treating encounter claim with that beneficiary. The ordering telehealth NPI submits CGX orders for beneficiaries across multiple state Medicaid programs in one week. Beneficiary residence ZIPs cluster far outside the laboratory's CMS-855B service area on file. The same beneficiary receives duplicate hereditary cancer panel CPT codes from unrelated laboratory NPIs within a short window. No oncology or family-history diagnosis appears anywhere in the beneficiary's claim history supporting the panel.
638.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the days between the CGX date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Telehealth orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and distinct laboratory NPIs on ordered molecular pathology CPT lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Germline panel duplication: on beneficiary x CPT, compute the count of distinct laboratory NPIs paid for hereditary cancer panels in the member's lifetime; fires when that count exceeds one; action prior-authorisation requirement.

639.ways_to_identify: This is an annual statistical collections announcement with no named defendant, no claim and no adjudication point. The reported totals aggregate many unrelated civil and criminal matters. The nearest non-claims route is per-case tracking of False Claims Act and Controlled Substances Act resolutions in the district's debt files.
