639.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on each resolved provider TIN, compute open judgment balance against current enrolment status and refer active billers to integrity-agreement monitoring.

640.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, inpatient rehabilitation facility claims lack a documented IRF-PAI showing the required intensive therapy tolerance and multidisciplinary need. Compare the beneficiary's prior claims: admissions arriving directly from the same acute hospital under common ownership suggest routing rather than clinical need. The certifying physician NPI on the IRF preadmission screen signs a share of admissions far above same-specialty peers. Case-mix group distribution on the facility's claims skews to high-weight CMGs relative to state IRF peers. Short lengths of stay with rapid discharge home contradict the certified need for hospital-level rehabilitation.
640.features_to_create: 1) IRF certification concentration: on certifying physician NPI x quarter, compute the count of IRF admissions certified and the share lacking a prior 3-day acute stay or qualifying condition in the 60% rule list; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Therapy intensity shortfall: on claim (IRF stay), compute total therapy minutes from the IRF-PAI divided by length of stay in days; fires when below the intensive-therapy threshold in the coverage rule; action prepay edit. 3) Referral funnel: on referring hospital NPI x IRF NPI, compute the share of that IRF's admissions originating from one commonly owned hospital per CMS-855A ownership fields; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer IRFs; action postpay audit.

641.ways_to_identify: This is an office personnel announcement with no claim, no defendant, and no adjudication point to intervene at. No dates of service, HCPCS codes, or provider NPIs are identified, so no edit can be written. The nearest non-claims route is tracking case outcomes into the payer's provider-sanction and OIG LEIE screening feed.
641.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Ingest published settlement and exclusion outcomes into the enrolment screening file so affected NPIs and owners are re-screened at revalidation.

642.ways_to_identify: This is a resignation press release with no billing conduct, no claim line, and no adjudication point. The recoveries mentioned involve contractors and software vendors rather than payer-adjudicated claims. The nearest non-claims route is contract and grant oversight by the awarding agency's inspector general.
642.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Certified EHR vendor attestations can be re-verified against ONC certification records during incentive-program audits.

643.ways_to_identify: This announces a new prosecutorial unit, not a scheme, so there is no claim and no adjudication point. No provider NPI, code, or date of service is identified for an edit. The nearest non-claims route is routine referral of payer analytics leads to that unit.
643.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Maintain a standing referral pipeline from payer program-integrity analytics to the prosecuting office.

644.ways_to_identify: This is customs duty underpayment on imported goods, with no health care claim and no adjudication point. The relevant record is the CBP entry summary and commercial invoice, not a remittance file. The nearest detection route is CBP reconciliation of declared entered value against the importer's paid-invoice and wire-transfer records. Prior auditor warnings to the importer create a documented knowledge trail for penalty exposure.
644.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. CBP can compare declared value per entry summary against the importer's ledgered payments to the supplier and open a focused assessment on divergence.

645.ways_to_identify: At enrolment reconciliation, compare the plan's broker compensation payments against CMS broker compensation caps in the plan bid and marketing files. Payments labeled as marketing, co-op, or data fees to a field marketing organization exceed per-enrollee caps in the same period. Enrollment files show one broker NPN steering a dominant share of members into a single contract despite multi-carrier appointment. Disenrollment within 90 days of a broker-sourced enrollment runs far above the contract's own trailing baseline. Enrollment rates for beneficiaries with disability-based original entitlement fall below plan-service-area demographics in the CMS enrollment data.
645.features_to_create: 1) Broker payment cap test: on broker organization TIN x contract x year, compute total payments of all types divided by enrollments produced; fires when the quotient exceeds the CMS compensation cap for that year; action payment suspension. 2) Steering concentration: on broker NPN x quarter, compute the share of enrollments going to one parent-organization contract; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers appointed with the same carrier set; action postpay audit. 3) Disability enrollment shortfall: on contract x county, compute the ratio of disabled-entitlement enrollees to the county's Medicare disabled share; fires when below the calibrated percentile versus peer contracts in the same market; action documentation request (ADR).

646.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on high-cost molecular CPT claims has no prior office or telehealth E/M encounter with that beneficiary. One ordering NPI's beneficiaries span many states outside the ordering physician's licensed state per the state licence board file. Ordered panels repeat the same CPT set for nearly every beneficiary, indicating a template rather than clinical selection. No downstream treatment, drug NDC, or follow-up E/M claim appears in the beneficiary's claim history after the result date. The telehealth E/M that does exist is a minimal-duration code billed on the same day as the order for dozens of patients.
646.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the specimen date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that ordering NPI and beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer panel uniformity: on ordering NPI x month, compute the distinct-value count of molecular CPT combinations divided by the count of beneficiaries ordered for; fires when below the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Result non-use: on beneficiary x molecular CPT, compute the count of subsequent E/M, drug, or procedure claims by the ordering NPI within 180 days; fires when that count is zero for a provider whose zero-rate is above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action postpay audit.

647.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the group's ratio of surgical debridement CPT 11042-11047 to nonsurgical CPT 97597-97598 sits far above same-specialty peers. Rendering NPIs show no wound care or surgical specialty in NPPES taxonomy or board certification files. Modifier 25 appears on nearly every E/M line paired with a same-day debridement by the same rendering NPI. Debridement counts per rendering NPI per date of service across multiple nursing facilities imply impossible travel and service minutes. Serial debridements recur on the same beneficiary and wound site at fixed intervals regardless of MDS-documented wound status.
647.features_to_create: 1) Surgical debridement mix: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute surgical debridement lines divided by all debridement lines using CPT 11042-11047 and 97597-97598; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit on the surgical codes. 2) Modifier 25 saturation: on rendering NPI x month, compute the share of E/M lines carrying Modifier 25 with a same-day global-period procedure by that NPI; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension pending documentation request (ADR). 3) Per-day service feasibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of CMS time or work-value proxies for all debridement and E/M lines plus travel between distinct facility addresses; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action payment suspension.

648.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on the lab's molecular claims has no prior claim history with the beneficiary establishing a treating relationship. A single billing agent's submitter ID files claims for multiple lab NPIs with identical panel composition and coding patterns. Beneficiary residence ZIPs cluster far outside the lab's CLIA site and service area on the CMS-855B enrolment record. Ordering NPIs are concentrated in a handful of physicians producing volumes above same-specialty peers. The lab's paid volume rises from near-zero to top decile within weeks of a new billing submitter ID being registered.
648.features_to_create: 1) Submitter fan-out: on billing submitter ID x month, compute the distinct count of billing lab NPIs and the correlation of their CPT mix; fires when distinct NPIs and mix similarity are both above the calibrated percentile versus peer submitters; action prepay edit. 2) Treating-relationship test: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the count of E/M claims between that ordering NPI and beneficiary in the prior 12 months; fires when the count is zero; action claim suspension. 3) Geographic dispersion: on lab NPI x month, compute the share of beneficiaries whose residence state differs from the CLIA laboratory state; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action site visit.

649.ways_to_identify: At MLR reconciliation, compare the plan's reported allowed medical expenses in the DHCS financial template against claim-level paid detail by provider NPI. Large lump-sum provider payments lacking encounter records or member attribution indicate non-claims spending booked as medical. Payment issue dates fall after the contract period close but are booked to the prior period, visible in the general ledger date fields. Retroactive rate increases appear in provider remittance history without a corresponding amended contract in the contract file. Payments trace to consultant and technology vendors downstream of the provider, visible in the provider's own subcontractor disclosures.
649.features_to_create: 1) Unmatched medical expense: on plan contract x rate year, compute reported allowed medical expense minus the sum of adjudicated claim and encounter payments tied to member IDs; fires when the residual exceeds the plan's own trailing baseline residual share; action postpay audit with documentation request (ADR). 2) Backdated booking: on payment transaction, compute days between check issue date and the end of the accounting period credited; fires when the gap exceeds the contractual accrual window; action payment suspension of the reconciliation settlement. 3) Incentive lump-sum test: on provider NPI x payment, compute the ratio of non-claim incentive dollars to that provider's adjudicated claim dollars in the same period; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer providers in the network; action prepay edit on the settlement release.

650.ways_to_identify: At MLR reconciliation, reported allowed medical expenses exceed the sum of member-attributable adjudicated claims in the encounter file. Bulk incentive payments to network providers carry no encounter records or quality-measure numerators in the quality reporting file. Ledger entries show service dates backdated into the closing rate year while checks issued afterwards. A retroactive rate increase appears in remittance history without an executed contract amendment on file with DHCS. Funds paid to providers are re-routed to consultants and IT vendors, traceable in subcontractor disclosure forms.
650.features_to_create: 1) Encounter-backed expense ratio: on plan contract x rate year, compute adjudicated claim dollars tied to member IDs divided by reported allowed medical expense; fires when below the 85% floor stated in the funding rule; action payment suspension of the reconciliation. 2) Incentive without measure: on provider NPI x incentive payment, compute the count of linked quality-measure numerators or encounters; fires when the count is zero; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Period-shifting: on payment transaction, compute the gap in days between the credited period end and the actual disbursement date in the bank account record; fires when the gap exceeds the contractual accrual window; action postpay audit.

651.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, facility payroll-based journal nurse-hours per resident day fall far below the CMS staffing expectation for the billed RUG or PDPM level. MDS assessments report wound care and feeding assistance at frequencies unsupported by the PBJ staffing hours filed for the same days. Resident weight-loss and pressure-ulcer quality measures in MDS worsen while high-acuity per-diem billing rises. Charted service entries carry timestamps clustered in bulk after shift end, visible in EHR audit-log exports. State survey deficiency citations for care planning coincide with the billed dates of service.
651.features_to_create: 1) Staffing-to-acuity mismatch: on facility CCN x quarter, compute PBJ nurse hours per resident day divided by the case-mix-expected hours implied by billed PDPM components; fires when the ratio falls below the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension. 2) Charting burst: on facility CCN x date of service, compute the share of clinical entries whose EHR audit-log creation timestamp is more than one shift after the documented care time; fires when above the facility's own trailing baseline; action postpay audit. 3) Outcome divergence: on facility CCN x quarter, compute the change in MDS-derived unplanned weight loss and new pressure ulcer rates alongside the change in high-acuity per-diem share; fires when outcomes worsen while acuity billing rises above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action site visit.

652.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, implantable neurostimulator CPT 64553/64555 is billed with an office place of service rather than a facility operating room. No corresponding implantable pulse generator HCPCS or device NDC appears on any claim for that beneficiary. No facility, anesthesia, or imaging claim exists on the same date of service for a purported surgical implantation. The rendering NPI's NPPES taxonomy carries no neurosurgical or pain-implant privileges in the state licence board file. Beneficiaries receive repeat implantation codes at short intervals, which is impossible for a single implanted device.
652.features_to_create: 1) Device-absent implant: on claim line, compute the count of matching implantable device HCPCS or facility claims for the same beneficiary within the implant date window; fires when the count is zero for CPT 64553-64595; action prepay edit. 2) Place-of-service impossibility: on claim line, compare the place-of-service code against the CMS facility-only list for the billed implantation CPT; fires on exact mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Repeat implantation: on beneficiary x implant CPT, compute the count of paid implantation events in a rolling 12 months; fires when the count exceeds one without a documented revision or removal code; action postpay audit.

653.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, total billed psychotherapy minutes from timed CPT 90832-90838 for a rendering NPI on one date exceed 24 hours. Dates of service overlap periods when the rendering NPI has no in-state activity, testable against travel or hotel records obtained on audit. Claims list the supervising psychiatrist as rendering while shift schedules show other practitioners delivered the sessions. Face-to-face place-of-service 11 is billed on days the provider filed no other local claims across any payer in remittance history. The same rendering NPI appears on claims from multiple distant practice addresses on identical dates of service.
653.features_to_create: 1) Minutes-per-day feasibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of CPT-defined service minutes for all timed psychotherapy and E/M lines; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours or exceeds the calibrated percentile of peer psychiatrists; action prepay edit. 2) Geographic impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the maximum straight-line distance between billed service addresses; fires when travel between them is infeasible within the same day; action claim suspension. 3) Incident-to substitution: on rendering NPI x week, compute the count of face-to-face lines billed under that NPI divided by documented on-site hours from facility timesheets; fires when the quotient exceeds one; action documentation request (ADR).

654.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the facility's share of ultra-high therapy RUG or highest PDPM case-mix levels far exceeds same-state SNF peers. Therapy minutes on the MDS cluster just above the threshold for the top payment tier. EHR audit logs show MDS and assessment fields edited by a user whose licence in the state board file does not permit clinical documentation. Claims are submitted before the assessment reference date documentation is finalised, visible in the gap between claim receipt date and record completion timestamp. Therapy volume per resident rises without corresponding change in admission diagnosis mix on the claim header.
654.features_to_create: 1) Threshold clustering: on facility CCN x quarter, compute the share of MDS therapy-minute values falling within a narrow band just above the top payment tier cut-point; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Unlicensed record edit: on MDS assessment record, compute the count of clinical field edits by user IDs whose credential in the state licence board file lacks clinical scope; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 3) Claim-before-documentation: on claim, compute days between claim submission date and the completion timestamp of the supporting assessment; fires when the value is negative; action prepay edit.

655.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, rapid strep CPT 87880 and influenza CPT 87804 are billed without any symptom-bearing ICD-10 diagnosis on the same claim. Testing rate per E/M visit at the clinic NPI far exceeds same-specialty urgent-care peers. Level 4 and 5 E/M code share for respiratory diagnoses sits above the clinic's own pre-pandemic trailing baseline. Documented visit time on the record falls below the minimum time floor for the billed time-based E/M code. Positivity rate on the billed rapid tests is far below the regional public health reporting rate, indicating untargeted testing.
655.features_to_create: 1) Test-without-indication: on claim line, compute whether any ICD-10 code on the claim appears in the coverage-approved indication list for CPT 87880 or 87804; fires on exact mismatch with the covered-diagnosis file; action prepay edit. 2) E/M level drift: on billing NPI x quarter, compute the share of E/M lines at levels 4-5 for respiratory diagnoses; fires when above the provider's own trailing pre-period baseline and above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 3) Reflex testing rate: on clinic NPI x month, compute rapid antigen test lines divided by distinct E/M visits; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus urgent-care peers; action documentation request (ADR).

656.ways_to_identify: This is an annual collections round-up that names no billing mechanic, code, payer, or conduct period. Without a claim type or provider NPI, no adjudication-point edit can be specified. The nearest non-claims route is matching restitution and forfeiture judgments to the payer's overpayment recovery ledger and to grant-award oversight.
656.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Reconcile court-ordered restitution judgments against the payer's accounts-receivable file so recovered amounts offset outstanding overpayments.

657.ways_to_identify: At benefit recertification, the claimant's sworn EN-1032 earnings certification reports no work while state wage-reporting records show covered employment. Commercial driver licence and DOT medical certification records show an active CDL held during the disability period. Employer quarterly wage filings under the claimant's SSN identify a trucking employer during certified non-work months. Public volunteer fire department rosters list the claimant during the same benefit period. Medical restrictions on file conflict with the physical demands documented in the CDL medical examiner certificate.
657.features_to_create: 1) Earnings certification match: on claimant SSN x certification period, compute wages reported in state new-hire and quarterly wage files during months certified as no-work on the EN-1032; fires when reported wages exceed zero; action payment suspension. 2) Licence activity conflict: on claimant SSN, compute whether an active CDL and DOT medical certificate exist with issue dates inside the disability period; fires on exact registry match; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Duration outlier: on claimant x injury code, compute total benefit months paid versus the same injury-code cohort; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers with equivalent impairment ratings; action postpay audit.

658.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, HRSA Uninsured Program claims carry patient identifiers that match an active commercial or Medicaid coverage record in the eligibility clearinghouse. The submitter's own intake file already contains a payer name and member ID for the same patient encounter. Duplicate paid claims exist for the same beneficiary and date of service in a commercial payer's remittance history. The share of claims submitted with missing or placeholder demographic fields is far above peer submitters. Eligibility verification transaction logs show a 271 response confirming coverage before the uninsured claim was filed.
658.features_to_create: 1) Coverage crossmatch: on claim line, compute whether the patient identifier matches an active coverage segment in the eligibility file on the date of service; fires on exact match; action prepay edit. 2) Verification contradiction: on claim, compute the count of 270/271 eligibility transactions by that submitter for the same patient returning active coverage before submission; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 3) Data-integrity rate: on submitter NPI x month, compute the share of claims with missing SSN, date of birth, or address fields; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer uninsured-program submitters; action documentation request (ADR).

659.ways_to_identify: At invoice adjudication, the unit price billed exceeds the ceiling price on the contract line item in the federal supply schedule file. Price variance for the same part number differs across federal customers within the same period. Credit memos issued to complaining customers exist without matching corrective credits to other customers who bought at the same wrong price. Contract modification effective dates precede invoices still charging the superseded higher price. Discount terms in the pricing agreement are absent from the vendor's order-entry system extract.
659.features_to_create: 1) Contract price mismatch: on invoice line, compute billed unit price minus the contract ceiling price for that part number and effective date; fires when the difference is positive; action prepay edit. 2) Cross-customer price dispersion: on part number x quarter, compute the distinct-value count and range of unit prices charged across federal customers; fires when the range exceeds the contracted discount band; action postpay audit. 3) Unremediated credit: on part number x overcharge event, compute the count of customers charged the erroneous price minus the count receiving credits; fires when the difference exceeds zero; action payment suspension pending refund.

660.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on L-code brace and compounded pain cream claims has no prior E/M encounter with that beneficiary. One telemedicine ordering NPI signs orders for beneficiaries across dozens of states within a single week. Beneficiary ZIPs sit far outside the service area declared on the supplier's CMS-855S enrolment. The same beneficiary receives duplicate L-code braces from several unrelated supplier NPIs and pharmacy NPIs within 30 days. Supplier and pharmacy claim volume jumps from near-zero to peer-top-decile shortly after a PECOS ownership change.
660.features_to_create: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim linking that ordering NPI to the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Telemedicine orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct billing supplier or pharmacy NPIs on ordered DMEPOS and topical analgesic claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Duplicate device saturation: on beneficiary x HCPCS, compute count of distinct supplier NPIs paid in rolling 30 days; fires when count exceeds one absent documented replacement reason; action prepay edit.

661.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point here; funding flowed through an employer-sponsored HSA account-opening process. At enrolment, the employer TIN submitted to the third-party administrator has no wage filings and no state employer registration on record. Dozens of enrolled 'employees' share a small set of mailing addresses in one city unrelated to the employer's stated location. The nearest detection route is the administrator's account-opening KYC and card-shipping address controls.
661.features_to_create: 1) Employer verification mismatch: on employer TIN at account setup, compute a match indicator between the submitted TIN and state unemployment-insurance wage filings and IRS TIN-name records; fires on exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension of card funding pending verification. 2) Address concentration: on mailing address x employer TIN, compute count of distinct enrollee SSNs shipped cards to the same street address; fires when count exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peer employer groups of similar size; action documentation request (ADR) before card activation. 3) Funding velocity: on employer TIN x week, compute sum of pre-funded HSA dollars and share of cards drawn to zero within 14 days; fires when above the administrator's trailing baseline for comparable groups; action payment suspension.

662.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, claim lines show balloon sinus dilation CPT codes billed for six sinuses on the same beneficiary across staggered dates. The rendering NPI's rate of sinus dilation per unique beneficiary sits far above same-specialty otolaryngology peers in the payer's claims history. CPT 31235 sphenoid sinusoscopy is billed alongside dilation codes at a rate inconsistent with operative report availability. Prior imaging claims (sinus CT) are absent or show no obstructive disease before the dilation dates of service. The same beneficiary returns for additional sinus dilation lines within a short interval, indicating splitting rather than a single session.
662.features_to_create: 1) Sinus site saturation: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of distinct dilated sinus CPT/modifier sites billed within 180 days; fires when the count reaches all six sinuses without a documented CT indication claim; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Session splitting: on rendering NPI x beneficiary, compute the gap in days between successive balloon dilation dates of service and the count of such sessions per beneficiary; fires when multiple sessions occur within a window shorter than the provider's own trailing median; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Add-on endoscopy ratio: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of CPT 31235 lines to total sinus dilation lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

663.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, a small set of ordering NPIs accounts for a dominant share of one laboratory's total test volume across Medicare, Medicaid and TRICARE. Those same ordering NPIs appear as medical directors or consultants in the lab's CMS-855B ownership and managing-employee fields or in Open Payments records. Test volume per ordering NPI rises sharply in the months after the first consulting payment date in Open Payments. Marketer-linked referral clusters show identical panel composition across unrelated beneficiaries and practices. Ordering physicians' specialty in NPPES is unrelated to the panels they order at that laboratory.
663.features_to_create: 1) Orderer concentration: on laboratory NPI x quarter, compute the share of paid test dollars attributable to the top ordering NPIs and the Herfindahl index over ordering NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty laboratory peers; action postpay audit. 2) Payment-referral coupling: on ordering NPI x laboratory NPI, compute the change in monthly ordered test dollars before versus after the first Open Payments consulting or medical-director payment date; fires when the post-payment rate exceeds the orderer's own trailing baseline; action prepay edit on that pair. 3) Ownership overlap: on ordering NPI, compute an exact match against the laboratory's CMS-855B owner, officer and managing-employee fields; fires on exact registry match without a disclosed safe-harbour arrangement; action claim suspension.

664.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the rendering NPI bills surgical excisional debridement CPT 11042-11047 on nearly every nursing-facility visit for the same beneficiary. Debridement-per-visit ratio for the group TIN sits far above same-specialty wound-care peers in remittance history. Repeat excisional debridements recur at intervals shorter than plausible wound healing on the beneficiary's claim timeline. Facility MDS assessments for those beneficiaries record no pressure ulcer stage consistent with excisional debridement. Separately billed E/M lines accompany debridement lines at a rate above the practice's own trailing baseline, without modifier-25 support.
664.features_to_create: 1) Debridement-per-visit ratio: on rendering NPI x month, compute paid excisional debridement lines divided by total nursing-facility visit lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Repeat-debridement interval: on beneficiary x wound site, compute the gap in days between successive excisional debridement dates of service; fires when the median gap falls below clinically plausible healing intervals; action prepay edit. 3) Assessment corroboration: on beneficiary x date of service, compute a match between the billed debridement depth code and the wound stage recorded on the nearest MDS assessment; fires on exact registry mismatch or absent ulcer coding; action postpay audit.

665.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, OTC COVID test claims carry dates of service preceding the carrier's first shipment scan in the pharmacy's fulfilment records. Monthly test units per beneficiary approach the eight-test program cap for nearly the entire beneficiary panel. Claim counts for a single pharmacy NPI spike far above its own trailing baseline within days. Beneficiaries billed have no other claim history with that pharmacy NPI, indicating no dispensing relationship. Wholesaler acquisition invoices show test kit inventory far below the units billed for that month.
665.features_to_create: 1) Ship-date reconciliation: on claim line, compute the gap in days between billed date of service and the earliest tracking-number ship date supplied by the pharmacy; fires when no ship record exists or the ship date follows the service date; action prepay edit. 2) Inventory-to-billing ratio: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute billed test units divided by units acquired per wholesaler invoice or pedigree data; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action payment suspension. 3) Cap saturation: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of its beneficiaries billed at the full eight-test monthly maximum; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus pharmacy peers; action postpay audit and refund demand.

666.ways_to_identify: No health care claim exists and there is no payer adjudication point in this loan scheme. The nearest detection route is SBA lender underwriting cross-checking the applicant's IRS Form 941 and W-2 filings against the payroll figures claimed. Bank statements submitted as support can be verified through direct account-data feeds rather than uploaded PDFs. Repeated applications sharing one preparer IP address, phone number or bank routing account reveal coordinated filings.
666.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payroll attestation match: on loan application EIN, compute the difference between claimed annual payroll and IRS-transcript wage totals for the same tax year; fires on any mismatch beyond rounding; action documentation request before disbursement.

667.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, the usual-and-customary price submitted on the claim exceeds the pharmacy's own cash discount-program price for the same NDC and quantity. The reported U&C for a generic NDC sits far above the chain's median U&C across its other store NPIs. U&C fields stay static while the pharmacy's advertised discount-club price schedule shows a lower posted price. Reimbursement lands on the U&C price point rather than the lower MAC or FUL benchmark on the state's four-point pricing rule. Only Medicaid claims carry the higher U&C while commercial remittance history for the same NDC shows lower submitted prices.
667.features_to_create: 1) U&C versus cash price: on claim line, compute submitted usual-and-customary price minus the pharmacy's posted discount-program cash price for the same NDC and quantity; fires when the difference is positive; action prepay edit. 2) Chain U&C outlier: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x month, compute the ratio of reported U&C to the chain TIN median U&C for that NDC; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-chain peer stores; action claim suspension. 3) Payer-selective pricing: on NDC x pharmacy TIN, compute the difference between mean U&C on Medicaid claims and mean U&C on commercial claims from remittance history; fires when the difference is positive beyond the trailing baseline; action postpay audit.

668.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, controlled substance claims show refills dispensed before the prior fill's day supply has elapsed for the same beneficiary and NDC. Concurrent active claims for an opioid, a benzodiazepine and a muscle relaxant overlap in days supply for the same beneficiary. Daily morphine milligram equivalents computed from NDC, quantity and day supply exceed guideline ceilings without a prior-authorisation record. Beneficiaries fill the same controlled NDC across multiple pharmacy NPIs and multiple prescriber NPIs within one month. Prescriber NPIs concentrated at one store show controlled-substance shares far above same-specialty peers in PDMP and claims data.
668.features_to_create: 1) Early refill gap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute days between fill date and the prior fill date minus prior day supply; fires when the gap is negative beyond the allowed tolerance; action prepay edit. 2) Trinity overlap: on beneficiary x date, compute overlapping days supply across opioid, benzodiazepine and carisoprodol NDC classes; fires when all three overlap on the same day; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) MME ceiling: on beneficiary x day, compute total morphine milligram equivalents from quantity, strength and day supply across all pharmacy NPIs; fires when above the guideline ceiling without documented cancer or hospice status; action claim suspension.

669.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, controlled substance claims show refills before the prior day supply is exhausted for the same beneficiary and NDC. Opioid, benzodiazepine and muscle-relaxant claims overlap in days supply for the same beneficiary across the chain. Computed daily morphine milligram equivalents exceed guideline ceilings without any prior-authorisation record on file. Single prescriber NPIs supply an outsized share of one store's controlled-substance dispensing volume relative to peers. Beneficiaries fill the same controlled NDC at multiple store NPIs within the same chain in one month.
669.features_to_create: 1) Early refill gap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute fill date minus prior fill date minus prior day supply; fires when negative beyond tolerance; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber concentration at store: on pharmacy NPI x prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of that store's controlled-substance claim dollars from one prescriber; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-region pharmacy peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Cross-store duplication: on beneficiary x NDC x month, compute distinct dispensing pharmacy NPIs with overlapping days supply; fires when the count exceeds one; action claim suspension.

670.ways_to_identify: There is no payer claim adjudication point; the theft ran through the facility's resident trust accounts and check-writing system. Resident trust ledgers show cash disbursements to residents at frequencies and amounts far above the facility's own baseline, all authorised by one staff login. Cancelled checks bear a signature that does not match the on-file signature card for the named signer. Deductions continued for a supplemental insurance policy after the policy's termination date in the carrier file.
670.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Trust disbursement anomaly: on facility x preparer user ID x month, compute the count and dollar sum of cash disbursements from resident trust accounts and the share signed by a single signer; fires when above the facility's trailing baseline or when signer differs from the preparer's authorised signature card; action postpay audit by the state survey agency.

671.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point; the loss was grant funds spent on personal items. The nearest detection route is grantor-side review of the Federal Financial Report and the annual Single Audit against the general ledger. Vendor-level ledger analysis shows disbursements to merchant categories such as appliances, resorts and timeshares that are unallowable under the grant cost principles. Corporate card and check payees can be matched to the executive's home address and personal accounts.
671.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. 1) Unallowable vendor spend: on grantee EIN x quarter, compute the dollar sum of general-ledger disbursements to merchant category codes outside allowable grant cost categories divided by total federal draw; fires when the ratio exceeds zero beyond a documented exception; action grantor documentation request and drawdown suspension.

672.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, NEMT trip claims carry group-ride modifiers while only one beneficiary is billed for that vehicle, date and time. Trip claims exist on dates with no corresponding treatment encounter claim at the destination methadone clinic for that beneficiary. GPS or trip-log records submitted with the broker file show no vehicle movement matching the billed pickup times. Total billed loaded miles and trip counts per driver NPI exceed feasible hours in a 24-hour day. Beneficiaries billed for transport concurrently receive mileage reimbursement or self-transport payments in the same program records.
672.features_to_create: 1) Destination encounter match: on claim line, compute whether a same-day service claim exists for the beneficiary at the billed destination provider NPI; fires when no such encounter claim exists; action prepay edit. 2) Group-ride integrity: on vehicle or driver NPI x date x trip time window, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries billed with a group modifier; fires when the count equals one; action prepay edit and recoupment. 3) Driver-hours feasibility: on driver NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed trip durations plus estimated drive time between successive pickup and drop-off addresses; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action payment suspension.

673.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, ABA claim dates of service fall on days when no staff member appears on the agency's payroll or EVV records. BCBA supervision codes are billed without any paired technician direct-service line for the same beneficiary and date. Billed outpatient ABA dates overlap inpatient hospital claim spans in the beneficiary's other claims. Rendering staff identifiers on claims do not match any credentialed BCBA or RBT in the state licence and certification registry. Billed service hours per rendering staff member exceed 24 hours on individual dates of service.
673.features_to_create: 1) Payroll-claim reconciliation: on rendering staff x date of service, compute billed service units against hours recorded in payroll and EVV visit records; fires when billed units exist with zero corresponding paid or verified hours; action claim suspension. 2) Supervision pairing: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of BCBA supervision lines lacking a same-day technician direct-service line; fires when the count exceeds zero; action prepay edit. 3) Inpatient overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlap in days between outpatient ABA lines and inpatient facility claim spans; fires when overlap is greater than zero; action prepay edit.

674.ways_to_identify: At claim intake, disability and indemnity claims from many policyholders share one employer, one fax number and identical medical excuse note templates. The attending physician's statement bears an NPI whose NPPES address and specialty do not match the treating relationship claimed. No corresponding medical claim exists in the health plan's history for the treatment dates asserted on the disability form. A small set of claimants recur as witnesses, referrers or payees across otherwise unrelated claim files. Bank deposit data shows repeated transfers of a fixed percentage of paid benefits from claimants to one recipient account.
674.features_to_create: 1) Prescriber attestation verification: on claim, compute an exact match of the signing physician NPI, licence number and signature against NPPES and the state licence board file, plus a callback confirmation; fires on registry mismatch or unconfirmed signature; action claim suspension. 2) Submission cluster degree: on employer group x 90 days, compute the count of disability claims sharing the same submitting fax, IP, document template hash or attending NPI; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer employer groups; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Payout kickback pattern: on payee bank account, compute the count of distinct claimants transferring a similar fixed share of benefit payments within 30 days of disbursement; fires when the distinct-claimant count exceeds one; action payment suspension.

675.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, chronic care management CPT 99490 lines lack any time-stamped care-management contact log for the billed month. Total CCM minutes attributable to a single clinical staff member across beneficiaries exceed feasible working hours in the month. The practice bills CCM for nearly its entire eligible panel each month, above same-specialty peer rates. No documented patient consent or care plan claim history precedes the first CCM billing month for the beneficiary. Beneficiaries billed CCM show no chronic-condition diagnosis pair on any claim in the prior year.
675.features_to_create: 1) Staff-minute feasibility: on clinical staff identifier x month, compute the sum of billed CCM minutes implied by CCM code thresholds across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds available paid working hours for that staff member; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Panel saturation: on practice TIN x month, compute the share of attributed beneficiaries with a CCM line billed; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 3) Eligibility precondition: on beneficiary x month, compute the count of distinct qualifying chronic conditions in the prior 12 months of claims; fires when fewer than two conditions are present; action prepay edit.

676.ways_to_identify: At credentialing, the BCBA certification number submitted by the agency is already linked to a different individual and employer in the BACB registry. The supervising BCBA's home address and other claim activity place her in a different state from the billed service locations. Billed rendering-provider hours for the credentialed BCBA exceed 24 hours on individual dates of service. Payroll and agency personnel files list a service deliverer whose name never appears on any submitted claim line. The credentialed BCBA has no remittance or direct-deposit relationship with the billing agency's TIN.
676.features_to_create: 1) Credential identity match: on rendering NPI x billing TIN at enrolment, compute an exact match of certification number, name and date of birth against the BACB registry and state licence board file; fires on any registry mismatch; action claim suspension pending site visit. 2) Rendering-hours feasibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed service units converted to hours across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 3) Staff-claim reconciliation: on billing TIN x month, compute the count of claim-line rendering identifiers with no matching name in payroll or personnel records; fires when the count exceeds zero; action documentation request (ADR).

677.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, respiratory pathogen panel CPT codes are billed on specimens whose accompanying order lists only a SARS-CoV-2 test code. The share of RPP claims to total COVID test claims for the laboratory NPI far exceeds same-specialty laboratory peers. Beneficiaries billed carry no symptomatic respiratory diagnosis code on any claim near the specimen collection date. A single ordering NPI or facility supplies thousands of specimens per week from congregate settings and schools. HRSA Uninsured Program submissions duplicate beneficiaries who also have active Medicare or commercial coverage on eligibility files.
677.features_to_create: 1) Panel-to-order match: on claim line, compute whether the billed RPP CPT is present on the electronic order or requisition record tied to that accession; fires on exact mismatch between ordered and billed test codes; action prepay edit. 2) Reflex ratio: on laboratory NPI x month, compute paid RPP lines divided by COVID-19 test lines from the same accessions; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty laboratory peers; action payment suspension. 3) Coverage duplication: on beneficiary x date of service, compute whether an HRSA Uninsured Program claim coexists with active Medicare or commercial eligibility; fires on exact eligibility-file mismatch; action claim suspension.

678.ways_to_identify: At adjudication, skin-substitute Q-code units billed far exceed the documented wound surface area in square centimeters on the same claim. Beneficiaries with an active hospice election receive high-cost graft applications during the hospice period. Applications repeat on the same wound at intervals shorter than the product's labelled treatment schedule. A handful of nurse practitioner rendering NPIs generate graft dollars above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers. The billing entity's ownership on CMS-855B overlaps with distributor entities receiving the ordering volume, and Open Payments shows large distributor transfers.
678.features_to_create: 1) Graft size versus wound area: on claim line, compute billed Q-code square centimeters minus documented wound area from the wound measurement field or attached note; fires when billed units exceed documented area beyond allowed wastage; action prepay edit. 2) Hospice concurrency: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlap in days between the hospice election period and skin-substitute application dates; fires when overlap is greater than zero without a documented unrelated-condition attestation; action claim suspension. 3) Applier intensity: on rendering NPI x month, compute total paid skin-substitute dollars and distinct beneficiaries receiving repeat applications within the labelled interval; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension and postpay audit.
